### [`v3.18.0`](https://redirect.github.com/aws-amplify/amplify-ui/blob/HEAD/packages/react-storage/CHANGELOG.md#3180)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/aws-amplify/amplify-ui/compare/@aws-amplify/ui-react-storage@3.17.3...@aws-amplify/ui-react-storage@3.18.0)

##### Minor Changes

- [#​7046](https://redirect.github.com/aws-amplify/amplify-ui/pull/7046) [`25e8d96a4c8bee19409cf44f2df7856b52e56260`](https://redirect.github.com/aws-amplify/amplify-ui/commit/25e8d96a4c8bee19409cf44f2df7856b52e56260) Thanks [@​bobbor](https://redirect.github.com/bobbor)! - feat(storage): folder download support in StorageBrowser

  Enable downloading folders (and mixed file/folder selections) from the
  `StorageBrowser` download action. Previously the download button was disabled
  whenever the selection contained a folder.

  Folders are expanded to their files at the view level before the download
  runs: the `DownloadView` lists folder contents on open (with a "listing
  folder contents" state), so the resolved files render as rows and the archive
  is only dispatched once every selected folder is fully enumerated. Each file
  preserves its folder-relative path inside the zip. A single-folder selection
  names the archive after that folder; other selections use the longest common
  ancestor directory of the downloaded files. Building on the service worker
  streaming download, the zip transfer itself uses constant memory; folder
  enumeration holds the file listing in memory and is capped at 5000 files per
  download, above which the download is blocked with a message instead of
  producing a truncated archive.

  Also: individual expanded files can be removed from the pending download,
  enumeration can be cancelled or retried, and empty/errored enumerations are
  surfaced without starting a partial download.

- [#​7044](https://redirect.github.com/aws-amplify/amplify-ui/pull/7044) [`51bb14dfdc4209938dd17480a967218585f8c8d4`](https://redirect.github.com/aws-amplify/amplify-ui/commit/51bb14dfdc4209938dd17480a967218585f8c8d4) Thanks [@​bobbor](https://redirect.github.com/bobbor)! - feat(storage): service worker streaming zip download

  Replace the in-memory blob-based zip download with a service worker streaming
  architecture for `StorageBrowser` multi-file downloads. Files are streamed
  sequentially into a zip archive delivered via a service worker, removing the
  memory ceiling of the previous blob approach. Falls back to blob collection
  when the service worker is unavailable (unsupported browser, missing file, or
  insecure context).

  Note: per-file progress is now reported download-only by design — it reflects
  bytes read from S3, not zip finalization. Because entries are stored without
  compression (`level: 0`), the write/finalization phase is near-instant, so
  progress transitions directly from downloading to complete without a separate
  "zipping"/finishing phase.

##### Patch Changes

- Updated dependencies \[[`21fa602576b12fa59c0101b52eff8551d778352e`](https://redirect.github.com/aws-amplify/amplify-ui/commit/21fa602576b12fa59c0101b52eff8551d778352e), [`379f6c05bf36d0341de36441097ddb7984151e9c`](https://redirect.github.com/aws-amplify/amplify-ui/commit/379f6c05bf36d0341de36441097ddb7984151e9c)]:

author: guichduh33-arch
body:
Ferme l'alerte Dependabot [#47](https://github.com/guichduh33-arch/The_Breakery_ERP/security/dependabot/47) (high, CVSS 7.5 — `AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/C:N/I:N/A:H`), ouverte depuis le 4 août.

## Pourquoi

[GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895) est une **récidive** : l'advisory contourne la mitigation de CVE-2026-14257 — précisément celle que les overrides du repo appliquaient déjà. Les seuils étaient donc devenus insuffisants, sans que rien ne le signale hors de l'alerte.

Deux versions vulnérables étaient effectivement résolues dans le lock :

| Version | Seuil corrigé | Chaîne |
|---|---|---|
| 1.1.16 | ≥ 1.1.18 | `minimatch@3.1.5` ← eslint, eslint-plugin-import, eslint-plugin-react |
| 5.0.8 | ≥ 5.0.9 | `minimatch@10.2.5` ← terser, test-exclude |

## Portée réelle du risque

Faible. L'impact est **disponibilité uniquement** — ni confidentialité ni intégrité : un motif glob hostile fait exploser la mémoire du process qui l'expanse. Or les deux chaînes touchées sont du **tooling de dev/build** (lint, minification, couverture de test), et `brace-expansion` n'y expanse que des motifs écrits dans nos propres configs, jamais une entrée utilisateur. Rien n'atteint le bundle navigateur ni les Edge Functions.

Dependabot classe l'alerte en `scope: runtime`, mais c'est son heuristique sur lockfile qui se trompe : `pnpm why -r` ne remonte que des `devDependencies`.

## Ce qui change

Trois seuils relevés dans `pnpm.overrides`, plus une ligne ajoutée :

```
"brace-expansion@<1.1.16": ">=1.1.16 <2"        →  "brace-expansion@<1.1.18": ">=1.1.18 <2"
"brace-expansion@>=2.0.0 <2.1.3": ">=2.1.3 <3"  →  "brace-expansion@>=2.0.0 <2.1.4": ">=2.1.4 <3"
                                                +  "brace-expansion@>=3.0.0 <3.0.6": ">=3.0.6 <4"
"brace-expansion@>=5.0.0 <5.0.8": ">=5.0.8"     →  "brace-expansion@>=4.0.0 <5.0.9": ">=5.0.9"
```

**La ligne 3.x est un ajout au-delà du strict nécessaire** : aucune 3.x n'est dans l'arbre aujourd'hui, mais l'advisory couvre cette plage et la borne basse de la dernière ligne descend à `>=4.0.0` pour épouser exactement l'advisory. Sans elle, une remontée transitive future rouvrirait l'alerte en silence. Dis-le si tu préfères t'en tenir aux deux versions réellement présentes, je la retire.

## Vérification

- Après `pnpm install --lockfile-only`, le lock ne résout plus que **1.1.18 / 2.1.4 / 5.0.9** — les deux versions vulnérables ont disparu.
- `pnpm install` passe, `eslint` (consommateur direct de la chaîne 1.x) démarre toujours.
- `pnpm --filter @breakery/domain test` : **69 fichiers, 786 tests, tous verts**.
- Aucun changement de code applicatif : le diff se limite à `package.json` et `pnpm-lock.yaml`.

Même geste que la PR #343 sur `js-yaml`.

body:
## Outcome

Reconcile AVC repository/navigation truth with current executable mainline, GitHub control-plane evidence and the dependency owners established on 2026-08-10, and provide one dependency-ordered full-stack recovery design/implementation plan.

## Current truth fixed by this PR

- #297 is historical/closed; #408 is the active PR Runner Bridge pre-status incident.
- Exact current `main` `a7bef68322d05bf1fb867ec3e61d1832e5924ae1` has a complete green historical `avc/ci-local` status set; that evidence does not certify later PR heads.
- GitHub reports private `main` `protected:false` / required checks off; private-repository rulesets are unavailable under the current entitlement. #83 owns the entitlement/compensating-control decision.
- Deleted workflow id `316851241` / `BuildFailed` remains `state: deleted` but can still create `startup_failure` runs; #321 owns GitHub UI/Support cleanup.
- Workforce/Personal contracts already exist on main; the missing layer is executable runtime binding, not another agent framework.
- #410 owns provider invocation authorization from canonical Mission/Job execution authority; routing/target eligibility is not invocation authority.
- #412 separates machine Cloudflare Service Auth from human AVC membership/session acceptance; #318 owns live Cloudflare activation.
- #413 now owns persistent ServiceOps D1 proposal/idempotency parity before final full-stack acceptance.
- Historical large/stale PRs are source archives, not merge candidates: #350→#343–#349, #351→#411, #363–#370→#361 re-cuts, #376/#402 Platform source, #383/#384 Attention/Marketplace source, #401 protected-session source→#412/#318.

## Full-stack execution design added

- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-10-avc-fullstack-runtime-recovery-design.md`
- `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-10-avc-fullstack-runtime-recovery.md`

The execution order is intentionally strict:

```text
#408 exact-head Runner Bridge recovery
→ #409 disposition against the proven root cause
→ #410 canonical provider-invocation authority
→ #405 governed Hermes/Intelligence wiring
→ Workforce A3 read-only Kernel eligibility + Registry
→ Capability Graph + deterministic Worker Scheduler
→ Chief Operator proposal/materialization
→ #343–#349 Business Brain/Context Compiler
→ #412 source hardening + #318 live protected Platform activation
→ #413 persistent ServiceOps PREPARE parity
→ bounded persistent ServiceOps channel-to-Outcome acceptance
```

The plan requires authentic RED→GREEN for each behavioral slice and does not use GitHub-hosted checks, deployment success or local harnesses as substitutes for exact-head `avc/ci-local`.

## Current #408 disposition

Controlled unchanged-head runs on unrelated #405/#407 produced a rapid Runner Bridge terminal result with **zero `avc/ci-local*` commit-status contexts**. Source audit narrows this to verifier launch/root alignment or an early controller preflight, but physical protected logs remain required before claiming root cause.

A self-contained read-only host-worker execution packet has been posted on #408. It captures systemd WorkingDirectory/ExecStart/EnvironmentFile, protected `AVC_REPO_ROOT`, verifier readability/path, controller HEAD/origin and exact #405/#407 logs without exposing tokens. It explicitly prohibits host mutation until the first failing boundary is observed.

author: benbaichmankass
body:
Follow-up to #8693 (merged). New PR because a merged PR cannot track new work; the six commits here are the unmerged remainder, rebased onto current `main`.

## 1. The verdicts

**Population: 7 of the 8 live `ict_scalp` legs, 4 ladder cells each = 28 cells.** The 8th (`ict_scalp_mgc_15m`) stays `blocked:data_missing` — its XAU proxy frame is gone from the trainer, so it was not measured and is not recorded as a negative.

GH Actions **run [31344328313](https://github.com/benbaichmankass/Metis-Insights/actions/runs/31344328313)** — 7 parallel free runners, **7/7 `success`**, ~38 min, $0. Config-exact per leg, IS/OOS split `2025-07-01`, yearly walk-forward on anything clearing the pre-filter.

| | |
|---|---|
| `honest_negative` | **26 / 28** |
| passed the gate **and** the yearly walk-forward | **2 / 28** — `ict_scalp_sol_15m` `bank0.25@1R` and `bank0.5@1R`, both 3/4 usable folds (need 3) |

Coverage: **312 → 319 of 376** live cells. Delta cross-checked as exactly 7 against `git show HEAD:`, not by re-reading the file.

**The two SOL cells are a Tier-3 PROPOSAL, not a ship.** `config/strategies.yaml` is untouched. Two cautions carried into that decision, both visible in the table: the OOS edge is thin in absolute terms (+0.17R / +0.34R over 142 trades) even though the IS edge is not, and **`ict_scalp_sol_5m` — the same symbol one timeframe down — is a clean negative on all four cells**, so whatever makes banking work here is not a property of SOL.

## 2. I was wrong, and my own run is the disproof

Memo § 11.1, written hours before these numbers existed, argued from first principles that banking **necessarily** lowers net_R and lowers maxDD, so nothing shaped like it could ever pass: *"P(pass) = 0, a priori."*

| claim | measured over 28 cells |
|---|--:|
| necessarily **lowers net_R** | net_R **rose** in **6/28** IS and **8/28** OOS |
| **lowers maxDD** | maxDD **rose** (got worse) in **7/28** IS and **14/28** OOS |
| **P(pass) = 0** | **2/28 passed**, incl. walk-forward |

**Why it was wrong.** The argument followed only the *winner* side of the distribution. On a fixed 1.5R bracket with a 1.0R rung, banking also converts a loser that first printed +1R from a full −1R into `0.25·(+1) + 0.75·(−1) = −0.5R` — so where that population is large it *earns* net_R. And maxDD is a property of the equity **path**, not of individual trade sizes: capping the biggest winners removes the recoveries that used to *end* drawdowns, so peak-to-trough deepened on **12 of the 16** 5m OOS cells.

This is the failure mode RULE ONE names explicitly — *"verify your own output too, hardest when it confirms what you expected."* § 10.1 had **already** recorded that the fat-tail premise does not transfer to a capped-upside strategy; § 11.1 asserted the general form anyway, one section later. It felt like a derivation, so it was never queued for measurement.

**Corrected in place, not deleted** — the claim was written into a canonical memo and acted on, so the correction needs a findable home: § 11.1 keeps a strike-through + retraction banner, § 10.6 is the measurement, `m20_banking_risk_adjusted.py`'s docstring is rewritten, and `BL-20260810-BANKING-GATE-CANNOT-PASS` is rescoped **under its original id**.

**§ 6.2's measurements were never in doubt and stand.** What fell is the claim that they *had* to come out that way: those 20 cells are trend-following legs whose edge genuinely is the fat right tail, so the prior is real but does not transfer.

**Net effect: the finding is a stronger negative, not a weaker one.** On three of the four 5m legs banking lost on **both** axes out-of-sample — not a tail-for-smoothness trade, simply worse.

## 3. Also in these commits

- **Capital efficiency** — the exit-refinement skill has always declared *net_R per position-day* as the gate's tiebreak and **no harness ever computed it**. Now emitted, and **capital-weighted** for banking (`capital_bars`), because unweighted `bars_held` would score banking identically to doing nothing. `bar_minutes` is **measured** from the frame's own timestamps, never assumed from the label; `position_days`/`capital_days` are `None`, never `0.0`, when unmeasurable.
- **A green run that delivered nothing.** The verdict-posting step logged `core.warning` and exited 0 when it could not resolve the PR — so all 7 jobs went green having posted zero verdicts (#8693 had merged two minutes earlier). It now resolves from `context.sha` and `core.setFailed`s. This run's verdicts were recovered from the job logs.
- **Wrong dataset caught before it mattered** — an earlier trainer attempt silently picked up `data/` (2021+) rather than `m27_data/` (the vintage every other M27 verdict in these rows used). Re-routed; the run above is on the correct frames.
- `artifact-validity-guard` caught `m20_banking_risk_adjusted.py` absent from `RESEARCH-CAPABILITY-INDEX.md`. Indexed.

## Architecture impact

- [x] **Not applicable** — docs/JSON, research tooling, one workflow. **Tier 1.** No `config/`, no `src/`, no order path, no DB write, no VM state change. The backtest harness places no orders.

## Test plan

- [x] All 7 sweep jobs `success`; verdicts transcribed from job logs and cross-checked by arithmetic (28 cells, counts recomputed rather than eyeballed — a hand count of pending-by-lever was off by 2 and the script caught it)
- [x] Coverage delta asserted as **exactly 7** against `git show HEAD:`, with row count and key set unchanged
- [x] Backlog rebase conflict resolved by taking `main` **verbatim** and re-appending only my rows, with an id-set assertion that no `main` row was dropped or reordered (438 rows, no duplicates)
- [x] `canonical-doc-coherence` passes
- [x] Guards **33 PASS / 1 FAIL** — the failure is `layer-guard`, exit **127**: `lint-imports` is not installed in this sandbox (`which` confirms). Not a finding; CI provides it
- [ ] CI green

## Operator decisions this surfaces

1. **Tier-3:** ship `ict_scalp_sol_15m` `bank0.5@1R` (the stronger of the two survivors)? Nothing is merged toward it.
2. `BL-20260810-BANKING-GATE-CANNOT-PASS` rescoped: the only remaining question is whether the **prop sleeve** should be gated on survival-weighted EV rather than net_R, given a daily-loss or static-DD breach there is terminal. `PB-20260712-PROP-BANKING-EV` has the tooling and has sat unused for a month.

## Discovery probe closeout

This fail-closed probe tested exactly **MB100-075 — Washington, District of Columbia** against production `main` at `cfd74943896abec154abfd6fa2d0b37feede1e15`.

### Result

- Workflow run: `31346919106` — expected failure
- Evidence artifact: `9047626592`
- Artifact digest: `sha256:3dd4eaf371469182b25b69a7978ce919c734cbb34998243d7ce233416994972d`
- Selector matched: `ocd-division/country:us/district:dc`
- RAW retained: `TRUE`
- Identifier join: `TRUE`
- Deterministic parity: `TRUE`
- Source provenance: `TRUE`
- Generated Division: `divisions/dc/local/district_of_columbia__6cd1ebf4-57c3-5814-bb6e-2fcf9577c250.yaml`
- Jurisdiction path: missing
- Normalized/QA/COMPLETE_OK: `FALSE`

### Root cause

The pinned generator correctly routes the `district:dc` Division under `dc/`, but its jurisdiction seed treats an admin-1-only `district:` OCDID as division type `unknown`. The existing no-match continuation logic therefore writes a stub Division but cannot generate the federal-district government Jurisdiction.

This branch is intentionally closed unmerged. The next step is one reusable federal-district root rule with focused upstream regression tests; no workbook status was advanced.

author: izumacha
body:
## 概要

Dependabot PR #272（npm-minor-and-patch グループ 11 件）が CI レッドで止まっていたため、**同じ依存更新を取り込んだうえでブロッカーを解消**した差し替え PR です。#272 はこの PR がマージされた時点でクローズされます。

## ブロッカー 1: Stripe の API バージョンのピン留め

```
src/lib/stripe.ts(39,7): error TS2322:
  Type '"2026-06-24.dahlia"' is not assignable to type '"2026-07-29.dahlia"'.
```

stripe SDK が 22.3.2 → 22.4.0 に上がったことで `apiVersion` の型が `'2026-07-29.dahlia'` に切り替わり、`src/lib/stripe.ts` のピン留め定数が型と食い違って typecheck が落ちていました。

`STRIPE_API_VERSION` は定数のコメントどおり「インストール済み SDK が対応するバージョンに合わせる」方針なので、**SDK を上げたら同じコミットで追随させるのが正しい形**です。ピン留め自体は残しています（Stripe 側が API バージョンを更新しても、こちらの意図しないタイミングで挙動が変わらないようにするため）。

なお、この変更は Webhook の署名検証には影響しません（`constructEvent` の検証は endpoint secret による生ペイロードの HMAC で、クライアントの `apiVersion` に依存しないため）。

## ブロッカー 2: `@typescript-eslint/parser` の宣言範囲が peer 制約に違反していた

`/code-review ultra` の指摘で発見。Dependabot の group 更新は `@typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin` の範囲を `^8.66.0` へ上げた一方、**`@typescript-eslint/parser` の範囲を `^8.65.0` のまま残していました**（lock だけが 8.66.0 に動いていた）。plugin 8.66.0 は `peerDependencies` で parser `^8.66.0` を要求するため、宣言範囲の下限が peer 制約に違反した状態です。

現状動いているのは npm が範囲内の最新を選んでいるからにすぎず、下限に落ちる解決（parser を明示的に 8.65.0 へ固定する / override 付きで lock を再生成する等）では ERESOLVE で失敗します。lock は既に 8.66.0 を解決済みなので、`package.json` の範囲を実態に合わせるだけで解消します。

これが「11 件目」で、当初の説明が 10 件しか列挙していなかったのもこの取りこぼしが原因でした（下表は修正済み）。

## 取り込んだ更新

**すべて minor/patch で、メジャーバージョンの更新は含みません。**

| パッケージ | 変更 |
|---|---|
| `@hookform/resolvers` | ^5.5.7 → ^5.7.1 |
| `react-hook-form` | ^7.83.0 → ^7.84.0 |
| `stripe` | ^22.3.2 → ^22.4.0 |
| `@playwright/test` | ^1.62.0 → ^1.62.1 |
| `@types/react` | ^19.2.17 → ^19.2.18 |
| `@types/react-dom` | ^19.2.3 → ^19.2.4 |
| `@typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin` | ^8.65.0 → ^8.66.0 |
| `@typescript-eslint/parser` | ^8.65.0 → ^8.66.0（本 PR で追加。上記ブロッカー 2） |
| `eslint-config-next` | ^16.2.12 → ^16.3.0 |
| `postcss` | ^8.5.9 → ^8.5.26 |
| `tsx` | ^4.23.1 → ^4.23.9 |

## 検証

`npm ci` → `npm run db:generate` の後、CI と同じコマンドをローカルで実行:

- `npm run lint` — 通過（ESLint 警告・エラーなし）
- `npm run typecheck` — 通過
- `npm run test` — 1273 passed / 195 skipped（#286 マージ直後と同数。挙動不変）

## 見送り（本 PR の範囲外・いずれも既存の課題）

`/code-review ultra` で挙がったうち、以下 2 件は本 PR で導入したものではないため扱いません。

1. **`@typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin` / `parser` は直接の依存として使われていない** — `eslint.config.mjs` はルール名 `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars` を指定するだけで、これらを import していません。実際に ESLint が読むのは `eslint-config-next` 経由の `typescript-eslint@8.58.1` にネストされた copy（実測で確認）で、ルートの 8.66.0 は読まれません。つまりこの 2 件の bump は lint の挙動に影響せず、インストールツリーの重複だけを増やしています。削除が妥当ですが、依存の棚卸しは group 更新とは別の変更なので分離します。
2. **`eslint-config-next` (^16.3.0) と `next` (^15.5.15) のメジャー不一致** — `eslint-config-next` は `next` を peer に持たないため npm が警告しません。解消するには `eslint-config-next` を 15.x に戻すか `next` を 16 へ上げる必要があり、後者は #273（Next 16 移行）そのものです。

## 残る Dependabot PR

本 PR で解消するのは #272 のみです。残る 4 本はいずれもメジャー移行で、原因を特定したうえで**別途対応が必要**です。

| PR | 内容 | ブロッカー |
|---|---|---|
| #273 | next 15 → 16 | `revalidateTag` の引数が変更され `notify.ts` / `notification-actions.ts` で TS2554 |
| #274 / #275 | @prisma/client・prisma 5 → 7 | メジャー 2 段。契約テストも失敗 |
| #276 | undici 7 → 8 | メジャー |

author: potaetoe
body:
The owner's ruling on #178, plus #174 as its one control group, plus
the gate arm that stops the drift class recurring.

**The instrument de-cards.** Six runner-headed `.tool` sections — Key,
Published, Membership, Result, Charts, Publish — and one box left. The
runner's rule spans the wide column and IS the divider, so every
section is the same width by construction rather than by nine boxes
agreeing. Measured at 1350px: all six at x=264, w=1047. Inside them
#71 survives — prose and inputs at 736 centered at x=420 — and only
the eighteen-column table and the charts take the runner's width,
named as exceptions so a section added later is narrow by default.

**The one box did not satisfy the ruling on its own.** `body.wide
.narrow` set max-width and auto inline margins and no `width`, and
auto margins in a flex column's cross axis suppress stretch — so each
box took its own content's width and the five of them rendered at 255,
520, 163, 736 and 736 px, on the page whose ruling opens "cards to all
be the same width". One declaration fixes it; all five now measure 736
at x=420.

**#91's chip goes in, reversing that ticket's call for a reason that
did not exist then.** #91 left the `caution` off because a two-word
chip only repeated the sentence. The rule pinned here changes what the
chip is for: on this surface a box IS the warning, so the chip is how
a box says so, and a box that says nothing is a tool that kept its
card. `Result` moves flag → runner in `LABELS` in the same change: it
names one of six sections now rather than reporting a verdict.

**#174.** Three downloads, one role — `secondary` for all three,
because `primary` still means something here (Fetch and decrypt, Add,
Publish snapshot) and three fills would read as three consequential
acts. The pressed control takes the filled family's colors for four
seconds: unmistakably not the hover treatment, since the button under
the cursor is the one just pressed, and already a measured pairing
because it is `.primary`'s. It must not claim the file arrived — the
browser never tells the page — so the class is spent on the press and
the live region says handed to the browser.

**Check 25** compares the geometry each card page RESOLVES from its
own body classes, and pins every surface-qualified rule that paints a
card component in `CARD_SCOPES`, both directions. Shaped so an edit to
`.card` itself moves both pages together and stays green — a check
that reddens when the design legitimately evolves everywhere at once
gets edited until it stops (#142). Which page wears which grammar is
derived from `SHELLS` and `SURFACES` rather than becoming a third
hand-kept roster (#206).

**A defect in that check, found by the mutation meant to arm it.** It
resolved by "last declaration wins", which is the cascade with
specificity left out — and a surface override written above the
component it overrides wins in a browser and lost here. The mutation
is the honest shape of the mistake: scope declared, roster satisfied,
class on one page's body. The whole gate stayed green through it. The
third commit computes specificity; the same mutation now names the
property, both pages and both values.

**The member pages never drifted, and that is the finding** — every
card on submit.html and dashboard.html already measured 736 at x=420
with identical padding, radius, border and gap, now machine-compared
rather than assumed. They did carry `.narrow` on four boxes, a class
declared only under `body.wide`, saying in the markup that a box was
narrower than its neighbours and painting it the same. Removed, and
refused there.

Mutations, ten, all reverted and re-verified clean: an undeclared
surface scope · a stale `CARD_SCOPES` pin · a scope declared honestly
on one card page (the agreement arm itself) · the same edit moved
everywhere at once, which stays QUIET and is the negative control · a
tool keeping its card · a warning box losing its chip · a section

author: dmccoystephenson
body:
<!-- gardener-tend-dispatch -->

## Summary

Three defects in `/resetspawn` sender feedback are fixed, and the documentation claim that this project has no automated tests is corrected.

- **Misleading success (#67).** `/resetspawn <player>` sent a green "Spawn reset for X!" unconditionally. `UUIDChecker.findUUIDBasedOnPlayerName` returns `null` for an unknown name, and `PersistentData.resetSpawn(null)` is a no-op, so an operator was told a reset had happened when nothing changed. An unresolvable name is now reported as not found and no reset is claimed.
- **Silent no-op from the console (#68).** `execute` wrapped its whole body in `if (sender instanceof Player)` with no `else`, while `CommandService.interpretCommand` still returned `true`, so Bukkit suppressed its own fallback message too. A non-player sender received nothing at all. Such senders are now told the command is for in-game players only, which is what `COMMANDS.md` already documented.
- **Swallowed exception.** The target notification was wrapped in a `try` whose `catch (Exception e)` block was empty, absorbing the `NullPointerException` thrown when `getPlayer(<name>)` returned `null` for an offline target. The target is now looked up by UUID and null-checked, so the offline case is expressed rather than caught.
- **Documentation drift (#69).** `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and `.github/copilot-instructions.md` each stated that no test suite exists. JUnit 5 and Mockito are configured in `pom.xml` and 24 tests now run under `mvn test`. All three files are corrected, and the manual server-verification steps are kept as the complement for behaviour needing a live Bukkit runtime.

## Supporting change

`ResetSpawnCommand` now takes an `org.bukkit.Server` instead of the plugin instance, and `CommandService` passes `dansSpawnSystem.getServer()`. This is what makes the command testable at all: `DansSpawnSystem` is `final` and `JavaPlugin.getServer()` is `final`, neither of which Mockito's default (subclass) mock maker can stub, whereas `Server` is an interface. No caller outside `CommandService` constructs this class.

The self-reset path also now uses `player.getUniqueId()` directly instead of round-tripping the sender's own name through `UUIDChecker`. Behaviour is identical for an online sender — the checker scans online players first and matches by name — but the same null-returning failure mode is removed from that path.

## Test plan

- [x] `mvn test` — 24 tests pass (8 new in `ResetSpawnCommandTest`, 16 pre-existing).
- [x] Regression evidence confirmed empirically, not by reasoning: with the previous command body restored (the `Server` parameter kept so the tests still compile), `mvn test` reports 4 failures — `execute_nonPlayerSender_isToldTheCommandIsPlayerOnly`, `execute_unresolvableTargetName_reportsNotFoundAndResetsNothing`, `execute_onlineTargetName_alsoNotifiesTheTarget`, and `execute_noArguments_resetsTheSendersOwnSpawn`. All pass again once the fix is restored.
- [ ] Manual server check recommended before release: run `/resetspawn` from the server console (expect the player-only message), `/resetspawn NoSuchPlayer` in game (expect not-found, no success), and `/resetspawn <online player>` (expect both messages). Event-driven and on-disk behaviour is out of reach of the unit suite.

## Documentation

`COMMANDS.md` and `USER_GUIDE.md` were re-checked against the implementation and need no change — the documented syntax, permission nodes, and the "in-game players only" note all still match, and the permission strings match `plugin.yml`. `CONFIG.md` is unaffected. `CHANGELOG.md` gains an `[Unreleased]` section describing this change.

## Deferred this cycle

The remaining open issues were filed during this cycle's triage and are intentionally left for a later one:

- **#70** (`develop` branch referenced in contributor docs) — the branch-workflow lines are a project policy statement rather than a factual error, so a maintainer decision on the intended target branch is wanted before they are rewritten. The purely factual test-framework line in the same file is corrected here under #69.
- **#71** (spawns with a zero coordinate discarded on load) — the fix requires extracting the record parsing in `StorageService` from its file and world-creation concerns before it can be tested, which exceeds a polish-sized change.
- **#72** (sign types newer than Minecraft 1.15 unrecognised) — blocked on a `spigot-api` version bump or a deliberate move away from the enum switch, both of which change the supported server range and belong to the maintainers.

Closes #67
Closes #68
Closes #69

This PR description was drafted during a Gardener session (https://github.com/Stephenson-Software/gardener).

author: os-project-manager
body:
Fixes #7107

## What was wrong

`scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` applied `isChangesetFile()` to the **head** path only:

```js
const basePath = fields[1];
if (!file || !isChangesetFile(file)) continue;
```

`basePath` — the pre-rename name an `R` row is read at, and the whole reason `R` is readable — was then handed straight to `git show` with no guard of its own. Git pairs renames by **content**, not by name, and the pathspec is `.changeset/*.md`, which `.changeset/README.md` matches. So an `R` row can legitimately arrive as `.changeset/README.md` paired with `.changeset/x.md`, and the majors README appears to declare get subtracted from the head file's majors — reporting a brand-new whole-stack major as **exempt** rather than introduced. That is this gate's expensive direction.

The two siblings PR #7106 fixed (`check-empty-changeset.mjs`, `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`) already carry `isChangesetFile(basePath)` explicitly. This file is the third member of the family; the gap was not a missing helper but a guard applied to one of the two paths.

## The change

One condition, transcribed from the siblings rather than invented:

```js
const baseText = status === 'A' || !isChangesetFile(basePath) ? null : showOrNull(from, basePath, cwd);
```

For `M` the guard is a no-op — `basePath` is the path already accepted on the line above. Only `R` can reach it with a different name.

## The fixture, and why it is not vacuous

**This defect is dormant.** The real `.changeset/README.md` is boilerplate with no frontmatter fence, so `majorPackagesIn()` returns `[]` on it and nothing is subtracted today. A careless fixture would therefore pass with or without the guard and would *certify* the hole. So the new self-test case:

1. commits a **major-shaped** `.changeset/README.md` at the branch point, so the unguarded path really has something to subtract;
2. asserts git actually emitted `R`, matching the whole row against `/^R\d+\told\tnew$/` via a new `renameRow` helper (the same shape both siblings use) — too small a body and git degrades the pair to add-plus-delete, and the case would silently be testing an ordinary `A`;
3. keeps both sides byte-identical, so the only thing that could excuse the head file's major is a major read off README.

Measured control, git 2.43.0:

```
R100	.changeset/README.md	.changeset/was-the-readme.md
```

## Ablation (direction predicted before running)

Prediction: removing the guard makes `already` become `['@objectstack/spec']`, `added` empties, and the row flips from `introduced` to `exempt` — so exactly the three new assertions go red and nothing else moves.

With the guard (this PR):

```
✓ check-changeset-no-major --self-test: 117 assertions (frontmatter dialects measured
  against @changesets/parse + the pre/exit exemption switch in both directions +
  the #7005 diff scoping over real temp git repos + the #4690 pins + the wiring).
exit 0
```

With the guard deleted (the one-line revert, run on a copy of the script so the real file stayed untouched):

```
✗ check-changeset-no-major --self-test — 3 failure(s)

  • #7107: a changeset paired with a major-shaped README.md by rename detection inherits NOTHING — got []
  • #7107: ... and it is certainly not exempt — got [".changeset/was-the-readme.md"]
  • #7107: ... so with pre-mode exited that PR is RED
exit 1
```

Predicted direction confirmed, including the `exempt` value the defect produces. Assertion count 113 on `origin/main` to 117 here — the four assertions added, no case re-spelled or removed.

## Verification

- `pnpm check:changeset-gate-self-tests` (the exact step lint.yml runs) — all three family gates green: 105 / 142 / 117 assertions.
- `pnpm check:nul-bytes` — 75 self-test assertions plus a clean 6592-file scan.
- `npx eslint scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs --no-inline-config` — exit 0.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base origin/main` on this branch — `✓ This diff introduces no major bump.`

## Changeset

None, deliberately: a `scripts/`-only diff releases no package. `skip-changeset` applied instead, matching the precedent of #7048, #7104 and #7106.

author: masked-kunsiquat
body:
Root cause was the test helper, not the ViewModel. **Supersedes #29**, which recorded this as open tech debt with an unverified hypothesis — that entry should be dropped rather than merged.

## What was wrong

`runCurrentUntilOrTimeOut` **returned silently** when it exhausted its bound. A timeout therefore surfaced as whichever assertion came next — so a machine too busy to propagate a Room invalidation in time reported:

> pendingSession must have moved on to a new session B

which names neither the cause nor the location, and sends the reader to inspect ViewModel state that is perfectly fine. That is why these looked mysterious.

The bound was also too tight: 200 attempts ≈ 1 real second. Ample on an idle machine, demonstrably not on a loaded one. The sibling helper in `BackfillViewModelTest` already documents **5 seconds** as the generous-but-bounded figure — this one being 5× tighter was an accident, not a decision.

## Measured, not assumed

A timing change can pass by perturbing the schedule rather than removing the cause, which looks solved and isn't. So:

| | Result |
|---|---|
| Baseline on `main` | **5 failures / 15 runs** (~33%) |
| After the fix | **0 failures / 25 runs** |

At the old rate, 25 consecutive passes is roughly a 1-in-14,000 event.

**Honest limit:** 25 runs cannot prove zero. A low residual rate can't be excluded by this evidence. What it does establish is that the 33% rate is gone.

## Why this is a real fix rather than a raised timeout

The `fail()` half is the substantive part. If the awaited work genuinely never happens, the test now says *that*, at the point it happened. Previously that case was indistinguishable from a slow machine, and both got reported as an unrelated assertion. The larger bound removes the false positives; the explicit failure means the true positives stay visible.

## Testing

- [x] `./gradlew :shared:jvmTest :shared:testDebugUnitTest` — green, plus the 25-run loop above
- [x] `./gradlew :app:assembleDebug` — CI runs this
- [ ] `./gradlew :app:connectedDebugAndroidTest` — n/a, no app code changed
- [ ] Ran on a real device — n/a

Compose screens tested: none changed.

## Known gaps

Only the residual-rate caveat above. The other tests in this class use the same helper and were never observed failing, but they benefit from the same change.

Documentation-impact: updated - added `docs/NEXTCLOUD_TALK_BOT.md` and updated `docs/BOT_GUIDE.md` for Nextcloud Talk setup and usage.
Cache-impact: none - no provider-visible prompt, tool schema, memory prefix, output style, skill index, request serialization, or cache-key behavior changes.

System-prompt-review: author-verified - `internal/config` only adds Nextcloud Talk connection credential fields; generated system-prompt content is unchanged.

## Summary

Adds **Nextcloud Talk** as a first-class Reasonix bot/channel, implementing #8117.

This PR includes:

- `PlatformNextcloudTalk` as a first-class bot platform identifier.
- A new `internal/bot/nextcloudtalk` adapter using Nextcloud Talk's official signed webhook bot API.
- HMAC-SHA256 verification for inbound Talk webhook requests.
- Signed outbound messages to the Talk OCS bot message endpoint.
- Mapping of Talk conversation tokens, actor IDs, message IDs, display names, and text into Reasonix's generic bot message model.
- `replyTo` support for outbound replies.
- Loop protection for bot-authored ActivityStreams events.
- Persistent Nextcloud-specific connection settings: server URL, listen address, webhook path, and secret environment reference.
- Runtime registration in `internal/botruntime`.
- `reasonix bot start --channels nextcloud-talk` support.
- `reasonix bot doctor` checks for Nextcloud configuration and secret availability.
- Desktop **Settings -> Bots -> Nextcloud Talk** setup UI.
- Desktop connection diagnostics and test-send support.
- Sidebar/session mapping and per-connection access/routing integration.
- English, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese UI strings.
- Unit tests for webhook authentication, outbound signing/replies, runtime binding, config rendering, and desktop credential round-trip.
- Setup documentation in `docs/NEXTCLOUD_TALK_BOT.md` and `docs/BOT_GUIDE.md`.

## Security

The Talk shared secret is referenced through an environment variable / Reasonix secret handling and is not stored directly in TOML configuration. Incoming webhook requests fail closed unless their Talk HMAC signature verifies.

The adapter defaults to a loopback listener (`127.0.0.1:38017`) and can be published through an HTTPS reverse proxy for a remote Nextcloud server.

## Nextcloud API

The implementation follows the official Talk bot API model:

- signed ActivityStreams webhook events
- `X-Nextcloud-Talk-Random` / `X-Nextcloud-Talk-Signature`
- outbound `X-Nextcloud-Talk-Bot-Random` / `X-Nextcloud-Talk-Bot-Signature`
- `POST /ocs/v2.php/apps/spreed/api/v1/bot/{token}/message`

## Setup

The documentation includes the required `occ talk:bot:install` registration, webhook/response features, reverse-proxy guidance, desktop configuration, and headless usage.

## Verification

- Nextcloud Talk adapter unit tests cover signed inbound webhooks, bad signatures, outbound signing/replies, and bot-event loop protection.
- Runtime/config/desktop tests cover channel registration, credential rendering, and desktop credential round-trip.
- Frontend integration adds the Nextcloud Talk setup surface and locale strings.

Closes #8117.

## Summary

This integration PR supersedes the unqualified Dependabot runtime-stack update in PR #9 and applies it on top of merged hardening PR #11.

- Upgrade `librosa` from `0.10.2.post1` to `0.11.0`.
- Upgrade `soundfile` from `0.12.1` to `0.14.0`.
- Update every CI CPU matrix stack to install the same new audio baseline.
- Keep the requirements-based `pip-audit` flow from PR #11.
- Update validation documentation to record the newly qualified baseline.

## Qualification evidence

Local qualification on this branch:

- CPU matrix: 9/9 cells passed across Python 3.10, 3.11, 3.12 and JAX 0.4.30, 0.5.3, 0.6.2.
- Each CPU cell: strict verification passed, golden/frontend gate 22 passed, full suite 255 passed and 32 skipped.
- CUDA JAX 0.6.2 on RTX 3070: golden 17 passed, frontend 5 passed, full suite 255 passed and 32 skipped.
- CUDA `pip-audit -r requirements-gpu.txt`: no known vulnerabilities.
- CPU/CUDA finite forward and parity passed for all three models. Maximum absolute differences were below `5e-5`.
- CUDA CLI smoke and compilation-cache warm/reuse passed.
- Wheel and sdist build: passed.
- Package-content gate: 9 passed.
- Wheel and sdist clean-room install, `pip check`, strict artifact verification, finite forward, and CLI smoke: passed.
- `twine check` for wheel and sdist: passed.
- `pip-audit -r requirements-jax.txt`: no known vulnerabilities.
- CI YAML parse and `git diff --check`: passed.

## Why this is not PR #9 as-is

The previous PR #9 hosted run was based on the old `main` commit and old CI workflow. Its failed jobs were therefore not a valid qualification of this new audio stack:

- The audit job used the old local audit path and reported the old runner's `setuptools 79.0.1` advisory.

This PR makes the hosted matrix install `librosa==0.11.0` and `soundfile==0.14.0` directly, while retaining the audit hardening from PR #11.

## Release policy

No version bump, tag, GitHub Release, PyPI upload, or public package publication is included. PR #9 is intentionally not merged as part of this PR; it can be closed as superseded after this integration PR is green.

author: nogate-ai
body:
## Summary

Fixes #845: the `pipeline` construct has its own SV expression emitters (`src/codegen/pipeline.rs`), and they never called the `BitSlice`/`PartSelect` base hoist. So **both** arch#807's `Concat`/`Repeat` fix (PR #811) and arch#810's `FunctionCall`/`MethodCall` fix (PR #844) were inert inside a pipeline stage — the base was still emitted bare, producing SystemVerilog no supported frontend will compile, for input `arch check` accepts.

```systemverilog
- s0_cap <= 8'(w)[5:2];                  // verilator: syntax error, unexpected '['
                                         // iverilog:  Malformed statement
+ logic [8-1:0] arch_idx_base_0;
+ assign arch_idx_base_0 = 8'(w);
+ s0_cap <= arch_idx_base_0[5:2];
```

## Why it wasn't a one-line reuse of `hoist_slice_base`

The pipeline emitters rewrite identifiers as they render (a stage reg `cap` becomes `s0_cap`, a cross-stage `S0.cap` read becomes `s0_cap`), and pipelines have no `module_scopes` entry (resolve.rs builds those for modules and fsms only). A hoist driven off the raw AST would emit a temp whose RHS — and whose `$bits(...)` width fallback — named identifiers that do not exist in the emitted SV.

**Fix: parameterize the existing hoist on its emission scope, don't copy it.** `hoist_slice_base` → `hoist_slice_base_in` and `infer_sv_width_str` → `infer_sv_width_str_in`, both taking

- `emit: &dyn Fn(&Expr) -> String` — how to render a sub-expression in the caller's scope. Used *only* inside `$bits(...)` fallbacks; width sub-expressions of a type (`UInt<W>`'s `W`, `.trunc<N>()`'s `N`) stay on `emit_expr_str`, since those are const/param expressions, never stage-rewritten signal references.
- `signal_width: &dyn Fn(&Expr) -> Option<String>` — optional declared-width resolution for a plain signal reference, consulted just before each `$bits(...)` fallback.

The module/fsm path passes `(emit_expr_str, |_| None)`, which is behavior-identical to before. The pipeline path passes its stage-prefix-rewriting emitter plus a new `pipeline_signal_width_str`, which resolves through the pipeline's own AST — the same two shapes (bare ident against the hinted stage then the ports; explicit `Stage.signal`) that arch#808's `try_emit_pipeline_reverse_chunked` already resolves. The `&dyn Fn` callback shape matches the house style already used for `emit_method_call_str(..., MethodCallHost::Pipeline, ...)`.

**Which base kinds are claimed, the runtime-`for`-loop-variable bail, and the shared `arch_idx_base_<n>` counter / `index_hoist_lines` drain are unchanged and still live in exactly one place.** The bail semantics are preserved verbatim.

## Placement of the temp: now handled entirely by #846's `HoistScope`

A hoisted temp is a module item — a variable declaration plus a continuous `assign` — and a pipeline interleaves its reading statements with other `<=`/`=` statements inside two procedural blocks:

- the stage-update `always_ff`
- the `always_comb` it emits for a non-trivial (branching) stage `comb`

A variable declaration is legal only at the *top* of a procedural block, so an inline drain lands it mid-block and the file is rejected outright (`%Error: syntax error, unexpected IDENTIFIER` / `Malformed statement`). I hit this on the first pass and originally carried my own opt-in sink (`deferred_hoist_lines` + `begin/end_module_scope_hoists` in pipeline.rs) to splice the temps above each block.

**That is now deleted.** #853 (issue #846) landed `HoistScope`, which keys on *the SV block being emitted* rather than on which emitter queued the temp — and the pipeline's `always_ff`/`always_comb` openers go out through `line()` like any other, so `HoistScope::Procedural` splices their temps to module scope automatically. The two mechanisms were solving the same problem at different granularities; #853's is the more general one, so this PR carries none of its own. Net effect on this PR: −45 lines of pipeline.rs, one fewer `Codegen` field, and one placement mechanism in the tree instead of two.

Emitted result, unchanged from before the rebase:

```systemverilog
  logic [8-1:0] arch_idx_base_0;
  assign arch_idx_base_0 = 8'(w);
  // ...four more...
  always_ff @(posedge clk) begin
    ...
      capture_cap_trunc <= arch_idx_base_0[5:2];
```

These forms are already accepted by `arch check` today; only the emitted SV shape changes. `is_portable_bit_slice_base` (src/typecheck.rs) is untouched — retiring that allowlist is #813 P1, a spec-surface widening blocked on maintainer sign-off, and this fix is independent of it.

Also fixed one stale doc reference #853's rename left behind (`index_hoist_lines` -> `index_hoist_temps`).

**Fast gate (re-run post-rebase):** `cargo build --release`, full `cargo test --release` — every suite green, **zero failures** (805 integration — my 2 plus #853's, none lost — + 56 fp + 29 formal + the rest; the 2 Lean-replay `formal_test` tests pass once `proofs/lean_thread_lowering/.lake` is present). `cargo fmt --check` clean. `cargo clippy --release --all-targets` reports no errors.

**Dual-simulator behavioral** — new fixture `tests/icarus_portability/PipeSliceHoist.arch`, 9 outputs covering `Concat` / `Repeat` / `.trunc` / `.zext` / `.reverse` × `BitSlice` / `PartSelect`, across all three positions a pipeline emits expressions into:

## What

**Owner decision, 10.08.2026:** adopt `0108_trial_grace_read_only_enforcement` from `codex/improvement-campaign-20260808`, extending decision #15 — the 09.08 UI-only soft block gains a database floor. Renumbered to **`0092`**; content unchanged except the number.

The model: **30-day trial → 7 full grace days → tenant-wide read-only at the row boundary**, enforced by a `zz_organization_write_guard` trigger on every `org_id` table — including through `service_role` and SECURITY DEFINER writers. Reads never close ("הנתונים שמורים במלואם" stays true). `security_events` is exempt so an expired platform operator can still step up and recover a tenant. `set_organization_lifecycle` remains the only lifecycle writer, now behind fresh reauthentication.

## Verified

* Fresh `supabase db reset`, then `0092` applied cleanly — the md5 ancestry guards (`auth_org`, `set_organization_lifecycle`) match a fresh reset. (The stale local DB initially suggested a mismatch; the reset resolved it — the guards are correct.)
* `p22_trial_read_only` passes end to end locally, including its closing assertion that **every `org_id` table carries the latch** — future tables cannot silently omit it.
* Gate registration: **30 SQL suites**; `check:counts` and `check:exemptions` green (registry 66 → **67**; the new row is an honesty entry — A5 cannot see a trigger that names no table); full `npm run build` exit 0, 427/427 tests.

`p22`'s closing assertion means **PR #9 (`0091_feedback_notes`) must merge first**: on a fresh reset 0091 < 0092 lexically so the trigger loop covers `feedback_notes`, but if this PR merged first and #9 after, p22 would fail on the next run (correctly). After #9 lands I will merge main into this branch and re-run the counts.

## Not in this PR

* Deployment (remote apply follows the documented order; `0091` before `0092`).
* Grace-aware UI (`trial.ts` work from the codex checkpoint) — follow-up from the campaign rework.

author: pd-product
body:
Answers `temp/design-handoff/og-card-generator-brief.md`. Design specified the card rather than blessing it, so the values are the authority and this replaces the committed PNG. The reply is `v2.4-delta.md`.

## What changes

`_tools/make_og_card.py` draws the whole card instead of compositing a headline band onto the previous one. `assets/og/default.png` is its output.

The card's type turned out to be the site's own rules enlarged, which is what made it specifiable: the eyebrow is `.intro .eyebrow`, the wordmark is `.site-title`, the url is `.site-nav a`. Same family, weight, case and token in every case.

The headline is now centred between the eyebrow's baseline and the rule rather than anchored at a fixed cap-top, so one to five lines all set correctly and the rule and footer never move. Copy that does not fit is refused with the offending line named, never shrunk.

## Against the card it replaces

2.41% of pixels change.

| element | before | after | largest per-pixel change |
|---|---|---|---|
| eyebrow | x79-446 y81-95 | x79-446 y81-95 | 2 of 255 |
| headline | cap-tops y172/241/310/379 | y171/240/309/378 | 217 of 255 |
| rule | x78-1121 y497 | x78-1121 y497 | 0, byte-identical |
| wordmark | x79-241 y531-554 | x79-241 y531-554 | 2 of 255 |
| url | x972-1120 y535-554 | x972-1121 y534-553 | 121 of 255 |

Two elements move by 1px. The eyebrow and the wordmark redraw onto their own ink boxes, which is the strongest evidence available that the recovered values are right: the eyebrow's size and tracking were the least recoverable numbers on the card.

## Verified by execution

- line counts 1-5 render with the rule, footer and eyebrow pixel-identical; 6 refuses, naming the 6px clearance it would leave
- a re-run reproduces the committed card exactly
- built pages carry the right dimensions and alt on home and story
- every pixel on the card is a site token blended into `--bg`; 0 off-hue

## One defect this caught

Chrome antialiases large glyphs to greyscale and small ones to LCD subpixels. Drawing the small elements through a browser for the first time put colour fringes on 1327 of 1907 eyebrow pixels. It moves nothing, so no geometry check can see it, and it would have shipped in the PNG. `--disable-lcd-text` is required and the gate proves it ran.

## Not in scope

Per-story cards are not switched on. `draw()` takes an eyebrow and lines so one is a call rather than a second code path, but `_layouts/default.html:37` emits the dimensions and alt only for the default card, so a story card today would ship worse metadata than the one it replaced. That block has to be extended first. Owner's call.

author: johnsampson
body:
## Summary
- Push notifications for new matches and new 1:1 messages, on iOS and Android, via the standard Web Push API against the existing PWA — no native app, no App/Play Store, no Apple Developer Program, no DUNS. Closes out the backlog line in issue #2 ("Can this application tool up Push notifications on iphone and android?").
- `src/lib/webPush.ts`: RFC 8291 message encryption + RFC 8292 VAPID JWT signing implemented directly against Workers' native `crypto.subtle` — no new npm dependency. The encryption path is verified byte-for-byte against RFC 8291 Appendix A's own published test vector (fetched from the actual RFC text, not from memory), not just a round-trip self-test.
- `push_subscriptions` table (migration `0012`, plus `0013` adding a `user_id` index found in final review) — includes `created_at`/`updated_at` per this repo's just-adopted schema convention (see `CLAUDE.md`). `notifyMatch`/`notifyMessage` (`src/lib/notifications.ts`) now push to every subscription on file alongside the existing email, including for recipients with no email at all — `email_sent_at` is repurposed to mean "processed via any channel," and `sendDelayedMatchNotificationEmails`'s cron query is broadened so a push-only recipient's match isn't silently skipped.
- `/api/push/vapid-public-key` (unauthenticated), `/api/push/subscribe`, `/api/push/unsubscribe` — auth-gated, upsert-by-endpoint, validated (non-empty strings, well-formed https URL) to avoid poison rows and a request-forwarding primitive.
- `public/sw.js` gains `push`/`notificationclick` listeners; Settings gets a "Enable notifications" toggle (only path to `Notification.requestPermission()` — nothing automatic) and an iOS-only "Add to Home Screen" banner, since iOS blocks push entirely outside an installed PWA.
- Design spec, native-app roadmap (Plan 2, deliberately lightweight — mostly external account setup, not code), and the full task-by-task implementation plan are committed under `docs/superpowers/`.

## Process notes
- Built via subagent-driven-development: 5 tasks, each independently implemented and reviewed, plus a final whole-branch review.
- The final review caught two things no task-scoped review could see: the production `VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY` was still a placeholder (push would have been 100% non-functional on deploy), and message-push notifications deep-linked to `/messages` with no `matchId` (the page can't render without one). Both fixed, along with 5 other Important findings (a `serviceWorker.ready` hang risk in Settings, inline-awaited push sends adding latency to message-send, an account-switch subscription-ownership edge case on shared devices, a missing index, and endpoint validation).
- One fix in that pass introduced a regression (the account-switch fix reopened the hang risk the `serviceWorker.ready` fix had just closed) — caught by the scoped re-review and fixed in a follow-up commit.
- This branch was rebased against `main` twice during development, both times because concurrently-merged PRs claimed the same migration numbers this branch was using (`0009` once, then `0010`/`0011` a second time — the second collision came bundled with a new project-wide schema convention requiring `created_at`/`updated_at` on every table, which `push_subscriptions` now also complies with). The second merge's manual conflict resolution briefly introduced its own bug (a dropped function call caught immediately by the full test suite going from 626 passing to 7 failing) — fixed before push.

## Test plan
- [x] `npx vitest run` — 626/626 passing
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [ ] Manual browser verification of the service worker's push/click handling (`public/sw.js` has no automated test coverage — consistent with this repo's existing lack of SW test infrastructure)
- [ ] Before deploying: `wrangler secret put VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY` and `wrangler secret put VAPID_SUBJECT` (documented in `README.md`'s updated secrets list and operational checklist)

## เล็กเพราะก้อน a เตรียมไว้ครบแล้ว

`setsSpecial` เดินทางในสัญญา/draft/payload อยู่แล้ว (ไม่ทำแบบนั้น **ธงจะถูกล้างทุกครั้งที่แอดมินแก้ฟิลด์อื่น** — เหตุผลเต็มใน #100)

ก้อนนี้เหลือ "ทำให้เห็นและกดได้" 3 จุด: หัวตาราง · ช่องติ๊กในเซลล์ · ข้อความสรุปคอลัมน์ขวาสุด

## ช่องติ๊กอยู่ถัดจาก VIP และ **ติดพร้อมกันได้**

เป็นคนละธงกันจริง ๆ — ป้ายหนึ่งใบเป็นทั้ง VIP และพิเศษได้ (ไม่ใช่ radio)

## กฎเดาอัตโนมัติ — **ลำดับสำคัญ**

`/พิเศษ/` **ต้องอยู่ก่อน** กฎ "ตัวเลขล้วน" (`/เลข|ผลรวม|…|มงคล|ศาสตร์/` → `ignore`)
ไม่งั้นชื่ออย่าง **"หมวดพิเศษมงคล" จะไปเข้ากฎ `มงคล` แล้วถูกสั่งข้ามทั้งหมวด** แทนที่จะติดธง — มีเทสต์ยิงชื่อนี้ตรง ๆ

## **จงใจไม่เดาจากคำว่า "ป้ายคำ"**

ทั้งที่ป้ายคำ = หมวดพิเศษ: **A1 ติดธงนี้ให้เองอยู่แล้วจากตัวอักษรในทะเบียน** ซึ่งเชื่อถือได้กว่าชื่อหมวดที่ร้านตั้ง
⇒ เดาซ้ำไม่ได้อะไรเพิ่ม (หลักการเดิมของตารางนี้: "เดาน้อยแต่ไม่มั่ว")

## จุดที่พลาดง่าย

`suggestedDraft` มีด่าน *"เดาได้แต่หา master ไม่เจอ = ไม่เดาดีกว่า"* ที่เช็ค
`plateTypeId === null && vehicleTypeId === null && !setsVip` — **ต้องเติม `&& !setsSpecial`**
ไม่งั้นหมวดที่เดาได้ว่า "พิเศษ" อย่างเดียวจะคืน `null` แล้วปุ่ม "เดาให้อัตโนมัติ" **ข้ามแถวนั้นเงียบ ๆ**

## เทสต์ (5 ใหม่)

`signalSummary` แสดง "VIP · พิเศษ" พร้อมกัน และ "พิเศษ" เดี่ยว ๆ ได้ · เดาชื่อ "หมวดพิเศษ" ได้ (ธงอย่างเดียวเป็นสัญญาณสมบูรณ์) ·

Part of #1988 (Korean runtime guides). Rebuilds #2007 on `main` after #2006 squash-merged; only this PR's two commits are carried over.

Completes the Korean Codex guide: Troubleshooting, Cost, Active Conductor / Synapse. Both partial-translation banners come off, since `codex.ko.md` now covers the whole English document.

## Four facts ported into the English guide

Running the citation-set comparison **in both directions** — not just English-to-Korean — showed citations present in `codex.ko.md` and absent from `codex.md`. Each marked something an English reader could not get:

1. **Setup's global artifacts.** `ensure_config_dir()` creates `~/.ouroboros/data/` and `~/.ouroboros/logs/` (`cli/commands/setup.py:2632`), and a fresh config gets `~/.ouroboros/credentials.yaml` at mode `0600` (`:2771`). The English list covered `~/.codex/` only.

2. **The Synapse capability table.** `SessionSignalCapabilities` has six fields; Codex declares three (`orchestrator/codex_cli_runtime.py:453`). The English prose named `inform` and `after_turn` as supported and `redirect`/`replace` as not advertised, leaving `background_reply` and `owned_turn_abort` unaccounted for. Added the table and the consequence: **to change direction during a long turn, you wait for that turn to finish.**

3. **`subagent_orchestration=INTERNAL` and why** (`:448`). `codex mcp-server` exposes only `codex` and `codex-reply`, so Codex's native multi-agent team tools are unreachable by an external driver — Ouroboros can continue a Codex thread but cannot orchestrate Codex children.

4. **The `CLI path:` verification note** (`cli/commands/config.py:696-701`), found by re-running the check on this rebuild. The English verification block still ran `codex --version` unconditionally, but the standalone path exists **for** users whose only Codex executable is the macOS ChatGPT bundle and is not on `PATH`. Those users complete setup successfully and are then told a working install is broken. The Korean guide got this correction during #1989 review; I applied it there and did not carry it across.

That fourth one is why the check is worth running as a step rather than once: I had already run this comparison on #2007, fixed three, and a fourth appeared on the rebuild because I had corrected the Korean side again in between.

## Verification

Relative links resolve. The 22 skill-table rows diff clean against `ls skills/` in both directions. The banner reflects full coverage. Remaining Korean-only citations are line references to topics the English guide now covers in prose.

## Closes the Codex track in #1988

author: willeastcott
body:
## What

Adds an **Edit on StackBlitz** button to the example chrome (between Fullscreen and View Source). Clicking it opens the current example as an editable StackBlitz project, with the example open in the editor and running in the preview pane.

## Why

Every example shared in Discord, the forum, or on social media becomes a one-click, forkable workspace. Because the generated project uses StackBlitz''s `node` template, opening it boots a WebContainer and runs a **real `npm install` of `playcanvas` and `@playcanvas/web-components`** - driving actual npm registry traffic and landing users in a project where the packages are already dependencies they can carry into their own apps. (A CDN-based CodePen/JSFiddle export would not touch npm at all.)

## How it works

On click, `examples/js/stackblitz.mjs`:

1. Fetches the current page''s raw HTML.
2. Rewrites `../dist/` to the npm package and `../node_modules/` to project-root `/node_modules/` (installed from npm), and points example-relative resources (`assets/`, `css/`, `js/`, `modules/`) at the deployed examples site, which serves CORS `*`.
3. Scans the result for every referenced package, so e.g. 3D Text picks up `earcut` + `opentype.js`, Tweening picks up `@tweenjs/tween.js`, and the AR examples pick up `@mediapipe/tasks-vision`. Versions are pinned from this repo''s own `package.json` (devDependencies take precedence, so the project gets the exact engine build the deployed examples run against).
4. POSTs `index.html`, `package.json` and a `README.md` (with User Manual / API Reference / GitHub links) to StackBlitz''s [POST API](https://developer.stackblitz.com/platform/api/post-api), targeting a tab opened synchronously on click so popup blockers attribute it to the user gesture.

No dependencies added - the POST is a plain HTML form submission.

## Notes for reviewers

- An offline check ran the transform over all 33 example pages: no repo-relative paths survive and every referenced package resolves to a known version.
- Verified live: the generated project boots on StackBlitz, `npm install` runs (a `package-lock.json` appears), `serve` comes up on port 3000 and the preview attaches. Cross-origin asset fetches and ESM imports from the GitHub Pages site were confirmed working.
- Examples that need camera/XR permissions won''t get them inside StackBlitz''s embedded preview iframe; the preview can be popped out into its own tab instead.
- Projects generated from a local checkout reference the *deployed* assets and the *published* npm packages, so unreleased local changes won''t be reflected in the StackBlitz project until deploy/publish.

body:
## Summary

The add-game wizard previously lost all in-progress state on any dialog close, in-app navigation, or app restart. This adds durable draft persistence:

- New `addGameWizardDraft` key on `ElectronStoreService` (electron-store-backed, survives closing/relaunching the whole app), owned by a new `GameWizardDraftService` (get/save/clear, degrades to `null`/no-op on any corruption rather than throwing).
- Three new IPC channels (`games.draft.get/save/clear`) on `GamesController`, bridged through preload to `window.hyveon.games.draft.*`, and thin renderer wrappers on `api.service.ts`.
- `AddGameWizard` debounce-autosaves the draft (~1s idle after an edit), flushes any pending save immediately on close/unmount, clears the saved draft only on a successful submit, and accepts optional `initialDraft`/`initialStepIndex`/`hideTrigger` props to reopen pre-filled.
- The games list page shows an "Unfinished draft: `<name>` — Resume / Discard" banner when a saved draft exists; it never auto-opens the wizard on its own.
- Scope: add-game wizard only. The edit-game form is unaffected — it's always re-seeded from the live config, so there's nothing to recover.

Built via OpenSpec (`openspec/changes/add-game-wizard-draft-persistence/`) as 9 sequential tasks, each independently reviewed, plus a final whole-branch review that caught and fixed one real cross-task bug (a stray duplicate "Add game" trigger button left behind after resuming a draft and then closing without submitting) and tightened a corruption-guard check (`stepIndex` now validated as a non-negative integer, not just a number).

author: emersonian
body:
LightdInfo.lightwalletProtocolVersion is not populated. It is declared in the generated walletrpc bindings and read by clients, but not served by lightwalletd.

The field is specified in lightwallet-protocol at lightwallet-protocol/walletrpc/service.proto:118:

    string lightwalletProtocolVersion = 18; // version of
    // https://github.com/zcash/lightwallet-protocol served by this server

and the same specification makes checking it a client requirement, in the documentation of BlockRange at service.proto:35-38:

    Clients MUST verify that the version of the server they are
    connected to are capable of returning pruned and/or transparent
    data before setting `poolTypes` to a non-empty value.

Both were introduced together in lightwallet-protocol v0.4.0, which is what ties them: the version string is the means by which a client discharges that MUST. 

**The consequence of leaving the field empty is that it is indistinguishable from a pre-v0.4.0 server.**

A client that honors the MUST has no way to tell a server that serves transparent and Ironwood data inside compact blocks from one that does not, so it must fall back to shielded-only scanning, against servers that have in fact served the data since 0.5.0.

Confirmed against a public 0.5.2 deployment: GetBlockRange with poolTypes set returns vin, vout and ironwoodActions exactly as specified, while GetLightdInfo on the same server reports no protocol version at all.

The practical result is that transparent light-wallet support looks unavailable everywhere, and clients that want it have to be told out of band, by the operator, to disregard the probe.

### Implementation Note

This reports the version as a constant rather than one of the build-stamped variables above it: it describes the protocol served, not the build, and letting 'make build' overwrite it would defeat the point. It must be updated together with the lightwallet-protocol subtree, and only once the server actually serves what the named version specifies. The subtree is currently at v0.5.0.

author: flyger1an
body:
## Finding
The `pages_public` sync trigger (`private.nz_sync_pages_public`) mirrored `public.pages.agent_memory` onto the **anon-readable** `pages_public` projection. `agent_memory` is owner-authored free-text (currently one seeded QA note: "Seeded to smoke-test..."), never intended for buyers.

Surfaced during the platform-wide adversarial/regression sweep. Low severity today (no real owner data in the field yet), but it's a latent owner-note-to-buyer leak with **no functional purpose**: no code reads `agent_memory` off the public view. The MCP discovery select (`MCP_DISCOVERY_SELECT`) never included it, and it survives only as a static capability-label string in `buildMcpDiscoveryPage`.

## Fix
1. Rewrite `private.nz_sync_pages_public()` to stop copying `agent_memory` (removed from the insert column list, values list, and `ON CONFLICT` update set). Otherwise byte-for-byte identical.
2. `ALTER TABLE public.pages_public DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS agent_memory`.

Order matters and is encoded in the migration: the trigger is rewritten **before** the column is dropped, else the next published-page write errors on an unknown column.

The base `public.pages.agent_memory` column is untouched — owners keep their notes; they simply stop being mirrored to the public projection.

## Applied to production
Already applied via MCP (Supabase migration `drop_agent_memory_from_pages_public`). Verified live:
- Column gone from `pages_public`, still present on `pages`.
- `pages_public` row count unchanged (11 = 11 published).
- A live `UPDATE ... SET updated_at = now()` on a published page re-synced its public row with no error (proves the rewritten trigger round-trips).

This PR mirrors that exact DDL into `supabase/migrations/` so source and prod don't drift.

## Test impact
The SEV1 `pages-public-parity` guard asserts `PUBLIC_PAGE_SELECT ⊆ projection`. `agent_memory` was never in `PUBLIC_PAGE_SELECT`, so the assertion still holds; the guard's regex keys on `CREATE ... AS SELECT` + `ADD COLUMN` and is unaffected by a `DROP COLUMN`. No test changes needed.

## Scope
Independent of PR #1 (the negotiation retry-loop work) — based off `main`, separately reviewable and mergeable in any order.

## Summary

The weekly refresh's discovery step created a duplicate entity: **"Bali Marathon"** (`bali-marathon`, added this week from `finishers.com`, `reliability_score: 40`, no research) is the same real-world race as the already-existing **"Maybank Marathon 2026"** (`maybank-marathon-2026`, `reliability_score: 88`, official-site sourced, already has a published review) -- same date (2026-08-23), same region, same distance lineup. Added a second check: same `category_id` + `region_id` + `core_facts.date` as an existing entity is a strong signal of the same dated event discovered under a different name, so that combination is now skipped (with a skip-reason log naming the specific existing entity it matched, so a genuine same-day-different-race false positive is easy to spot and manually re-add). Guarded on `date` existing, matching the pattern the file already uses for its date-window check, so dateless verticals are unaffected.

author: ken19960728ken
body:
## 問題

`npx eslint .` 目前會噴 **186 個問題（154 errors）**，全部來自 `supabase/.temp`（Supabase CLI 產生的暫存檔），與本專案原始碼無關。真問題會被埋在裡面看不見。

根因是 `eslint.config.mjs` 的 `globalIgnores` 相對根目錄錨定：`.next/**` 只匹配根目錄那一個，匹配不到 `.claude/worktrees/*/.next` 這類平行開發時產生的建置產物。

## 為什麼不改 eslint.config.mjs

該檔有 `config-protection` hook 保護，訊息是「不要靠放寬 linter 設定來規避修正原始碼」——**這道護欄的理由是正當的**，只是它分不出「放寬以掩蓋自己的問題」與「排除第三方產生的檔案」。改在 npm script 層補旗標，護欄維持不動。

## 改動

```diff
-"lint": "eslint . --ignore-pattern \"supabase/**\""
+"lint": "eslint . --ignore-pattern \"supabase/.temp/**\" --ignore-pattern \".claude/**\" --ignore-pattern \"**/.next/**\""
```

順帶把 `supabase/**` **收窄**為 `supabase/.temp/**`——未來新增 Edge Functions（`supabase/functions`）仍會照常被檢查，不會因為這條忽略而漏掉。

## 驗證

- `npm run lint` → 零輸出
- 在 `src/lib/domain/` 故意注入 `export const x: any = 1` → **仍被正確抓出**（證明沒有把真原始碼一起忽略）
- 對部署零影響：`next build` 本來就不執行 eslint（目前 186 個問題的狀態下建置仍成功）

### Explanation of Change

The Role field in the member details panel was passed `disabled`, and `MenuItem` dims any disabled row to `opacity: 0.5`, so a read-only role looked greyed out. `interactive` / `shouldShowRightIcon` used a different condition that ignored the owner and current-user cases, so the caret could still show.

body: ## Summary The recording feature had several silent failure modes: empty share links with no playback page, lost takes on tab close, upload failures with no retry, Safari MIME unsupported, `requires_screen_recording` that was cosmetic only, and a 24h auto-delete that never ran. This hardens the full lifecycle so recordings survive capture → upload → share → complete → cleanup. ## What changed ### Capture (doesn't lose the take) - Shared MIME negotiation across Chrome/Edge/Firefox **and Safari** (`video/mp4` fallback) via new `mediaRecorder.js` - Friendly toasts for permission denial / missing devices (no more silent `NotAllowedError`) - `MediaRecorder.onerror`, `requestData()` flush on stop, and `beforeunload` warning while recording - **Live IndexedDB chunk persistence** every timeslice + crash-recovery prompt on next visit ### Upload (survives flaky networks) - Chunked `uploadBlob` retries with exponential backoff on 408/429/5xx/network errors - Clear error messages for 413 (too large) and 502 (storage down) ### Share & playback (links actually work) - New public `/recording/:token` page (no login) - New `GET /api/recordings/{token}/stream` (Range-aware, no JWT) so anyone with the link can watch - Library preview uses a real `

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary
Moves the service from Java 1.8 / Spring Boot 1.4.4.RELEASE to Java 21 / Spring Boot 3.5.16. Boot 1.x cannot run on a JDK 21 runtime, so the Boot upgrade is the load-bearing part; the source itself needed almost no change (no `javax.*` usage, no removed Boot APIs).

Build wiring:
- Root `pom.xml` becomes a thin aggregator that inherits `spring-boot-starter-parent:3.5.16` and sets `java.version=21` + `maven.compiler.release=21`; `licensing-service/pom.xml` now parents off `tmx-parent-pom` instead of declaring the Boot parent again.
- `jackson-bom.version` is pinned to `2.21.5`, ahead of the version Boot 3.5.16 manages, because the managed one still carries the `@JsonView`/`@JsonIgnoreProperties` bypass advisories.
- The abandoned `com.spotify:docker-maven-plugin:0.4.10` is removed (it breaks on modern JDKs and hasn't shipped since 2016). Image builds now go through buildpacks:
  ```
  - mvn clean package docker:build
  + mvn clean package spring-boot:build-image   # image name johncarnell/tmx-licensing-service:chapter2
  ```
  The `maven-resources-plugin` filtering of `src/main/docker` is kept so the hand-written Dockerfile still works for a plain `docker build`.

Behavioural note for anyone hitting the service: in Boot 3 actuator endpoints live under `/actuator`, so health moved `/health` → `/actuator/health` (README updated).

Also: `Dockerfile` base `openjdk:8-jdk-alpine` → `eclipse-temurin:21-jre-alpine`; `.travis.yml` jdk `oraclejdk8` → `openjdk21`; controller's `@RequestMapping(method=...)` replaced with `@GetMapping`/`@PutMapping`/`@PostMapping`/`@DeleteMapping`.

Added `ApplicationTests` — the repo had no tests, so there was nothing proving the Boot 3 context even starts. It boots the app and asserts the license endpoint payload and `/actuator/health`.

## Security impact
An OSV.dev scan of the resolved runtime dependency set goes from **182 advisories (37 critical) on `master` to 0 on this branch**. Notably retired: Spring4Shell (CVE-2022-22965), `spring-web` unsafe deserialization (CVE-2016-1000027), SnakeYAML constructor RCE (CVE-2022-1471), and the Tomcat 8.5.11 critical set — none of which are patchable while on Boot 1.x. Pre-existing non-dependency findings (no authentication on any endpoint including actuator, container runs as root, `docker login -p` in CI) are unchanged by this PR and tracked separately.

## Verification
On JDK 21: `mvn clean package` green, jar boots logging Spring Boot v3.5.16 / Java 21, `GET /v1/organizations/org-1/licenses/lic-1` → `{"id":"lic-1","organizationId":"org-1","productName":"Teleco","licenseType":"Seat"}`, all four verbs mapped, `/actuator/health` → `{"status":"UP"}`, adversarial probes return 404/405 with no 5xx. Details in the verification comment below.

## What
The severe-weather (rain) alert bar showed up on **every** rain-relevant trade because it auto-enabled from the tenant's trade keywords (plumbing, waterproofing, sump, …). author: chelojimenez
body:
PR 5 of the local-computer-engine program (PRs 1–4: #3799, #3805, #3812, #3815, all merged). Foundation only — **no visible UI change yet**; the tab/rail faces (PRs 6–7) build on these hooks. Almost entirely client-side, plus one small server touch (token-scoped revoke, below).

## What this adds

**Parser** (`useProjectComputer.ts`) — `engines` + `defaultEngine` are always present *post-parse*: servers that predate PR 4's shape (and malformed `engines` blocks — read like an old server, never half-trusted, since a partial parse could invent a local engine) get the legacy-pair derivation, in which the local engine never exists. The fetch-failure fallback keeps its assume-local-data-plane semantics with no phantom local engine. The module cache + in-flight dedupe from PR 2 are unchanged.

**Engine storage** (`lib/computer-engine-storage.ts`) — per-project Local⇄Cloud choice in localStorage, deliberately **device-scoped** (the choice is about *this machine*; a teammate opening the same project must never inherit it). Per-project keys (no shared map to clobber across tabs); custom event for same-tab sync (tab + rail move together), `storage` event for cross-tab.

**Consent client** (`lib/local-computer-consent.ts` + `useLocalComputerConsent()`) — client of PR 3's capability. `granted` is a **synchronous projection of localStorage** (via `useSyncExternalStore`): consent exists iff a capability token is stored on this device. There is deliberately no client-side verify loop — the server re-verifies the token on **every actual use** (the engine resolver, PR #3812), so a stale or tampered token just fails the next turn's server check; earlier revisions that pre-verified on mount grew five review rounds of out-of-order/self-supersede/cross-tab guards for no safety the server wasn't already providing. Grant = mint on server, then persist; a persist failure (storage blocked/full) reports `false` rather than a granted state nothing can read back. Revoke forgets locally first (synchronously), then issues a best-effort, **token-scoped** server revoke: the server unlinks only if the presented token still matches its stored hash, so a delayed revoke resuming after a newer grant can't sever the capability that grant just rotated in. That scoping is this PR's one server change (`/local-consent/revoke` accepts an optional token; bodiless stays unconditional for the storage-was-empty "sever this device" case). Calls ride `authFetch` (inspector session + verified WorkOS bearer), matching the routes' `requireVerifiedAuth`.

**Resolution** (`hooks/useComputerEngine.ts`) — one rule for every consumer:
1. Hosted ⇒ cloud; toggle hidden; storage never read.
2. Else the first qualifying candidate of `[stored pref, server defaultEngine, local, cloud]` — where `local` qualifies only when available **and consent is stored on this device** (the server re-verifies on every use). A stored "local" pref without consent falls through to cloud: the badge can never say "This machine" while commands go elsewhere.
3. Nothing qualifies ⇒ `cloud` with `cloudAvailable:false` (the existing unavailable state). PR 4's `defaultEngine: null` slots in as a non-qualifying candidate.

"Default = Local in local mode" lands as: the server's `defaultEngine:"local"` wins the candidate race as soon as consent exists — no stored preference required; granting consent is what flips a fresh install over.

## Tests

Suites cover the resolution matrix (hosted × availability × stored pref × consent, incl. consent-gates-local rows and the honest empty state), parser back-compat (full shape, old server, malformed block, `defaultEngine: null`, failure fallback), the consent projection (grant/persist-failure honesty, cross-tab grant/revoke events, hosted short-circuit, token-scoped storage-free server revoke), storage event scoping, and — server-side — the scoped revoke (stale-token revoke no-ops, bodiless revoke unlinks). Client typecheck exit 0.

## Next
PR 6 (Computer tab "This machine" face + WebMCP hoist) and PR 7 (Playground rail + chat `computerEngine`/consent-header transmission — including clearing the stored token when the server definitively rejects it, so the UI re-prompts) consume these hooks; PR 8 (node-pty terminal) flips `terminalAvailable`; PR 9 renders the transcript badge off the PR-3 `engine` stamp.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches local-computer consent capabilities, engine resolution, and verified-auth API paths; server-side verification on actual use limits client-only mistakes, but grant/revoke race handling is security-relevant.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **foundation-only** client plumbing for per-project Local⇄Cloud computer engine choice (no UI in this PR). Future tab/rail surfaces will consume these hooks.
> 
> **Config parsing** extends `/api/web/computers/config` handling so `engines` and `defaultEngine` are always present after parse: legacy servers and malformed `engines` blocks fall back to derivation where **local is never offered**; fetch-failure fallback stays “assume local data plane” without inventing a local machine engine.
> 
> **Device-scoped storage** (`computer-engine-storage`) persists each project’s engine under its own `localStorage` key with same-tab/cross-tab sync.
> 
> **Consent** (`local-computer-consent` + `useLocalComputerConsent`) treats a stored capability token as granted via synchronous `useSyncExternalStore` (no client verify loop); grant mints then persists, revoke clears storage first then token-scoped server unlink. **`authFetch`** now attaches hosted auth for `/api/mcp/computers/local-consent`.
> 
> **`useComputerEngine`** applies one resolution rule everywhere: hosted ⇒ cloud; else first qualifying candidate among stored pref → server `defaultEngine` → local → cloud, with **local gated on stored consent** so UI cannot show “this machine” while routing elsewhere.
> 
> **Server**: `/local-consent/revoke` accepts optional token (scoped no-op if superseded); grant/revoke run under an in-process mutation lock to prevent races with concurrent grant.
