body:
<!--
Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need.

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111922
-->


### Changelog category (leave one):
- CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
...

### Description

Related: #111922
CI report: https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=108078&sha=1588d96287dc9c13f42492972c510487be49b696&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_debug%2C%20parallel%29

`04499_system_cluster_access_types` ran `SYSTEM START CLEANUP ON CLUSTER test_shard_localhost` with no
table name. That cluster routes the entry back here, and the no-table form is host-global:
`InterpreterSystemQuery::startStopAction` walks every database and per table calls
`onActionLockRemove(Cleanup)` (wakes the cleanup thread, which drops empty parts) and
`ActionLocksManager::remove` (drops a table-scoped `SYSTEM STOP CLEANUP` lock). The test has no `Tags:`
line, so it hits other tests' tables.

So `04323_text_index_marks_empty_part` failed on an unrelated PR: its deliberately empty active part was
dropped between its two `SELECT`s and the reference line `0\t0` vanished. Five parallel tests (`02340`,
`02421`, `02486`, `03100_lwu_40_cleanup_race`, `04338`) hold table-scoped `STOP CLEANUP` locks and were
exposed the same way. #114070 converts 04323 to an integration test, which does not fix this.

The four no-table probes now go to `test_cluster_multiple_nodes_all_unavailable` with
`distributed_ddl_task_timeout = 0`; its nodes are `127.0.0.{1,2,3}:1234`, so `findCurrentHostID` never
matches and the entry executes nowhere. The tested branch is unaffected: the access check in
`executeDDLQueryOnCluster` runs on the initiator before the enqueue. The table-scoped probes keep
`test_shard_localhost` and keep executing, so no `no-parallel` tag is added, and the wrong
`parallel-safe` comment is deleted.

Two `system.clusters` guards pin that routing, so `.reference` grows from 4 to 6 `ok` lines. An entry is
claimed here only when its port equals `tcp_port` or `tcp_port_secure` exactly, so the guards assert that
no node of the unavailable cluster carries either port, and the negative one aborts before the probes
rather than only reporting. A config change making the entry executable here stops the test.

Validation: the old test drops another database's empty part and releases a held lock while the new test
leaves both intact; reintroducing the pre-fix access type on each no-table branch separately reddens the
test; each guard reddens when its cluster is swapped. 50/50 green for both tests.

<details>
<summary>Measured arms</summary>

Fixture is 04323's table shape in a separate database; a table-scoped `SYSTEM STOP CLEANUP` is held
across each run.

| arm | `rows, marks` after | `Will drop empty part` | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| old test (pristine) | *(zero rows)* | 1 | part dropped, lock released |
| new test | `0\t0` | 0 | part survives, lock held |
| `SYSTEM START CLEANUP` no table (direct) | *(zero rows)* | 1 | reproduces the CI signature |
| `SYSTEM START CLEANUP <db>.<tbl>` (control) | `0\t0` | 0 | table-scoped form is harmless |

Mutation arms, each reintroducing the pre-fix access type on one no-table branch:

| mutated branch | new test |
|---|---|
| `START/STOP CLEANUP`, no table | FAIL |
| `START/STOP VIRTUAL PARTS UPDATE`, no table | FAIL |
| none (final) | OK |

Guard arms, on a stock `tcp_port=9000` / `tcp_port_secure=9440` server: pointing guard 1 at
`test_shard_localhost`, at a nonexistent cluster, or inverting guard 2 each turn the test red. Dropping
the `count() = 0` term makes a nonexistent cluster pass vacuously.

The only other no-table `SYSTEM START/STOP` sites in stateless tests are
`01563_distributed_query_finish` and `04117_parser_system_query_variants`, both already `no-parallel`
(and the latter only runs `EXPLAIN SYNTAX`), so no other test needs changing.

</details>

## Human Written Description

La dernière pièce : l'interface qui rend le mode réunion réellement utilisable. Tout le backend est mergé et validé Windows ; ici on le relie au parcours utilisateur, avec les trois choix produit qu'on avait retenus (moins de friction + sérieux sur le consentement).

## Ce que fait cette PR

Nouvelle section **« Mode réunion »** dans la barre latérale des réglages :

- **Démarrer / Terminer** — un seul bouton selon l'état (démarrage → capture → finalisation → compte rendu). Appelle `invoke("start_meeting")` / `invoke("stop_meeting")` avec les étiquettes « Vous »/« Autres » **traduites** (i18n).
- **Consentement au 1er usage** — un dialogue bloquant explique la responsabilité légale (prévenir les participants) ; « Démarrer la capture » reste **désactivé tant que la case n'est pas cochée**. L'acquittement est mémorisé (`localStorage`) → plus jamais redemandé.
- **Badge de capture** — un bandeau rouge « Capture de … » reste visible tant que la réunion tourne, **sans moyen de le masquer** : transparence, jamais de capture silencieuse.
- **Compte rendu** affiché à l'arrêt, avec le nombre de passages transcrits / ignorés ; message clair si personne n'a été entendu.
- **Erreurs à codes stables traduites** (pas d'app de réunion, Windows trop ancien, déjà en cours…).

## Langage visuel

Réutilise les composants canoniques (`SettingsGroup`, `Button`, `Dialog`) et les tokens de couleur, icônes SVG lucide (**zéro emoji**). Textes **FR + EN rédigés**, 20 autres langues = EN (convention du dépôt).

## Décisions laissées ouvertes

- **Déclenchement** : ici c'est un bouton dans la section Réglages (simple, testable). Le « démarrage en un clic sur détection de réunion » directement dans l'overlay est une amélioration possible ensuite — plus ambitieuse et plus dure à tester à l'aveugle.
- **Palier** : la section n'est **pas gatée** pour l'instant, pour que tu puisses la tester. Le palier (Pro/Ultra) reste à décider.

## Testing

- `tsc --noEmit` — OK
- `eslint src` — OK
- `prettier --check .` — OK
- `check:translations` — 21 langues complètes
- Composant construit sur les composants existants ; le job Playwright de la CI couvre le rendu de l'app.

**Reste : un test réel de bout en bout sur Windows** — démarrer une vraie réunion, parler, terminer, vérifier le compte rendu « Vous »/« Autres ».

body:
The debrief control wore `TiffMark` for a day — the full 44px glass face, breathing halo, chevron and sparkle. Off, on Isaac's call.

The argument for taking it off is the same one that put the console there in #325: the surface under it is **already** unmistakably Tiff's — ink, the masked gradient rim, the frame's own aurora — so a mark *on* the control was Tiff said twice in one object. The word is the only thing the surface could not say, which is what pressing it does.

The material stays, and that is what keeps this the topbar button's sibling rather than a generic pill: same glass, same inset highlight, same rim. Capsule 56px → 48px with symmetric padding now there is nothing to seat.

`.wb2-debriefmk` and the re-pointed `.tiffbtn-*` hovers are deleted rather than left behind. `TiffMark` stays — the topbar and sheet buttons are still its callers.

## A real bug shipped in #325, found on the way

That rule wrote `-webkit-backdrop-filter` beside `backdrop-filter`. The trap this repo recorded in July is that the pair collapses to the **prefixed** property, which current Chrome doesn't support, so the blur silently dies — the Design Studio's "glass" card was never actually frosted for months because of it.

Ran the build's own transformer rather than trusting the note. At **lightningcss 1.32.0 it collapses the other way**: the standard property survives and the prefixed line is dropped.

```
.a{-webkit-backdrop-filter:blur(14px) saturate(150%);backdrop-filter:blur(14px) saturate(150%)}
.b{backdrop-filter:blur(14px) saturate(150%)}
  →  .a, .b { backdrop-filter: blur(14px) saturate(150%); }
```

Same output with and without browserslist targets. So the blur was working and the twin was dead weight — but removed anyway, because the *direction* of the collapse is a version detail and `.tiffbtn-topbar .tiffbtn-face`, the glass this is a sibling to, has only ever written the standard one. Verified through the transformer that all 17 `backdrop-filter` declarations in the shipped stylesheet are now standard and none are prefixed.

## Verification

4,917 jest tests, `tsc`, `eslint`, `lightningcss`, and the static `public/` harness at 1500×950 measured through the DOM: capsule 105×48, **zero `svg` inside**, glass `rgba(255,255,255,.06)`, backdrop `blur(14px) saturate(1.5)`, rim `mask-composite: exclude`. React Compiler still accepts note-token (819 slots), tiff-button (51), tiff-mark (35).

The test that pinned the mark now pins its absence.

Still not walked signed-in — same reason as #325.

author: harukimoriarty
body:
Fixes #289.

## Root cause

On `(`, `factor` tried three alternatives — `tuple_lit`, the silent `paren_expr` (wrapping `group_expr`), then a bare `factor` — and each fully re-parsed the same nested interior before failing. pest has no memoization, so nested parens cost Theta(3^depth): the 38-byte fuzz artifact took ~13s, blowing the per-input `-timeout=10` added in #287.

## Fix

One rule now owns `(` and parses the interior exactly once; commas decide the form, the same way rustc and CPython separate grouping from tuples:

```pest
paren_factor = { "(" ~ paren_elem ~ ("," ~ paren_elem)* ~ trailing_comma? ~ ")" }
paren_elem = _{ arithmetic_expr | placeholder }
trailing_comma = { "," }
```

`parse_paren_factor` in the lowering turns any comma into a tuple literal; a comma-free interior is grouping (multi-term becomes `Factor::Group`, single-factor collapses to the bare factor, as before).

## Surface changes

- Trailing commas in tuple literals are accepted (`(a, b,)`), matching Rust; `Display` renders canonically without the comma.
- `(_)` moves from a generic pest syntax error to a dedicated `ParseError::GroupedPlaceholder` with a `(_,)` hint. Everything else parses exactly as before.

## Validation

- Issue artifact `timeout-c11d1ee5`: ~13s before, **2ms** after; 4096-byte paren bombs (open and closed) run in <1ms with no stack issues.
- New regression tests: 200-deep nests (well-formed and unclosed), `()`, `(a, b,)`, `(_,)`, and the pinned `GroupedPlaceholder` error.
- `cargo test` workspace, clippy `-D warnings`, rustfmt, typos all green; fixture suites are running locally (CI gates them regardless); I will confirm on this PR.

Follow-up (out of scope here): `as_cast | call_expr` has the same latent re-parse pattern on a different head token (`as(x, 5)` fails late in `as_cast`, then `call_expr` re-parses the interior); worth a `!as_kw` guard on call names in a separate change.

author: ezz-ae
body:
From an outside critique of this architecture. Most of it describes mechanisms this system deliberately doesn't have — but underneath the first point is something real.

## The real point

Every verdict in the placement audit waits on **leads**, which are rare. A placement can burn weeks of budget before enough of them exist to prove anything, and a placement buying nothing but cheap impressions spends the whole of that wait.

**Clicks are plentiful.** A placement clicked significantly less than the rest of the campaign separates from the field in a fraction of the time.

So there's now an earlier read, `noClicks`. Two things make it honest rather than trigger-happy:

- **Same significance machinery as the lead verdict** — not an invented threshold. The critique proposed *"50,000 impressions in two hours at a low CPM"*. That number would condemn a genuinely expensive, slow, high-intent audience for behaving exactly as it should, and it needs a new polling cron to compute. Significance against the rest of the campaign needs neither.
- **It never overrides a lead verdict.** A placement proven to convert better converts better whatever its click rate — some audiences click little and buy anyway. Reading the shallower event as the truer one would be a regression dressed as a feature.

Nothing new is fetched; `clicks` is already in every placement row.

## What the critique gets wrong about this system

Recorded so the next version of it doesn't cost another day:

- **"Advantage campaign budget force-feeds the cheap ad set to clear its quota"** — there is no shared campaign budget to reallocate. `is_adset_budget_sharing_enabled` is `false`; every ad set holds its own daily budget.
- **"Audience Network dumps 4 AED CPM inventory"** — Audience Network is never bought. `ALLOWED_PLATFORMS` is facebook and instagram, and an absent platform list is *refused at launch* as Advantage+ placements.
- **"The audit automatically offers placements for permanent exclusion"** — the placements route is read-only and says so in its header. It recommends; a human acts.

## Verification

- `scripts/placement-audit-test.ts` — 5 new assertions, including that a slow expensive audience is left alone and that a lead verdict is never overridden
- `pnpm typecheck` ✓ · `pnpm i18n` ✓ · `pnpm guards` ✓ · production build ✓

author: naturallaw777
body:
## Context

`fort-nix/nix-bitcoin` is shutting down / unmaintained. `Sovran_SystemsOS` imports it as `nix-bitcoin.nixosModules.default` in `flake.nix` for 6 services:

`bitcoind` / `electrs` / `lnd` (+`lndconnect`) / `rtl` / `btcpayserver` / `mempool`

Evaluating 28 modules + 3 pinned `nixpkgs` (`25.11`, `25_05`, `extra-container`) to use 6 is heavy and will break on the next `nixos-unstable` / `26.11` bump with no upstream fixes.

This PR makes Sovran sovereign: vendor only what we use, get packages directly from `nixpkgs`.

## Changes

**`flake.nix`**
- Remove `inputs.nix-bitcoin = github:fort-nix/nix-bitcoin/release`
- Add `overlay-sovran` (`pkgs/sovran-overlay.nix`) for gaps only
- Import `./modules/vendor/nix-bitcoin/modules.nix` instead of `nix-bitcoin.nixosModules.default` in both `nixos` and `iso` configs
- `flake.lock` will drop `nix-bitcoin` + `nixpkgs-25.11/25_05/extra-container` on `nix flake update`

**`modules/vendor/nix-bitcoin/` (new, 3,150 lines)**
Vendored minimal subset, patched to use `pkgs.*` instead of `config.nix-bitcoin.pkgs.*`:
- `bitcoind.nix` → `pkgs.bitcoind` / `pkgs.bitcoind-knots`
- `electrs.nix` → `pkgs.electrs`
- `lnd.nix` + `lndconnect.nix` → `pkgs.lnd` / `pkgs.lndconnect`
- `rtl.nix` → `pkgs.rtl`
- `btcpayserver.nix` → `pkgs.btcpayserver` / `pkgs.nbxplorer`
- `mempool.nix` → `pkgs.mempool-backend` (+ nginx conf fallback)
- Supporting: `secrets/secrets.nix`, `onion-services.nix`, `onion-addresses.nix`, `operator.nix`, `nodeinfo.nix`, `security.nix`, `versioning.nix`, `lib.nix`

Keeps `nix-bitcoin.*` option namespace for compat — `bitcoinecosystem.nix` / `mempool.nix` work unchanged:
`nix-bitcoin.generateSecrets`, `nix-bitcoin.onionServices.*`, `nix-bitcoin.operator`, `services.lnd.macaroons.albyhub`

**Trimmed per review:**
- `backups.nix` **removed** — Sovran uses `services.rsnapshot` to `Second_Drive/BTCEcoandBackup` (hourly + 21:50 daily, `/home`+`/var/lib`+`/etc/nix-bitcoin-secrets`). The `duplicity` remote backup only covered Bitcoin data, redundant for Sovran.
- `netns-isolation.nix` **stubbed to 16 lines** (was 365). Original `nb-br` bridge `169.254.1.10` + `iptables` + `ip netns` broke `Caddy`/`AlbyHub`/`RTL`/`nwc-wallets` (requires `enable=false`). Stub keeps option valid but warns if enabled — can't break system again.

**`pkgs/sovran-overlay.nix` (new)**
Only gaps where `nixpkgs` is missing:
- `lndinit 0.1.3-beta` (not in nixpkgs)
- `netns-exec` no-op stub
- `nbxplorer` fallback if missing

**Other files:**
- `modules/bitcoin-core.nix`: `config.nix-bitcoin.pkgs.bitcoind` → `pkgs.bitcoind`
- `modules/core/role-logic.nix` + `modules/bitcoinecosystem.nix`: comment that `useVersionLockedPkgs` is now no-op

## Why nixpkgs-only?

- Faster eval, smaller ISO, no 3 extra nixpkgs fetches
- Security updates follow `nixos-unstable` you already track
- No single-point-of-failure on archived `fort-nix` repo
- 2-4h/month maintenance: `nix flake update` + integration test

## Testing

- [ ] `nix flake check --no-build`
- [ ] `nix build .#nixosConfigurations.nixos.config.system.build.toplevel --dry-run`
- [ ] `nix build .#nixosConfigurations.sovran_systemsos-iso.config.system.build.isoImage --dry-run`
- [ ] `sudo nixos-rebuild dry-activate --flake .#nixos` on `server_plus_desktop` + `node` role
- [ ] Verify `AlbyHub`/`RTL`/`BTCPay` still reach `lnd` at `127.0.0.1:10009`

## Next steps after merge

1. `nix flake update` (done in follow-up commit)
2. Monthly `nix flake update && nix flake check`
3. If `pkgs.rtl`/`pkgs.mempool` lag in nixpkgs, add temporary override in `sovran-overlay.nix`

No breaking change for existing `custom.nix` / roles.

author: arniesaha
body:
The Claude card merged **two different subscriptions**. A personal account runs on the Mac mini and the NAS, a work account on the work laptop, and the probe labelled all three `Claude Code` -- so grouping collapsed them into one card showing personal consumption against a work machine:

```
mac-mini     label='Claude Code'  plan='max'   windows=4   <- personal, real data
nas          label='Claude Code'  plan='max'   windows=0
work-laptop  label='Claude Code'  plan=None    windows=0
```

versus Codex, which never had this problem because its probe reports a real account:

```
mac-mini     label='arnabsahacanada@gmail.com'
```

## The fix

The identity was available and simply unused. Anthropic's usage endpoint says nothing about *which* account it answered for, but the CLI's own config does -- `oauthAccount.emailAddress` in `~/.claude.json`, read per host:

```
oauthAccount.emailAddress              = 'arniesaha@gmail.com'
oauthAccount.organizationName          = "arniesaha@gmail.com's Organization"
oauthAccount.organizationRateLimitTier = 'default_claude_max_5x'
```

The probe now reports it, falling back to `organizationName` then `accountUuid`, and finally to the generic name when the config is unreadable -- no worse than before this existed. Distinct accounts produce distinct labels, distinct dedup keys and distinct cards, **with no change to the grouping code**.

The label is reported on failure paths too, so a degraded card still says which subscription it is degraded for.

## The assumption that caused it

The grouping doc comment claimed collapsing generic labels was safe "because the fleet has one operator". That is exactly what produced the bug, and it is replaced with what actually happened. Identity that is *reported* beats identity that is *assumed*.

## Testing

Four new tests: two hosts on different accounts get different labels and different dedup keys; the fallback chain through org then uuid; an unreadable config keeps the generic label without failing the probe; the label survives onto failure snapshots. Full server suite 1557 passed, 28 DroverKit presentation tests pass. The two failures are pre-existing on `main` and unrelated.

author: grantedhub
body:
Two commits: the state audit as a doc, then step 1 of the build order it records. They share a PR because this session is pinned to one branch name — say the word and I'll split them.

- `ae07339` — `docs/pursuit-state-audit-2026-08.md` (doc only)
- `a11eabc` — migration 0074 + the corrected status semantics

---

## Part 1 — the audit doc

Read against `d27e4a3` by grepping every `fetch`/server-action in the Pursuit tree rather than trusting comments. The finding that shapes everything: the flow is a complete shell with real server-side logic at both edges and **zero content persistence in the middle**. It records the six-step build order and, in §4, the status-semantics trap that step 1 closes.

## Part 2 — step 1

### Migration

```sql
alter table intellengine_drafts
  add column if not exists content jsonb not null default '{}'::jsonb;
```

Additive, on a table holding one row, for a feature gated off clients. No RLS change (0062's policies are `for all`, so a new column is already covered by both the staff and `is_client_member_of` branches). No backfill. **Nothing writes it yet** — wiring the forms is step 2. The column and the honest reporting land first.

### The actual fix: status carried two meanings

`status` was advanced by clicking Continue, so three clicks through empty screens set it to `complete` — and the hub, the client dashboard, the staff console panel, **and** the roster all read that as progress. "Ready to submit" at 100%, every box checked, on a draft holding nothing.

Split in two:

| | means | stored? |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | furthest screen **opened** — a resume pointer, all `resumeStep` ever needed | yes (unchanged column) |
| completeness | derived from `content` | **no** |

Derived, it can't be faked by navigating and can't go stale. That extends `draftProgress`'s existing "no stored progress column, on purpose" one step further.

### Three states, not two

A rung is `done`, `todo`, or **`unknown`**. Compliance is `unknown`: its document list is hardcoded until step 4, so there's no honest predicate, and returning `done` would put a green check exactly where the gate removed one. Unknown rungs render as a dash and are **excluded from the denominator** — scope done with build outstanding reads 1 of 2, not 1 of 3, so a draft isn't marked down for a check the product can't run.

### Consequences, all deliberate

- **PATCH refuses `status='complete'`.** It isn't a screen, and a button click is the wrong evidence that a proposal is finished. Rejected rather than ignored, so an un-updated caller is visible.
- **"Save & return to IntellEngine" → "Return to IntellEngine."** Its only write *was* that status; with it gone the button saves nothing, and a button labelled Save that saves nothing is the lie the gate went up to stop. It becomes a real save in step 2.
- **Captions count captured steps**, not flow position: "2 of 2 steps captured", "draft 50% captured". The qualifiers that existed to stop a reader taking screens-visited for work-done are gone along with the cause.
- **Files stay out of `content`** — a stored filename with no object behind it is the same looks-received lie. Files arrive with a bucket in step 3.
- **Template text is never stored**, so "section is non-empty" means authored, by construction, rather than true at creation.

### Expected, not a regression

The one existing draft sitting at `status='complete'` with no content now reads as nothing-captured. That's the correction landing — it was falsely claiming complete.

`readDraftContent` is tolerant like `readAllowableUses`, so an **unapplied 0074 behaves exactly like an empty column** rather than 500ing a page.

### Surfaces touched

`tsc` caught three consumers I hadn't traced from the audit — the staff-side IntellEngine hub, the all-clients roster percentage, and portal search. Search now shows the resume pointer ("left off in the builder"), which is the right thing for a search hit to say and makes no completeness claim.

### Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean, `next build` passes
- No protected files, no `client_documents` or storage changes
- **Migration-first: 0074 needs applying before the preview check**

Preview check (staff-side, since the flow is gated off clients): derived progress renders on the hub and the console panel, a draft at `status='complete'` with empty content no longer says "Ready to submit", and compliance shows a dash rather than a check.

author: os-help
body:
Fixes #7135

The services half of #7070, mirroring PR #7140 (the identity half, merged 2026-08-09). #6523 / PR #7068 converged 36 contract signatures onto the full `resolveAuthzContext` envelope, applying the #6206 ruling — enforcement adjudicates on the whole envelope, never a per-site subset. The implementations behind those contracts still annotated their own parameters with the six-field shape the contracts used to name, so nothing they could *read* had widened.

## Premise re-verified on `origin/main` @ `aeadbd6`

The card's counts were measured @ `445a0c2` and the dispatching seat re-measured @ `6146b67`. Both still hold at my branch point:

| file | narrow-type refs before | after |
|:---|---:|---:|
| `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts` | 27 | 0 |
| `packages/plugins/plugin-reports/src/report-service.ts` | 14 | 0 |
| `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-node.ts` | 2 | 0 |

(Two doc-comment mentions of the old name survive, in prose explaining what each cast replaced.) After this PR the only remaining references repo-wide outside `packages/spec` are `plugin-sharing/src/index.ts`'s re-export and a comment in `plugin-sharing`'s pin.

## What changed

- **`isOverrideActor()` reads a declared `posture`.** This is the load-bearing one the card names. That gate decides whether a platform or tenant admin may release a STUCK approval — one routed to an unstaffed position, which is the only in-product recovery from a permanently locked record — and it read the derived `posture` (ADR-0095) through an unchecked `(context as any)`. An erasure sitting directly on an enforcement input: a mistyped rung would have compiled and silently denied every override.
- **Both services' `SYSTEM_CTX` is typed as the envelope and passed as itself**, retiring the `SYSTEM_CTX as unknown as ...` double casts at `approval-service.ts:2773, 2813, 3259`.
- **The `(context as any).userId` / `.tenantId` reads in `ApprovalService` now read declared fields.**
- **`OwnerContextResolver` returns the envelope**, which is what a scheduled report actually resolves for its owner (#2849 / #2980).
- 43 parameter/return positions across the three files now name `ExecutionContext`.

## Scope held

- **`organizationId` is untouched**, per the boundary inherited from #7070: it is not a field of the envelope at all, and that spelling has its own history (#5858 / `check:org-identifier`). The four reads of it stay cast, and the asymmetry is now documented at each site — the `tenantId` half of each `??` chain lost its cast, the `organizationId` half did not, which makes visible which of the two names the contract actually knows. `check:org-identifier` is green.
- **`approval-node.ts:174` keeps a cast, and this is a correction to the card**, which lists it as deletable. The literal there names `organizationId`, so a fresh literal in argument position is rejected by TypeScript's excess-property check against the envelope; removing the key would be the RUNTIME change #7070 held out. The assertion was still improved rather than left alone: `as unknown as SharingExecutionContext` became a single `as ExecutionContext`. Dropping the second hop matters — `as unknown as` erases the value entirely, while a single assertion still requires the literal to be comparable to the envelope, so a `userId: 42` there is once again a compile error.
- **`SharingExecutionContext` is NOT removed**, even though PR #7140 landed first and the coordination point on the card assigns the deletion to the second lander. Per the scope ruling recorded in the claim comment: the type is DEFINED at `packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts:191`, and `packages/spec` is single-owner. `packages/spec/**` and `plugin-sharing/**` are completely untouched here. **The type-retirement follow-up is filed separately by the PM.**
- No public export changes shape; `check:api-surface` / `check:export-origins` should be unaffected.

## The pins, and why they exist

A re-narrowed annotation would compile, ship and pass every test in these packages — the values were always complete at runtime, so there is no compiler pressure in either direction and nothing would notice. Each package gets an `exec-context-annotation.pin.ts` handing each parameter a fresh literal naming envelope-only fields (`posture`, `accessible_org_ids`, `org_user_ids`), which excess-property checking rejects the moment a parameter narrows back, plus `@ts-expect-error` negatives so a parameter erased to `any` cannot pass either.

**Pin placement was measured per package rather than assumed**, and the two differ:

- `plugin-approvals/tsconfig.json` excludes `**/*.test.ts` — same as `plugin-sharing`, so the #7140 reasoning transfers directly and a pin in a test file here would be a phantom check.
- `plugin-reports/tsconfig.json` does **not** exclude test files, so a pin there would in fact be type-checked. The `.pin.ts` convention is used anyway: it does not depend on that exclusion staying absent, it survives a vitest-only run that never type-checks, and it keeps both halves identical in shape.

Neither pin is imported by anything, so tsup (entry `src/index.ts`) never bundles them into `dist`.

## Reverse verification — the predicted direction, and it held

Predicted before running: a full revert leaves the runtime suite **green** and turns **only the pin** red. That is what happened. The fix was taken out with `git checkout origin/main -- ...` (never `git stash`), pins left in place:

```
REVERT: plugin-reports   Test Files  2 passed (2) / Tests  54 passed (54)
REVERT: plugin-approvals Test Files 19 passed (19) / Tests 446 passed (446)
REVERT_TEST_EXIT=0
```

500 of 500 tests pass with the change fully reverted — confirming #7140's measurement that a green suite is not evidence for this family. Typecheck on the same reverted tree, exit 2, every error inside a pin file and none outside one:

```
plugin-reports   src/exec-context-annotation.pin.ts(70,50): error TS2353: Object literal may only specify known properties, and 'posture' does not exist in type 'SharingExecutionContext'.
plugin-reports   src/exec-context-annotation.pin.ts(72,38): error TS2353: ... 'org_user_ids' does not exist in type 'SharingExecutionContext'.
plugin-reports   src/exec-context-annotation.pin.ts(79,39): error TS2339: Property 'posture' does not exist on type 'SharingExecutionContext'.
plugin-approvals src/exec-context-annotation.pin.ts(66,39): error TS2353: ... 'posture' does not exist in type 'SharingExecutionContext'.
plugin-approvals src/exec-context-annotation.pin.ts(68,40): error TS2353: ... 'accessible_org_ids' does not exist in type 'SharingExecutionContext'.
```

Each package was also reverse-verified alone, because a parallel `--workspace-concurrency=2` run can mask the second package behind the first failure. Both bite independently (6 errors in approvals, 7 in reports).

## Verification

Dependency closure built first (`--filter '...^...'`), then:

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals --filter @objectstack/plugin-reports typecheck` — green (exit 0). This is what proves the pins' positives AND their `@ts-expect-error` negatives are all satisfied; an unsatisfied expect-error fails the build.
- `pnpm --filter ... test` — `19 passed (19)` files / `446 passed (446)` tests in approvals, `2 passed (2)` / `54 passed (54)` in reports.
- `npx eslint packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src packages/plugins/plugin-reports/src` — clean.
- `node scripts/check-org-identifier.mjs` — `OK (1726 author-facing source file(s), no removed session.tenantId alias)`.
- `node scripts/check-nul-bytes.mjs` — `OK (scanned 6607 text file(s) ...)`, plus a control-byte self-scan over every touched file.

Changeset: patch on both packages, type-side only, citing the #7140 precedent.

## Out of scope, filed not fixed

**#7204** — `executeReport()` in `report-service.ts` rebuilds a five-field subset of the envelope before the engine read that produces the report, dropping `accessibl

author: dmitriyg228
body:
Follow-up to [#928](https://github.com/Vexa-ai/vexa/pull/928), promised in its review.

#928 replaced *"no Vexa maintainer has run Vexa against a FunASR or SenseVoice gateway"* with *"Vexa's actual `TranscriptionClient` **has been run** against…"* — passive voice that a reader takes as Vexa having validated the path. The run is the FunASR maintainers', not ours.

That distinction is the whole purpose of the note being replaced. A reader deciding whether to trust this path needs to know the witness is upstream and that we have not reproduced it. Naming the witness makes the evidence **more** useful, not less: an upstream maintainer validating our client is a stronger signal than an anonymous "has been run", and it tells the reader exactly which gap remains.

#928 was merged first rather than held for this, because the page it corrected was instructing readers to set a Hub checkpoint path (`FunAudioLLM/SenseVoiceSmall`) as the served model id, which does not work. Leaving a broken instruction live to preserve an attribution nuance was the worse trade.

Verified against the tree before publishing either change: `TRANSCRIPTION_SERVICE_URL`, `TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL` and the `/v1/audio/transcriptions` shape are exactly as the page describes.

author: roblourens
body:
Fixes #329880

## Summary

Improves Agent Host session-list startup by preventing list-time worktree-root normalization caches from thrashing on large session catalogs, and restores aggregate change counts from the renderer startup cache.

## Root cause

[#328375](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/328375) added synchronous list-time repair for legacy linked-worktree repository metadata. Both successful-resolution caches were limited to 100 entries. A single `git worktree list --porcelain` result containing hundreds of linked checkouts could immediately evict most of the paths it had just discovered, so later sessions spawned Git again.

In the captured reload, the first AHP `listSessions` took 52.2s and sampled 404 distinct `getWorktreeRoots → git spawn` invocations. A controlled cold-start benchmark against 979 sessions reproduced 543–569 Git processes and 69–115s inside the normalization barrier.

## Changes

- Size the session-to-root normalization cache to the provider catalog before enrichment.
- Size the shared checkout-to-primary-root cache to the provider catalog before enrichment.
- Preserve successful-result and failure-retry semantics.
- Persist only the small aggregate change summary in the existing startup cache so recent session badges render before the live listing finishes.
- Keep full changesets and diffs live-only.
- Document the startup-cache and host normalization behavior.

## Performance

Controlled runs used fresh APFS copy-on-write clones of the same user-data profile for each new Code OSS and Agent Host process:

| Mode | Git processes | Worktree-normalization time |
|---|---:|---:|
| Original 100-entry caches | 543–569 | 69–115s |
| Catalog-sized caches | 21–28 | 1.1–2.8s (1.83s median) |
| Skip normalization | 0 | 0s |

The fix removes approximately 97–99% of the list-time normalization cost. Moving the legacy repair off the synchronous listing path remains a possible follow-up to recover the remaining 1–3s.

## Validation

- `npm run compile`
- `npm run hygiene`
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- 364 affected tests passing; 28 existing tests pending
- Focused cache and startup-persistence regression tests
- `git diff --check`

(Written by Copilot)

author: denislibs
body:
Порт модели применения данных из tweb: сущности сводятся реконсайлом, порядок вычисляется из данных, а не берётся из позиции в ответе сервера. Продолжение PR #164.

## Чинит измеренный баг

Список чатов перетасовывался через ~250 мс после первого кадра:

```
было:  t=121  «Денис Марамыгин»  →  t=375  «Команда Альфа»
стало: t=148  «Команда Альфа»    →  t=3996 «Команда Альфа»
```

Причина — правил порядка было **два** и они расходились: `setDialogs` брал порядок из входного массива (как пришло от сети или из персиста), а `upsertDialog`/`applyNewMessage` двигали строки вручную через `firstUnpinned` + `slice`. Кэш давал один порядок, ответ сети другой.

## Что сделано

**Ядро реконсайла** (`core/store/reconcile.ts`) — порт намерения tweb `saveDialogFilter` (`filters.ts:513-518`). Там UI на Solid, поэтому поля сливают **в** существующий объект: идентичность сохраняется, реактивность ловит изменения полей. React сравнивает ссылки, мутация прошла бы мимо мемоизированных строк — поэтому у нас то же намерение выражено обратной механикой: вернуть старый объект, если после слияния он структурно не изменился. Идентичный ответ сети не даёт ни перерисовки, ни записи в IDB.

**Порядок диалогов** (`core/dialogs/dialogIndex.ts`) — порт `generateDialogIndex` (`dialogs.ts:605-608`). `applyDialogs` стал единственным местом, где меняется список; ручных перестановок в сторе не осталось.

**Cache-first** — порт `getDialogFilters` (`filters.ts:475-484`): данные уже в памяти → в сеть не идём вовсе. Применено к папкам, черновикам и балансу звёзд. У последних двух проверено, что события логируются с плотным `pts` и попадают в `/difference`, то есть пропуски после оффлайна догоняются.

**Снимок вместо рефетча** — `folder_update` и `chat_update` теперь применяются из события. Здесь мы делаем лучше tweb, и это следствие протокола, а не самодеятельность: наш бэкенд шлёт абсолютные снимки, а tweb на `updateDialogFilters` вынужден перезапрашивать весь список, потому что апдейт MTProto фильтров не несёт.

Масштаб для `chat_update`: `publishChatUpdate` зовётся из **13 мест** бэкенда (переименование, фото, участники, права, настройки, слоумод), и каждое заставляло клиент **каждого участника** перезагрузить весь список диалогов.

## Два осознанных отступления от tweb — оба против недетерминированности

В tweb младшие 16 бит индекса это `++this.dialogsNum`, инкрементный счётчик экземпляра. Он зависит от порядка вызовов, то есть различается между кэшем и сетью — ровно та недетерминированность, ради устранения которой затевался порт. Взят `chatId`: так же разводит ничьи, но одинаков при любом порядке обработки.

Там же пустой диалог получает `topDate ||= tsNow()` — текущее время, разное на каждом вызове. Оставлен `0`: диалог без активности стабильно внизу.

## Что нашлось при исполнении

**Оговорку про `pos` папок проверили по бэкенду, а не угадали.** Снимок приходит на одну папку — если бы мутация сдвигала `pos` у соседей, порядок табов ломался бы молча. Оказалось: `pos` присваивается один раз при вставке (`foldersrepo.go:72`), `Update` его не трогает (`:82-83`), `Delete` соседей не перенумеровывает (`:96-97`), эндпоинта переупорядочивания не существует. Значит локальная сортировка по `(pos, id)` даёт ровно тот же порядок, что `List`.

**Регрессия, которую план бы протащил.** `AddMember` тоже зовёт `publishChatUpdate` (`group.go:151`), а у добавленного участника этого чата в списке ещё нет. Буквальное «чата нет — ничего не делаем» означало бы, что новая группа не появляется до ручной перезагрузки: сервисное сообщение не спасает, `applyNewMessage` для неизвестного чата это no-op. Обработчик разветвлён: известен → снимок без сети, неизвестен → один дебаунснутый `/chats`.

**`photoUrl` нельзя строить через `mediaContentUrl`**, как предлагал план: тот выдаёт URL с 15-минутным токеном, а модель хранит путь. В долгоживущей модели каждый рефреш токена выглядел бы изменением и ломал бы весь смысл реконсайла.

**Cache-first ломал два живых вызова** `loadFolders`, служивших «перечитать после локальной операции» — откат неудавшегося удаления папки и вступление в папку по ссылке. Обоим проставлен `overwrite`.

**При cache-first проекция становится единственным живым источником баланса** — в сеть за ним больше не ходим. В плане это не было учтено; добавлен тест на живой кадр `balance_update`.

## Проверки

- `npm run typecheck` — чисто
- `npx vitest run` — **154 файла, 1012 passed, 2 skipped**
- линт по затронутым файлам — ноль замечаний
- живой стенд: перетасовки нет, замер выше

**Все тесты проверены мутационно, а не только на зелёный прогон.** Это дало результат в каждой задаче. Самое показательное: мутант, ломающий глубокое сравнение массивов, проходил все 8 тестов ядра из плана — «не изменилось → та же ссылка» зеленеет и при сравнении-заглушке. Добавлен парный негативный кейс. Тест на снятый рефетч потребовал прокрутки фейковых таймеров за дебаунс 300 мс — иначе он тоже проходил бы на сломанном коде.

## Инварианты

- `stores/noManualOrder.test.ts` — вне `applyDialogs` нет `splice`/`sort`, детали формулы не расползлись по стору.
- Три правила записаны в `web-client/CLAUDE.md`.

author: j6626
body:
The current version of the deprojection function fills in NaNs with 

```
        r = np.where(np.isfinite(r_obs), r_obs, rf)
        t = np.where(np.isfinite(t_obs), t_obs, tf)
        z = np.where(np.isfinite(z_obs), z_obs, zf)
```
However, this creates a discontinuous grid at sufficiently high inclinations and leads to the addition of artificial disk components. I removed these lines and added np.nan_to_num calls around other functions that depend on r, t, and z. Since the current interpolation routine is leaving NaNs in the middle of the grid, I replaced it with SciPy's interpolation routine, which does not appear to exhibit the same issues.

author: shawngresham90-cell
body:
**Operations, not features.** No product behaviour changes. One new pure module, one new test harness, six operational documents. **Nothing in `src/` imports the new module** — that is asserted by a test, and it is the point.

Branched from `main` at `b6a1260`. **Touches none of PR #272's files.**

---

## The stop policy is code as well as prose

`src/lib/navigator/pilot-stop-policy.ts` carries **14 P0 conditions and 9 P1s**, each with its own owner actions and resume criterion. `docs/operations/navigator-pilot-stop-policy.md` is the same catalogue rendered for a person, and the test compares them **in both directions** — every id, every severity, every threshold. The markdown and the module cannot drift into telling you different things six weeks from now.

Three rules are settled in code so they are not re-derived under pressure:

| Rule | Why it is written this way |
|---|---|
| **One confirmed P0 stops the pilot** | Not a rate. A rate-based rule assumes the next occurrence is as survivable as the last one, and a bridge strike is not survivable. |
| **A P0 *reported but not confirmed* pauses expansion** | You do not hand a possible strike-path defect to a second driver while you are still working out whether it was real. |
| **A judgment condition can never be fired by a count** | "The outage handling was confusing" is a verdict. Inventing a threshold for it would be arithmetic worn as rigour. Three P1s carry `judgment: true` and the classifier refuses to trigger them from occurrences — only from you confirming them. |

**The module has no lever.** No flag, no fetch, no timer, and a test walks all of `src/` to prove nothing imports it. An automated stop driven by field reports would hand anyone who can file one the power to kill a driver's navigation mid-trip, on an unconfirmed claim.

## Rollback — drilled, not assumed

`docs/operations/navigator-release-register.md` records what is deployed, what is known good, and what you roll back to, with an evidence grade nothing can promote itself through. **KNOWN-GOOD requires a date and a drive**, and the test fails the build if a row claims it without one.

Today the best target is `94fc659`, graded **CANDIDATE** — 22 Navigator harnesses pass and it builds cleanly, and **nobody has driven it**. The register says that rather than rounding up.

### What the drill actually did

Three real production builds of `origin/main`, served locally and probed over HTTP. No production system was touched.

| Request | flag **unset** | flag on, **no password** | flag on, password, **no cookie** |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /` | `200` | `200` | `200` |
| `GET /drive` | **`404`** | `307` → access | `307` → access |
| `GET /navigator` | **`404`** | `307` → access | `307` → access |
| `POST /api/navigator/route` | **`404`** `not-enabled` | **`401`** | **`401`** |
| `GET /api/navigator/destination-search` | **`404`** `not-enabled` | **`401`** | **`401`** |

- **The feature-disable lever really disables** — every Navigator surface 404s while the rest of the site serves normally.
- **A misconfigured deploy fails closed** — flag on with no password redirects to a screen that can never succeed, and both APIs 401.
- **`/navigator/access` stays reachable in every state.** By design (gating the password screen behind the password would loop) — but note the consequence: feature-disabling does not *hide* that a pilot exists.

Then the gate was attacked. Eleven cookies — forged MAC, MAC signed with a different password, tampered `issuedAt`, correctly signed but 13 hours old, correctly signed 10 minutes in the future, wrong version prefix, no dots, four parts, non-numeric `issuedAt`, empty, percent-encoded RTL override — **all 401**. A 20,000-character cookie was refused at `431` before the app saw it. Only a correctly signed current cookie reached `/drive`. No secret-shaped value appeared on the homepage or the access page.

### Stopped deliberately

| Step | Status |
|---|---|
| Publish an earlier Netlify deploy | **OWNER AUTHORIZATION REQUIRED** — production mutation |
| Change any Netlify environment variable | **OWNER AUTHORIZATION REQUIRED** |
| Revert a commit on `main` | **OWNER AUTHORIZATION REQUIRED** — auto-deploy would publish it |
| Confirm what is actually deployed right now | Netlify state is not readable here. The register records `b6a1260` as the newest commit on `main`, **not** as a confirmed deploy |

### One open question worth five minutes

**Does changing `NAVIGATOR_PREVIEW_PASSWORD` in Netlify take effect without a redeploy?** Every pilot cookie is an HMAC keyed by that password, so it is the fastest access stop in the system — if it works instantly you can revoke every session in under a minute with no build. The code reads it per call, so the answer depends entirely on how Netlify serves env changes to a deployed function, which **cannot be established from this repository**. Test it once on a day nobody is driving, and write the answer into the register.

## Gates

**Wave 0** — 63 lines you drive yourself, 20 marked 🛑 as safety-critical, none pre-marked. An unmarked line counts as `NOT TESTED` and blocks Wave 1 exactly like a failure does. Section 8 covers the #272 missed-turn behaviour and has to be run against the #272 preview build, because it is not on `main`.

**Wave 1** — capped at **2–3 drivers, hard stop**, with 22 entry requirements, operating limits, and 10 exit criteria. It is currently:

# 🔴 NO GO

| Blocker | State |
|---|---|
| PR #272 owner road retest | **NOT PERFORMED** |
| Wave 0 road test | **NOT STARTED** — 0 of 63 lines marked |
| Known-good rollback target | **CANDIDATE only** — never driven |

The exit criteria say plainly that 2–3 drivers **cannot produce statistical significance about anything**. What that size of pilot can establish is coverage and the absence of known harm, and that is what is asked for — 10 trips, 3 per driver, 20 hours, five road types, three real off-route events.

## ⚠ Owner decision that blocks Wave 1

**Where does a driver send a problem report?** The app generates a report and copies it to the clipboard. Nothing in this repository names a destination, and the only address defined anywhere is `privacy@…`, which is the privacy contact and not a pilot support channel. Nothing was invented — guessing would send truck-route defect reports somewhere nobody reads.

## Validation

| | |
|---|---|
| New harness | `navigator-stop-policy` — **327 passed, 0 failed** |
| Full repository suite | **142 harnesses, all passed** |
| TypeScript / ESLint / Prettier / `git diff --check` | clean |
| Production build | succeeded (three times, in the drill) |

## One observation, not fixed here

author: nateisern
body:
Adds `docs/adr/0004-local-explainable-pricing.md`. Docs only — the engine, the column drop and the deletions are #369.

## Why

The current "ethical price" score is calibrated for one market family and applied to all of them. **Executed** against `packages/shared-types/src/ethicalPricing.ts` at HEAD (`bun` running `validateEthicalPricing`, not hand arithmetic):

| scenario | proposed | `suggestedRent` | `maxRent` | `withinEthical` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Barcelona, 2-bed 70 m², lift + furnished | 1 450 | 276 | **317** | **false** |
| the same flat with area typed as 753 ft² | 1 450 | 1 320 | 1 518 | **true** |
| Bucharest, 2-bed 65 m² | 3 200 (RON) | 122 | **140** | **false** |
| Warsaw, 2-bed 60 m² | 4 500 (PLN) | 112 | **129** | **false** |
| Buenos Aires, 2-bed 70 m² | 450 000 (ARS) | 131 | **151** | **false** |
| Austin TX, 2-bed 900 ft² | 1 800 (USD) | 1 789 | 2 057 | **true** |

`withinEthical === false` is exactly what `app/properties/[id]/index.tsx:151` gates the red "Not a fair price" banner on. Every correctly-entered European listing fails; the area unit alone flips the verdict; only the Austin row lands near its input, because Austin is one of the 17 US cities in `LOCATION_MULTIPLIERS` and everywhere else resolves to its `default: 1.0`.

## Decisions

The eight mandatory principles of #348, adopted as binding decisions:

- **D1** no single global truth of "ethical price" — **no default parameter entry may exist**; a jurisdiction miss is an error, never a substitution (the shape being retired is `ethicalPricing.ts:92`).
- **D2** nothing published without jurisdiction, currency, area unit, date and methodology — all five required, non-nullable.
- **D3** a comparison must show sample, sources and confidence, reachable in one interaction.
- **D4** `insufficient` is a first-class, **visible** result with machine-readable reasons — never rendered as "average" or "not fair".
- **D5** price / total cost / conduct / experience are four separate dimensions; **no aggregate grade** may be computed, stored, exposed or ranked on without a successor ADR.
- **D6** versioned + reproducible: `methodologyVersion` + `inputDigest`, immutable rows.
- **D7** official vs market data tagged `observationKind` and **never blended**; `hybrid` means both reported, not averaged.
- **D8** a methodology change inserts a new row and never rewrites history.

Contracts: `PricingAssessment`, `PricingExplanationItem` (a stable `code` + i18n `messageKey` + typed values, so it renders in `en-US`/`es-ES`/`ca-ES`/`it-IT` — the current `reasoning: string[]` is server-formatted English with a hard `$`), `PricingSourceRef`, `TotalCostAssessment`, `PricingJurisdictionCapability`, `HousingAssessment`. Four deviations from the reference shape, each stated with its reason.

Also decided: the comparables policy (11 mandatory filters, a 1 km → 2 km → 5 km → neighborhood → city ladder with **no country or global rung**, IQR outlier trimming with the median as the headline instead of the mean, per-offering max observation age, duplicate suppression with `observationCount` and `sampleSize` published separately, no FX inside a statistic, area normalised at ingest, stay-length-aware short-term comparison, per-offering minimum samples, official-index licensing); the capability registry, which **ships empty** so every market is `supported: false` at cutover; the UI rules (badge, banner, filter and sort all deleted, replaced by neutral percentile bands gated on `confidence >= medium`); four worked numeric examples (monthly rent, short-term, sale, and two shapes of insufficient data); a three-phase retirement plan; and twelve required tests.

## Premises verified, not assumed

- **"dollars" — CONFIRMED**, and it reaches the UI: all four locale bundles carry `property.suggestedRent = 'Suggested: ${{amount}}/month'` and `property.maxEthicalRent = 'Max Ethical: ${{amount}}/month'` untranslated, shown to a landlord in Barcelona or Rome.
- **"square feet" — CONFIRMED and sharper than stated.** The calculator treats the column as ft² (`BASE_PRICES_PER_SQFT`), but the *stored* column is m² for ~35 providers (openrent and rightmove convert and say so) and **raw square feet** for `providers/ca/realtorCa/parse.ts:143` and every US JSON-LD path — `parse/jsonLd.ts:372-375` discards `unitCode` while `providers/us/{zillow,apartmentsCom}/fixtures.ts` declare `FTK`. The create wizard labels the field "Square Footage"; every display string says m².
- **"US cities" — CONFIRMED.** 17 US cities plus `default: 1.0`.
- **"fixed utility costs" — CONFIRMED narrowly, understated broadly.** `utilities_included: 80` is a flat +$80. But total cost is not modelled *at all*: a grep of the three scoring modules for `deposit|applicationFee|lateFee|cleaningFee|serviceFee|taxesPercent|petFee|agencyFee` returns **zero**, though every column exists.

**Two defects the issue does not name.** (1) `buildBaseComparableFilter` never filters by currency, so ARS and USD listings in one Buenos Aires block are averaged together — reachable, not theoretical (`providers/ar/argenprop/fixtures.ts:12,34`). (2) An external listing with **no** comparables is labelled "not a fair price" (`priceEthicsService.ts:72-74` → the red banner), i.e. absence of Homiio data presented to the user as a finding about the landlord — pinned by `__tests__/unit/priceEthicsService.test.ts:183`.

## Measured consumer inventory

`git grep -nE` (never a `dir/**/*.ts` pathspec) over `ethic|fairPrice|fairness|priceScore|areaPrice|pricePerSq|sqft|sqm|squareFootage` etc.: **763 hits across 148 files**, every file assigned to one of eleven categories — the rent model (2), the scoring service (2), persistence (5), write-path triggers (4), the HTTP filter/sort/insights surface (5), the wire contract (4), frontend (27), ops scripts (4), tests (24), docs (5), ingest area parsing (55). Every entry is `file:line` anchored; **all 91 unambiguous references were machine-checked to resolve and be in range.**

**Sindi: measured NIL.** No AI route, controller, service or prompt reads the score, so #348's "what happens to any Sindi ranking" has the answer *none exists*.

**Residual — 11 files the sweep could not attribute, each explained individually** rather than dropped, because an inventory that only reports what it classified cannot tell "there is nothing else" from "I stopped looking". Two real findings came out of it: `controllers/property/offeringRules.ts:57-60` computes a **second** price-per-area nobody would look for under this heading, and `services/telegramService.ts:329` hard-codes `m²` on a broadcast surface no frontend audit covers. Also dead: `constants/amenities.tsx`'s `ethicalNotes`/`maxFairValue`/`ethicalPriority` (129 hits, zero readers).

## Retirement plan highlights

- **Phase 0 costs one line.** Stop emitting `priceEthics` from the serializer — every frontend read already degrades correctly on an absent block (checked read by read: `Boolean(...)` → no badge, `=== false` → no banner, `0` vs `0` → no reorder).
- `fairPrice` / `sortBy=fairness` are accepted and **ignored with a `filter_retired` warning**, because silently returning an unfiltered list reads to a user as "all of these are fair".
- **`saved_searches.filters` is opaque jsonb "exactly as the client sent them"** (`db/schema/saved.ts:114-124`), so a saved search can carry `fairPrice: true` forever — its execution drops the key, surfaces the warning, and the alert sweep re-confirms before firing on a set whose meaning changed.
- Phase 1 retains history in `retired_price_ethics` (**133 of 17 644 rows** at the production census of 2026-08-06, `db/schema/properties.ts:55` — re-measure at migration time) before dropping the eight columns, two indexes and one CHECK.
- `services/areaPriceComparison.ts` is **re-contracted, not deleted**; `area-insights` survives as the facts endpoint.

## Flagged for product sign-off

The landlord-facing `EthicalPricingRecommendation` is **deleted, not ported** — on the measure

author: neaox
body:
## Problem

AWS accepts "the name or the unique stack ID" for every stack-scoped operation's `StackName` member — and after a stack is deleted, the ARN is the *only* handle that still resolves, which is exactly what CDK's deploy monitor polls with during a destroy. Overcast resolved by name only everywhere except `RollbackStack`, so any ARN-passing client got:

```
ValidationError: Stack [arn:aws:cloudformation:…:stack/…/58eb88e4-…] does not exist
```

for a stack that was right there (observed in the wild against a CDK deployment).

The audit also turned up two adjacent defects on the same lookup path:

- **`CreateChangeSet` (CREATE type) with an unknown ARN minted a placeholder stack literally *named* the ARN**, with a doubly-nested ARN as its StackID (reproduced in `TestCreateChangeSet_missingStackByARN_doesNotMintPlaceholder`'s pre-fix failure).
- **Mutating a retained `DELETE_COMPLETE` record was possible**: `UpdateStack` by name resurrected a deleted stack, and a repeat `DeleteStack` re-ran the provisioner and appended a second wave of delete events.

## Fix

- `getStackByNameOrARN` now resolves an ARN by extracting its name segment and verifying the stored record's `StackID` matches the full ARN — O(1), no region scan, and a stale ARN from a deleted-and-recreated name resolves to nothing instead of aliasing the new incarnation. (`RollbackStack`, its only prior user, keeps its behaviour; its existing ARN test still passes.)
- Every stack-referencing call site on **both** dispatch paths (legacy `handler.go` and typed `typed_logic.go`) goes through it: `DescribeStacks`, `DescribeStackEvents`, `ListStackResources`, `DescribeStackResources`, `GetTemplate`, `GetTemplateSummary`, `UpdateStack`, `DeleteStack`, `CreateChangeSet`, `DeleteChangeSet`.
- `DescribeStackEvents` fetches events under the **resolved stack name** — event rows are keyed by name, so an ARN reference previously would have scanned an empty prefix even with resolution fixed.
- New `getLiveStackByNameOrARN` gives mutations AWS's deleted-stack semantics: `UpdateStack`/`CreateChangeSet` on a `DELETE_COMPLETE` stack answer "does not exist", repeat `DeleteStack` is a no-op success, and a CREATE-type change set can never be created from an ARN reference.
- `CreateChangeSet` records the change set under the resolved stack name (not the caller's reference), and `DeleteChangeSet` resolves the change set before deleting so ARN-addressed deletes actually delete (its `StackName` requirement is also relaxed to match `DescribeChangeSet`/`ExecuteChangeSet`: optional when `ChangeSetName` is an ARN).

## Deliberate divergence (AWS is the tie-breaker, noted per CONTRIBUTING)

Real AWS stops resolving a deleted stack **by name** the moment it reaches `DELETE_COMPLETE`. Overcast keeps name-based reads answering with the retained final state: the emulator's own integration tests (`waitForStackStatus`) and the web UI poll `DescribeStacks` by name through deletion, and AWS SDK waiters accept either outcome (`stack-delete-complete` matches `DELETE_COMPLETE` *or* the does-not-exist ValidationError), so the lenient read costs no client compatibility while the strict mutation rules above close the paths where the divergence could corrupt state. Documented in `docs/services/cloudformation.md`.

## Compat suites — the first CI run caught a real dependency on the old bug

The go-sdk and python-sdk suites' `DeleteStack` tests deleted the **group's shared stack**, so their `UpdateStack` tests (which run after) only ever passed because Overcast let an update resurrect a `DELETE_COMPLETE` stack — behaviour real AWS rejects and this PR removes. Both suites now exercise delete on their own `compat-del-<RunID>` stack, the shape the cli suite already had, keeping the group order-independent. No baseline edits; the tests go back to passing on their own merits.

## Tests

Failing-first, both paths:

- `internal/services/cloudformation/stack_ref_test.go` — legacy dispatch path (`h.dispatch`): all read ops by ARN, deleted-stack reads by ARN, `UpdateStack` by ARN and on a deleted stack, `DeleteStack` by ARN, repeat-delete no-op (event-count assertion), stale-ARN-after-recreate store test.
- `tests/integration/cloudformation/stack_arn_ref_test.go` — typed path end-to-end: read ops by ARN, update by ARN, delete by ARN + post-delete describes/events by ARN + repeat-delete event count + update-after-delete, stale ARN vs new ARN after recreate, change-set ops by stack ARN, ghost-ARN CREATE change set.

Verification: full `internal/services/cloudformation` + `tests/integration/cloudformation` suites green; `verify-changed.sh` (golangci-lint, three-tag-set compile matrix, scoped tests) passed locally; `go build ./...` / `go vet ./...` (and `-tags slim,dev` for the service) clean; docs index regenerated.

body:
> Targets `main` directly — #605 has merged.
>
> _Supersedes #607, which GitHub auto-closed when its base branch was deleted on merging #605. Same branch, same commits._

## The bug

Day-of formatted every time with `formatTime` — `new Date(ts).getHours()`, the **device's** timezone — while the volunteer briefing beside it pinned Eastern. Same event, same instant, three device timezones, measured off the rendered DOM:

| device timezone | header clock | run of show |
|---|---|---|
| America/New_York | 10:16 PM | 5:00 · 5:30 · 5:50 · 6:00 · 6:40 · 6:55 PM |
| America/Los_Angeles | 7:16 PM | 2:00 · 2:30 · 2:50 · 3:00 · 3:40 · 3:55 PM |
| Asia/Tokyo | 11:16 AM | 6:00 · 6:30 · 6:50 · 7:00 · 7:40 · 7:55 AM |

Two phones in the same room read a different run sheet, and a leader who travels sees times their crew doesn't.

### Before — the same event on a Tokyo phone

![before: the run sheet reading 6:00 AM in Tokyo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Supa-Media/events-os/fix/dayof-event-timezone/docs/design/day-of/before-tz-tokyo.png)

### After — the same phone

![after: the run sheet reading 5:00 PM EDT in Tokyo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Supa-Media/events-os/fix/dayof-event-timezone/docs/design/day-of/after-tz-tokyo.png)

And on a Pacific phone, [before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Supa-Media/events-os/fix/dayof-event-timezone/docs/design/day-of/before-tz-los-angeles.png) / [after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Supa-Media/events-os/fix/dayof-event-timezone/docs/design/day-of/after-tz-los-angeles.png). After the fix all three renders are identical:

| device timezone | header clock | run of show |
|---|---|---|
| America/New_York | 10:24 PM · EDT | 5:00 · 5:30 · 5:50 · 6:00 · 6:40 · 6:55 PM |
| America/Los_Angeles | 10:24 PM · EDT | 5:00 · 5:30 · 5:50 · 6:00 · 6:40 · 6:55 PM |
| Asia/Tokyo | 10:24 PM · EDT | 5:00 · 5:30 · 5:50 · 6:00 · 6:40 · 6:55 PM |

## Where the timezone comes from

**`eventTimeZone(event)` in `@events-os/shared`** — one seam that every event clock asks, and deliberately *not* `EASTERN_TIME_ZONE` inlined at the call site.

Today it answers with the org's home zone, because **no `timeZone` column exists** on `events` or `chapters`. That is the honest state of the data, and it is the same "single-valued for now" note `PLANNING_TIME_ZONE` in `shared/ai.ts` already carries. It is a function anyway, so the day a chapter outside ET launches, the change is confined to that one body — add the column, read it here. Hard-coding Eastern in the screens instead would fix today's symptom and rebuild this exact bug for the first event outside ET. A test pins the seam by passing a `timeZone` through it and asserting Tokyo wins.

Day-of, the briefing's run of show, and the briefing header all format through `formatTimeInZone` / `formatDateTimeInZone` with that resolved zone, so the leader's copy and the volunteer's copy cannot drift apart. The Eastern-only wrappers (`formatTimeEastern`, `formatDateTimeEastern`, `canFormatEastern`) are **deleted**, not deprecated — nothing should be reaching for a literal zone.

The briefing's "all times Eastern (ET)" line now reads the zone name from the same resolver ("all times EDT"), so the sentence can't outlive a change of zone.

### Two riders, both on this screen

- **The header clock reads in the event's zone too**, and prints the zone name — "NOW · EDT". If the clock and the rows disagreed the highlight would look wrong; and without the label the fix is invisible to exactly the person it protects, since a travelling leader can't tell an event-zone 5:00 PM from their own phone's.
- **`isLocalMidnight` → `isMidnightInZone`.** The "set a start time" nudge asked a device-local question, so a Pacific viewer got it on a 3 AM ET event and missed it on a real midnight one.

## What is still device-local — reported, not half-converted

The write path is the bigger half of this, and it is genuinely a different change:

- `components/ui/DateTimeField.tsx` (`DateTimePanel`, `TimeColumns`) reads **and writes** wall clock with the local `Date` constructor. Picking "7:00 PM" on a Pacific phone stores 10:00 PM ET. It is shared with the event header's reschedule popover, so converting it is its own PR.
- `components/grid/RunTimeCell.tsx` — the run-of-show TIME column, same read-and-write pattern.
- `app/(app)/event/new.tsx` + `parseDateTimeInput` — the event start anchor the whole run of show derives from.
- Display-only, event times, still device-local: `EventsCalendarView`, `EventHeader`, `ticketing/TicketingTab`, `door/DoorModeScreen`, `giving/gifts.tsx` + `giving/sponsorship/[id].tsx` event dates.
- Check-in stamps (`CheckInResultBanner`, `AttendeeCheckInList`, `AdminCheckInRoster`) are arguably event-zone too.

The one `formatTime` left on Day-of is in `StartTimePrompt`, echoing the picker's draft — it must keep matching what the user just dialled, and there is a comment saying so.

Everything on the backend and every public/email surface (`lib/landingPage.ts`, `ticketingEmails.ts`, `reminders.ts`, …) is already ET-pinned; no gap there.

## Tests

`apps/mobile/lib/format.test.ts` (new) and `apps/convex/tests/runOfShow.test.ts`. No `Date.now()` anywhere — every input is a fixed instant built with `zonedTimeToUtc`, which is a real inverse of the formatters rather than a hand-computed offset, so they read the same on a UTC CI box and on a laptop in Denver:

- one instant renders 5:00 PM / 2:00 PM / 6:00 AM in three zones
- **DST both directions**: 7:00 PM Eastern either side of the 2026 spring-forward both render "7:00 PM", and the two instants are asserted 47h apart so the test can't pass by nothing happening
- a zone that flips the calendar day (Aug 29 ET → Aug 30 Tokyo) carries the date with it
- `zoneAbbreviation` gives EDT in August, EST in January, and **empty** rather than a wrong label on an unusable zone
- `eventTimeZone` falls back to the org zone for `undefined` / `null` / no column, and an event's own zone wins when one exists
- `isMidnightInZone` is asserted in two zones against the same instant
- liveness is asserted to be an *instant* question, so the device's zone can't move the badge either

## Verification

Isolated Chromium (not the shared MCP context), `location.href` re-asserted before every measurement, against a seeded event from the Worship With Strangers template. Mobile typecheck error count unchanged at 288; shared package clean.

## Academy

No update needed — no lesson quotes a timezone or the briefing's clock label.

author: sjparthi
body:
## Summary

Two things: the terraform apply that rebuilt the prod box died on its last step and is fixed here, and four layers of the 16-connection Dhan feed design (#1731) are built.

**The box is rebuilt and healthy.** The apply from #1732 created `i-0c3fe906dad5492fc` — r8g.xlarge, **ap-south-1b**, 100 GB gp3, EIP `13.234.145.177` re-attached. The AZ un-pin is what actually ended the 2026-08-06 outage: `moved.tf` adopted the subnet (`aws_subnet.public has moved to aws_subnet.public["a"]`, `Plan: 9 to add, 29 to change, 0 to destroy`) instead of destroying it.

**But the apply still finished red**, three minutes after the instance came up:

```
Error: reading ZIP file (./.lambda-zips/dhan-token-minter.zip):
       open ./.lambda-zips/dhan-token-minter.zip: no such file or directory
```

`dhan-token-minter` reached `Cargo.toml` and terraform but never the workflow's `BINS` list. `cargo lambda` builds every bin in the crate so the build was green; only the `cp` loop is driven by `BINS`. Terraform reads that path via `filename`, which plan does not validate — so it failed at **apply** time, after real infrastructure had already changed.

## Items completed

- [x] `BINS` fixed in **both** build steps (plan job and apply job — the plan job produces the zips terraform plans against, so a one-sided fix still diverges)
- [x] `lambda_zip_bins_lockstep_guard.rs` — 5 tests, bite-verified
- [x] Layer 1: reconnect ladder, idle watchdog, pool budget
- [x] Layer 4: depth-20 / depth-200 parsers
- [x] Layer 5: multi-timeframe aggregator rebuild
- [x] Layer 6: tick persistence + 5-key DEDUP
- [x] `.claude/rules/dhan/full-market-depth.md` un-stubbed (it still said depth was FORBIDDEN FOREVER)

## The three protocol facts that drove layer 1

Each cited to a line in the docs pack rather than inferred:

| Fact | Consequence |
|---|---|
| Server pings every 10s, closes after 4 unanswered | Idle threshold is **27s** — we reconnect on our terms at 2–3 missed pings rather than being dropped |
| The 6th socket does not get rejected — it silently disconnects the **oldest** with code 805 | A naive retry quietly kills a healthy connection, so `pool_budget` refuses to open it |
| Depth is a different protocol: 12-byte header, f64 prices, bid/ask as separate packets | Separate parser; where the doc's prose contradicts its own code table on buy/sell, the code table is authoritative |

## Complexity — stated honestly

`MultiTfAggregator::consume_tick` is **O(1) and allocation-free**: one `HashMap::get` on a `Copy` key, one `Vec` index, then `TF_COUNT` (compile-time 21) scalar folds. Constant in instrument count and tick history.

Two paths are **not** O(1) and are labelled, not relabelled:
- slot growth past the pre-allocated size — `Vec` realloc + memmove, cold path, once per instrument per process
- `force_seal_all` / `catch_up_seal_all` — O(N × 21) full scans, by design, on the day boundary; never per tick

The pre-commit gate flagged the original unsized `Vec::new()`/`HashMap::new()`. It was right; pre-sizing to the design's adaptive-universe start (1,000) is the fix rather than an `APPROVED` annotation.

## Two things the gates caught, and what I did

**Banned-pattern scanner** flagged the unsized allocations above → fixed properly, not annotated away.

**Pub-fn-test guard** blocked the push: untested count 380 → 382. The two were `stop_reason()` and `consumed_bytes()` on `DepthFrameIter`. Both are how a caller tells "frame ended cleanly" from "I silently got fewer packets than the wire carried", so they got three real tests, including a non-vacuity case proving `Complete` actually carries information. Back to 380. **Baseline not overridden.**

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p tickvault-core --lib` — **2155 passed**
- [x] `cargo test -p tickvault-storage --lib` — **742 passed**
- [x] `cargo test -p tickvault-trading --lib candles` — **76 passed**
- [x] `cargo clippy -p tickvault-core --lib -D warnings -W clippy::perf` — clean
- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check` — clean
- [x] Lockstep guard bite test: removing the entry fails 2 of 5 with the exact diagnostic
- [x] All 12 pre-push gates green

Core was verified centrally because the two agents authoring it hit a session limit mid-verification.

## Honest envelope

100% inside the tested envelope, with ratcheted regression coverage: the CI regression cannot recur silently (build-failing lockstep guard, bite-proven); depth and tick decode are total over arbitrary bytes with per-packet golden vectors; the aggregator is sparse by construction and I-P1-11-keyed with fail-closed slot exhaustion; the tick DEDUP key carries `capture_seq`, tested in both directions (N ticks in one second produce N rows; a constant seq collapses them to one).

**NOT claimed:**
- **No socket is opened.** All four modules are pure logic. Nothing spawns `TickWriter` or the aggregator yet.
- **No live QuestDB.** DDL, ILP bytes and the `/exec` arms are tested against a mock; real DEDUP behaviour on a real table is unproven here.
- **No live frame decoded.** Layouts are verified against the documentation pack only. The 1-based-payload-table hazard means golden vectors prove self-consistency with the docs, not with the wire.
- **Zero-allocation in the aggregator is by construction and review, not measured** — no DHAT test or Criterion bench yet.
- The 2026-07-13 retirement reason for the Dhan feed (p99 46s delivery lag, 29–67 silent instruments/minute) is **unaddressed and unaddressable here** — every cause was Dhan-side. The 15:31 REST cross-verify remains the only ground truth and must be live from day one.

## Remaining in the design

Wire the 16 pools into boot; the synthetic tick-gap detector (the feed has **no sequence number**, so loss must be inferred from LTT monotonicity, volume/OI deltas and silence timers); the 15:31 cross-verify.

author: george43g
body:
Five TUI reliability bugs, found by driving the real TUI to exhaustion against the live DB (5-agent swarm) plus heap-snapshot diffing. This is the batch that targets George's "less reliable than Messages.app" report.

## 1. SEVERE — unbounded heap leak in every session (the crashes)

Idle heap ramped ~+9MB/min until the RSS watchdog killed the process (repeatedly, at 1024MB, within minutes). Heap-snapshot constructor-diff named the retainer exactly:

```
Δcount   Δbytes  constructor          (5 idle minutes)
+74667    4.56MB obj:PerformanceMeasure  (11447→86114)
+666921  19.82MB (string)                (195914→862835)
```

**Cause**: the `imsg` bin runs with `NODE_ENV` unset, so the externalized `react-reconciler` loads `react-reconciler.development.js`, which calls `performance.measure()` on every commit. Those entries accumulate forever in Node's user-timing buffer and are never GC'd.

**Fix**: `ensureProductionReactForTui()` sets `NODE_ENV=production` before the TUI's first Ink import — on **both** dispatch paths (the commander action *and* the manual switch; patching one silently did nothing, which is how the first attempt failed).

**Verified**: `PerformanceMeasure` 11,447 → **1**; live heap flat at 46MB after heavy activity (was 112MB and climbing). Note: the RSS watchdog was *correct* — this was a real leak, so no robustness-kit change is needed.

## 2. SEVERE — analytics view re-fetch loop
Opening a second analytics view re-ran `getMessagesInWindow` (6.4k rows) ~8×/sec with cache hits:0 — heap 332→1517MB in 20s. `useImsg()` returned a fresh object each render and the analytics load effect has it in deps. Fixed by memoizing the hook's return.

## 3. SEVERE — `q` in visual-select quit the app
Input-guard-law violation: select mode fell through to browse handlers. Movement-key whitelist added; pinned by a new assertion in the existing guard test.

## 4. HIGH — merged threads falsely "exhausted" mid-scroll
Big merged threads (46k messages, 6 legs) stopped loading at arbitrary points, presenting a recent date as the thread start with tens of thousands of messages unreachable and no indicator. The cursor used min ROWID while the DB paginates by `(date, ROWID)` — orders that diverge in merged threads. New `oldestMessageCursor` picks the min `(date, ROWID)`; progress is measured by dedup, not ROWID comparison.

## 5. HIGH — `:` date jump never loaded older history
The loop read `state.messages`/cursor from a frozen closure, so it couldn't observe its own dispatched prepends (zero DB queries fired, reproduced 3×). Now driven off a local cursor + each fetch's return, with selection via a new `SELECT_MSG_BY_DATE` action that runs against live reducer state.

## Validation
- Full suite **1009 green** (+14 new: cursor/select-by-date semantics, select-guard).
- Leak fix verified by heap snapshots on the real DB (counts above).
- Swarm reports (5 agents, feature-matrix coverage) in the session scratchpad; remaining findings tracked as follow-up tasks (drawer polish, blank-boot indicator, filter-Esc stale pane).

Cuts 1.21.2.

author: joshtgi
body:
Closes [ENG-162](https://linear.app/maain/issue/ENG-162/adoption-docs-validated-against-a-real-install).

The last task of the [ENG-137](https://linear.app/maain/issue/ENG-137/distribute-jen) distribution epic. jen is installable today — `@reveer/jen@0.0.0` is public and `npx jen init` writes a working workflow — but nothing tells an adopter how, what they may do with it, or which files are theirs to edit.

## What this carries

- **The repository model, stated correctly.** A project installs jen into its own repo; jen owns the root and `src/` holds the project's own tracked sources. The fork model is gone from `AGENTS.md` and from the `agent-instructions` capability that mandated it.
- **Adopter-first README**, led by the ownership boundary, with contributor material moved to `CONTRIBUTING.md`. The documented path gets executed against a scratch project before it ships.
- **Apache-2.0**, replacing the `UNLICENSED` declaration on a package anyone can already install. Decision confirmed on the issue ahead of design.
- **`keywords`**, absent today, so the package is unsearchable.

## Review notes

The estimate was 2 points, set before this absorbed the licensing decision and before design found a contradiction in the repository model — three sources disagreed about what `src/` is. Now five spec deltas, two rewritten documents, and a full adoption run.

Migrating an *existing* project onto jen stays out of scope: `jen init` refuses a project holding a differing `AGENTS.md`, and `project-install` records that as unsupported adoption rather than a defect.

author: bonztm
body:
## Summary

Six remote media-proxy routes piped an axios `responseType:"stream"` upstream to the client response with a bare `.pipe(res)` and no close-event cleanup. Node's `pipe()` unpipes when the destination closes but never destroys the source, so every client seek/skip left the upstream sidecar/YouTube socket open and buffering until its 300000ms timeout — exhausting the connection pool under normal use. Release-blocking resource leak.

## Sites fixed (all with the guarded `res.on("close")` destroy pattern already used by the podcasts proxy)

- `backend/src/routes/tidalStreaming.ts` — Tidal stream proxy
- `backend/src/routes/youtube.ts` — YouTube stream proxy
- `backend/src/routes/youtubeMusic.ts` — authenticated `/stream/:videoId` and public `/stream-public/:videoId`
- `backend/src/routes/artists.ts` — preview stream primary path and 401 public-fallback path

## Tests

One focused runtime test per site (6 total) asserting the captured `close` handler destroys the upstream stream exactly once and respects the `destroyed` guard (no double-destroy). Verified each test fails against the unfixed source.

## Verification

- Targeted jest (4 touched suites): 91/91 passed
- `tsc --noEmit`: clean
- `prettier --check` on all changed files: clean
