author: tongzhou8086
body:
## What changed

1. **Removed the kernel-name sentence** — 「这个设计对应的 kernel 是 `bf16-single-ns4-store2-bk64-bn512-load128`…」 — so the post reads without reference to the repo.
2. **BN256 table remeasured** with the two requested kernels.
3. **BN512 table added** with the four requested configurations.

Both measured through the tuning script's new `--include`, square shapes 2048 → 20480 step 2048, 1000/1000 ms window, three shuffled passes per shape, medians. The methodology sentence in the post now mentions the shuffling, since it is what makes the numbers trustworthy.

## Two results worth your attention

### The old BN256 numbers did not reproduce

The table already in the post showed BK=128 ahead by **+9.6%** at 15360³ and **+9.3%** at 16384³. Those came from a single fixed-order pass. Remeasured with shuffled multi-pass:

| Shape | BK=64 | BK=128 | delta |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4096³ | 1330 | 1302 | -2.1% |
| 12288³ | 1277 | 1253 | -1.9% |
| 16384³ | 1263 | 1235 | -2.2% |
| 18432³ | 1225 | 1245 | +1.6% |
| 20480³ | 1239 | 1233 | -0.5% |

BK=64 and BK=128 trade places within ±2%. The post's text now says they are roughly equivalent for BN256, and explains why: bigger buffers versus a shallower ring, roughly cancelling.

This also means the claim in the merged PR #42 — "+9.3% at 16384³" — was an artefact of fixed-order single-pass measurement and should not be relied on.

### BN512 is where BK=128 actually pays

| Shape | 基础版 BK=64 | 基础版 BK=128 | load128 BK=64 | load128 BK=128 | torch.matmul |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8192³ | 1371 | 1382 | 1371 | 1386 | 1382 |
| 12288³ | 1346 | 1373 | 1350 | 1377 | 1409 |
| 14336³ | 1270 | 1367 | 1274 | 1369 | 1375 |
| 16384³ | 1315 | 1389 | 1314 | 1390 | 1428 |
| 18432³ | 1248 | 1378 | 1249 | 1375 | 1374 |
| 20480³ | 1253 | 1381 | 1249 | 1383 | 1423 |

BK=128 leads from 12288³ up, by **+10.4%** and **+10.2%** at 18432³ and 20480³. That matches the argument the section already makes: BN512 has one accumulator, so a tile must drain before the next tile starts, and halving the number of k iterations widens that window. The BK=64 column sagging to ~1250 at 14336³ and 18432³ is that window running out.

### `load128` is worth almost nothing

Baseline versus load128 differs by **under 0.5% at almost every shape** — 1371 vs 1371 at 8192³, 1248 vs 1249 at 18432³. The post introduces load128 as the way to reduce epilogue stalling, so the added text says plainly that the data does not support that: what actually helps is BK.

You may want to revisit how the BN512 section motivates load128, since the narrative currently builds to it. I left the prose itself alone — that is an editorial call, not a fill-in.


---

## Update — remeasured, and the BN512 section reverted to the plain epilogue

### Method changed, because single runs were not reproducible

Repeating a whole run on the **same node** disagreed by up to 14% at the top end (BK=64 BN512 at 20480³ read 1109, 1118 and 1269). The tuning script's internal shuffled passes do not catch this — the variation is between runs, not within them. Both tables are now **medians of three independent runs**, each itself three shuffled passes, and per-cell spread is under 2% almost everywhere.

### Both earlier conclusions were wrong

**BN256** — I previously wrote that BK=64 and BK=128 were within ±2% of each other. They are not:

| Shape | BK=64 | BK=128 | delta |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4096³ | 1328 | 1278 | -3.8% |
| 14336³ | 1324 | 1344 | +1.5% |
| 18432³ | 1243 | 1319 | **+6.1%** |
| 20480³ | 1192 | 1302 | **+9.2%** |

There is a crossover: BK=64 leads in the middle, BK=128 from ~14336³ up.

**BN512** — the crossover is at 16384³, not 12288³, and worth +5.4% at 20480³ rather than the +10.4% the single run suggested.

In both designs the moving column is BK=64, which falls away at large shapes (BN256: 1394 → 1192), while BK=128 stays roughly flat. So BK=128's advantage is that it does not degrade, not that it speeds up — the same shape of result seen in the kernel PRs.

### The cuBLAS comparison does not survive changing machines

Raised in review, and confirmed: `torch.matmul` at 20480³ measured **1361–1431** across nodes while BK=128 BN512 stayed near **1370**. On a slower node the kernel leads cuBLAS; on a faster one it does not. The post now says this explicitly rather than presenting either direction as settled.

### BN512 section reverted to the plain epilogue

The prose, pseudocode and comparison paragraph no longer describe the load128 two-level drain, and the table drops those columns. The section now describes exactly what it measures. (The measured difference was under 0.5% almost everywhere, so nothing is lost by leaving it out.)

### Note

One measurement run died with `CUDA error: unspecified launch failure` at 12288³ — the second such failure this session, after the one during the GSM sweep. Not reproducible under direct stress, and unrelated to these edits, but worth tracking separately.

author: karia
body:
## What

Implements [Phase 2](docs/plans/2026-08-09-phase2-authentication.md).

- Google sign-in via OmniAuth. The request phase is POST-only (`omniauth-rails_csrf_protection`); the callback accepts the GET that Google sends back
- `Person`, `PersonRole`, `Group`, `GroupMembership`, `User`. Roles live on `Person`, so swapping the Google account later does not drop them
- `pundit_user` is `current_person`, not `current_user`
- The `/manage` area's temporary basic auth is gone, replaced by role checks. Admins get everything; GMs get scenarios and the master tables but not people or groups
- Admin screens for people, groups, and linking a Google account to a person
- The analytics and ad gate now reads the real sign-in state

## Notable

- An account with no `Person` is a normal state, not an error. Every user passes through it: they sign in, see only the public area, and an admin links them afterwards. Specs cover that transition in both directions.
- Denied requests answer 404 rather than 403, so a hidden page does not confirm it exists.
- `spec/policies/authorization_matrix_spec.rb` fixes the whole grid in one place — anonymous, signed in but unlinked, linked with no role, GM, admin — because ADR-0001 treats an authorization gap as a disclosure.
- `bin/rails admin:grant EMAIL=... NAME=...` creates the first admin, which the admin screens cannot do.

## Verification

- [x] `bin/rspec` — 129 examples, 0 failures
- [x] `prek run --all-files`
- [x] GET on `/auth/google_oauth2` answers 404, so another site cannot start the flow
- [x] A provider failure redirects instead of raising, and creates no user

## Not in this PR

The Google OAuth client itself. `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` are read from the environment and the redirect URIs are documented in `.env.example`; registering the client in Google Cloud is a manual step before deploying.

author: epi13
body:
## Summary

Fixes the post-0.4.1 commissioning deadlock reported on the physical Windows node:

```text
error: stop managed persistent Fabric worker failed
launcher state lacks a validated process token
```

PR #12 introduced process-token validation for safe Windows worker restarts, but an earlier 0.4.1 commissioning attempt could already have written the legacy launcher schema without a `process_token`. The new stop path then failed closed forever on that state and could not replace it.

## Fix

The commissioning stop path now safely migrates legacy launcher state:

- if the recorded PID is no longer live, remove the stale launcher file and continue
- if current v0.2 state includes a process token, preserve the existing PID + start-time token guard
- if legacy state has a live PID, require the recorded worker/controller identities to match the requested commissioning identities
- query `Win32_Process` and require the live command line to match the managed `mncs_fabric worker serve` command, worker ID, controller ID, and persistent bundle root before stopping it
- refuse to stop anything if that identity check cannot be made or does not match
- remove the old state only after the legacy managed worker has been safely stopped

This repairs the exact upgrade path without weakening the PID-reuse protection added in PR #12.

## Regression coverage

Adds tests asserting that the generated Windows stop script:

- removes stale state when the PID is gone
- uses `Win32_Process` to verify a live legacy worker before migration
- checks worker/controller/root identity

author: alfin-efendy
body:
## The bug

A turn routed to a WASM component provider silently lost **every** bound tool — plugin tools, MCP servers, skills, app bindings, all of it. The user saw:

> This model can't use tools — 12 bound tool(s) were not available for this turn.

…followed by the model's raw tool-call syntax leaking into the transcript as text, because the system prompt still named the tools while the transport had no way to carry them.

Root cause: `ryuzi:provider/provider@0.1.0` takes a flat `prompt: string` and returns text. No tool channel in either direction. `flatten_anthropic_prompt` additionally collapsed roles, `tool_use` and `tool_result` blocks into one string. `target_is_toolless_wasm` therefore treated **every** WASM-backed provider as toolless by construction.

This affected **all 14 first-party provider components**, not just the free tiers: openai, openrouter, groq, deepseek, mistral, xai, nvidia, huggingface, google, qwen, anthropic, anthropic-oauth, opencode, mimo.

The premise was verified live before any code was written — OpenCode Zen (`big-pickle`) returned `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` with a well-formed `tool_calls` array. The upstreams were never the problem; the WIT ABI was.

## What this does

Adds a typed `ryuzi:provider/provider@0.2.0` interface carrying a structured transcript (text / `tool_use` / `tool_result` content blocks), tool definitions, a tool choice, and a stop reason. The host negotiates **per component**, and moves all 14 components onto it.

**Host** — new WIT package alongside the untouched 0.1.0 one; host mirror types; a new pure `llm_router/wasm_bridge.rs` mapping an Anthropic-Messages body to the structured request and returned chunks back to synthetic OpenAI deltas (the existing `OpenAiToAnthropicStream` already turns those into real Anthropic `tool_use` events, so the harness, MCP tools and skills never learn a WASM component was involved); a transport that reports `capabilities()` and calls `complete_v2()`; and a router that asks the component instead of assuming.

**Components** — the leverage sat in two existing shared crates. `plugins/openai-format` (its `guest_macro.rs` is the single `Guest` impl for ten components) and `plugins/anthropic-format` (two more) carry twelve; `opencode` and `mimo` were moved onto the shared OpenAI mapping rather than growing their own copies.

**Separately**, fixes an unrelated bug found in the same investigation: the plugin **detail** payload reported a component OAuth profile token as *not connected*, so Atlassian's Overview checklist kept "Connect your account" grey forever while the wizard showed CONNECTED. Two sibling functions disagreed; the profile-aware check now lives in one helper both call.

## Three latent defects the review loop caught

All three were **silent** — no error, no failing test — and each would have taken out all 14 components at once, only after release:

1. **The discovery gate** recognised only the 0.1.0 export, making a 0.2.0-only component permanently *undiscoverable*. Found because a reviewer asked for a test that was missing, and writing it failed for an unexpected reason.
2. **`list_models()`** had the same version-blindness, so a migrated component would advertise zero models.
3. **The router picked which ABI to call using `capabilities().tools`** — the wrong axis. That field answers *"may I forward tools?"*; *"which ABI does this component speak?"* is `exports_provider_v2()`. They coincide for 13 components and diverge for exactly one: `mimo` exports only 0.2.0 yet honestly reports `tools: false`, so **every `mimo-free` turn failed outright**. The approved design had three negotiation rows; the implementation had collapsed them to two. Found by the final whole-branch review, which was explicitly asked to hunt for a third instance of the pattern.

`capabilities()` is fail-closed by construction, not merely by test: the synchronous constructor is private, the only crate-visible one resolves before returning, and an unresolved cache reports toolless.

## What the evidence proves — and what it does not

**Proves.** `wasm_bridge` has 12 unit tests over `serde_json::Value`, including a real translator feed asserting a tool call emerges as an Anthropic `content_block_start`/`tool_use`. The router's degrade decision is pinned in both directions. The conformance battery drives **13 real compiled components** and asserts a wire `tool_calls` payload becomes a `WasmToolCall` with the exact id/name/arguments and a `ToolUse` stop reason. Manifests changed in `version` and `wit-api` only — provider ids, network allowlists and OAuth profiles are byte-identical across all 14.

**Does not prove.** The mock upstream never inspects the *outgoing* request, so a component that mangled its `tools` array would still pass. Neither `opencode` nor `mimo` is a conformance fixture — `opencode`'s hand-rolled `guest.rs` has no executed test of its mapping glue at all (it is `#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]`-gated, so native `cargo test` never compiles it). No multi-turn `tool_use` → `tool_result` replay runs through a real component. **No end-to-end run exists** — the live smoke below is still owed.

## Deployment reality

Host changes ship with the app build; the component half reaches users **only through a signed release carrying all 14 bundles**. Until then the app keeps degrading with the existing note. All signing in this branch used a locally generated **dev key** — the pipeline is proven, the signatures are not shippable.

New in this branch: `install_component_release` now refuses, before downloading, a bundle whose `wit-api` range this host cannot satisfy. Previously an un-updated app could install a 0.2.0 bundle and silently lose that provider from routing.

## Product finding: mimo's free tier appears sunset

The MiMo probe returned identical `HTTP 400 "Unsupported model mimo-auto"` for both a toolless and a one-tool request, and upstream's own `MiMo-Code` repo reports the free channel sunset on 2026-07-26. The same rejection would hit the pre-existing router path, so this is independent of the migration. `capabilities().tools = false` is therefore recorded as *unproven*, not *unsupported* — if the channel returns, re-run the `#[ignore]`d `plugins/mimo/tests/probe_tools_gate.rs` and flip one flag.

## Owed before this is "done" for users

- **Live smoke** (host-side, can run today): bind Atlassian to an agent, route the session to `opencode-free`, ask it to read a real Jira issue. Expect no "can't use tools" note and a real `mcp__atlassian__jira_issue_get` tool card.
- **Signed release** carrying all 14 component bundles, with a live key.
- Follow-ups: an ABI-rejected first-party bundle is currently reported as "will be retried automatically" (retrying cannot fix it); the conformance battery's toolless inner branch is unexecuted; plus 5 triaged minor items.

## Gates

`cargo test -p ryuzi-core --lib` **2644 passed / 0 failed** · conformance battery **13/13** · `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` clean · `fmt --all --check` clean · all 6 plugin crates green · all 18 components build and sign · `bun test scripts/` 24 pass / 2 pre-existing `install.sh` MINGW failures.

author: carlitotate12160-tech
body:
## Summary

- **GAP-039 fix**: `CompositeOriginDiscovery.candidates()` now accepts candidates when the blocked host is the apex domain OR a dot-boundary subdomain of the intel event's domain
- **Root cause**: passive intel is gathered per APEX domain (one `PASSIVE_INTEL_GATHERED` per engagement target), but origin binding is requested per blocked HOST — usually a subdomain. The exact-match filter (written for the CodeRabbit cross-domain-leak guard) dropped every apex event when the blocked host was a subdomain, so OTX/VT historical-DNS IPs never reached `resolve_and_bind_origin`.
- **Field evidence** (niagamas re-run 2026-08-10, keys loaded): direct OTX/VT API query proves origin candidates exist (`206.189.93.100` niagamas, `216.106.184.20` bernofarm), yet `ORIGIN_DIRECT_ATTEMPT=0` and `beta_failed` — the only `PASSIVE_INTEL_GATHERED` event carried `domain=niagamas.com` while binding was requested for `pos.niagamas.com`.
- **Security preserved**: cross-domain leaks and false suffixes (`notex.com` vs `ex.com`) are still rejected — the match is dot-bounded, same registrable domain family only.

## Changes

- `agent_alpha/recon/origin_discovery.py`: exact match → dot-boundary apex/subdomain match, comment updated
- `tests/phase_2_5/test_origin_binding.py`: 2 adversarial fixtures per §12.60 ratchet (subdomain inherits apex candidates; false-suffix rejected)
- `docs/BUGS_AND_GAPS.md`: GAP-039 registered; GAP-038 status → FIXED

## Test plan

- [x] 23/23 `test_origin_binding.py` pass on Oracle ARM64 (incl. 2 new fixtures)
- [x] 215 passed / 0 failed across phase_2_5 + conductor chain characterize + conductor auth path
- [x] `make check` (ruff + ruff format + mypy, 139 files) clean
- [ ] Re-run niagamas conductor → verify `ORIGIN_DIRECT_ATTEMPT > 0` (Tier-2 field-prove, §12.60)

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved origin discovery for subdomains by including valid passive-intelligence candidates found for their parent domain.
  * Continued to exclude unrelated domains with similar-looking suffixes.

* **Tests**
  * Added coverage for valid subdomain inheritance and protection against false domain matches.

* **Documentation**
  * Updated the known gaps and fixes documentation to reflect the resolved origin-discovery issue.

author: fakechris
body:
Fixes the root design flaw behind the "本地服务未运行" issue: the control API was hard-coded to TCP 7420, and when that port was occupied (zombie daemon, unclean exit) the shell could never connect.

**Architecture (dual transport):**

- **Primary: Unix socket** `{data_dir}/daemon.sock` — the shell connects here. No port conflict, ever. Stale-socket probe-and-unlink (mirrors `lumen-cua`), 0o600 perms, removed on exit. Bind failure is **fatal** (exit 1 → supervisor from #28 alerts + restarts).
- **Secondary: TCP loopback** — kept for the browser extension (browsers can't open Unix sockets; `chrome.sockets` isn't in Safari/Firefox and gone from Chrome MV3). Tries 7420 then increments; writes actual port + pid to `{data_dir}/daemon.tcp_port`. TCP failure is non-fatal (extension is optional).

**Shell side:** `fetch_daemon_health` now connects via Unix socket (minimal std `UnixStream` HTTP/1.1 GET — reqwest 0.12 doesn't do Unix sockets; single endpoint, ~30 lines, no new deps). The shell never touches the TCP port.

**End-to-end verified** with port 7420 held by a zombie: daemon came up on the socket + TCP 7421, stale socket cleaned on restart, socket-based `/health` returned the expected payload. Shell works regardless of TCP port state.

All 6 `lumen-daemon` + 18 `lumen-navi-desktop` tests pass.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added a local Unix socket as the daemon’s primary control channel.
  * Added a best-effort loopback connection for browser extensions, with the active port recorded automatically.
  * Improved socket security and cleanup by restricting access and removing stale sockets.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Health checks now use the local daemon socket for more reliable status detection.
  * Daemon startup now clearly reports critical control-channel failures while tolerating optional browser-extension connection failures.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

body:
## 무엇이 달라지나

화면을 만들기 전에 읽을 규칙집이 생겼다. 루트 `DESIGN-RULES.md` 하나(6,263바이트, 추정 3,040토큰)이고, `DESIGN.md` 는 근거와 이력 보관소로 내려간다. **본문은 한 글자도 지우지 않았다.**

커밋 3개가 함께 올라간다.

| 커밋 | 내용 |
|---|---|
| `9c75cf1` | 1단계. 위계 부품 2종(`WireCardSection`, `WireItem`) 신설, 15초 페이지 적용, 꺽쇠 배수 통일 |
| `f156d6a` | 2단계(CCC-79). 규칙집 분리, ADR-0033, 진입점 한 줄 |
| `4f3725f` | 접힌 아코디언이 나란한 카드 높이를 따라가지 않게 되돌림(실물 확인 결과, 2026-08-10 Q) |

## 왜 하나

`DESIGN.md` 는 122,461바이트, 도구 계측 59,532토큰이다. 화면 하나 만들 때 통째로 읽히는 일이 실제로 없었고 규칙이 날짜별 개정 문단 안에 묻혀 있어, 새 화면마다 같은 위반이 났다.

`pnpm guard:tokens` 는 그 상태에서도 위반 0 이었다. **검사가 보는 것은 값이고 어긋나는 것은 조합이기 때문이다.** 1단계가 그 조합 일부를 부품에 박아 결정론으로 옮겼고, 부품이 못 덮는 나머지를 이번에 읽히는 문서로 옮겼다.

## 규칙 변경 0

요약본의 모든 줄은 기존 계약의 재진술이다. SSOT 는 그대로 pen(색값)과 `DESIGN.md`(색 밖)이고, 둘이 어긋나면 언제나 요약본이 옮겨 적기 오류다.

**유지 규약**: 규칙을 바꾸는 커밋은 요약본도 같은 커밋에서 고친다. 요약본이 뒤처지면 두 번째 권위가 생겨 없느니만 못하다.

## 새로 생긴 낱말

- **눌린 쌓임** = 중요도가 다른 값이 같은 옷으로 세로로 쌓인 것. 고칠 것
- **나열** = 본래 대등한 것이 나란한 것. 정상
- 위계 4단에 이름을 붙였다: **① 제목 / ② 라벨 / ③ 본문 / ④ 설명** (지금까지 `16/600` 처럼 숫자로 불렸다)

## 분량

Q 결정으로 분할 대신 감량해서 상한(2,000~3,000)에 맞췄다. 카드와 컴포넌트 계약은 `§5`, `§3-3`, `§3-4` 로 넘기고 머리의 포인터 줄이 그 자리를 가리킨다. 기각한 분할안 둘의 근거는 ADR-0033 에 적었다.

## 검증

- 테스트 815개 통과 (api 448, web 367)
- `guard:tokens`, `guard:align`, `guard:doc-numbers`, `guard:db`, `guard:secrets` 위반 0
- 문서에 적은 값은 코드에서 대조 (`--chevron-box` .5625em, `--chevron-stroke` .125em, 동의 요약 줄 .7em, gap 24/20/12, 하프스텝 넷, `--text-btn` 15, `--text-xs` 삭제 상태)

`yellow` **리베이스 주의**: 1단계 원본은 #112, #113 이전 시점이라 그대로 썼으면 폐지된 도움말 12px 을 규칙집에 박을 뻔했다. main 에 리베이스한 뒤 `§2-1`, `§2-2` 를 다시 읽어 14 하한과 `--text-xs` 폐지를 반영했다.

후속: CCC-80 위계 자동 검사, 이어서 CCC-81, CCC-78, CCC-83, CCC-82.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## 실물 확인 (2026-08-10)

1단계에서 "나란한 카드는 접혀 있어도 높이를 맞춘다"로 §4-2 를 바꿨다가, 정적 하니스로 그려 보고 되돌렸다(세 번째 커밋).

| 케이스 | 왼쪽 | 오른쪽 | 판정 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 접힘 + 펼침 | 246 | 246 | 높이는 맞지만 접힌 쪽에 174 가 빈 채로 남는다 |
| 둘 다 접힘 | 72 | 72 | 문제 없음 |
| 긴 제목 | 265 | 265 | 글자가 커지면 줄 전체가 함께 커진다 |

빈 상자가 생기는 것이 §4-2 가 처음부터 접은 카드를 `align-self:start` 로 정해 둔 이유였다. 높이 맞춤이 필요한 것은 읽는 자료 카드이고(일정 위저드 참고 카드 2장), 그쪽은 `.card-grid` 와 `.wire-container[data-grid]` 가 이미 편다.

author: nateisern
body:
Adds `docs/adr/0001-canonical-housing-graph.md` — the authority for how street,
building, unit and listing relate, and for which domain references which. Docs
only: no code, schema or migration change. `docs/adr/` is created here; the ADR
index, the other three ADRs (#346/#347/#348) and the `AGENTS.md` / architecture
doc updates (#349) are deliberately not in this PR.

## The decision

**A listing is not the permanent identity of a dwelling.** The permanent identity
of a place is an `addresses` row at a declared level (`STREET`/`BUILDING`/`UNIT`);
`properties` is a temporary, sourced advertisement pointing at one. Every domain
is assigned to one, the other, or both, in an explicit table.

- `addresses` **evolves** into the place spine — no parallel hierarchy. Justified
  against the alternative, as the issue requires, on the measured fact that
  exactly **5 foreign-key columns in 2 tables** reference `addresses.id`
  (`properties.address_id` and `reviews`' four level columns), that the level
  derivation is already a generated column, and that the spatial and trigram
  indexes the whole search surface stands on live there. What is missing is not a
  table: it is a self-reference, a key that discriminates the level it declares,
  and a CHECK.
- A second `identity_key` is added **beside** `normalized_key`, never overwriting
  it — the schema and the service both record that `normalized_key` was copied
  verbatim by the backfill and must not be recomputed. Collisions are **recorded
  as merge proposals, not merged.** Forward-only, and the ADR says plainly that
  rows already collapsed cannot be split because the database never recorded the
  second flat.
- One dwelling on three portals becomes **three listings, one group, one place**.
  Today's `findDuplicate` returns `status: 'skipped'` and discards portals 2 and
  3; that becomes `'grouped'`.
- Precision becomes a **serializer argument**, and `normalizedKey` — an internal
  dedup hash currently on every public address response — leaves the wire.

## The measurement that drives it

The identity key and the generated `address_level` column **read different
fields**. The key hashes `street|number|unit|building_name|block|postal_code|city_id|country_code`;
the level derives from `floor/unit/subunit` (UNIT) and
`number/building_name/block/entrance` (BUILDING). So `floor`, `entrance` and
`subunit` decide the level and are absent from the key.

Run against a real, freshly migrated PostGIS 17 / 3.5 database (the repo's own
`docker-compose.postgres.yml`, 10 migrations applied by the real `db/migrate.ts`),
calling the real `findOrCreateCanonicalAddress`:

```
floor 3r                 ROW-A level=UNIT floor=3r
floor 4t                 ROW-A level=UNIT floor=3r
no floor (the building)  ROW-A level=UNIT floor=3r
unit 1a                  ROW-B level=UNIT unit=1a
unit 2a                  ROW-C level=UNIT unit=2a
entrance B               ROW-A level=UNIT floor=3r

3r and 4t are the SAME row: true
the building and 3r are the SAME row: true
entrance B and the building are the SAME row: true
unit 1a and unit 2a are DISTINCT rows: true   <- positive control
```

**ROW-A is the building, flat 3r, flat 4t and entrance B at once.** And the
identity is **order-dependent** — same six inputs, building written first:

```
building-first: level=BUILDING
  3r resolved to the same row: true  (level now BUILDING)
```

Which page renders, which aggregate counts a review, and what a review attaches
to therefore depend on which advertisement Homiio ingested first.

It is cheap to fix now and expensive later: **`reviews` was empty in production at
the 2026-08-06 census**, so nothing is misfiled yet. Every review written before
the key change is a row #366 will have to audit.

## Evidence gathered

Against this checkout and a real database, with the commands shown in the ADR:

- migration finished — no live mongoose import, `models/` and `database/` gone,
  no mongo package in any manifest, and the live worker task definition carries
  `DATABASE_URL` and no `MONGODB_URI`
- 61 tables; 16 FK columns into `properties`, 5 into `addresses`
- 4 collision classes over 14 key fixtures, with a passing positive control
- `address_level` generation verified on a real server, including the
  empty-string `floor` → `BUILDING` truthiness case
- the partial unique index permits multiple NULL keys and refuses a duplicate
  (both directions)
- `cities_region_name_key` is **case-sensitive**: `Barcelona` and `barcelona`
  both stored
- the literal `'Unknown'` region fallback collapses two genuinely different
  homonymous cities into one row
- `show_address_number` is enforced in exactly **one** place — the moderation
  subject label — and not in the serializer that publishes the number
- `LISTING_DEDUP_ENABLED` is absent from the live worker task definition, so
  cross-portal dedup is off in production

## Evidence NOT gathered

**Production is unreachable from this machine.** The connection string reads fine
from SSM, but `postgres.internal.oxy.so` has no A record outside the VPC:

```
$ getent hosts postgres.internal.oxy.so
(no A record)
```

So the real-address-shape census the issue requires **has not been run**. No
figure in the ADR is invented: §11.2 writes out twelve exact SQL queries (A1–A10,
R1–R2) to run as a read-only one-shot ECS task, and the acceptance box *"El ADR es
revisado contra datos reales"* is marked **PENDING as of 2026-08-10**. Figures
carried from the 2026-08-06 production census are labelled with their source and
date, including the instruction to re-verify that `reviews` is still empty —
exactly the kind of fact that stops being true quietly.

## Contents

Entity → responsibility → visibility → natural key → public URL table for all 16
entities the issue names; identity fields per level and what may be missing
without creating a duplicate; review hierarchy for write, read and aggregation;
privacy (internal precision may exceed public, with the four cases decided); a
phased, non-destructive compatibility plan whose phase 0 is the census; nine
worked examples plus a tenth fixture, each stating what a **wrong**
implementation produces; a mermaid diagram with cardinalities; the inventory of 7
new and 6 altered tables, the DTO changes, and the `@homiio/shared-types`
changes; deduplication, merge and community-correction rules; and eight explicit
open decisions so no downstream feature invents an answer.

Measured shared-types gap worth calling out: **`AddressLevel` does not exist in
the package at all** — the wire has carried `addressLevel` since the port and no
consumer can type it; `review.ts` re-declares it inline. `AddressDocument`
declares `normalizedKey: string` as required against a nullable column, and that
field is deleted rather than made optional because §6 removes it from the wire.

## Noted, not fixed here

`packages/backend/services/addressService.ts` still says *"`models/Address.ts` and
`geoResolutionService.ts` are deliberately still alive"* and *"ingest is still
Mongo (batch 3)"*. Both are false. The repository's `AGENTS.md` has the same drift
in its own bullet list. That is #349's scope; the ADR flags it in §1.1 so nobody
reads a stale comment as current, and every claim it makes was re-derived from
code and from a running database instead.

Closes #345

author: pratyush-panda-2006
body:
﻿## Description

PaySphere's export service (\ ackend/src/services/export.service.js\) currently spawns an unbounded Node.js \Worker\ thread for every PDF/CSV export request. Under concurrent load during end-of-month payroll processing, this causes CPU thrashing and RAM exhaustion. This PR implements a bounded Worker Thread Pool, task queueing, memory recycling, and pre-signed S3 upload streaming.

**Fix / Implementation:**
1. **WorkerThreadPool Class**: Implemented \WorkerThreadPool\ in \ ackend/src/services/export.service.js\ capped at system CPU core limits (\os.cpus().length - 1\).
2. **Task Queueing**: Queues incoming export tasks in FIFO order when worker concurrency capacity is saturated.
3. **S3 Upload Streaming**: Added \uploadToS3(filename, content, mimeType)\ method providing pre-signed download URLs with expiration TTLs to avoid returning heavy binary buffers over Node process memory.
4. **Unit Tests**: Added unit tests in \ ackend/src/services/__tests__/export.service.test.js\ verifying pool limits and task queueing.

author: eltovar
body:
## El problema

El liderazgo del scheduler se decidia con un **unico** `SET NX` al arrancar, y `shutdown_event()` paraba el scheduler pero **nunca liberaba el lock**.

En un redeploy: el worker viejo muere, su lock sobrevive hasta 300s, el worker nuevo arranca dentro de esa ventana, lo encuentra ocupado y **se queda sin scheduler de forma permanente** — no hay reintento.

Ninguno de los 13 jobs corre: `rescue_stalled_leads`, `reconcile_owner_ids`, `memory_watchdog`, `scheduled_messages`, `apt_reminders`, `followup_24h`… Y el deploy reporta **SUCCESS**. Nada avisa.

### Ocurrido en produccion el 10-ago-2026

```
02:00:48  deploy toma el lock          (TTL 300s -> expira 02:05:48)
02:04:52  deploy entra 56s antes       -> omite scheduler
02:09:20  primer redeploy, aun ocupado -> omite scheduler
02:15:13  segundo redeploy             -> LEADER (recuperado)
```

Dos redeploys y ~10 minutos sin ningun job de fondo.

## Los cambios

| # | Pieza | Que resuelve |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Ceder el lock en el shutdown** | El arreglo principal: cubre el 100% de los casos vistos (redeploys con SIGTERM). El relevo es inmediato |
| 2 | **Reintentos al adquirir** (3 x 2s) | Railway levanta el worker nuevo antes de matar el viejo; el lock puede seguir ocupado unos segundos durante el rollover |
| 3 | **Heartbeat cada 120s** | Sin renovacion el lock caduca a los 300s **aunque el worker siga sano**, y otro podria levantar un SEGUNDO scheduler: recordatorios y followups duplicados. No habia explotado todavia |

**Borrado condicional via Lua.** Un `DEL` a secas podria borrar el lock que otro worker acaba de tomar tras expirar el nuestro, dejando dos schedulers activos. El script solo borra si el valor sigue siendo nuestro PID.

**El log de fallo pasa de INFO a WARNING** y dice cuantos intentos se hicieron. El modo de fallo era silencioso y eso fue justo lo que costo el diagnostico.

## Test plan

- [x] **11 tests** (`tests/test_scheduler_leader_lock.py`) con un doble de Redis que replica la semantica de `SET NX` / `EX` / `EVAL`
- [x] **Comportamiento, no solo estructura**: el heartbeat renueva el TTL de verdad; la liberacion borra el lock propio; **no** borra el ajeno; la adquisicion tiene exito al 3er intento tras encontrarlo ocupado
- [x] **Validacion por mutacion**: 6 de 6 guardas estructurales detectan el codigo pre-fix (incluido T7, que se afino para identificar el `set()` del lock por su clave — la primera version daba falso positivo porque `startup_event` tiene otros `.set()` dentro de bucles)
- [x] PRs anteriores intactos: failsafe 11/11, rescate 14/14, ordering 5/5, ownership 13/13, memory-leak 11/11
- [x] **Baseline sin cambios**: 32 panel, 7 middleware — identico antes y despues
- [x] **Ruff F,E9**: 5 hallazgos antes, 5 despues, **ninguno** en el codigo nuevo

## Riesgo

| Riesgo | Nivel | Mitigacion |
|---|---|---|
| Dos schedulers si la liberacion falla | **Muy bajo** | El borrado es condicional; ante fallo de Redis se conserva el TTL como red de seguridad |
| Startup mas lento | **Bajo** | Solo si el lock esta ocupado: +4s como maximo (2 esperas de 2s). En el camino normal, cero |
| Un job mas en el scheduler | **Muy bajo** | El heartbeat es un `SET` cada 120s; se registra solo si hay lock real |
| Fallo del heartbeat | **Bajo** | Non-fatal y quedan ~2 ciclos de margen antes de que el TTL expire |
| Perder liderazgo en un corte de Redis | **Bajo** | El heartbeat re-escribe el valor, asi que recupera el puesto en vez de dejarlo vacante |

**Alteracion esperada:** ninguna en el comportamiento normal. Con el lock libre, el camino es identico al actual salvo un `SET` extra cada 120s.

## Notas para el reviewer

- `/tests/` esta en `.gitignore`, el archivo de test no viaja en el PR
- El fallback sin Redis (`_is_scheduler_leader = True`) deja `_scheduler_lock_held = False` a proposito: corre los jobs pero no reclama un lock que no tiene, asi que el shutdown no intenta liberar nada inexistente
- La liberacion va **despues** de `scheduler.shutdown()` para que el heartbeat no reescriba el lock justo despues de borrarlo

Grain: MED/notebook-dotnet — lane myia-po-2024:CoursIA — prev: MED/notebook-python #10266

#9434 precision-drain : retirer les timings machine-dépendants de la prose d'interprétation de **Sudoku-1-Backtracking-Csharp**. **Work-type distinct** des enrichissements précédents (drain de précision #9434, pas insertion de transitions) + famille fraîche (Sudoku) + rotation de genre (python→dotnet).

## La dérive mesurée firsthand

La cellule d'interprétation `[11]` portait une **table markdown restatant des temps d'horloge précis** (`0,4354` / `141,0824` / `4 127,7309` ms) ainsi que des claims en prose (« moins d'une demi-millisecond », « Plus de 4 secondes », « 29 fois plus de temps »). Or ces timings **dérivent d'une machine à l'autre** (charge CPU, JIT, fréquence) — c'est exactement la classe de dérive que #9434 veut tenue par l'exécution, pas par la prose.

Le détecteur `check_machine_dep_timing.py` flaggait `cell[11]` (« 4 secondes », wallclock).

## Principe appliqué : drainer le machine-dépendant, garder le déterministe

Le notebook produit **deux** sortes de quantités :

| Quantité | Exemple | Machine-dépendant ? | Décision |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Appels récursifs** | 122 / 490 304 / 12 625 368 | **Non** (combinatoire exacte, reproductible) | **GARDÉ** dans la prose |
| **Facteur d'augmentation** | 4 019x / 103 489x | **Non** (ratio de comptes) | **GARDÉ** |
| **Temps d'horloge (ms)** | 0,4354 / 141,0824 / 4 127,7309 | **Oui** (wallclock) | **DRAINÉ** de la prose |

Les temps d'horloge **restent dans l'output de code** (`Temps de résolution: X ms`) — c'est la **mesure vivante**, et une sortie DOIT porter la valeur réelle mesurée (`secrets-hygiene.md` règle 6 : maquiller une sortie est banni). Seule la **prose qui restate** ces timings est drainée : elle devient qualitative et s'appuie sur les comptes déterministes.

## Changements (cell[11] markdown, 4 points de drain)

1. **Table** : colonne `Temps (ms)` retirée (3 colonnes désormais : Difficulté / Appels récursifs / Facteur d'augmentation — tous déterministes).
2. **Point 2** « moins d'une demi-millisecond » → « quasi instantané (122 appels seulement) » (ancre sur le compte déterministe).
3. **Point 3** « Plus de 4 secondes » → « Plus de 12 millions d'appels » (ancre sur le compte).
4. **Note technique** « prend 29 fois plus de temps » → surcoût temporel qualitatif (« non mesuré ici, machine-dépendant… seuls les comptes d'appels sont reproductibles »).

## G.1 — preuve du livrable

- **Markdown-only** : 0 cellule code touchée, 0 output modifié (vérifié : 0 ligne `execution_count` changée, les timings **restent** dans l'output code). Exception C.2 (modifs uniquement markdown) → **0 re-exécution due**.
- Raw-text replace (pas de json round-trip) → 0 churn sur les 18 autres cellules. LF préservé (0 CRLF des deux côtés). JSON valide, H.3 0 violation.
- **Déterministe préservé** : tous les comptes (122 / 490 304 / 12 625 368), ratios (4 019x / 103 489x / « 25 fois plus d'appels »), et claims qualitatifs (« coû t en temps varie énormément ») intacts. Le message pédagogique (complexité exponentielle) est porté par les comptes, pas par les ms.

## Contrôle positif #10158 respecté

Sudoku-13-SymbolicAutomata (contrôle positif du détecteur, wallclock=29) **non touché** — il reste détecté, prouvant que le détecteur fonctionne. Je draine un notebook distinct (Sudoku-1), pas la référence.

## Twin parity — rebaseline (commit 2)

Sudoku-1 est un twin (`sudoku-1-backtracking.yaml`). Le drain markdown déplace le `content_csharp_sha` → DRIFT. Rebaseline via `check_twin_parity.py --update --pair "Sudoku-1 Backtracking" --by "myia-po-2024:CoursIA"` APRÈS le commit contenu. Registry nested 4-space → --update clean ; date 2026-08-10 unique → pas de latest-tiebreak.

## Scope (un sujet par PR)

Une PR = un notebook, drain #9434 de la prose d'interprétation. Ne touche PAS : le code, les outputs, le contrôle positif Sudoku-13, le catalogue (byte-identique à main), les notebooks frères.

prev = MED/notebook-python #10266 (c.81, GenAI test-time scaling). Ce grain = MED/notebook-dotnet sur **Sudoku** (backtracking). **Work-type distinct** : drain de précision #9434 (pas enrichissement de transitions). G-VAR-3 OK (genre python→dotnet, pas 2 consécutifs same-genre). G-VAR-1 OK (MED + CONTENU). Substance distincte non scan-générable (jugement déterministe vs machine-dépendant, ancrage aux comptes).

author: gui-fernandesbr
body:
Closes #953.

## Why

Free-form fin sets were the only aerodynamic surface without a stochastic counterpart, so a rocket using them could not be varied in a Monte Carlo run.

## What

### `StochasticFreeFormFins` (`ENH`)

`shape_points` does not fit the one-number-per-input assumption `StochasticModel` makes, and a fin shape is only meaningful as a complete set of points. So the outline is randomized **as a block**: one sampled deviation applied to every coordinate of every point.

Two formats needed handling before reaching the base class, both of them the natural thing for a user to write:

- **a bare outline** `[(0, 0), (0.08, 0.1), (0.12, 0)]` is a `list`, which the base class reads as a list of candidate values and would have sampled a *single `(x, y)` point* from. It is wrapped as the one candidate outline it is, so a list of outlines still means a choice between shapes.
- **`(nominal outline, standard deviation)`** has a list where `_validate_tuple` requires a number. Only that first item is special-cased; the deviation and the distribution name still go through the base class, so they are checked the same way as everywhere else and the distribution is drawn from this model's generator.

All six formats are accepted:

```python
StochasticFreeFormFins(fins, shape_points=0.001)                    # std on every coordinate
StochasticFreeFormFins(fins, shape_points=(0.001, "uniform"))       # std + distribution
StochasticFreeFormFins(fins, shape_points=(outline, 0.001))         # nominal + std
StochasticFreeFormFins(fins, shape_points=(outline, 0.001, "wald")) # nominal + std + distribution
StochasticFreeFormFins(fins, shape_points=outline)                  # one fixed outline
StochasticFreeFormFins(fins, shape_points=[outline_a, outline_b])   # choose between shapes
```

An outline that cannot mean a fin shape — empty, ragged, fewer than three points, three-dimensional — now fails during validation rather than reaching `FreeFormFins`.

Also adds `StochasticRocket.add_free_form_fins`, the `rocketpy` / `rocketpy.stochastic` exports, the API reference page, and a note in the stochastic usage docs about `shape_points` being the one argument randomized as a block.

### Deterministic surfaces were never accepted (`BUG`)

Found while wiring the above, kept as its own commit so it can be reviewed or reverted independently.

`_add_surfaces` wrapped a plain surface with `stochastic_type(component=...)`, but none of the stochastic aero-surface classes take a `component` keyword — each names its first parameter after its own surface (`nosecone`, `tail`, `trapezoidal_fins`, ...). Passing anything other than an already-stochastic surface to `add_nose`, `add_trapezoidal_fins`, `add_elliptical_fins` or `add_tail` therefore raised a `TypeError`, even though all four document the deterministic type as accepted:

```
TypeError: StochasticTrapezoidalFins.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'component'
```

Passed positionally instead, which reaches every class regardless of what it calls that parameter.

## Tests

24 new tests: the six accepted formats, nine invalid inputs, choice between outlines, the nominal outline surviving when nothing is randomized, and `StochasticRocket` integration. Plus an integration test that runs a real 2-simulation Monte Carlo and asserts the perturbed `shape_points` survives JSON serialization as an outline rather than as a single point.

The regression test for the `component=` bug fails with the `TypeError` above without the fix.

Locally: 1926 unit + 153 integration passing, plus the 5 slow Monte Carlo tests. `ruff check`, `ruff format` and `pylint` clean (10.00/10).

author: nishantsoni7
body:
Six phases of payroll work, in seven commits. The first fixes a defect that overcharges employees; the rest build on it.

## The defect this starts from

A working day with exactly one punch was handled two different wrong ways depending on the fingerprint export format, and both cost the employee money.

- **Format A** dropped OUT-only days entirely, so payroll charged a **full-day absence** for a day the employee was present.
- **Format B** filed every lone punch as `check_in_at` whatever the clock said. A departure punched at 18:36 became an **arrival at 18:36**: a 2-hour missing-punch charge plus roughly nine hours of "lateness" — about ₹896 on a ₹26,000 salary, **more than the day was worth**.

## Commits

| SHA | Phase |
|---|---|
| `8bdded1` | Classify and persist single-punch direction |
| `15c111d` | Versioned calculation settings |
| `4bd5594` | Period snapshots, admin settings API and page |
| `e598829` | Whole-rupee salary calculation |
| `fda7307` | Adjustment categories |
| `083d8ac` | Salary-processing report and sharing |
| `0ec17ad` | Documentation |

## What changed

**Single punch.** The XLS parser, previously duplicated across the attendance import and preview routes, is now one module both call. Format A reads the machine's IN/OUT marker (`confirmed`); Format B classifies a lone punch with a 14:00 IST divider (`inferred`). The engine stacks a late-arrival line on a missing punch-out **only when the direction is `confirmed`** — charging lateness on a guessed direction is charging an employee for a guess. Legacy `NULL` resolves to `inferred`, the reading that cannot over-charge.

**Central Payroll Settings.** Every shared constant is now an admin-editable setting. `DEFAULT_PAYROLL_SETTINGS` is built *from* the old constants rather than retyped, so the move is provably behaviour-neutral — all 2,664 pre-existing tests still pass. Storage is append-only, so the audit trail is the table's shape rather than a second table.

**The snapshot.** Each period pins the settings it was calculated with, **before the first employee is calculated**. A generated period with no snapshot resolves to the documented legacy constants, **never to today's settings** — the convenient fallback would silently restate every pre-feature payslip on the first settings edit. Regeneration keeps its pin; only an explicit `recalculate_with_current_settings` replaces it, so an attendance correction cannot smuggle in a rule change.

**Whole rupees.** Each monetary line is rounded as it is built, and every total is the sum of those rounded lines. The order is the rule: `round(a) + round(b)` ≠ `round(a + b)`, and only the first gives a payslip whose printed lines add up to its printed total. Rounding is half-up *away from zero* — `Math.round(-10.5)` is `-10`, which would make a deduction and a recovery of the same size round to different magnitudes.

**Adjustment categories.** The existing model was inspected first and genuinely cannot express them: five of the seven categories are all `addition`, separated today only by free-text description. One nullable column, one CHECK pairing category with direction.

**Processing report.** Admin-only, per period, with selection, preview, copy and WhatsApp. Every figure comes from stored `payroll_results` — the page never calculates a salary.

## Migrations — already applied to production

Applied and verified **before** this PR, because merging deploys:

| Migration | Adds |
|---|---|
| `20260827000000` | `attendance_records.punch_direction_source` |
| `20260828000000` | `payroll_settings`, `payroll_periods.settings_snapshot` |
| `20260829000000` | `payroll_pending_adjustments.adjustment_category` |

`supabase migration list --linked` reports **0 pending, 0 remote-only**. Each new column and table was then probed read-only through PostgREST and returned rows.

**Why the order is not optional:** the new code names these columns in its select lists, and PostgREST answers an unknown column with error `42703` rather than a null — so app-first does not degrade, it breaks payroll generation, Monthly Review, attendance import and preview outright.

All three are purely additive: nullable columns with **no defaults** (no table rewrite), guarded statements (safe to re-run), **no backfill**, and no change to any existing RLS policy or grant. The only DML is a seed row into the table its own migration creates, guarded by `WHERE NOT EXISTS`.

## Privacy and authorization

- `payroll_settings` is admin-only in full: RLS on, one admin SELECT and one admin INSERT policy, **no employee policy at all**, no UPDATE/DELETE policy for anybody, plus a trigger refusing both even for the service role.
- `GET /api/payroll/salary-report` is `requireAdmin`-only and takes **no `employee_id` input** — the only parameter is `period_id`, so there is nothing for a non-admin to aim at.
- The report deliberately does not select the adjustment `description` (admins write private context there) or `monthly_salary`. No punches, objections, comments, correction remarks or settings are read.
- Adjustments belonging to excluded employees are filtered out of the **response**, not merely the render.
- Deleted and payroll-excluded employees go through the shared `participatesInPayroll` predicate, so the report and real generation cannot disagree.

## Historical stability

No existing payroll is recalculated, unlocked, backfilled or modified. Settlement deliberately does **not** round on read: a month generated before the whole-rupee rule keeps its stored figures, paise and all, because its stored deduction lines are fractional too and rounding the total would stop it matching the column above it.

## Verification

- **2,870 tests / 599 suites / 0 fail** (`npx tsx --test "src/**/*.test.ts" "src/**/*.test.tsx"`)
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — exit 0
- ESLint without `--fix` on every changed file — exit 0
- `next build` — compiles successfully, with `/payroll/settings`, `/payroll/results/[periodId]/salary-report`, `/api/payroll/settings` and `/api/payroll/salary-report` all present
- `git diff --check` — clean

Eight existing test files had expectations updated from full-precision amounts to values derived through `roundRupees`, and one engine-call assertion from six arguments to seven. Each now asserts the rule rather than one salary's answer, and the tolerance comparisons became exact equality.

## Rollback

Each migration carries its own rollback in its header comment. All three are lossless for payroll: with the columns gone, every day reads as `inferred`, every period resolves to the legacy constants, and the report falls back to its Other lines — which is the behaviour that preceded this work. Reverting the application commits alone is also safe: old code does not select the new columns, and `NULL` satisfies every constraint.

## Known limitation

A **confirmed** Format A 19:00 arrival with a missing punch-out still costs about 11 hours, exceeding a full day. That figure is stated by the file rather than guessed, so it is not the defect fixed here — a per-day cap is a reasonable future setting.

Reviewed the project against Awana Clubs International's published Trademark Guidelines and renamed the shipped product from "Awana Label Printer" to **"Club Label Printer"** — their guidelines say they don't grant permission to create products bearing their name.

## What changed
- Every user-visible string: Electron window titles, tray tooltip/menu, error dialogs, the installer artifact (`Club-Label-Printer-Setup.exe`), the browser-extension widget ("Club Print"), the print-server dashboard/phone/bookmarklet pages, the website, and the docs.

- `electron-app/package.json`'s `"name"`/`"appId"` (`awana-label-printer`) — electron-builder derives the install directory and `userData` path from `"name"`, not `productName` (confirmed in `build-electron.yml`'s own CI comment). Renaming it would orphan every existing install's config/roster.

## 🎯 What is this PR?

백엔드 전체에서 발생하는 예외를 공통 `ApiResponse` 형식으로 처리할 수 있도록 
공통 예외 처리 구조를 추가했습니다.

제품, 각인, 마이페이지 및 게임 API에서 동일한 오류 응답 구조를 사용할 수 있습니다.

## ✨ Changes

- HTTP 상태와 기본 메시지를 관리하는 `ErrorCode` 추가
  - 400 잘못된 요청
  - 404 데이터 미존재
  - 500 서버 내부 오류
- 예상 가능한 오류를 표현하는 `BusinessException` 추가
- `GlobalExceptionHandler`를 통한 전역 예외 처리
  - 비즈니스 예외
  - 요청값 검증 실패
  - 잘못된 JSON 요청
  - 예상하지 못한 서버 오류
- 공통 오류 응답 테스트 추가
- 클래스와 메서드의 역할을 설명하는 주석 추가

## 📷 Result

- `.\gradlew.bat test` 성공
- 400·404·500 오류 응답 테스트 통과
- 기존 테스트를 포함한 전체 테스트 통과

## 💬 To Reviewer

백엔드 전체에서 공통으로 사용할 예외 처리 구조를 구성했습니다.

이번 PR에는 개별 기능 API가 포함되지 않았습니다.  
향후 제품·각인·마이페이지 및 **A파트 기능에서 예상 가능한 오류가 발생하면, `BusinessException`과 `ErrorCode`를 사용해 주세요.**

발생한 예외는 `GlobalExceptionHandler`가 공통 `ApiResponse` 형식으로 변환합니다.

예상하지 못한 서버 오류는 내부 상세 내용을 클라이언트에 노출하지 않고 공통 500 메시지만 반환하도록 처리했습니다.

앞서 작성한 공통 API 응답 PR이 아직 리뷰 대기 중이어서, `dev`에 병합하지 못했습니다.  
따라서 `chore/api-foundation` 브랜치에서 이어서 작업했습니다.

**`chore/api-foundation → dev` PR을 먼저 병합**한 후 **, 이 PR을 `dev`에 병합할 예정**입니다.

author: texasdaddy
body:
Follow-up to #13, driven by keystone#15 (auth throttling), which is shipping in `v0.1.0-rc.6`.

Keystone's auth surface is now rate-limited **per account AND per source IP**. Behind a reverse proxy the socket peer is the **proxy**, so unless the proxy is named:

- every visitor shares **one** per-IP bucket — a couple of dozen failed logins from anyone would 429 the whole login surface, which is an attacker-triggerable outage; and
- every `auth_events` / `user_sessions` row records the proxy's address instead of the caller's.

`X-Forwarded-For` is believed **only** from a listed peer (the app then walks the chain right-to-left to the first non-proxy hop). The default is blank, so the header is ignored entirely unless an operator opts in — neutral, and the correct setting for a directly-exposed container, since the header is otherwise caller-supplied and would let an attacker mint a fresh bucket per request.

`Display="advanced"`, `Required="false"`, empty default — no operator host, IP, or subnet is baked into the template.

author: etacassiopeia
body:
The fleet request journal drew seven columns and could fill four. **Node, status and latency rendered a pending marker on every row**, because nothing recorded them. All three are real now.

Bumps `vendor/rift` to `6f3a67c` ([rift#940](https://github.com/achird-labs/rift/pull/940)), the upstream half, which added the fields and the `attach_response` hook this implements.

## The node is stamped by the writer

Upstream carries `node` but never sets it — single-node Rift has one node and no name for it. `ClusterJournal::record_indexed` is the layer that knows, so it stamps its own id there, and **it is the same identity the entry is keyed by**. A merged read therefore cannot show a row whose `node` disagrees with the shard it came from.

Deliberately *not* inferred at merge time from whichever shard an entry was found in: that would re-derive a fact rather than report one, and the two would part company the moment an entry moved between shards.

## Status and latency attach after the response

`attach_response` mirrors `attach_match` exactly — same binary search over a deque held in ascending seq order, and the same `debug_assert!` of that invariant, because a violation would not fail loudly: it would annotate the **wrong entry**. An entry evicted or cleared between the record and the response is a no-op rather than an error, on the same principle — a diagnostic annotation must never be able to fail a request.

## Absent is not zero

All three render `—` when the engine did not record them. `status` and `latencyMs` attach only once a response exists, so the `X-Rift-Debug` path and a request journalled before an error legitimately carry neither. A `0 ms` there would report an instant answer nobody observed.

A **present** `0 ms` is a reading, and renders as one — a stub answered from memory is sub-millisecond, and blanking it would hide that the mock was fast rather than unmeasured. There is a test for each case, because they look identical in a screenshot and mean opposite things.

The status code reuses the shared `Status`, which encodes in glyph and value as well as hue. 2xx against 5xx is the pair in this table an operator most needs to tell apart, and green↔red measures 5.8–7.2 ΔE under protanopia and deuteranopia — so it must not rely on colour.

## A note on the tests, because one of them was worthless

The first draft of the console test asserted `row.textContent).toContain("3")` for the node id. **It passed with the node cell hard-coded to a dash** — because `"503"` in the status cell also contains a `"3"`. A row-wide `toContain` on a short value is an assertion that cannot fail for the reason it claims to test.

The assertions are per cell by testid now, and I re-ran the same mutation to confirm the test *does* fail when the cell is broken. Worth knowing if you review the diff: the testids on those three cells exist for that reason, not decoration.

## Verification

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo fmt` | clean |
| `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` | **exit 0** |
| `cargo test --workspace` | **41 suites, 1177 passed, 0 failed** |
| `pnpm typecheck` / `pnpm lint` | clean |
| `pnpm test` | **899 passed** (3 new) |

`web/src/api/schema.ts` is regenerated from the OpenAPI change.

Local repro note: the cluster-spawning suites need `ulimit -n` raised (8192 suffices). Below that they fail `Too many open files (os error 24)`, surfacing as misleading errors like ``` `git --version` could not be run ``` — deterministic, not flaky.

## Scope

The per-imposter request log is unchanged — it has a different column set that predates the design's seven-column fleet journal, and widening it is not what #364 asks for.

Closes #364

author: suchethac
body:
Refs #1645. The two **mechanical** halves of that issue — detection and recording. Prevention (coupling the redshift and SFH-age draws) is a design decision about what the mock population *is*, and is deliberately left open.

`make_population` samples redshift and the SFH age parameters independently, so a mock can request an SFH that does not fit inside cosmic time at its own redshift. The excess is truncated and the prediction stops representing the requested SFH. On the ESS sweep's own fixed-key population, **all four galaxies truncate — 2.7%, 5.4%, 8.7% and 69.2%** — and nothing downstream could tell.

## 1. The warning carries the exact fraction

The raise site computed `frac_pre_bb` and then threw it away:

```python
frac_pre_bb = mass_pre_bb / max(mass_total_sfh, 1e-30)
if frac_pre_bb > 0.01:
    warnings.warn(f"...forms {frac_pre_bb:.0%}...")   # rounded to whole percent
```

So "69%" is anything in 0.685–0.695, and recovering it meant regex-parsing prose that breaks the moment the sentence is reworded. It is now raised as an instance with `truncated_fraction` attached — exact.

## 2. `MockPopulation.truncated_fraction` records it per galaxy

Following the `n_halpha_absorption` precedent already in that class — *"Never dropped; reported to avoid selection bias."* Same policy: measure, report, never silently drop. A caller can exclude or flag affected galaxies instead of reading stderr.

## 3. `max_truncated_fraction` is opt-in, default `None`

**Off by default deliberately.** The fixtures this repository ships contain such galaxies — the four-galaxy sweep mock truncates 69% on one — so a default limit would reject the project's own populations rather than fix them. That would be a breaking change wearing a mechanical disguise.

## The bug my own unit tests did not catch

The capture wraps **both** prediction calls, not just the first. `predict_photometry` runs the traced path, where this check is deliberately skipped; the warning comes from the **eager** path, which here is `measure_line_fluxes(fast=False)`.

Wrapping only the photometry call recorded `0.0` for every galaxy while the warnings still reached stderr. The unit tests passed and the wiring was wrong — only the end-to-end check surfaced it.

Captured warnings are re-emitted, so a caller watching stderr today sees exactly what they see now. Capturing is for measurement, not suppression.

## Also: per-galaxy ESS in the sweep

`ess.at_mode` is already shape `(N,)` and was reduced to three order statistics before writing. That made the minimum unattributable: at width 0.5 the population showed `min=57.4` against `median=max=125.0` — exactly one galaxy degraded — while exactly one galaxy truncates 69%. Testing whether those are the same galaxy needed the vector that was already computed and discarded.

## Verification

End-to-end, not just unit:

| check | result |
|---|---|
| recorded fractions | `[0.0268, 0.0535, 0.6917, 0.0873]` |
| vs warning payloads | identical values |
| warnings still visible to caller | 4 (unchanged) |
| `max_truncated_fraction=0.5` | raises, naming 1 of 4 |
| default | accepts, records |

Plus 42 passing across the new tests and the population contract/regression suites; `ruff check src/ tests/` clean; taxonomy markers clean.

## Caveat recorded in the docstring

The raise site's own threshold is `frac_pre_bb > 0.01`, so a recorded `0.0` means **"at most 1%", not "none"**.

body:
## Claim

After this candidate is accepted, the `clippy::collapsible_if` lint violations in `perl-dap`, `perl-symbol`, `perl-module`, and `perl-lsp-perltidy` are fully eliminated; the `policy/clippy-debt.toml` tracking comment reflects the reduced scope.

## Controlling issue

Closes #6359 (perl-dap: 18 collapsible_if findings across 13 files)
Relates to #6305 (parent burndown — collapsible_if debt)
Additional fixes in `perl-symbol`, `perl-module`, `perl-lsp-perltidy` are part of the #6305 burndown but not tracked by a separate child issue.

## Governing contract

`policy/clippy-debt.toml` — the `collapsible_if` debt entry lists affected crates and tracks which are clean. This PR updates that list to remove the crates now proven clean.

## Changed production path

No production path change. All edits are pure control-flow restructuring: nested `if A { if B { … } }` blocks are collapsed to `if A && B { … }` using stable Rust let-chain syntax (stabilized in 1.79; workspace MSRV is 1.95). The compiled output is identical — same branches, same conditions, same bodies.

## Proof

```bash
# Zero collapsible_if violations in perl-dap lib (the issue's stated proof):
cargo clippy --lib -p perl-dap --locked -- -D clippy::collapsible_if -A clippy::all
# → Finished, zero errors

# Zero violations in related crates:
cargo clippy --lib -p perl-symbol    --locked -- -D clippy::collapsible_if -A clippy::all  # clean
cargo clippy --lib -p perl-module    --locked -- -D clippy::collapsible_if -A clippy::all  # clean
cargo clippy --lib -p perl-lsp-perltidy --locked -- -D clippy::collapsible_if -A clippy::all  # clean

# Tests green across all changed crates:

body:
This PR establishes the V1 baseline for a composable tag-based book discovery app (author + genre filters stacked together, live narrowing), with AI-assisted discovery explicitly deferred. It also documents the intended backend/frontend/data architecture and initial Postgres schema shape.

- **Product brief and scope (`README.md`)**
  - Replaced placeholder README with the full V1 definition:
    - status, stack, and deployment targets
    - non-goals for V1 (no auth, no runtime external API dependency)
    - composable tag-search feature scope
    - local setup/runtime instructions
    - roadmap and project layout

- **Database schema reference (`docs/schema.md`)**
  - Added draft schema documentation for:
    - core tables: `books`, `authors`, `tags`
    - join tables: `book_authors`, `book_tags`
    - relationship model and query intent for composable/intersection filtering

- **Repository scaffold alignment**
  - Added minimal directory/file scaffold to match documented structure:
    - `backend/requirements.txt` (FastAPI/uvicorn baseline)
    - `frontend/.gitkeep`
    - `data/.gitkeep`

Example schema excerpt introduced in docs:

```md
### `book_tags`
- `book_id` (UUID, FK -> `books.id`, NOT NULL)
- `tag_id` (UUID, FK -> `tags.id`, NOT NULL)
- Primary key: (`book_id`, `tag_id`)
```

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> # Find Your Next Book, Your Way
> 
> A composable, tag-based book discovery app. Search by author and genre at the same time, stacked as tags, with results narrowing live — no more choosing author *or* genre *or* title like Goodreads and library catalogs force you to.
> 
> ## Status
> 
> 🚧 V1 in progress. Core tag search first; AI-assisted discovery page deferred until built in-house (see [Roadmap](#roadmap)).
> 
> ## Tech Stack
> 
> - **Backend:** FastAPI (Python)
> - **Database:** Postgres, hosted on [Neon](https://neon.tech)
> - **Frontend:** React
> - **Hosting:** Vercel (frontend) + Render (backend)
> - **Data source:** Curated dataset from Google Books API / Open Library API (no live-API calls at demo/runtime — avoids rate limits and uptime risk)
> 
> No authentication in V1 — no user accounts or saved data yet, so there's nothing to protect.
> 
> ## Features (V1 Scope)
> 
> - [ ] Curated book/author/genre dataset loaded into Postgres
> - [ ] Composable tag search: type → live suggestions → click to tag → results narrow instantly
> - [ ] Stack multiple tags in any order (author + genre together)
> - [ ] Browse-first option: see unfiltered results, add tags whenever
> 
> ## Getting Started
> 
> ### Prerequisites
> - Python 3.11+
> - Node.js 18+
> - A free [Neon](https://neon.tech) Postgres database
> 
> ### Setup
> ```bash
> # clone the repo
> git clone <your-repo-url>
> cd <repo-name>
> 
> # backend
> cd backend
> python -m venv venv
> source venv/bin/activate
> pip install -r requirements.txt
> 
> # frontend
> cd ../frontend
> npm install
> ```
> 
> ### Environment Variables
> Create a `.env` file in `backend/` with:
> ```
> DATABASE_URL=<your-neon-connection-string>
> ```
> 
> ### Running locally
> ```bash
> # backend (from backend/)
> uvicorn main:app --reload
> 
> # frontend (from frontend/)
> npm run dev
> ```
> 
> ## Project Structure
> ```
> .
> ├── backend/          # FastAPI app, Postgres models, routes
> ├── frontend/          # React app
> ├── data/               # scripts for pulling/loading curated dataset
> ├── docs/
> │   └── schema.md       # database schema reference
> └── README.md
> ```
> 
> ## Database Schema
> 
> See [`docs/schema.md`](./docs/schema.md) for full table definitions and relationships (`books`, `authors`, `tags`, and their join tables).
> 
> ## Roadmap
> 
> - **V1:** Tag search only, no AI, no auth
> - **Later:** "Not Sure What to Read?" AI-assisted page — built in-house once NLP coursework supports it, not as a wrapped LLM API call
> - **Later:** Own tag-based recommendation model (content-based / collaborative filtering)
> - **Later:** User accounts, if saved books/personalization is added
> 
> ## License
> 
> TBD


</details>

author: hyeonjoong
body:
## Problem

`paper/paper.md` states that *"the validation script, the audio manifest, and the
raw per-track parameter matrix are released alongside the paper."* None of them
were actually in the repository — only the prose in `docs/validation.md`. As
written the paper made a reproducibility promise the repo did not keep, which is
exactly the kind of claim a JOSS reviewer checks.

## Changes

```
validation/
├── README.md                     benchmark description, provenance, licensing, limitations
├── run_validation.py             manifest + audio  -> parameter matrix
├── analyze_results.py            parameter matrix  -> statistics + figure
└── data/
    ├── audio_manifest.csv        60 tracks: IDs, durations, source IDs
    ├── parameters_60tracks.csv   raw analyze_audio() output per track
    ├── summary_statistics.csv    medians, Cliff's δ, Mann–Whitney p
    └── run_metadata.json         category counts + timing (2026-05-27 run)
```

Both scripts were cleaned up before publication: paths are CLI arguments instead
of hard-coded `/Users/...` absolutes, they import the installed package rather
than a local clone, and the figure jitter is seeded so the plot is reproducible.

`analyze_results.py` also computes the **Benjamini–Hochberg q-values the paper
reports** — the original internal script only produced raw *p*-values, so that
particular claim was previously not reproducible from any released code.

## Verification

Running `python validation/analyze_results.py` on the published matrix
reproduces the paper's numbers:

- 3/12 parameters at uncorrected *p* < 0.05 ✔
- smallest BH *q* = **0.189** (paper: "smallest *q* = .19") ✔
- 58/60 tracks complete on all twelve parameters; `hnr_db` undefined for
  `C017`/`C020` ✔ (paper: "58 of 60 … two HNR values undefined")

One discrepancy surfaced and is **not** fixed here — it belongs in a paper edit:
the paper says C separates from *both* A and B with |δ| ≥ 0.7 on **eight**
parameters, but crest factor is δ = +0.68 against B, just under the threshold, so
the correct count is **seven**. Tracked separately.

## Audio

Not redistributed — DEAM and FMA carry their own terms and the BELL-001 stimuli
are proprietary clinical-trial material. `README.md` documents where each source
comes from, so the analysis stays checkable even though the audio is not open.

Test suite unaffected: 56 passed.

author: davemoudy
body:
Documentation and project process only — no functional change.

Opening Portwood to community development surfaced several docs that were telling a new contributor the wrong thing.

## The thing that most blocked contribution

`CONTRIBUTING.md` told people to run **`scripts/e2e-test.apex`, which does not exist**, and to expect `PASS: 23` from it. It never mentioned `npm run qa` — the 12-suite harness with an offline mode, report generation and a real exit code. A first-time contributor's very first command failed while the good tooling stayed invisible.

Now: `npm install` → `npm run org:new` → `npm run qa`, with `npm run qa -- --offline` called out as the path for someone without an org.

Its architecture table was also wrong: it named `docGenPdfMerger` and `docGenZipWriter` as components, but both are *modules inside* the `docGenRunner` and `docGenAdmin` bundles — and `docGenCanvas`, the flagship, was missing entirely.

## New: `.claude/skills/`

Seven skills packaging the knowledge that isn't visible from the code. They load automatically under Claude Code and read as plain Markdown otherwise.

| Skill | Covers |
|---|---|
| `dev-setup` | Fresh clone → working, tested org |
| `run-tests` | QA harness, e2e scripts, prettier, Code Analyzer |
| `triage-report` | Is a report a real defect or a template issue? |
| `fix-merge-tag` | The resolution paths, and how not to half-fix one |
| `html-template-authoring` | CSS 2.1 constraints, charts, fonts, images |
| `canvas-designer` | Artboard, serializer, importer |
| `managed-package-rules` | `global` visibility, Flow Apex-Defined types, namespace traps |

`.gitignore` already whitelisted `.claude/skills/`, so this ships as intended.

## Corrected: chart guidance was backwards

`CLAUDE.md` said to steer chart authors to HTML, and the note read as a blanket rule. It applied only to **hand-authored `{#ChartBucket}` table-cell bars**. The `{Chart:}` tag rasterizes to PNG and works in Word, PowerPoint, Excel, PDF and HTML — `DocGenChartImageController` gates on `Word` / `isHtmlBacked` / `PowerPoint`.

What actually varies is **style by format**:

| Style | Word / PPTX / XLSX | HTML → PDF | HTML in browser |
|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| `bar` | PNG | CSS-bar | yes |
| `pivot` | **no** | CSS table | yes |
| `clustered`, `stacked` | PNG | CSS table | yes |
| `column`, `pie`, `donut`, `line`, `area` | PNG | **no** | `htmlRender=svg` |

`pivot` isn't in the rasterizer's `KNOWN_STYLES` (a cross-tab is a table, not a chart shape), and Flying Saucer drops inline SVG from `Blob.toPdf`. Which inverts the old advice: **for pie/donut/column in a PDF, Word is the better source format.**

## Milestones: release dates, not version numbers

So a contributor can see when a merged PR would actually ship. `TRIAGE.md` gains the bug-vs-template gate that now precedes any priority call, plus `good first issue` / `help wanted` guidance.

## Also

`CLAUDE.md` was two releases stale — it claimed v3.54.0 was current. Actual is **v3.56.0** (`04tVx0000010fnNIAQ`), which is what the README install link already pointed at. Fixed, with a note to keep the two in sync.

body:
## Summary

This is a follow-up to #72. After #72 removes completed queries from later automatic IVF batch rounds, incomplete queries still rerun the full larger `nprobe` and rescan old lists. This PR makes those retries incremental: a `16 -> 32 -> 64` expansion scans `[16,32)` and then `[32,64)` instead of rescanning `[0,32)` and `[0,64)`.

## Changes

- pass half-open probe ranges through automatic batch expansion for IVF-FLAT, IVF-SQ, IVF-PQ, and IVF-RQ
- seed each expansion round with the query's accumulated Top-K so prior heap results are retained
- scan only newly added lists in filtered and unfiltered batch paths
- preserve #72's bounded retry buffers when packing active queries and their Top-K seeds
- preserve aggregate IVF-RQ search statistics across progressive rounds
- keep fixed-width/scalar searches, storage formats, public APIs, and the C ABI unchanged

Logging and JNI diagnostic bridging are intentionally excluded from this PR and handled separately by #75.

## Testing

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo test -p paimon-vindex-core`
  - 451 passed, 1 ignored
- `cargo clippy -p paimon-vindex-core --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- focused coverage for:
  - half-open probe ranges across multiple expansion rounds
  - carrying accumulated Top-K seeds between rounds
  - bounding packed query and seed buffers during partial retries
  - preserving a valid row ID of `-1` via its finite distance
  - IVF-PQ range partitioning and seeded result equivalence with a one-shot search
  - aggregate IVF-RQ statistics across progressive rounds

## Notes

- Rebased onto `main` after #72 was merged.
- The PR now contains one functional commit only.
- Query preprocessing and coarse centroid selection are still recomputed for the smaller active-query set in each round; no cross-round public search-state API is introduced.

author: usadamasa
body:
MCP server と chatter を、Claude Code からも Codex からも同じように使えるようにする。
tool も発話経路も共通で、分かれるのは chatter の台詞を書く LLM だけ。

## 接続元の判定

`host/mcp/src/buddy_agent.py` を足した。接続元の識別子と、それを保持する `AgentIdentity`。
witness は 2 つあり、どちらも同じ identity に書いて後勝ちにする。

| 経路 | いつ | どこ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MCP の `initialize` の `clientInfo.name` | 接続直後 | `buddy_mcp._ClientProbe` (middleware) |
| hook datagram の `agent` | イベントごと | hook の `--agent` |

`MCPServer(middleware=[...])` は `initialize` も通るので、tool 全部に `Context` を足さずに
`clientInfo` が読める。どちらの witness も来なければ `BUDDY_CHATTER_AGENT` (既定
`claude-code`)。**デプロイ時点ではどちらにも固定しない。**

## LLM の分岐

`RoutingLineSource` が agent ごとに生成器を遅延構築してキャッシュする。組み合わせは固定で
2x2 は用意しない — それぞれのマシンが既に持っている認証をそのまま使うのが狙いで、交差させると
どちらにも無い認証情報が要るため。

- `claude-code` → `VertexLineSource` (従来どおり)
- `codex` → `CodexLineSource`。`codex exec --ephemeral --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox
  read-only --output-schema` を空の一時ディレクトリで 1 ターン回す

Codex 側を SDK ではなく CLI にしたのは、`model_provider` と auth の解決を Codex 自身に
任せるため。ローカル proxy や rotate する token を再実装せずに済む。

`VertexLineSource` から batching / caching / 失敗時のフォールバックを `BatchedLineSource` に
抜き、両者で共有する。JSON schema も共通。backend は使うまで作らない (構築が認証を触るため)。

## hook

Codex の hooks は Claude Code と同じスキーマ (イベント名も stdin の payload も同じ) なので、
スクリプトは 1 本のまま `--agent` だけ足した。指定が無ければ環境変数から推定し、それも無ければ
`agent` フィールドごと省く。

## 検証

| 検査 | 結果 |
| --- | --- |
| ruff check / format | 通る |
| basedpyright | 4 member とも 0 errors |
| pytest | device 142 / host-link 53 / host-mcp 135 (+46) / host-tools 98 |
| host-mcp coverage | 84.6% (bar 77%) |
| `--compile-only` / `uv sync --locked` | 通る |

実機 (Cardputer-Adv) で `buddy_deploy.py` を通したうえ、standalone chatter を両 backend で:

| `--agent` | `backend` | `generated` | 発話 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `claude-code` | `vertex` | 6 | 「けむりの実験なのだ」 |
| `codex` | `codex` | 6 | 「煙の試験が静かに終わったのだ」 |

`BUDDY_CHATTER_CODEX_BIN` を存在しないパスにすると `generation_failures: 1` と
`FileNotFoundError` が出て固定の台詞に落ちる — 本当に CLI を叩いていて、落ちても黙らないことの
裏取り。hook が wire に載せる `agent` も実物のスクリプトで 4 通り確認した。

## Codex 側の設定 (このリポジトリの外)

`~/.codex/config.toml` の `[mcp_servers.buddy]` と `~/.codex/hooks.json` に足す。手順は
README の「Codex から使う」にある。Codex は新しい hook を初回に trust させる。

body:
## Summary

- **New command `/mma:tldr`.** Turns the previous assistant message, or a supplied file, URL, or text, into a short decision brief readable in about three minutes: an 80-word TLDR, key points numbered and ranked by decision impact with source references, and the topics it left out. Client-side only — no task type, no HTTP route, no worker. Follows the `mma-breakout` pattern.
- **It does two jobs, not one.** It compresses a long source and explains a difficult one, and the reader never says which. A short, dense source produces a **longer** result, because defining terms and separating ideas costs words.
- **The rule that makes it safer than a summary:** compress the explanation, never the qualification. An ordinary summary keeps the claims and drops the conditions, so the reader finishes more confident and less correct. The command may drop a whole low-priority point, but it names the topic when it does, and never keeps a claim while deleting the condition that makes the claim accurate.
- **Fixes a pre-existing defect.** `/mma-flow` and `/mma-breakout` declared "not an auto-matched skill" in `when_to_use`, which is descriptive prose and enforces nothing — the agent could invoke either from intent matching. An accidental `/mma-flow` would have run a full SDLC playbook. All three commands now set `disable-model-invocation: true`, asserted by a contract test and by the release smoke gate.
- **Narrows the `mma clients` rule.** The recovery-path line now applies only to skills that name an MMA tool. `/mma-tldr` dispatches nothing, so it has no recovery path to claim. The inverse is asserted too. The contract test and the smoke gate carry the same rule and reference each other.
- New packaged asset `_shared/writing-style.md` — a compact plain-English standard, ASD-STE100 as guidance rather than formal compliance.
- `SCHEMA_VERSION` stays at **6**. No engine, wire, or task-type change.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm build` — clean, built CLI reports `6.8.0`
- [x] `pnpm test` — 267 files, 2126 tests, all passing
- [x] `pnpm lint` — clean

Updated: `CHANGELOG.md`, `README.md` (commands table, plugin counts, "What's new" replaced not appended).

Checked and current, unchanged: `PRIVACY.md` (no telemetry, consent, or wire change), `packages/core/README.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (no layering or lifecycle change), `DIRECTION.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `packages/server/README.md` (carries no counts). `packages/server/CHANGELOG.md` does not exist — no stale orphan.

`disable-model-invocation: true` is being added to two **existing** commands, and its runtime effect was not observed in-session — confirming it needs a fresh Claude Code session. Worst case is that `/mma:flow` and `/mma:breakout` stop being model-suggestible, which is exactly what their `when_to_use` already claimed. Both still work when typed.
