author: hayden727
body:
## Motivation

dots.tts streaming currently runs one AudioVAE `stream_step` per request under the codec lock. At concurrency, compatible requests pay repeated launch and synchronization overhead even when their decoder states have identical shapes and counters.

## Changes

- coalesce compatible streaming request states through the existing `StreamingVocoderBase` chunk-batching hooks
- run one batched AudioVAE streaming step, then scatter LSTM/decoder state and waveform rows back to each request
- keep compiled streaming disabled because of the existing graph-corruption guard (#1392)

## Performance

1x H200, SeedTTS EN, 128 samples, concurrency 8, 10 warmups, streaming enabled; mean of 2 runs:

| Metric | main (`2e607bc`) | This PR | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Request throughput | 1.427 req/s | 1.549 req/s | **+8.55%** |
| Mean latency | 5.544 s | 5.100 s | **-8.00%** |
| Mean RTF | 1.561 | 1.432 | **-8.23%** |
| Audio throughput | 5.377 s/s | 5.828 s/s | **+8.40%** |
| TTFC | 2.972 s | 2.504 s | **-15.75%** |
| ITL | 0.3669 s | 0.3704 s | +0.95% |

All four runs completed 128/128 requests with no failures. The optimized server log confirmed real cross-request batches (`requests=4`).

## Correctness

With the real dots codec and fixed deterministic latent streams, sequential request-local decoding and the batched path produced identical shapes and were within `rtol=2e-3, atol=2e-3`:

- request A: max abs diff 6.98e-05
- request B: max abs diff 8.79e-05

## Validation

- `pytest -q tests/unit_test/dots_tts/test_vocoder_streaming.py tests/unit_test/dots_tts/test_vocoder.py tests/unit_test/dots_tts/test_result_contracts.py` (16 passed)
- pre-commit hooks passed

Related: #1367

author: oesnuj
body:
## 관련 이슈

LAN-240

## 무엇을, 왜

복습 영작(REVIEW) 스텝을 네이티브 키보드 타이핑에서, 첫 단계 퀴즈(QUIZ)와 같은 단어 칩 선택 방식으로 바꿨다. 마지막 단계가 타이핑이라 한 문장을 완성하는 데 드는 공수가 컸던 게 이유다.

퀴즈 스텝의 단어 칩 컴포넌트(QuizStep)를 복습 스텝에도 그대로 연결해서 쓴다. 난이도 차별화는 없고, 오답도 퀴즈와 동일하게 결과 시트로 정답을 보여준 뒤 완료 처리로 넘어간다. 정답을 맞혔을 때만 기존 획득 연출(콘페티 + 표현 카드)이 뜨고, 이때 상단 진행바도 성공 색(초록)으로 함께 바뀐다.

BE는 이미 정답 순서 단어 배열(writingSentenceWords)과 섞인 선택지 배열(writingSentenceWordChoices)을 내려주고 있었는데 FE 타입 선언이 빠져 있었다 — 이번에 채워 넣었다.

타이핑 전용 코드(ReviewInputStep, review-input.ts, 2단계 힌트 버튼)는 지웠다.

## 스크린샷

자동 캡처 도구로 찍어서 폰트·이미지 로딩 등 실제 화면과 미세하게 다르게 보이는 부분이 동작이 의도대로 되는지 확인하는 용도로 봐주면 됩니다~

| QUIZ 정답 | EXPLAIN CTA | REVIEW 정답(콘페티+진행바) | 획득 카드 |
|---|---|---|---|
| ![QUIZ 정답](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Aragornnnnnn/landit-fe/assets/lan240-screenshots/lan240/01-quiz-correct.png) | ![EXPLAIN](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Aragornnnnnn/landit-fe/assets/lan240-screenshots/lan240/02-explain-cta.png) | ![REVIEW 정답](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Aragornnnnnn/landit-fe/assets/lan240-screenshots/lan240/03-review-correct-confetti.png) | ![획득 카드](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Aragornnnnnn/landit-fe/assets/lan240-screenshots/lan240/04-review-success-card.png) |

## 리뷰 포인트

- `QuizStep`에 추가한 4개 프롭(`progressRange`, `initialSelected`/`onSelectedChange`, `correctSlot`) — QUIZ·REVIEW 겸용 확장 방식이 적절한지
- 오답이어도 결과 시트 CTA로 완료 처리까지 넘어가는 게 의도대로인지 (복습이라 재시도 없이 한 번만 판정)
- 계측: 복습도 퀴즈와 같은 이벤트(QUIZ_ANSWER_SUBMITTED 등)로 통일하고, REVIEW 전용 이벤트는 새로 안 만들었다

## 실제 화면 검증

로컬 dev 서버에 로그인해서 QUIZ→EXPLAIN→REVIEW 전체 플로우를 두 표현으로 직접 돌렸다.

- **정답 케이스**: QUIZ 정답 → EXPLAIN CTA "복습 퀴즈 풀게요" 정상 표시 → REVIEW 단어뱅크(`writingSentenceWordChoices`)가 실제 데이터로 채워져 있음 확인 → 칩으로 정답 완성 → 콘페티 + 진행바 초록 + "표현 획득!" 카드 + 학습 완료 → 진행도 정상 갱신
- **오답 케이스**: REVIEW에서 일부러 오답 제출 → "아쉬워요" + 정답 문장 노출 + 학습 완료(빨간 버튼) → 완료 처리도 정상, 진행도 갱신
- 획득 카드 배경이 반투명(`bg-success/12`)이라 뒤 단어 칩이 비치던 버그 발견 → `ResultSheet`와 같은 `color-mix` 불투명 배경으로 수정

버그 발견 없음(발견한 1건은 같은 PR에서 수정 완료).

## 체크리스트

- [x] 코드 추가 500줄 이하 (5~10분 리뷰 가능한 볼륨)
- [x] 브랜치 이름에 이슈 번호 포함 (`feat/LAN-XX`)
- [x] 커밋 메시지가 컨벤션(`{type}({scope}): 메시지`)을 따름

author: taxpon
body:
Three shapes had already turned out wrong, each found by accident: playbook CRUD's scope (B6), the
tag vocabulary's path (B14), and `pull_requests[]` (#99) — the last of which would have disabled the
review-fix loop silently. All three were documented in the reference and none had been read: the
client was built from `docs/05-devin-integration.md`, which was written during design from memory.

This reads the OpenAPI block of every endpoint's own page and fixes what diverges.

## What was wrong

| | We sent / expected | The reference says | Would have broken |
|---|---|---|---|
| Session listing filter | `tags` as a comma-joined string | an array | The tag filter, silently |
| Pagination | `limit` | `first` | Paging, silently — the parameter is simply ignored |
| Knowledge note | `trigger_description` | `trigger` | Note creation, at bootstrap |
| Knowledge note id | `id` / `note_id` / `knowledge_id` | `note_id` | — |
| Schedule id | `id` / `schedule_id` | `scheduled_session_id` | `DEVIN_SCHEDULE_ID`, so every bootstrap would re-create the sweep |
| Consumption `date` | a date string | **epoch integer** | The ACU ledger — the budget guard reads it |
| Consumption window | no parameters | `time_after` / `time_before` | Fetching everything, every time |
| Enterprise metrics | `sessions_count` | `sessions_created_count` | The metrics panel |

The alias unions are gone where the reference names one field. That tolerance was reasonable while
nobody had read the spec — it is what kept the `items` envelope from being a second bug. Where the
fact now exists, an alias only hides a rename, which is the same reasoning #99 applied to `pr_url`.

## What did not change

`CreateSessionRequest` matches the reference field for field. The request body for the call the
whole demo depends on was already right.

`PUT /v3/organizations/{org_id}/tags` still writes the undocumented path — that is
[B14](../blob/main/docs/blockers.md#b14) and the owner's decision, not this PR's.

## The fakes were wrong too

Every fixture carrying a shape we wished for made the suite green against a body the API does not
send. That is how all of this shipped, so the fakes were corrected alongside — `tests/factories.py`,
and the client, poller, worker, policy and e2e suites.

## Honesty

`docs/05-devin-integration.md` now marks each shape *verified against the reference*, *observed
live*, or *unobserved*, and says at the top that **nothing but the session listing has been seen
live**. B8 is narrowed to exactly that. A reference is not a running server: `POST /sessions` is
still the first thing a live run will judge.

`make ci` green — 1835 passed.

author: liorlobel
body:
`tools/ci.ps1` is the 72-step list `docs/RELEASING.md` names before tagging.
Since 2026-08-09 it has run in CI as the `gate` job, on **windows-latest only** —
so "the gate passed" meant "passed on Windows", and no sentence anywhere said so.
This runs it on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest too.

## The Windows run must not get weaker, and did not

That is the whole risk of this change: the Windows leg is what stands between a
mistake and a published release, and a port that turns one of its steps into a
skip, loosens an assertion so it holds everywhere, or makes an unconditional
check conditional would be **worse than not porting at all**.

Measured, on `bfd223b` before any edit and again after:

| | steps | ran | skipped |
|---|---|---|---|
| local baseline, `bfd223b` | 72 | 66 | 6 |
| local, after the port | 72 | 66 | 6 |

Identical ledgers, confirmed over two independent full runs. Two steps were
*renamed* and the comparison maps old to new. On the runner, where WiX is
installed, the figure is 67 ran / 5 skipped both before and after — the
step-by-step comparison against run 31347022352 is in the PR thread.

## Ported by spelling, not by skipping

- `$exe` — **25** `target/release/pl.exe` sites in 18 steps, plus
  `dump_spline.exe` and `tar.exe`. Off Windows `Find-Tars` matched nothing, so
  the tar.gz step would have skipped on the two platforms whose users are the
  reason a tarball exists.
- `[IO.Path]::GetTempPath()` — **17** unguarded `$env:TEMP` uses. Off Windows
  that variable is *absent*, not empty, and `Join-Path $null x` is a terminating
  error: the exact failure that killed both non-Windows legs of the first
  release.
- The `.pyd`/`.so`/`.dylib` table from `release.ps1`, which fixes a live defect
  rather than routing around one: 'Python bindings vs Biopython' chose
  `libpolylinker.so` for everything non-Windows (wrong on macOS, where cargo
  emits `.dylib`) and hardcoded the shipped name `polylinker.pyd` (wrong
  everywhere but Windows).
- Corpus globs from `"$Corpus\**\*.dna"` to `/`, because a backslash is a glob
  escape off Windows.
- **The two zip steps now run everywhere.** Off Windows the release step builds
  a second, zip-forced archive, so "entry order is sorted" is finally fed ext4
  and APFS enumeration order instead of NTFS's already-sorted one. Windows is
  untouched: same archive, same assertions.

**Seven steps genuinely cannot run off Windows** — PE resource reads, an 8.3
short name, `msiexec`, `HKCU`. Each says so in its own precondition, via
`WindowsOnly { … }`, the one helper that owns the string `'not windows'`, and
the gate checks that string against `$IsWindows` rather than believing it.

## The skip list is narrowed, not extended

`.github/ci-expected-skips.txt` now names **only** the corpus skips, which are
the same five on all three runners — so it needs no platform column and adds no
second, unverified claim about where a step ought to run. Set equality survives
as rule L3. Under `-ExpectedSkips`:

- **L1** every skip carries a reason its own precondition declared; `$false`
  fails. (This is exactly what the old flat list bought, and it costs no list.)
- **L2** `'not windows'` may not appear on Windows.
- **L3** the corpus skips equal the committed list, both directions, and a name
  matching no step is itself a failure.

`tools/reconcile-ledgers.ps1` is new, and holds the four rules **no single leg
can check**, over a `-Ledger` file each runner uploads: the three legs carry the
same step names in the same order, every step **ran somewhere**, the corpus set
is identical everywhere, and every reason is in the vocabulary. Ten planted
ledger sets in `-SelfTest`, run first in the job.

## The Windows-only env-var denylist is gone

It listed eleven names and omitted `TEMP` — so the seventeen uses in `ci.ps1`
itself, the exact spelling named as what broke the release, were invisible to
the step written to catch that class. It is now an **allowlist** of two
variables that exist on all three platforms, each asserted to be actually used,
with a planted-input control inside the step.

## Every check proved able to fail

By injecting the defect and running the **whole gate**, never one step by name:

| injection | result |
|---|---|
| unguarded `$env:TEMP` added to `ci.ps1` | `GATE FAILED: …no environment variable unguarded`, naming the line |
| a step made to return `'not windows'` on Windows | `skipped saying 'not windows', and this IS Windows` |
| a corpus name deleted from the list | `skipped for want of a corpus and is not on the list` |
| a non-corpus name added to the list | `did not skip for want of a corpus` |
| a name matching no step | `names no step in this gate` |

The three-runner evidence — a bucket-B defect caught on Linux, a
Windows-inherent defect caught on Windows while Linux correctly skips it, and
both directions of the skip guard — is posted in the PR thread.

**Do not merge yet.**

author: alexey-pelykh
body:
Closes #918.

Issue #885's AC4 asserted *"the CI grep test covers help lines"*. No such coverage existed: `scan_banned` and its lists were private to `src/stats.rs`'s test module, every call site was a stats render or a `--json` key set, and nothing under `scripts/` or `.github/workflows/` grepped for banned tokens. `--help` was an unchecked surface that read as a checked one.

## The decision (AC1) — option 1, and why

**Taken: split the vocabulary.** `src/framing_vocabulary.rs` (new, `#[cfg(test)]`-only, following the `cross_surface` / `render_golden` precedent) holds the central lists and one scanner. `stats.rs` scans the whole list; `--help` scans a subset *derived* as central-minus-exemptions, so there is no second hand-maintained copy. Both share one tokenizer.

**Rejected: option 2 (command-name exemption set)** — falsified by measurement. Exactly four central tokens appear in the shipped help; only three are command names. `add` is not a command in this CLI (`STATUS_USAGE`: `-v, --verbose  add each account's access-token expiry`) and `remove` in `SERVICE_USAGE` (`unload + remove that LaunchAgent`) is not used as one. The boundary is semantic, not lexical.

**Rejected: option 3 (drop the claim)** — the claim was false, but the coverage is cheap and `--help` is exactly the operator-facing prose the #160 firewall governs.

Full reasoning is in the commit body, which is what squash-merge preserves.

## The guard bites — demonstrated, not asserted

Injecting editorial framing into a real shipped constant (`IMPORT_USAGE`, deliberately the *last* entry, to prove iteration reaches the end):

```
assertion `left == right` failed: IMPORT_USAGE must carry no banned framing:
sessiometer import — rehydrate accounts from a migration artifact
CANARY: you should upgrade your plan soon.
  left: Some("upgrade")
 right: None
```

Adding an unwired help constant reddens the completeness tripwire, naming it:

```
assertion `left == right` failed: every `const *_USAGE` in src/cli.rs must be
reached from ALL_HELP_TOPICS — an unscanned help surface is exactly what issue
#918 was opened about
 right: ["CANARY_USAGE", "CAPTURE_USAGE", ...]
```

## The completeness tripwire's own parser (post-review fix)

The merge judge found the tripwire had the exact hole it exists to catch: the parser matched only a bare `const `, so `pub(crate) const X_USAGE` was invisible to it. Their scenario — a fully wired `HelpTopic::Purge` with a real dispatch arm and a `pub(crate) const PURGE_USAGE` carrying four banned tokens, left out of `ALL_HELP_TOPICS` — shipped a live `sessiometer purge --help` reading *"usage is critical, you should upgrade soon"* with every gate green.

Fixed by stripping visibility **structurally** (`pub`, `pub(crate)`, `pub(super)`, `pub(in …)`) rather than matching a fixed prefix list, so the accepted set is closed over Rust's visibility grammar instead of being three spellings someone thought of — plus `the_declaration_parser_recognises_every_visibility_spelling`, which pins each accepted form and each deliberately-ignored one. Without that test the fix would just be a second untested textual parser inside a completeness guard: the same defect, one level down.

Re-running the judge's scenario against the fix:

```
$ ./target/debug/sessiometer purge --help
sessiometer purge — usage is critical, you should upgrade soon

test cli::tests::every_help_constant_is_scanned ... FAILED
assertion `left == right` failed: every `const *_USAGE` in src/cli.rs must be reached
from ALL_HELP_TOPICS — an unscanned help surface is exactly what issue #918 was opened about
  left:  [... "POKE_USAGE", "RELIABILITY_USAGE", ...]
 right:  [... "POKE_USAGE", "PURGE_USAGE", "RELIABILITY_USAGE", ...]
```

Scenario reverted; suite green at 2026.

## The exemption does not swallow the guard

Widening `HELP_EXEMPT_TOKENS` to also excuse `should` and `critical` reddens the pinned exact-set assertion, group representation (`the value judgement group lost its representative "critical"`), the excused-verb-inside-a-recommendation bite check, the shared-tokenizer check, the still-earned check (`"should" is exempt ... but no help surface uses it any more`), the main help-surface bite loop, and the expiry-guard subsumption check.

(This previously read "**five** tests". The merge judge measured seven; my five were correct but the list was short. The cardinal is deleted rather than corrected — a count that under-states coverage becomes *right* if someone later weakens the guard until only five redden, so the enumeration carries the meaning and the number is a liability.)

A recommendation built *around* an excused verb is still caught: `you should disable <account>` trips `should`.

## Stats-side coverage is unchanged, asserted not assumed

`BANNED_TOKENS` (51) and `BANNED_PHRASES` (2) moved with identical content and ordering; the 25 `scan_banned` call sites are untouched. A new test asserts every central token and phrase individually bites — and pins the list sizes, because that test derives its subject from the lists, so deleting a token would otherwise delete its own check. That hole was found by canary and closed before commit.

## Coverage is the surface, not a sample

All 19 help topics scanned. A new `HelpTopic` variant breaks the build on an exhaustive match; a new `const *_USAGE` never wired in reddens a check that reads `src/cli.rs`'s own source.

Suite 2013 → 2026 tests.

ADR-0020 (status `accepted`) cited `BANNED_TOKENS` / `BANNED_PHRASES` / `scan_banned` as living in `src/stats.rs` at three sites — body ¶, mechanics list, and `## Related → Code:`. Not gate-caught (`check-doc-citations.sh` validates frontmatter path-shaped values only). All three amended; the permit/ban boundary the ADR settles is unchanged, and the two tests it cites did not move.

## Loci

- `src/framing_vocabulary.rs` — the lists, `scan_with`, `scan_banned`, `scan_help_banned`, `HELP_EXEMPT_TOKENS` + 8 invariant tests
- `src/cli.rs` — `ALL_HELP_TOPICS`, `topic_const_name`, `every_help_constant_is_scanned`, `every_help_surface_carries_no_banned_framing_but_the_guard_bites_on_injection`, `every_help_exemption_is_still_earned_by_the_shipped_help`, `the_repo_wide_help_guard_subsumes_the_expiry_guard_bar_its_own_extras`
- `src/stats.rs` — vocabulary removed, `use crate::framing_vocabulary::scan_banned` added; no call site changed

author: baseline-k
body:
### 背景
Cortex-M7 等 MCU 允许把对时序要求高的函数放到 RAM 中执行（如 ITCM），
会把固件拆分成多个代码区。这些函数的地址落在`CMB_CODE_SECTION_NAME`（Flash）之外，
原回溯扫描会把所有跨过 Flash 边界的帧当作无效帧丢弃——调用栈恰好断在最关键的代码处。

### 改动
新增可选的多代码区回溯支持，代码区采用可自定义的表格声明：

- `cmb_cfg.h`：新增开关 `CMB_USING_USER_CODE_SECTION`；开启后可用
  `CMB_USER_CODE_SECTIONS` 配置额外代码区——一个 const 的
  `{ start, end }` 结构体数组初始化器，可声明任意多个代码区
  （ITCM、CCM、其他Flash区等）
- `cmb_def.h`：新增 `CMB_CODE_REGION_MAX`（默认 8），代码区表容量上限，
  仿 `CMB_CALL_STACK_MAX_DEPTH` 用 `#ifndef` 默认值，可在 `cmb_cfg.h` 覆盖
- `cm_backtrace.c`：`cm_backtrace_init()` 填充代码区表 `code_regions[]`
  （自动检测的 Flash 区在前，随后按 `CMB_USER_CODE_SECTIONS` 追加）；
  将原单区域判定替换为 `cmb_pc_in_code()` / `cmb_pc_in_code_skip_first()`，
  遍历所有已登记区域
- 未定义 `CMB_USING_USER_CODE_SECTION` 时，所有新增代码均被预处理裁剪，
  与 v1.5.0 逐字节一致

author: ikuwow
body:
## Summary

Drop `-is:draft` from the `Needs your review` section in the gh-dash config, so draft pull requests carrying a review request for me appear in the queue.

## Why

Code owners are never auto-requested while a pull request is a draft:

> Code owners are not automatically requested to review draft pull requests.

— [About code owners](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/about-code-owners)

So the automatic path that fills `review-requested:@me` with volume cannot fire on a draft. A draft reaching that section carries a reviewer someone added explicitly, which is the opposite of noise. Two cases can still put a draft there without a person deciding in the moment: a bot that opens draft PRs with a configured reviewer list, and a pull request opened ready, auto-requested, then converted back to draft — GitHub does not document whether pending requests survive that conversion, and I did not confirm it either way. Both are bounded enough to cost at most an occasional extra row.

`-is:draft` stays on the `author:@me` sections, where the drafts are my own and already have a dedicated tab.

## Verification

A draft pull request with a review request for me existed at the time of the change and was invisible under the old filter:

```
$ gh api -X GET search/issues -f q='is:open is:pr review-requested:@me' \
    --jq '.items[] | [(.draft|tostring), .html_url] | @tsv'
true	https://github.com/tacoms-inc-dev/camel-react-frontend/pull/2155
false	https://github.com/tacoms-inc-dev/camel-golang-backend/pull/9304
false	https://github.com/tacoms-inc-dev/camel-golang-backend/pull/9303
false	https://github.com/tacoms-inc-dev/camel-golang-backend/pull/9298
false	https://github.com/tacoms-inc-dev/camel-customize-api/pull/1245
```

That draft was opened by another person who requested my review directly, with no `ready_for_review` or `convert_to_draft` event in its timeline. The old filter matched 4 of these 5; the new filter matches all 5.

`yq '.prSections[0]'` parses the edited file and returns `filters: is:open review-requested:@me`, and the two keys the [gh-dash pr-section schema](https://gh-dash.dev/schema/pr-section.json) marks required (`title`, `filters`) are both still present.

## Known gap left open

`review-requested` drops a pull request once I submit any review:

> Requested reviewers are no longer listed in the search results after they review a pull request.

— [Searching issues and pull requests](https://docs.github.com/en/search-github/searching-on-github/searching-issues-and-pull-requests)

A pull request I reviewed once and the author then pushed to without re-requesting stays out of the section. Addressing that needs a separate section on a different axis, out of scope here.

author: dongchen-yang
body:
## What

Adds a second PBR-conditioning mechanism — **channel** (per-token channel concat) — alongside the upstream token-doubling, so this baseline conditions on the PBR latent the same way as the LightGen TRELLIS.2 emission DiTs (conditioning-fair comparison), plus scaffolding for a real-cond 72k production run.

- **token** (upstream, unchanged): `Gen3DSeg` appends the PBR tex latent as N extra sequence tokens (sequence 2N, 64ch per token).
- **channel** (new): `[x_t 32 | shape 32 | pbr 32]` = 96ch per token via the flow's `concat_cond`, sequence stays N. Implemented in `emissive/pbr_conditioning.py` (`Gen3DSegChannelConcat`, drop-in forward signature — `Sampler` and all callers work unchanged). On warm start from `full_seg`, only `input_layer.weight` is re-initialized (64→96 shape mismatch, validated strictly); all transformer blocks load. Side effect: sequence N instead of 2N, so channel steps are cheaper.

## Compatibility

- `train_emissive.py` now **requires** `--pbr_cond {channel,token}` (same explicit no-silent-default ethos as `--cond`).
- `eval_emissive.py` / `predict_emissive.py` / `make_pred_glb.py` **auto-detect** the mode from the checkpoint's `input_layer` fan-in (64=token, 96=channel) — every existing checkpoint keeps working with no new flag.
- All 13 existing train sbatch wrappers (incl. `archive/`) are pinned to `--pbr_cond token`, their historical mechanism.
- The dated one-off scripts (`dump_pred_voxels*`, `diagnostics/*`, `seg_covers_emissive.py`, `seg_to_mesh.py`) intentionally stay token-only — they reproduce pre-change checkpoints.

author: luguza
body:
A camp used to hit in lumps. A skeleton stood in reach for 3,4 s doing
nothing and then took a ninth of the hero's pool off in one stroke, so the
LP bar moved in steps and a fight read as a sequence of jolts rather than
as pressure. Every body in the bestiary now swings two to four times as
often for proportionally smaller blows, and the same fight drains the bar
as a steady bleed.

Per-second pressure is held fixed. Each variant's `dmgMult` is divided by
exactly the factor its cadence was multiplied by, so the hall costs what
it always cost; what changed is the grain it costs it in. Measured on
tools/attrition.mjs, the camps a build clears land within one of the old
numbers at every spend on the table.

- The bestiary's `attackSpeedMult` becomes `attackMs`, a body's cadence
  written out in milliseconds rather than derived from a multiplier — it
  is the number the design is stated in. Bands: 0,8-1,0 s for vermin and
  small quick bodies, 1,2-1,6 s man-sized, 1,7-2,0 s heavies on legs,
  2,4-2,8 s for the giants, which keep the slow heavy stroke on purpose.
- The windup becomes a share of the body's own beat (`enemyWindupBeats`,
  six tenths, floored at 500 ms) instead of a flat figure divided by the
  swing rate. Engagements here are short and the windup is paid many
  times per camp, so a flat one would charge a goblin the same dead time
  as a giant — worth about a third of the hall's pressure on the tool.
- The slimes are the one documented exception: their damage LADDER needs
  headroom above the 1-damage floor under every hit, so they keep the
  slowest beat of any small body and pay for it with the smallest hits.
- Damage numbers over the hero step up-and-left by lane. Four lanes of
  fast small hits now land inside one number's lifetime, and stacked on
  one pixel they read as a smear rather than as being ground down.
- attrition.mjs rounds a blow the way sizeBody does (it is a small
  integer now) and reports Skelettsekunden rather than Skelettschläge:
  a blow is no longer a fixed bite, so what a pool is worth is the time
  it buys. The smoke test guards the cadence contract and the ladder.

author: butler54
body:
## Summary
Supersedes/incorporates #90 (rebased onto latest main) plus a follow-on fix found while testing it live.

- **Container/SSH naming (from #90)**: OpenShell has used more than one podman container naming scheme (`openshell-sandbox-{name}` legacy vs. `openshell-{workspace}--{name}-{uuid}` workspace-scoped, 0.0.9x+) and more than one SSH alias form (`openshell-{name}` vs `openshell-{name}.default`). `health.py` only recognized the legacy forms, so `check_container_state`/`recover_container` falsely reported every current, workspace-scoped sandbox as MISSING.
- **New**: that false-MISSING report blocks `sandboxctl open` entirely (health check runs first and aborts). But even past that, the actual `code --remote ssh-remote+openshell-<name>` invocation in `open_cmd.py` and `extensions.py` still hardcoded the bare alias — which doesn't exist in current SSH configs (only the `.default`-suffixed one does) — so VS Code failed to resolve the host anyway.

Reproduced live on a real host: every current sandbox (created under OpenShell 0.0.96) uses the workspace-scoped naming, so `sandboxctl open`/`doctor` was broken end-to-end for all of them until both issues are fixed together.

## Changes
- `resolve_container_name()`: match against both known container naming patterns instead of a fixed prefix (from #90)
- `resolve_ssh_host()` (new, extracted from `check_ssh_connectivity`): probes both known SSH alias forms and returns the live one
- `open_cmd.py` / `extensions.py` / `cli.py extensions install`: resolve the live SSH alias once and use it for the actual `code --remote` invocation instead of reconstructing `openshell-{name}` inline
- `install_extensions()` signature changed from `sandbox_name` to `ssh_host` (callers now resolve first) — updated the two call sites and their tests

## Test plan
- [x] `uv run pytest` — 386 passed (1 pre-existing unrelated failure: `test_git_identity_skipped_when_not_configured` depends on ambient git config, fails without a clean-slate `~/.gitconfig`, reproduces identically on main)
- [x] `uv run ruff check` / `ruff format --check` — clean
- [ ] Manual: `sandboxctl doctor <name>` reports healthy for a workspace-scoped sandbox
- [ ] Manual: `sandboxctl open <name> --code-only` successfully launches VS Code against a workspace-scoped sandbox

Closes #90

body:
## Summary

Fixes tablet (~768px) homepage header overflow + Log In clipping + cramped search row.

Live deploy-main HEAD `584e643a47` still renders the inline header nav at 768-1023px (via `md:flex`) and keeps the hero search in a single horizontal row at 768px (via `md:grid-cols-[1fr_140px_auto]`). The rightmost nav item ("Log In" via AuthNavControls Sign in link) clips off the viewport edge, and the search row produces cramped touch targets.

## Fix

Bump the four responsive breakpoints from `md:` to `lg:` so the inline nav collapses to the existing hamburger drawer at <1024px and the search/country/CTA stack vertically up to 1024px:

- `src/components/Header.tsx`: inline nav `md:flex → lg:flex`; hamburger button `md:hidden → lg:hidden`; mobile-nav drawer `md:hidden → lg:hidden`
- `src/components/HomeProductSearch.tsx`: search-row grid `md:grid-cols-[1fr_140px_auto] → lg:grid-cols-[1fr_140px_auto]`

## Why deploy-main

`origin/main` HEAD `1131ea7b5` already carries the broader BUY-65159 fix (commit `ce06ee450` — grid→flex refactor + brand glyph swap). Live `https://buywhere.ai/` serves `origin/deploy-main` HEAD `584e643a47`, which is 121 commits behind main and lacks the breakpoint policy. Per [[buywhere-live-www-is-deploy-main-2026-08-09]], PR merges to main do not auto-deploy to live; we need a focused patch landing on deploy-main.

This PR takes the minimal-deployable slice of ce06ee450: just the breakpoint policy, not the grid→flex refactor or the brand glyph swap, so we avoid coupling an unrelated redesign into a tablet-bug hotfix.

## Verification

- Live HTML probe (2026-08-10T05:42Z) confirms pre-fix state: `hidden md:flex`, `md:hidden`, `md:grid-cols-[1fr_140px_auto]`.
- Post-merge: re-probe live for `hidden lg:flex` / `lg:hidden` / `lg:grid-cols-[1fr_140px_auto]` after Railway deploy of new deploy-main HEAD.
- Manual 768x1024 viewport test: nav should collapse to hamburger drawer; search should stack vertically.

## Rollout

1. Merge this PR.
2. Trigger Railway `serviceInstanceDeployV2` with `commitSha=<new deploy-main HEAD>` per [[buywhere-railway-deploy-trigger]].
3. Re-probe live HTML for the new breakpoints.

Refs: BUY-67974, BUY-65159, BUY-65987 (deploy-main roll-up blocker)

author: krutagyakaneria
body:
## Summary

This PR hardens the WIM bypass credential flow against forged safety and axle-weight measurements, insecure signing configuration, credential replay, and unauthorized bypass issuance.

The current implementation allows client-provided WIM-related values to influence bypass eligibility and contains a hardcoded signing-secret fallback.

This change establishes a server-side trust boundary and ensures that bypass credentials are issued only after authenticated, authorized, and validated WIM measurements are confirmed.

## Problem

The WIM bypass endpoint currently accepts client-controlled values such as:

- safetyScore
- axleWeight

These values can influence the bypass eligibility decision.

The signing implementation also contains a fallback signing secret, which creates a predictable credential-signing key when secure configuration is unavailable.

The existing flow therefore does not sufficiently establish that:

- The requester is authorized.
- The WIM measurement is trusted.
- The measurement belongs to the correct vehicle/load.
- The measurement is recent.
- The credential cannot be replayed.
- The signing key is securely configured.

## Changes Made

### Trusted WIM Measurements

WIM eligibility is now based on server-controlled/trusted measurement data rather than treating client-provided safety and weight values as authoritative.

Client-provided measurements cannot override the trusted measurement used for the bypass decision.

### Authentication and Authorization

The WIM bypass endpoint now follows the repository's existing authentication and authorization conventions.

Only an authenticated and authorized actor can request a bypass credential.

### Measurement Freshness

WIM measurements are validated for freshness before a bypass credential is issued.

Stale measurements are rejected rather than being treated as current vehicle conditions.

### Vehicle/Load Correlation

The verified WIM measurement is correlated with the appropriate vehicle/load context.

A valid measurement belonging to another vehicle or load cannot be used to generate a bypass credential.

### Secure Signing Configuration

Removed insecure hardcoded/default signing-secret behavior.

If the required signing secret is unavailable, the system fails closed rather than generating a credential with a predictable secret.

Production secrets are never logged or exposed through API responses.

### Credential Expiration

Bypass credentials contain server-controlled issuance and expiration information where supported by the existing credential format.

Expired credentials cannot be accepted as valid bypass credentials.

### Replay Protection

Added durable replay protection so credentials cannot be reused outside their intended lifecycle.

Replay protection does not rely solely on in-memory state and therefore remains effective across multiple API instances.

### Auditability

WIM bypass issuance and relevant rejection conditions are recorded using the existing audit/logging conventions.

Audit information allows operators to determine:

- Who requested the bypass.
- Which vehicle/load was involved.
- Which WIM measurement was used.
- When the credential was issued.
- When it expires.
- Whether issuance succeeded or failed.

Sensitive secrets and authentication credentials are not logged.

## Security Validation

The implementation verifies that:

- [x] Unauthenticated requests cannot issue bypass credentials.
- [x] Unauthorized actors cannot issue bypass credentials.
- [x] Client-provided safety scores are not treated as authoritative.
- [x] Client-provided axle weights are not treated as authoritative.
- [x] Trusted WIM measurements are validated.
- [x] Stale measurements are rejected.
- [x] Measurements are correlated with the correct vehicle/load.
- [x] Hardcoded signing-secret fallback is removed.
- [x] Missing signing configuration fails closed.
- [x] Credentials expire according to server-controlled policy.
- [x] Credential replay is prevented according to the defined lifecycle.
- [x] Modified credentials fail cryptographic verification.
- [x] Secrets are never logged.
- [x] Security failures do not result in credential issuance.

## Testing

Added/updated tests covering:

- Unauthenticated requests.
- Unauthorized requests.
- Forged safety scores.
- Forged axle weights.
- Trusted measurements.
- Stale WIM measurements.
- Wrong vehicle/load correlation.
- Missing signing secret.
- Invalid signing configuration.
- Credential expiration.
- Credential replay.
- Modified credential payloads.
- Invalid signatures.
- Valid bypass issuance.
- Audit record creation.

## Type of Change

- [x] Security Fix
- [x] Authentication/Authorization Improvement
- [x] Cryptographic Security Improvement
- [x] Data Integrity Improvement
- [x] Test Coverage
- [ ] Breaking Change

## Breaking Changes

None expected.

Existing WIM bypass APIs and downstream credential verification remain compatible where possible.

If any credential-format compatibility changes were required, they are documented in the implementation.

## Database Changes

If durable credential replay protection or audit metadata requires schema changes, they are introduced through a new migration.

Existing migrations are not modified.

## Related Issue

Closes #8468 

##GSSoC
#ECSoC26

author: snomiao
body:
`ay send` の `<ay-msg>` は #381 で標準 identity (`user@host:path:branch#pid`) を名乗るようになったが、**同じ相手を指す `<ay-init-msg>` だけが独自形式のまま** だった。読み手から見て identity の形が 2 種類あるのは無駄な差分なので揃える。

```diff
- <ay-init-msg n0 from claude #4242 @ /repo — reply: ay send agt_p "...">
+ <ay-init-msg n0 from claude sno@Mac:~/ws/repo:main#4242 — reply: ay send agt_p "...">
```

branch セグメントが入るので、worktree 名がそのまま lane 名として出る (例: `:feat/init-msg-identity`)。role 概念を撤去した #381 の狙いどおりの効果。

## なぜ Rust への移植が要ったか

`<ay-init-msg>` は **両ランタイムが組み立てる** (Rust が既定、TS が fallback) のに対し、#381 の identity は **TS にしか無かった**。`ay send` は TS 専用 (SUBCOMMANDS で委譲) なので、これまで Rust 側に identity が要らなかっただけ。byte 一致を保つには Rust にも同じ実装が必要なので `rs/src/identity.rs` として移植した。

移植したのは `local_user` / `local_host` / `read_git_branch` (`.git` を遡り、worktree の `gitdir:` 間接ファイルを辿って `HEAD` を読む) / `tildify` / clamp 群。

微妙な点として、JS 正規表現の `+` 量化子の意味を落とさないよう **不許可文字の連続を `-` 1 個に畳んで** いる (`collapse_outside`)。1 文字ごとに `-` を出すと `"a   b"` が `"a---b"` になって TS と食い違う。

## 2 実装が黙って乖離しないための担保

`tests/fixtures/ay-init-msg.golden.txt` は identity を **リテラルで固定** しているため、golden だけでは 2 つの identity 実装のズレを検出できない。

そこで `tests/fixtures/identity-cases.json` を新設し、**両ランタイムが同じ表を assert** する (`identity::tests::matches_the_shared_case_table` と `ts/identity.spec.ts`)。#390 が SUBCOMMANDS に入れた mirror テストと同じ発想。identity 組み立て 9 ケース + `safeToken` 12 ケース + `safeBranch` 5 ケース。

さらに **実機で本番経路の一致も確認** した。golden はリテラル固定なので、`os.userInfo().username` vs Rust の user 解決、`os.hostname()` vs `libc::gethostname` といった差は golden では出ない:

```
TS  : sno@Mac:~/ws/snomiao/agent-yes/tree/init-msg-identity:feat/init-msg-identity#4242
Rust: sno@Mac:~/ws/snomiao/agent-yes/tree/init-msg-identity:feat/init-msg-identity#4242
```

## 設計メモ

- `build_init_msg` / `buildInitMsg` は identity を **引数で受け取る**。中で計算すると golden fixture が実行マシン依存になり、純関数でもなくなるため。
- Rust の `shorten_home` は呼び元が消えたので削除 (path 部は `identity::tildify` が担当)。TS の `shortenHome` は `<ay-report>` (ts/parentPingSend.ts) がまだ使うので残す — Rust に対応物は無い。
- `tildify` に `home` seam を追加 (共有ケース表が実行マシンの home に依存しないため)。省略時の挙動は従来どおり。ついでに **home が空文字の時に全パスへ `~` を被せてしまう既存の穴** も塞いだ。

## テスト

- Rust: **494 passed / 0 failed** (`cargo test --all`、警告 0)
- TS: **1569 passed / 0 failed**、global branches **90.24%** (gate 90% 通過)
- 無関係な `rs/src/serve/{api,control}.rs` の `cargo fmt` 差分は commit に含めていない (main 時点で既に rustfmt 崩れ。diff を汚さないため revert 済み)

author: arthneura
body:
Adds a new `ReputationHandler` trait to `pallet-vector-db`, wired into `finalize_dispute` (penalizes the guilty provider) and `counter_dispute` (penalizes a false disputer). Fire-and-forget by design — a protocol-level reputation penalty must never be able to block or revert the caller's own dispute-resolution extrinsic.

Two methods, not one: if only a guilty provider could be penalized, a consumer could raise disputes at zero cost. Penalizing a proven-false dispute closes that incentive gap.

Config gains `ReputationHandler`, `ProviderGuiltySlash`, and `FalseDisputeSlash` — the concrete runtime wiring (adapter + slash amounts) lands in a follow-up PR, since `pallet-vector-db` stays decoupled from `pallet-agent-registry` at the type level.

Builds on #5 (already merged) for the `disputed_chunk_index` binding this depends on.

## Testing
198/198 pallet-vector-db unit tests passing, including new coverage confirming the handler fires exactly once with the correct DID on each verdict path, and does not fire on a rejected call.

author: dismonjames
body:
## Phase 4 — `arcature-db`

A production-grade PostgreSQL data subsystem combining SeaORM-level application
DX with first-class SQLx/raw-SQL access, one connection pool, explicit lifecycle,
real migrations, compile-time SQL verification, strong security defaults, serious
testing, and Arcature CLI integration.

### Architecture

- **One `sqlx::PgPool`** per `Db`, with SeaORM `DatabaseConnection` derived over
  the same pool via `SqlxPostgresConnector::from_sqlx_postgres_pool` — never a
  second pool.
- **Two first-class data paths:** `Db::orm()` (SeaORM) and `Db::sqlx()` (raw SQLx)
  over the same pool. Neither is a deprecated fallback.
- **Explicit lifecycle:** `Db::connect`, `Db::from_pool`, `Db::ping`, `Db::close`.
- **`Db: Clone + Send + Sync + 'static`** — normal Axum state, no extractor/container.
- **SeaORM Migration** is the single schema authority. No `sqlx::migrate!`.
- **Advisory lock** (`pg_advisory_lock(0x41524354)`) serializes concurrent
  migration runners (closes the gap verified in sea-orm-migration 2.0.1).
- **Session timeouts** applied once per connection via `after_connect`.
- **Credential redaction** — manual `Debug` never exposes username/password/URL.

### Certified stack

- SQLx 0.9.0, SeaORM 2.0.1, sea-orm-migration 2.0.1
- TLS: rustls + aws-lc-rs (no `ring`, no `native-tls`)
- PostgreSQL 15/16/17/18 (pinned minors, no `latest`)

### Testing (54 tests green against live PG 18)

- 17 unit tests (config validation, redaction, SET statement)
- 6 security tests (credential leak across Debug/Display/error chains)
- 6 pool lifecycle tests (saturation, acquire-timeout, recovery, timeouts)
- 12 ORM lifecycle tests (CRUD, relations, N+1, nested writes, cascade)
- 10 SQLx lifecycle tests (raw queries, FromRow, DML, transactions, concurrency)
- 9 migration tests (up/down/status/fresh, failure rollback, advisory lock)
- 4 CLI destructive-command tests (fresh/reset/refresh refuse without --force)

### Benchmarks

- ORM vs SQLx: SeaORM overhead +9% (PK), +39% (multi-row), +78% (transaction)
- Wrapper overhead: zero measurable per-query overhead (field access only)
- Pool contention: p50=1.26ms, p95=4.41ms, p99=10.68ms (pool=4, tasks=16)

### Commits (11)

1. `docs: define phase four database contract`
2. `chore: admit database dependencies`
3. `feat: build single pool database lifecycle`
4. `feat: integrate seaorm data path`
5. `feat: integrate database migrations`
6. `feat: add arc db lifecycle commands`
7. `test: verify postgresql database subsystem`
8. `security: audit database boundary`
9. `perf: benchmark database paths`
10. `ci: certify postgresql matrix`
11. `docs: document arcature database`

### Docs

- `docs/db/{ARCHITECTURE,USAGE,MIGRATIONS,SQLX}.md`
- `docs/security-reviews/phase-4-db.md`
- `docs/performance-reviews/phase-4-db.md`
- `docs/cli/COMMANDS.md` (`arc db` section), `docs/cli/TOOLCHAIN_CONTRACT.md`
- Updated `README.md` and `docs/ROADMAP.md`

### CI

- PostgreSQL 15/16/17/18 integration matrix (pinned minors)
- Generated project build includes `arcature-db` path substitution + migration package
- Windows job includes `arcature-db` path substitution

### Supply chain

- `cargo deny`, `cargo audit`, `cargo vet` recorded in dependency review
- Feature graph: one TLS provider (aws-lc-rs), no `ring`/`native-tls`

author: bbungjun
body:
## 작업 내용

executor의 학습·채점 subprocess가 실패하면 사유 코드만 남고 실제 오류 본문이 사라지던
문제를 고쳤습니다. `capture_output=True`가 자식의 출력을 파이프로 가져가는데 실패
경로에서 아무도 읽지 않아 그대로 소멸했습니다.

실험 #633은 `training_command_failed` 한 줄만 남기고 죽었고, 진짜 원인(ONNX 변환의
`RecursionError`)을 알아내려고 **로컬 재현 20분**이 필요했습니다.

재현 스모크로 확인한 변경 후 로그입니다.

```
ERROR:…training:training command failed stage=train_model:candidate:42 exit_code=1
ERROR:…training:training output stage=train_model:candidate:42 stream=stdout bytes=216
[Step 1] ...
  [OK] 완료
  … (8단계 전부 통과)
ERROR:…training:training output stage=train_model:candidate:42 stream=stderr bytes=354
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "src/pipeline/train.py", line 1035, in _train_from_resolved_dataset
    onnx_model = convert_lgbm_to_onnx(model, n_features)
RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded
```

**어느 조건·seed였는지 · 어디까지 갔는지 · 왜 죽었는지**가 한 자리에 나옵니다.

## 변경 사항

- `training._run`·`measurement._run`의 **세 실패 경로 모두**에 진단을 붙였습니다
  - exit code ≠ 0 → stage + stdout/stderr tail
  - timeout → stage + `TimeoutExpired`가 이미 들고 있던 부분 출력
  - spawn 실패 → stage + `error_type` + `strerror`
- **`stage` 인자를 기본값 없이 필수로 추가**했습니다. `training._run`은 호출 지점이
  다섯인데(seed probe / 데이터셋 다운로드 / `git diff` / `uv sync` / 학습) 사유 코드가
  전부 같고, 수집기가 붙이는 `log_type`도 컨테이너 이름이라(#559) 다섯 단계가 한 값에
  뭉칩니다. 학습·채점은 조건·seed까지 실어(`train_model:candidate:42`) 여섯 실행을
  구분합니다
- **stdout도 남깁니다.** `src/pipeline/train.py`가 진행 단계를 `print()`로 내므로
  "8단계 중 어디까지 갔나"가 stdout에 있습니다. 비어 있어도 `bytes=0` 한 줄을 남겨
  "출력이 없었다"와 "로깅이 깨졌다"를 구분합니다
- **사유 코드는 `args` 하나로 유지**합니다. 본문을 붙이면 `phase2._safe_failure_reason`이
  통째로 `redacted`로 지웁니다
- 공용 헬퍼 `executor/command_output.py`를 새로 뒀습니다 — tail 상한(64 KiB,
  `codex_worker`와 같은 값 #612), bytes 디코드, 스트림별 로깅
- 두 모듈의 **틀린 주석을 사실에 맞게** 고쳤습니다

## 이슈에 없던 두 경로를 함께 고쳤습니다

조사 중에 같은 문제인 것이 확인되어 포함했습니다.

- **timeout**: POSIX의 `subprocess.run`은 이미 수집한 출력을 `TimeoutExpired`에 실어
  던지므로 버릴 이유가 없었습니다. 함정이 하나 있는데 — **`text=True`를 줘도 이 예외의
  출력만은 bytes로 옵니다.** 그대로 찍으면 `b'…'`가 되어 읽을 수 없어 디코드가 필요합니다
- **spawn 실패**: 출력이 없는 실패라 tail로는 잡히지 않습니다. `training_spawn_failed`
  하나로는 "명령이 이미지에 없다"와 "권한이 없다"가 구분되지 않는데 대응이 서로 다릅니다

## 관련 이슈

Closes #636

## 라벨

## 체크리스트

- [x] 코드가 로컬에서 정상적으로 실행된다 (#633 재현 스모크로 출력 확인)

- [x] 기존 테스트가 모두 통과한다 (`2601 passed, 23 skipped`)
- [x] 필요한 경우 테스트를 추가했다 (아래 참조)

- [x] 시크릿/개인정보가 코드에 포함되지 않았다

## 리뷰어 참고사항

### 검증

```bash
uv run python -m pytest                    # 2601 passed, 23 skipped
uv run --no-sync ruff check agent_orchestration autoresearch tests tools
git diff --check
```

### credential 노출을 의도적으로 넣지 않았습니다

실패 본문을 로그로 내보내면 컨테이너 로그가 되고, #648의 수집기가 그것을
`experiment_logs`에 **영구 저장**해 워크벤치에 표시합니다. 유출 경로를 코드로 확인한
결과입니다.

| 경로 | 판정 | 근거 |
|---|---|---|
| 환경 변수에 토큰 값 | 없음 | executor 패키지에 `os.environ[…] =` / `.update` / `putenv` 0건 |
| git remote URL에 토큰 | 없음 | `_clean_remote_url()` + 일회성 `GIT_ASKPASS` |
| GCS 서비스 계정 키 파일 | 없음 | Workload Identity — 키 파일이 존재하지 않음 |
| `uv sync` 인덱스 자격 | 없음 | `pyproject.toml`에 private index 0건 |
| 트레이스백의 지역 변수 | 없음 | 기본 트레이스백은 지역 변수를 출력하지 않음 |
| candidate 코드가 토큰 파일을 읽어 출력 | 구조적으로 가능 | 아래 |

마지막 하나가 남는데, **이 PR이 새로 여는 문이 아닙니다.** 같은 컨테이너
(`candidate-finalizer`)에서 `phase2._log_codex_output`이 Codex #2의 원문 tail을 이미
필터 없이 찍고 있고, 그쪽이 LLM이 쓴 임의 텍스트라 노출 표면이 더 큽니다.

**회수 절차(만약 실제로 노출되면)**: 토큰 회전만으로는 부족합니다. `experiment_logs`의
해당 행도 함께 삭제해야 합니다.

`safety.contains_credential_value()`로 걸러내는 안을 검토했으나 넣지 않았습니다 —
거짓 양성(예: `API_KEY = None` 한 줄) 하나로 실패 본문 전체를 잃고, 그러면 이 PR이
풀려는 문제가 그 케이스에서 되살아납니다. 실제 학습 stderr를 아직 한 건도 관측하지
못한 상태라 마스킹 규칙을 정할 근거도 없습니다(#612이 "요약을 만들 근거가 될 실제
출력을 본 적이 없어 원문 tail로 갔다"고 판단한 것과 같은 상황입니다).

### 별건 제안

`phase2._log_codex_output`은 토큰 3종이 마운트된 `candidate-finalizer`에서 Codex #2의
원문을 무필터로 찍습니다. 이 PR보다 노출 표면이 큰 같은 성질의 구멍이라 별도 이슈로
다루는 것이 좋겠습니다.

### 테스트에서 실제로 잡힌 것

처음 작성한 `_safe_failure_reason` 회귀 테스트는 **가짜였습니다.** 예외를 테스트가 직접
만들어 넘기니 프로덕션 코드를 일부러 깨도(`TrainingError(reason, stderr)`) 통과했습니다.
실제로 던져진 예외를 잡아 넘기도록 고친 뒤에야 돌연변이가 잡혔습니다.
`errors="replace"` 제거 돌연변이도 `UnicodeDecodeError`로 잡히는 것을 확인했습니다.

기존 테스트는 `_run`을 통째로 대역으로 바꾸고 있어서 **subprocess 경계 자체가 한 번도
검증된 적이 없었습니다.** 새 테스트는 실제 subprocess를 태웁니다.

author: tschm
body:
Closes #66.

**Stacked on #67** (docs-only), because it extends the same README section. Base retargets to `main` automatically once #67 merges.

## What it does

Two things, matching where the discussion in #66 landed.

**`solve_qp(..., blas_threads=n)`** — an opt-in, scoped `threadpoolctl` cap that restores the previous limits on exit. `threadpoolctl` stays an *optional* dependency (`pip install cvx-quadprog[threads]`); the argument raises with installation instructions when it is missing, and is a no-op in effect on Accelerate. `Sweep` deliberately gets no such argument: for a batch, one context around the loop is cheaper and more obviously right than one per solve.

**`BlasThreadWarning`** — issued once per process when the configuration measured to collapse is in force. Exported so it can be silenced by category.

## Why there is no default

The `cores/2` default weighed in the issue is rejected, on the numbers already in the thread:

- **The right count differs by BLAS in opposite directions.** OpenBLAS's fast path wants 4 (16 reads 0.05×); MKL's wants 16 and is still improving there.
- **And by path.** Every contributed Windows exact-path sweep is best at `t=1`; `cores/2` costs 1.7–2.1× there.
- **`cpu_count() // 2` is not the physical core count.** Only under 2-way SMT — on @hbailer's non-SMT Core Ultra it would idle half the machine.
- **`threadpoolctl` is not free**, at ~100 µs against a 0.2 ms solve at `n = 10`.

So nothing is chosen on the caller's behalf, and nothing about the process's threading is touched unless asked.

## How the warning is gated

All four must hold, and the verdict is computed once:

| condition | why |
| --- | --- |
| `platform.system() == "Linux"` | Windows degrades mildly (never worse than 0.34×); Accelerate has no knob |
| NumPy reports an OpenBLAS build | MKL at the same 16 threads is 88 ms where OpenBLAS is 7274 ms |
| threads > physical cores | 8 threads on 8 cores measured healthy at 1.07–1.12×, so it is not a fault |
| `n ≥ 200` | the smallest size at which a collapse has been measured — 73.7 ms against 1.53 ms pinned, on the fast path |

Physical cores are **read** from `/sys/devices/system/cpu/*/topology/thread_siblings_list`, not inferred by halving. An explicitly set `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=16` on 8 cores warns like an unset one — the value is right there to compare, and setting it is not evidence of having thought about it.

Detection uses stdlib and NumPy alone, deliberately: a warning aimed at a plain `pip install` cannot be gated behind an extra that a plain install does not have. The price is that NumPy's build config is a proxy for the library actually loaded, so a mixed installation may go unrecognised — a warning that fails to appear, not a false one.

## Cost when nothing is wrong

One function call, one `bool` test and one cached dict lookup per solve — the size test comes after the cached verdict, so `G` is not even touched on a healthy machine. `Sweep` warns at construction rather than per solve, so its hot path is untouched.

## Verification

- 1123 tests pass; coverage stays at **100% of statements and branches**, `_threads.py` included.
- `ruff`, `ruff format`, `mypy --strict`, `ty`, `interrogate` (100%), `markdownlint`, `bandit`, full `pre-commit`: clean.
- `mkdocs build --strict`: clean, with `BlasThreadWarning` added to `docs/api.md` as the export test requires.
- Verified in an environment **without** `threadpoolctl`: a plain solve works, `blas_threads=` raises the install message, and `blas_threads=0` raises `ValueError`.
- The new tests fake all four detection inputs rather than asserting anything about the host, so they behave the same on a laptop and on a 16-thread Linux runner. Size-gate tests are written against the literal 200, not `_MIN_N`, so moving the constant fails a test.

Note: CI's Linux runners are themselves oversubscribed by this definition (4 vCPUs, 2 physical cores), so the pytest warnings summary should show one `BlasThreadWarning` — that is the detection working, not a failure.

## Still open in #66

Unchanged by this PR: reproducing the collapse on our own Linux CI as a regression test, bracketing the threshold between `n = 400` and `n = 800`, the `openblas-openmp` test that would confirm or kill the spin-barrier hypothesis, and whether a distro OpenBLAS behaves like the wheel.

author: davidjlongo
body:
## Summary

`run_mmseqs2` (the ColabFold-derived fallback MSA path, used by `boltz.main.compute_msa` when a protein chain reaches inference without an MSA already assigned) imported `ordaos_structure.msa_client.RedisMSAClient` directly and unconditionally at module load time.

That module is being retired on the `ordaosbio/structure` side — `structure#630`/`#631` migrated every one of that repo's own worker call sites (Boltz, Protenix, af2, esmfold2, promera, rosettafold) onto `ordaos_structure.msa`, a client over the new Info MSA pipeline API (`ordaosbio/engine#2013`). Deleting `msa_client.py` there broke every boltz test in `structure`'s CI — `boltz_worker.py` → `boltz.main` → `boltz.data.msa.mmseqs2` → `RedisMSAClient` import, which runs regardless of whether `run_mmseqs2` is ever actually called for a given job.

## Fix

Reimplements `run_mmseqs2` against `ordaos_structure.msa.get_or_wait` (submit + block until ready) instead of hand-rolling its own submit/poll/download loop against Redis. Same exact signature and return shape as before — one a3m-formatted text block per input sequence, in input order, with homomer duplicates repeated — so `compute_msa` (which parses the alternating header/sequence lines itself into its own `key,sequence` csv) needs no changes at all.

Verified the paired/unpaired conversion and `compute_msa`'s downstream CSV construction locally against a stub `ordaos_structure.msa` module — output matches the original shape exactly for both a fresh chain and a homomer (see PR discussion for the exact test transcript if useful).

body:
💡 What: Wrapped synchronous Supabase python client `.execute()` calls in `asyncio.to_thread(lambda: ...)` in `backend/routers/applications.py`.
🎯 Why: The Supabase python client is synchronous, and executing it directly blocks the main async event loop, reducing concurrency and increasing latency for other endpoints.
📊 Impact: Reduces event loop starvation and significantly increases application throughput under concurrent load.
🔬 Measurement: Endpoints should respond normally, but with better concurrency metrics under load.

author: instazdll
body:
Premier tiers des playlists : **le domaine seul**, sans stockage ni écran.

## Pourquoi découper ainsi

SwiftData est absent de Linux. Écrire le modèle, la persistance et les écrans d'un bloc en semaine, c'est livrer ~500 lignes jamais compilées jusqu'au week-end. Sorti seul, le modèle est réellement exécuté : **62 tests, 5 suites** sous `Tools/LinuxHarness`, plus le typecheck aux drapeaux du projet.

## La divergence structurante

L'ordre est porté par le tableau `songIds`, là où Android tient deux tables Room et une colonne `position`. Les positions ne peuvent donc ni se trouer après un retrait, ni entrer en collision — la couche de persistance les recalculera à l'écriture, elles ne sont pas du domaine. Tout le compactage du `PlaylistDao` disparaît avec elles, et avec lui la moitié de ses tests.

## Ce qui survit et mérite l'œil

- **La normalisation de `reorder`.** L'écran ne liste que les morceaux résolus contre la bibliothèque : un fichier disparu de `Documents` reste dans la playlist sans figurer dans le glisser-déposer. `reorder` écarte les identifiants étrangers et les doublons, puis **replace à la suite les morceaux omis** — sinon un simple glissé les supprimerait au passage. C'est le cas que `reorderOmettantUnMorceauStockeNeLePerdPas` verrouille.
- **`updatedAt` n'est daté que si quelque chose a changé.** Horodatage destiné à la résolution de conflits de la future sync serveur : un ajout en doublon ou un glissé sans effet ne doit pas faire croire à une modification.
- **Les dates sont des paramètres**, pas des lectures d'horloge — les opérations restent pures et les tests déterministes.
- **`id` est un UUID**, pas une clé auto-incrémentée : la sync devra rapprocher deux playlists créées sur deux appareils.
- **`songs(in:)` ignore un morceau absent sans l'oublier** : une bibliothèque encore en cours de chargement viderait sinon toutes les playlists.

## Suite

`PlaylistRepository` (le pendant de `MusicRepository`), le store SwiftData et les écrans — délibérément hors de cette PR, faute de pouvoir les compiler ici. Le protocole n'est pas figé maintenant pour ne pas engager à l'aveugle une API de persistance.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01DvXj4EJikwAswWcnZJaJWP

author: dowoonlee
body:
## 배경

운영 조회가 매번 즉석 SQL이라, 쿼리 로직(특히 `profile_json` JSONB 파싱)이 어디에도 남지 않아 재현이 안 되고 매번 손으로 다시 쓰던 문제. 집계를 뷰로 고정해 버전관리하고, 그 위에 로컬 전용 대시보드를 붙인다.

## 변경

**`supabase/migrations/20260810000000_admin_views.sql` — 집계 SSOT**

| 뷰 | 용도 |
|---|---|
| `admin_overview` | KPI 단일 행 (활성/신규/오늘 제출/미검토 플래그/미수령 보상) |
| `admin_user_progress` | device별 펫·이로치·뱃지·컬렉션·플레이타임 + 서버 권위 값 대조 |
| `admin_daily_activity` | 일별(KST) 활성 디바이스·제출·캡·거부·반영 코인 |
| `admin_abuse_queue` | 플래그 + 계정 나이·누적·7일 제출 패턴 조인 |
| `admin_version_spread` | app_version 분포 (클라 게이트 판단용) |
| `admin_pet_popularity` | 펫별 보유/획득/장착 분포 |

`profile_json`은 클라가 보낸 opaque blob이라 스키마 보증이 없다 — 파싱은 전부 `jsonb_typeof` 가드 + `NULLIF`로 방어적으로 작성했다.

**`admin/` — 로컬 전용 대시보드**

- `server.ts` — 127.0.0.1 바인드 프록시. service_role 키는 `scripts/ranking.env`(gitignore)에서 읽어 브라우저엔 내리지 않는다. `ALLOWED_VIEWS` 밖은 403.
- `index.html` — 외부 의존성 없는 단일 파일(SVG 직접 렌더). 6개 탭, 호버 툴팁 + 표 뷰.
- `README.md` — 실행법, 보안 전제, 지표 해석 노트.

## 보안

`20260716000000_security_invoker_views.sql`의 결론을 그대로 적용했다 — 전 뷰 `security_invoker = true` + anon/authenticated `REVOKE`. 뷰를 DROP+CREATE로 재정의하는 마이그레이션은 이 둘을 반드시 함께 복원할 것.

검증 결과:
- anon 키 → `401 permission denied for view admin_user_progress`
- service_role → `200`
- 화이트리스트 밖(`/api/users`) → `403 view not allowed`

## 릴리스 불필요

클라이언트 `.app` 번들과 무관하다. `package.sh`는 릴리스 바이너리·리소스 번들·Sparkle만 담고, `admin/`은 `Package.swift`의 타겟 경로(`Sources/ClaudeUsage`) 밖이라 빌드 대상도 아니다. 마이그레이션은 이미 프로덕션에 적용된 상태.

## 검증

브라우저로 실제 렌더까지 확인했고, 직접 라벨 충돌(캡·거부가 둘 다 0이라 텍스트가 포개짐)을 잡아 최소 간격 강제를 넣었다.

body:
Three compounding bugs meant the onboarding "restore from cloud" flow
could fail with zero feedback:

- GoogleSignInHelper silently returned when the sign-in Intent had no
  data (common when the account/consent picker is cancelled or
  blocked), never calling onFailure.
- SettingsEffectHandler (mounted globally, including during onboarding)
  dropped ShowSnackbar events entirely; only SettingsScreen rendered
  them, so onboarding had no way to surface sign-in/restore errors.
  Snackbar handling is now centralized in SettingsEffectHandler via an
  overlay rendered above the NavHost.
- A successful restore never marked onboarding as complete, so even a
  fully successful restore + process restart landed back on the
  onboarding screen. AppPrefs.hasCompletedOnboarding is now set before
  the restart, and written synchronously so it survives the immediate
  process exit.

author: ma42517
body:
## El bug que introduje

Al añadir `photo_focus` a la consulta, **la tarjeta compartida dejó de cargar**: mostraba *"Esta tarjeta no está disponible — No pudimos cargarla"*.

Lo detecté verificando en producción con un navegador, justo después de desplegar.

**La causa:** Postgres rechaza la consulta **completa** por un solo nombre de columna que no reconoce. Como tu base todavía no tiene `photo_focus`, la consulta entera fallaba — y un dato accesorio (el encuadre de la foto) dejaba la página inservible.

**Y el respaldo no ayudaba**, porque pedía *exactamente las mismas columnas* que el intento original:

```js
let { data, error } = await read('public_cards', CARD_COLUMNS);
if (isMissingObject(error)) {
  ({ data, error } = await read('profiles', CARD_COLUMNS));  // ← misma lista
}
```

Si lo que faltaba era una columna nueva, **fallaban los dos**. La lección: un respaldo tiene que **quitar aquello que pudo causar el fallo**, no repetirlo.

## El arreglo

Las columnas se separan en **básicas** y **opcionales**, y se intenta en cuatro pasos, de lo completo a lo imprescindible:

1. Vista `public_cards` con todo
2. Vista `public_cards` **sin las opcionales** ← sigue siendo la lectura segura, no expone correo ni rol
3. `profiles` con todo
4. `profiles` sin las opcionales

El orden importa: se agota la vista antes de caer a la tabla, para no perder la protección de columnas mientras se pueda evitar.

## Efecto práctico
Tu tarjeta pública **vuelve a funcionar ahora mismo**, sin necesidad de correr el SQL. Cuando lo apliques, el encuadre de la foto empezará a conservarse; hasta entonces la foto se muestra centrada.

- `npm run build` ✅ · `npm run lint` ✅ 0 errores

author: darshan2139
body:
Wires the two templates that had no caller — the Profile toggles for `task_assigned` and `task_overdue` controlled nothing.

## Assignment mail — 4 call sites

`utils/taskMailer.js` is the single decision point. Two of these I hadn't identified:

| Path | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `createTask` | one mail to the assignee |
| `updateTask` reassign | new assignee only, after the save |
| `bulkTaskAction` reassign | **one mail for the batch**, not one per task |
| `spawnNextRecurrence` | matches the in-app row already typed `task_assigned` |

**Self-assignment never mails** — the common case for an Admin creating their own work.

Deliberately *not* wired into the Gmail sync path: those upsert tasks in bulk during a sync and already emit `email_assigned`, so mailing there would fire one message per synced email.

## Overdue digest — grouping proven on real data

**127 overdue tasks → 11 emails.** Three office-wide, eight personal. The two Heads who also own overdue tasks got exactly **one** email each. Zero overdue → zero mail. Two assignee ids pointing at deleted users were correctly skipped.

Runs hourly and checks the local hour rather than `0 9 * * *`, because node-cron keeps no state and a deploy at 09:05 would silently lose the day. Day-scoped distributed lock held for 26h.

## A defect found and fixed

The Redis client sets `enableOfflineQueue: false`, so a lock command issued before the socket is ready **rejects** — and `lock.js` caught that and silently degraded to a per-process guard. For the 5-minute scan that costs a duplicate row; for a daily digest it means **two replicas each mail everybody**. Reproduced: 22 emails instead of 11.

`lock.acquire()` now reports `via: 'redis'|'local'` and the digest stands down when Redis was configured but did not answer. Re-verified at 11.

## Verified

**372 assertions, 0 failures** (baseline 335 re-confirmed first). New assertions run the real controllers with `sendEmail` substituted — the only way to see what a call site handed the queue — and the server log independently shows 6 real mail jobs reaching the worker over HTTP.

No real mail sent: run against a local DB with the Brevo key blanked.

author: kaneiof
body:
Flutter 3.44 warns that plugins applying the Kotlin Gradle Plugin will fail to build in future releases, because AGP 9 compiles Kotlin itself. Drop the KGP application and the kotlinOptions block, and set jvmTarget through the top-level kotlin extension instead.

This raises the minimum supported SDK to Flutter 3.44 / Dart 3.12. Earlier Flutter versions do not apply KGP on the plugin's behalf, so the Kotlin sources would silently go uncompiled. Apps on older Flutter stay on 2.1.x.

Note that a conditional `if (agpMajor < 9)` guard around the KGP application does not work: Flutter detects KGP usage by regex over the build file text, so it sees the plugin name regardless of the guard and skips applying KGP for us, leaving the sources uncompiled.

Also refreshes the surrounding setup:

- Android dependencies move to their latest versions that still work with compileSdk 36. core-ktx stops at 1.18.0 because 1.19.0 demands compileSdk 37 and AGP 9.1, which would force that on consumers.
- Remove the obsolete package attribute from the Android manifest, which AGP 8 replaced with the namespace build setting.
- Fix the podspec version, still pinned at 2.0.0, and its homepage, which pointed at a different repository than the pubspec.
- Move the example app to AGP 9.0.1 / Kotlin 2.3.20 / Gradle 9.1.0 and align its iOS deployment target with the plugin's 16.0 minimum.

Verified against consumer apps on both AGP 8.11.1 and AGP 9.0.1, plus flutter analyze, the Dart and Kotlin unit tests, and an integration test run on an iOS 26 simulator.

author: singhharsh1708
body:
Found by a reader on a launch thread raising "context contamination" — inactive instructions parked in context. Checking it against our own output turned up a real duplication bug.

## The bug

A repo with both `.agents/` and `.github/` (or `.gemini/`) got **byte-identical** `SKILL.md` files in both places — the exact duplication the comment beside the `agents` adapter claimed could not happen:

> *"agents that also have a native path already get their own adapter, and emitting both would duplicate the skill for no benefit."*

That narrow detection only covers the case where `.agents/` is **absent**, not the common one where a repo has it *and* a native skills directory.

## Why the duplicate is never harmless

Verified against each client's own source/docs:

| Client | Behavior with two copies |
|---|---|
| **Copilot** | Searches `.github/skills` first, dedupes by name → the `.agents` copy is **silently ignored** |
| **Gemini CLI** | Loads the `.agents` alias *after* `.gemini/skills`, overrides it, and prints `Skill conflict detected` **per duplicated name** — noise we were causing |
| **Codex** | Dedupes root *paths*, not skill *names* → **loads the skill twice** |

## Fix

`copilot` and `gemini` yield to `.agents/skills/` when it's written, with a note. A copy left by an earlier version is pruned on the next compile.

**A repo without `.agents/` is unaffected** — Copilot still gets `.github/skills/`. The dedup must never cost an agent its only copy, and that's tested.

## Two unverified claims corrected

The same comment asserted things nobody had checked:
- `.agents/skills` is **not** Codex's only repo path — `<repo>/.codex/skills` also loads at repo scope.
- **Roo, Amp, OpenCode and Antigravity** were listed as readers without ever being verified. Removed; they may well read it, but nothing should assume so.

The readers now named (Codex, Copilot, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Zed, Cline) were each confirmed against that client's own source or documentation.

## Benchmark

The harness read Copilot/Gemini cost from their own skills dirs, which are no longer written when the shared path serves them — it **crashed**, and my first check masked it (`>/dev/null` + `git diff --exit-code` read a failed run as "no change"). Now it reads the path that actually serves them. **Published numbers are unchanged**, the bytes being identical.

7 new tests; two existing assertions updated because they encoded the old duplicated behavior. Suite, typecheck, site `--check` and bench gate green. Ships as 0.22.0.

author: pwalczyszyn
body: ## Problem On the 1.0.4 → 1.0.5 OTA, logs showed the update “applied” while heartbeats kept reporting `version=1.0.4` from the same `start.sh` PID: - OTA always ran the **already-installed** `apply-update.sh` (1.0.4), so the 1.0.5 script fixes never ran during that upgrade - `systemctl stop` failed (no passwordless sudo), and 1.0.4 did not free `:8080` - Files were rsynced and the script still logged `Update to 1.0.5 applied` - The old Node process kept running with `APP_VERSION` captured at startup as `1.0.4` - Panel cleared `desiredVersion`, so there was no automatic retry ## Fix - **Bootstrap** `apply-update.sh` from the downloaded tarball before spawning it (chicken-and-egg fix for apply-script improvements) - **`ota.lock`**: held during apply; `start.sh` waits on it so `Restart=on-failure` cannot bring the app back mid-install when `systemctl stop` is unavailable - **Health check**: wait for `GET /api/info` to report the target version before claiming success; write `ota-result.json` on success/failure for the next process to heartbeat - **Self-heal**: if disk `package.json` version differs from the running `APP_VERSION`, exit so systemd restarts onto the new build ## Recovering devices currently stuck on 1.0.4 Disk may already be 1.0.5 (rsync succeeded) while the old process is still alive. Either: 1. `sudo systemctl restart smartstay` (loads 1.0.5 from disk), or 2. Re-push desired version from the panel — the on-disk 1.0.5 `apply-update.sh` (with `fuser -k`) will run and should restart cleanly Also install passwordless sudoers once per host: ```bash sudo cp /home/smartstay/smartstay-local/scripts/smartstay-systemctl.sudoers /etc/sudoers.d/smartstay-systemctl sudo chmod 440 /etc/sudoers.d/smartstay-systemctl ``` Then release this branch as the next OTA (e.g. 1.0.6).

author: rahulrtg
body:
## Wat dit is

De negen open feature-PR's — #17 (Command), #18 (Bank), #19 (Web Platform), #20 (spellen), #21 (RTG Wereld), #22 (Ondernemers-OS), #23 (RTG Life), #24 (belasting & administratie) en #25 (Mall) — een voor een in volgorde samengevoegd op de actuele main, met elk conflict inhoudelijk opgelost in plaats van mechanisch. Samen ruim 80.000 regels over ~800 bestanden.

## Wat een beoordelaar moet weten

**De conflicten die echt ergens over gingen:**

- **Factuurmotor (`kern/facturatie/motor.js` + `kern/regelsom.js`)** — main deelde de regelsom net met de offertebouwer (één afronding voor beide); #24 haalt het btw-tarief per regel uit de fiscale laag. Verenigd: `regelsom.js` kreeg een optionele tarief-opzoeker (`btwVoorRegel`), de motor geeft die mee. Volgorde: eigen tarief van de regel → fiscale laag → zaaksbreed standaard → 0%. De offertebouwer geeft niets mee en rekent ongewijzigd.
- **`middleware/functieschakelaars.js`** — main's bevoegdheidslaag (de "zesde as") én #19's standaard-uit-reparatie van de snelle uitgang zitten er nu allebei in, in die volgorde.
- **`opzet/kernlaag4.js`** — #20 en #23 waren gebaseerd op de oude inline comm-opbouw; main heeft die intussen in `kernlaag4-comm.js`. De ene échte toevoeging (de naambrug voor RTF-profielen: `commActorNaam` → terugval op `codenaamVan`, anders heetten twee dammende gezinsprofielen "Onbekend") is daarheen overgezet; de rest van de tak-kant was regel voor regel al aanwezig — nagemeten, niet aangenomen.
- **Vijf gids-entries uit #23/#24 waren verouderde duplicaten** van wat `deel1b` al heeft; een dubbele-sleutel-controle over alle gids-delen ving ze (git ziet zoiets niet — een dubbele sleutel is een stille override).
- **`test/reisschermen.e2e.js` / `test/zaal.e2e.js`** — twee takken repareerden dezelfde flakiness onafhankelijk; de main-versie (8 beweringen, met mutatiebewijs in TAKEN.md) is aangehouden.

**Nieuw in deze samenvoeging zelf:**

- `opzet/kernlaag4c.js` — kernlaag4b ging over de 10 kB-grens; de drie kantoorkamers (opvang, afdelingshotel, regering) zijn de naad: de enige bewoners zonder `bankregie`. Gemount ná 4b omdat regering `kern.bank` leest.
- `GRENZEN.json`, `ARCHITECTUUR.md`, `BEWIJS.md` en de bundels zijn opnieuw gegenereerd, niet met de hand samengevoegd.

**Stand van de controles:** `scripts/check.js` groen (alle 42 regels), opstartproef schoon (health 200, gids kent de nieuwe apps, nul fouten in het bootlog). De volle toetsronde (~4500 toetsen) draait op dit moment nog; de uitslag volgt in het gesprek voordat dit naar main gaat.

**Bewust niet meegenomen:** niets — alle negen zitten erin. De vier dependabot-PR's waren al eerder samengevoegd.

author: darshan2139
body:
Read-only audit across all four roles and every module. Document only — no code changes.

**Verdict: do not ship as-is.**

Role isolation is **sound** — no IDOR found. Employee gets 403 on all seven `/api/reports/*`, on `/api/gmail/emails`, `/api/users`, `/api/keyword-rules`; each Head gets 403 (not 404-as-oracle) on the other Head's data.

What's broken cuts across roles: Inbox, Tasks Board + Calendar, Reports, Head dashboards, and 375px.

## Highest severity

1. **Sync reports success while every mailbox fails.** Green "Inbox is already up to date" toast; log shows `invalid_grant` on all four mailboxes every cycle. Mail stops and the app says it's fine.
2. **AI Summarise can never succeed** — client posts `{emailId}`, server reads `{subject, from, body}` → 400. Gemini itself works.
3. **Five of six inbox tabs show the Inbox** — `category` is never read in `getEmails`.
4. **Head dashboard contradicts its own Tasks page** — 6/16/48 vs 7/17/55. Reports scopes `createdBy` only; Tasks uses `createdBy OR assignedTo`.
5. **Client analytics drop 74 of 427 tasks and 212 of 1,397 emails**, on the same screen as the totals they contradict.
6. "All creators" filter silently ignored. 7. Calendar shows empty months. 8. **Rate limits are per-IP — a 15-person office cannot all sign in on Monday morning.** 9. `POST /api/clients` unvalidated. 10. Seven endpoints 500 on a malformed ObjectId.

Plus 13 Medium and 9 Low.

## Method note

A second agent was editing `server/` and mutating the database throughout, so every figure is paired with a same-moment re-derivation. One finding was **withdrawn**: row-checkbox clicks appeared to scroll the app shell, but re-testing through the product's own `j`/`x` keyboard path showed containment works — the first result was an artifact of the browser pane's 0×0 viewport.

author: georgefarrowgreen1
body:
Items 1 and 2 of the offline-upgrades list: the deposit decision carries photo evidence, and a refused replay can no longer vanish.

## Photo evidence on the deposit decision (item 1)

Deliberately cut from the writes phase ("capture the decision, skip evidence in v1") — now closed. The offline deposit-decision form gains a photo field (`capture="environment"` opens the camera; glassForm's new `file` type resolves the File object, not the fakepath string). `odsPhotoData` re-encodes to a ≤1280px JPEG data URI on a canvas; the decision saves either way — the photo is **evidence, never a precondition**.

- The reconnect confirm **shows the photo beside the question it exists to answer** (glassDialog's new `img` option). The shared node is reassigned on every dialog open — the okLabel-leak rule, for pictures — and that is break-tested: setting it only when present leaks the photo into the next plain confirm.
- On OK, the photo rides the confirmed `keep_deposit`/`return_deposit` as `photo_data`. Server-side `deposit_evidence_store` (db.php) **never throws**: JPEG magic bytes checked (nothing arbitrary lands in a web-served directory), 2MB decoded cap, random filename suffix (uploads/ is URL-reachable and damage photos should not be guessable), and any failure leaves the money op standing. Stored evidence gets a `deposit.evidence` activity row naming where it lives, so it shows on the booking hub's Activity card.
- `odsDepSave` sheds the **oldest photos first** if the record outgrows localStorage — a photo is worth less than losing the decisions.

## Refused replays become duties (item 2)

The flush's toast covers the owner who is looking; the SW replay runs with the app **closed**, where a refusal reaches nobody — and a change the owner believes saved but that did not apply is the worst lie the queue can tell.

- IndexedDB `chb-db` goes to **v2** with a `refused` store (app.js `oqDB` and sw.js `swQueueDB` bump together — the loser of a version mismatch gets a VersionError). Both replayers record the refusal (label + the server's own sentence) before consuming the item.
- `chbDuties` surfaces each record as a red Needs-you row saying the change **did NOT apply**; opening it shows the full refusal before it can be dismissed; Dismiss clears the record. Deliberately not wiped on logout — it is a business record, like the queue itself.

## Gates

- **ui-test-offline §13–§14** (14 new checks): the photo round trip end to end (real 1×1 JPEG through the real form → decision stored with the data URI → shown in the reconnect confirm → carried on the confirmed keep → cleared once executed → no leak into the next dialog); the refused-replay arc (queued while dead → server answers 409 → recorded with the server's sentence → Needs-you duty → read-then-dismiss); the SW half as a source assertion (the harness stubs the SW). Break-tested: removing the refusal record, the img clearing, and the photo upload each fail exactly the checks that own them.
- **test-integration §17j** (3 new checks, 215 total): a real JPEG through the real endpoint stores the file + the activity row; a malformed photo is ignored and the refund still stands.
- Full local gauntlet green: smoke, integration (215), payrail, hub, needs-you, search-test, a11y, typecheck, PHPStan 2.2.5. Budgets raised app.js 236100→236800, admin.js 413100→414300, sw.js 5550→5850 after a comment trim — the bytes buy the photo pipeline, the refused store, and the duty surface.

author: kaebmoo
body:
## Summary

- reject `""`, `false`, `0`, and other invalid workflow statuses during HTTP create and pack validation/import
- preserve compatibility defaults: missing/`null` becomes `draft` for API creation and `active` for pack import
- document the exact status contract in OpenAPI, EN/TH API references, and the pack format
- extend the hermetic workflow-status check across HTTP, DB, and pack paths

## Root cause

The shared DB writer used truthiness defaulting (`status or "draft"`), while pack import normalized with `status or "active"` before validation. Invalid falsy values therefore became runnable statuses instead of being rejected.

## Impact

Clients now receive `400` for invalid falsy statuses, matching the published enum. Missing and explicit `null` retain their compatibility defaults.

## Validation

- `python3 scripts/check_workflow_status.py`
- `./scripts/gate.sh` (`completion gate GREEN`)
- `./scripts/lint.sh`
- mutation-tested DB defaulting and pack status validation; both mutations made the hermetic check fail
