author: barmal
body:
## Issue

Follow-up from an on-device screenshot of the Cards home screen ("the card stack needs to be centered on the page, and the preview still fails to render when the settings are in certain ranges") plus a separate report: "the card stack doesn't visually respond to scrolling until after the scroll is completed - it needs to track and react to the finger."

## Scope

**1. Card stack not centered (confirmed by the screenshot) -- shipped.** `CardStack`'s root `Box` never set `contentAlignment`, defaulting to `Alignment.TopStart`. Each entry is a `BoxWithConstraints` that wraps to its own card's size, not the stack's full allotted area, so whenever the card is smaller than the available area, every entry was pinned to the top-left corner. Fixed with `contentAlignment = Alignment.Center` on the root `Box`. Affects every `CardStack` usage: the notification stack, the unfolded rail, and the settings preview.

**2. Card stack doesn't track the finger during a drag -- shipped.** The stack only ever updated its rendered positions when the gesture *settled* (`onSettle`, called once at release) -- `entries` (and every animated offset) stayed completely static for the whole duration of an in-progress drag. Fixed by adding a live, un-animated pixel delta along the stack's own drag/settle axis, updated on every pointer move and added directly to the existing animated settle-axis offset in the render's `graphicsLayer` block -- deliberately *not* routed through `animateFloatAsState`, which would animate toward a constantly-moving target and lag behind the finger instead of tracking it 1:1. Mirrors an already-proven pattern in this codebase (`AdaptiveStageStagePager.kt`'s continuous drag position, written directly during the gesture and only animated on settle). Entirely internal to `CardStack.kt`; `CardStackInteraction`'s public shape -- and every existing caller -- is untouched.

**3. Settings preview "needs more space" -- NOT fixed, reverted to original.** Per the explicit ask to remove the fixed-range guess, I tried `weight(0.4f)` to give the preview an adaptive share of the settings page's real available height (twice, including once with an explicit `heightIn(min)` floor stacked underneath it). **Both attempts broke a real test** (`previewUsesTheLauncherWideReducedMotionPreference`): the preview's `CardStack` silently never composed in that test's compose context (no `fillMaxSize()`/bounded-height wrapper around the page), i.e. `weight()` degenerated toward zero in a way an explicit `heightIn(min)` on the same modifier chain did not prevent. Given two failed attempts and no way to run this locally to understand exactly why, I reverted to the exact `heightIn(min = 280dp, max = 340dp)` range already proven to pass in every context this app places this page in. **The underlying complaint ("still fails to render in certain ranges") is still open** -- this PR just avoids trading it for a strictly worse "never renders in some contexts at all."

## Architecture Decision Records

- ADR: N/A

## Verification

- [x] `./gradlew verify` -- ran in CI across several rounds on this PR; every failure was diagnosed from CI's own logs and fixed or reverted:
  - detekt's `LongMethod` (a threshold `CardStack` was already right at before this PR) -- suppressed, matching the same pattern already used on other genuinely complex composables in this codebase.
  - A missing `fillMaxSize` import -- straightforward compile fix.
  - An accidental deletion of a `var restoreKeyboardFocus` declaration during an earlier edit -- caught as four "unresolved reference" compile errors, restored.
  - The preview-weight regression described above -- caught twice by the same real `androidTest` failure; resolved by reverting rather than continuing to guess.
- Checked every `androidTest` for exact-position assertions the centering change could break: none exist anywhere in the suite; gesture tests use node-relative `Offset`s, not absolute screen coordinates.
- No new tests added for live drag tracking specifically -- it's a pure rendering/interaction change with no new externally-observable state to assert against short of pixel-level rendering, which this sandbox can't produce.

## Definition of Done

- [x] Tests added or updated: none added for the drag-tracking/centering changes (see Verification); the preview-collapse regression I introduced and then reverted was caught by an *existing* test, which now passes again (unchanged from origin/main).
- [x] Settings/default behaviour considered: centering and drag-tracking change rendered behavior for every existing user (fixing bugs that were quietly present). No net behavior change to the preview sizing (reverted to origin/main's exact behavior).
- [x] Accessibility, reduced motion, and permission impacts considered: none of these changes touch reduced-motion handling -- the live drag overlay only applies while a raw pointer gesture is actively in progress, unrelated to the existing settle-animation reduced-motion path.
- [x] Performance impact considered: one additional `MutableFloatState` read per rendered entry per frame during an active drag only; negligible.
- [x] Migration/persistence impact considered: none, no persisted state involved.
- [ ] Manual Android validation documented when local tests cannot cover the behaviour: not performed by me -- see Known Limitations.

## Known Limitations

- Still could not build, run, or screenshot the app in this sandbox (`dl.google.com` blocked). This PR's CI history is a good illustration of that cost: several of its commits exist specifically because a change that looked correct on paper didn't compile, violated a lint threshold, silently deleted a line, or broke a real emulator test -- all caught only once CI actually ran it, and in the preview-sizing case, not resolved even after two attempts. Please look at the live drag-tracking change on a real device specifically -- there's no automated test that can observe "does this visually track a finger."
- The original "preview still fails to render in certain settings ranges" complaint remains open. A real fix likely needs either understanding precisely why `weight()` collapses in that test's specific compose context, or restructuring how this settings page is tested (e.g. wrapping it in the same bounded-height container the real app always places it in) so an adaptive approach can be verified safely.

author: claude[bot]
body:
Closes #1233
Closes #1234

error-triage で原因確定済みの小さいバグ 2 件。どちらもアプリ側だけで閉じており、SQL の除外ルール・共通ライブラリ・他ワーカーの担当ファイルには触っていない。

---

## 件 A: プロフィール作成の check-then-insert 競合（#1233）

### 原因

`app-expo/features/profile/hooks/useProfile.ts` の `createUserProfile` が TOCTOU（check-then-insert）だった。

```ts
// 1. 既存プロフィールを SELECT
// 2. 無ければ INSERT   ← 1 と 2 の間に別の呼び出しが INSERT すると衝突
```

この関数はサインイン直後に **3 箇所から並走し得る**:

| 呼び出し元 | 渡す引数 |
| --- | --- |
| `app/[locale]/auth/callback.tsx` | `displayName` + `avatar` |
| `features/profile/components/OtpModal.tsx` | `displayName` のみ |
| `features/profile/hooks/useEnsureOwnProfileLoaded.ts` | なし（`{}`） |

実ログ: `duplicate key value violates unique constraint "users_pkey"` 1件/1人（2026-08-08）。

**実害はレコードではなく後発の処理**。プロフィール行は先着の INSERT で作られるが、後発は `if (insertError) throw insertError` で catch へ落ちるため、その回の **アバター画像のアップロードと `v1/users/me` への反映が丸ごとスキップ** される。引数を持たない `useEnsureOwnProfileLoaded` が先着すると、OAuth 由来のアバターがそのまま消える。

### 修正内容

- INSERT のエラーが **Postgres の `23505`（unique_violation）だったときだけ** throw せず、「他の呼び出しが一足先に作った」正常系として続行する（PostgREST は SQLSTATE をそのまま `error.code` に載せてくる）。
- 衝突した側も **アバターのアップロードと `v1/users/me` への POST は実行する**。
- 衝突した側は `user_profile_created`（log）を出さず、代わりに `user_profile_create_conflict` を **warn** で残す（起票対象にはしないが並走の頻度は追えるようにする）。
- SELECT は残した。競合していない大多数のケースで無駄な INSERT を避ける先読みで、正しさの担保は 23505 のハンドリング側にある。

### 判断したことと理由

**1. `upsert(..., { ignoreDuplicates: true })` ではなく 23505 の捕捉を選んだ**
どちらも指定された推奨案だが、`ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` は「挿入した」と「無視した」が呼び出し側から区別しづらく、`user_profile_created` を衝突側でも出してしまう（1 行に対してログが 2 件出る）。`23505` を明示的に見る方が分岐が読め、テストでも固定しやすい。

**2. 既存プロフィールの `display_name` は上書きしない**
INSERT は `display_name: displayName || "nickname"` を必ず書き込む。したがって衝突時点の行には既に名前が入っており、後発が上書きすると

- 先着が `useEnsureOwnProfileLoaded`（引数なし）→ 行は `"nickname"`。後発が名前を持っていれば改善するが、
- 先着が名前を持っていた場合 → 後発（引数なし）の上書きは **実名を `"nickname"` に落とす**

の両方が起こり得る。どちらが先着かは呼び出し側から観測できないため、名前の変更はプロフィール編集画面（`v1/users/me`）の責務に寄せ、ここでは触らないことにした。

**3. アバターは上書きしてよい**
衝突時点の行は「たった今別の呼び出しが INSERT したばかり」で、INSERT 文に `avatar_path` が無い以上 **必ず空**。ユーザーが選んだ画像を潰す経路が存在しないので、`display_name` と扱いを分けている。

**4. SELECT で既存が見つかったケース（衝突ではない）の挙動は変えていない**
こちらは「前のセッションで作られた行」で、毎回のサインインでアバターを再アップロードすることになるため、今回の scope 外とした。

**5. #1205 の前例との関係**
先行の二重実行ガード（#1205: `useCreateDishCategoryGroupVote` / `OtpModal` / `DialogProvider` 等）は同期 `ref` による **同一タスク内の連打**対策で、方針は「抑止された 2 発目は throw ではなく黙って返す」。本件はレンダーツリーもタイミングも異なる 3 経路の DB レベルの競合なので ref ガードでは塞げないが、**負けた側をエラーとして扱わない**という結論は揃えている。なお #1205 のコミット群は本ブランチの祖先には入っていない（別ブランチで進行中）ため、コードの共有は行っていない。

### テスト結果

`app-expo/features/profile/hooks/useProfile.test.tsx`（新規, 8 ケース）

- 衝突時に throw せず `user_profile_creation_error` を出さない
- 衝突時でも `uploadFile` と `v1/users/me` の POST が走る
- 衝突時に `display_name` を送っていない（上書きしない）
- 衝突時は `user_profile_created` を出さず `user_profile_create_conflict` を warn で出す
- **衝突以外の INSERT エラー（RLS 違反 `42501`）は従来どおり `user_profile_creation_error` を error で出す**（= 「INSERT のエラーを全部無視する」実装に退化すると赤くなる感度テスト）
- SELECT の失敗（`PGRST116` 以外）も従来どおり error
- 競合なしの通常経路 / SELECT で既存が見つかったら INSERT しない

---

## 件 B: ヘルスチェックの回線起因を error で記録している（#1234）

### 原因

`app-expo/components/HealthCheckInitializer.tsx` の catch が `error_level: "error"` 固定で `health_check_error` を出していた。このうち **レスポンスが 1 度も返ってこなかったケース**（HTTP ステータスを持たない）がトリアージに残っていた。

実ログ（2026-08-06〜08-10）:

```
"Network timeout (30000ms) while calling health"   1件（8/8）+ 1件（8/6）
"Network error while calling health"               2件（8/6）
```

同じ意味の失敗でも `api_call_error` 側は SQL の除外ルール **E3 `client_network`**（`eventName = 'api_call_error'` かつ `feHttpStatus = 0`）で既に落ちており、「イベント名が違うだけで片方は除外・片方は起票」という不整合になっていた。

### 修正内容

`.claude/skills/error-triage/TRIAGE.md` の方針どおり **SQL の除外ルールは触らず、アプリ側でレベルを決める**。

`resolveHealthCheckErrorLevel(error)` を追加（テストしやすいよう named export）。

```ts
export const resolveHealthCheckErrorLevel = (error: unknown): "warn" | "error" => {
	const apiError = error as ApiError | undefined;
	const hasHttpStatus = typeof apiError?.status === "number" && apiError.status > 0;
	return apiError?.code === "network_error" && !hasHttpStatus ? "warn" : "error";
};
```

### 判断したことと理由

**1. 判定条件は `useAPICall.ts` を読んで決めた（推測なし）**

`app-expo/hooks/useAPICall.ts` が投げるものを実際に確認した:

| 状況 | `code` | `status` | 本 PR でのレベル |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| レスポンスが返らない（fetch 失敗 / 30s タイムアウト、`!response` の分岐） | `network_error` | `0` | **warn** |
| メンテナンスモード | `maintenance_mode` | `503` | error |
| 強制アップデート | `unsupported_version` | `426` | error |
| 403 | `forbidden` | `403` | error |
| その他 HTTP エラー（400 等） | `http_error` | 実ステータス | error |
| JSON パース失敗 / 契約違反 | `invalid_response` / `api_error` | 2xx のステータス | error |
| トークン未確立 | `unauthenticated` | **なし** | error |

`code: "network_error"` は `!response`（= レスポンスが 1 度も返らなかった）のときにしか投げられず、そのとき必ず `status: 0` が付く。よってこの 2 条件で「HTTP ステータスを伴わないネットワーク失敗」を一意に特定できる。

**2. `code` だけでなく「ステータスを持たないこと」も条件に入れた**
将来 `network_error` を実ステータス付きで投げる経路が増えたときに黙らないようにするため。この条件は感度テストで固定している。

**3. 一律 warn 化は絶対にしない**
このコンポーネントは **メンテナンスモード(503) と強制アップデート(426) をアプリが知る唯一の経路**（フロントは Remote Config の `is_maintenance` / `minimum_supported_version` を読んでいない）で、#1092 のコメントどおりその検知が壊れたことに気付ける手段が error ログしか無い。`health_check_error` を丸ごと warn にするのが一番簡単な直し方なので、**それをやると赤くなるテスト**を入れてある。

**4. `unauthenticated` のレベルは変えていない**
SQL 側の **E2 `unauthenticated_race`** で既に除外されている（実測 561件/463人/日）ため、アプリ側でも下げると同じ事象への二重対応になる。

**5. `lib/transientHttpStatus.ts`（#1243）にも `lib/logQueue.ts` の `TRANSIENT_STATUSES` にも依存していない**
前者は本ブランチに存在せず、後者は import 先を変えるリファクタがマージ競合を生むため。判定は `useAPICall` の `ApiError` だけで閉じている（`ApiError` は type-only import なので実行時依存も増えていない）。

### テスト結果

`app-expo/components/HealthCheckInitializer.test.tsx`（既存ファイルに 11 ケース追加）

`resolveHealthCheckErrorLevel` の単体:

- `Network error` / `Network timeout (30000ms)` → **warn**
- **503（メンテナンス）/ 426（強制アップデート）/ 400 / `unauthenticated` → error のまま**（一律 warn 化を検出する感度テスト）
- `code: "network_error"` でも `status: 503` を持つなら error
- 素の `Error` / `undefined` は error

コンポーネントが実際に出すログ:

- ネットワーク断は `error_level: "warn"`、かつ `payload.code` / `payload.status` は落とさない
- 503 / 426 は `error_level: "error"`
- `unauthenticated` は `error_level: "error"`（`payload.code` も従来どおり）

---

```
$ pnpm --filter app-expo test
Test Suites: 20 passed, 20 total
Tests:       178 passed, 178 total
Snapshots:   0 total

```
$ pnpm --filter app-expo typecheck
> tsc -p tsconfig.dev.json --noEmit
（出力なし・exit 0）

新規テストが修正を捉えていることの確認として、`useProfile.ts` と `HealthCheckInitializer.tsx` の変更だけを stash して実行し、**13 ケースが落ちる**ことを確認済み（修正を戻すと赤くなる位置にテストが置かれている）。

body:
Prevents workflow validation from failing with exit code 141 when a repository has more than five branches. The diagnostic branch listing now uses `sed`, which consumes the complete input stream and remains compatible with `set -o pipefail`.

Replaces `git branch -a | head -5` with `git branch -a | sed -n '1,5p'` in `.github/workflows/validate-workflows.yml`. Unlike `head`, `sed` reads the entire input stream, so the upstream `git branch` never receives SIGPIPE and genuine validation failures are still detected under `set -euo pipefail`.

author: nd4y
body:
## Timing
Rounds fired on the exact interval and walked configs back-to-back in a fixed order — from the outside that is a burst of N handshakes, in the same sequence, on the dot. Now:

- the round period varies by `jitter` (default ±20%),
- the configs of one round are visited in random order, with random gaps covering `spread` of the period (default half).

Both are document fields, so they are tunable centrally without touching nodes.

Measured on a stubbed run (interval 20 s, 6 configs): order differs every round, configs spread over 3–8 s inside the round, round starts 22.6 s and 16.2 s apart.

## Volume tolerance
The download check answers "how much data does the tunnel pass before it is cut", not "how fast is it". The volume and the source file are now per point — how much a network lets through is a property of that network, not of the fleet. The point page gained "volume to push, MiB" and "volume test source"; empty means the fleet default, so nothing changes for existing points.

Note the source file must be at least as large as the volume being proven — a 1 MiB file cannot demonstrate a 10 MiB tunnel.

author: sukkis
body:
Add a create_directory tool

  Adds directory creation to emed-code's file-access tools, alongside the existing
  read_file/list_files/list_files_recursive/write_file/edit_file. Supports nested (mkdir -p-style) creation
  in one call, is idempotent when the target already exists, and goes through the same diff-and-approve
  confirmation flow as every other write — showing an itemized preview of each directory about to be created
  rather than a single vague prompt.

  Why: Previously, asking the model to put a file somewhere that didn't exist yet had no path to success —
  write_file requires its parent directory to already exist, with no way to create one. This closes that gap.

  Security-wise, nested creation needed its own validation approach rather than a naive create_dir_all:
  symlink-containment checks normally rely on canonicalizing a path that already exists, which doesn't work
  for a not-yet-existing level. The fix rejects ./.. path components upfront (so an unresolvable segment can
  only ever be a literal name) and walks the requested path one component at a time, canonicalizing and
  re-checking containment at every level that does already exist — catching a symlink planted at any depth,
  not just the final one. Content-sensitivity filtering (.env, .ssh, etc.) is applied at every planned level
  too, not just the leaf.

  Also: fixed a couple of stale comments in the local-feature integration tests (claiming a tool "isn't
  advertised" when it now is), added create_directory smoke tests against real Mistral/Ollama, and added just
  mistral/just ollama recipes to run each provider's smoke-test file in isolation. Swapped the README/--help
  example model from codestral-latest to mistral-medium-latest — manual testing found codestral notably
  weaker at tool selection, which matters more here than its code-completion strength.

  Test plan:
  - [x] cargo test (unit + integration, no live services)
  - [x] just mistral / just ollama (real-model smoke tests, including new create_directory coverage) — green
  - [x] Manual TUI testing against both providers: flat and nested create_directory → write_file flows,
  confirmation prompts, decline path
  - [x] README.md/ARCHITECTURE.md/SECURITY.md updated to match

author: fpt
body:
`docs/AUDIO.md` — the plan for what sits under sound port `0x9`, which today
records `SoundEvent { kind, id }` and synthesizes nothing.

**Doc only. No code, no crate, no dependency changes.**

The shape: a host-free `kessel-audio` crate driven by the event log the VM
already emits, rendered by whoever owns an audio device. The VM never produces
a sample; the synth never opens a device — the same boundary that keeps
`kessel-vm` snapshotable.

Decisions worth reviewing, because they're the expensive ones to unwind later:

- **`kessel-audio` depends on nothing; `kessel-vm` depends on *it*** for the
  `AudioEvent` type. That's what makes the crate reusable as a standalone
  instrument — the synth app doesn't link a stack machine, an assembler, and a
  blitter. The reverse direction kills that.
- **Two API layers**: `Synth` (voices, FX, master) for an instrument,
  `AudioEngine` (bank + sequencer + timestamped queue) for the console. One
  `render` serves realtime and offline.
- **Game triggers ride the frame clock; the music sequencer rides the audio
  clock.** A late frame must not stutter the BGM.
- **Patches are ROM metadata**, like `controls {}` and `screen {}` — not ROM
  bytes. Their grammar lives in `kessel-audio`, not `luax.rs`, so the synth app
  needn't link the game compiler.
- **Channel ≠ voice.** `play(inst, note, frames)` is fire-and-forget;
  `note_on(chan, …)` uses a game-owned slot. New device registers latch and
  commit on the register that pops last — the palette's rule.
- **`vm_reset`/`vm_restore`/ROM load emit `AudioEvent::Panic`**, or a rewind
  leaves a reverb tail and doubled music over the new timeline.

Build order puts `kessel render-audio` / `vm_render_audio` at step 4, so the
loop is observable (peak, RMS, clipped samples, voices stolen, event trace)
before any device is opened — the agent can't listen, so that's its observable.

Two costs the doc names but doesn't pay: moving the patch grammar out of
`luax.rs` is a bigger refactor than it sounds, and cpal is the first non-host-free
dep in `crates/cli`, so it wants the same feature treatment `play` already has.

author: keiranholloway
body:
`agent_runs` can already **price** a run — `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, and a `cost_usd` that is
a genuine provider price snapshot from OpenRouter's `usage.cost` rather than a local rate-table
calculation. What it could not say is **who asked**. A run records `agent_name` and an optional
`workflow_run_id`, neither of which identifies the plugin, so *"how much did tenant X spend via
plugin Y last month?"* has been unanswerable — and that question is the prerequisite for any credit
or tiering scheme.

## Why it is small

The plugin identity was already resolved at the exact point the row is created. `request_agent_run`
already takes `principal: ServicePrincipal` and already dereferences it four times; this reads one
more attribute off the same object. Nothing is threaded from the caller, and **no plugin changes.**

**`logical_names`, not `asserted_plugin`.** The former resolves a host-mounted plugin (via the
SigV4-signed `X-Biffo-Plugin` header the host binds) **and** an `isolated: true` plugin from its own
role ARN. The latter is `None` for the second. Both cases have a test, so that choice cannot be
quietly simplified later into something that silently stops attributing isolated plugins.

Because it comes from the verified principal rather than the request body, **a plugin cannot claim
to be another one** — asserted explicitly, since forgeable spend attribution would be worse than
none.

## What this column does NOT tell you

It records **who POSTed the run**. That is narrower than *"which product this run belongs to"*.

The orchestration engine creates fan-in synthesis runs *on a plugin's behalf*, and those record
`system:orchestrator` — correctly, because the orchestrator is what called. So **a per-plugin spend
total built on this column alone under-reports every plugin that uses fan-out/fan-in**, which today
is the main agentic consumer. Attributing a whole chain needs a `causation_id` join as well.

That limit is written into the model docstring, both schemas and the migration rather than noted
once, because the failure mode here is a number that *looks complete and is not* — which is worse
than an absent one.

## Two things the existing tests caught

Worth recording, because both would have shipped silently:

**`_summary` lazy-loaded a deferred column.** Adding the field made it read a column `list_runs` had
deferred via `load_only`, which under async SQLAlchemy raises `MissingGreenlet` rather than returning
`None`. That is the exact hazard the function's own docstring warns about, and the same reason
`dry_run` is already in that list. Both `load_only` blocks now carry it.

**`AgentRunResponse` needed it too**, not just `AgentRunSummary` — the create route returns the
former, so without it the new column was invisible on the one response that proves it was recorded.

## Verification

- `uv run pytest services/api/tests/` — **1373 passed**, 14 skipped
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` / `pyright` on changed files — clean
- Migration `0015` follows `0013`'s nullable template; `test_migration_chain.py` passes
- Four new tests: host-mounted plugin, isolated plugin, spoofing attempt, and a non-plugin caller
  resolving honestly to `NULL`

Refs #1438
Epic: #1436

## Summary

The Sitting J engine extension (spec §4/§5): the context compiler plus registry and typed-projection emission, gated behind the extended-star activation switch. Engine moves to v0.2.0. No contract or transform change in this PR — the emission set stays the 19-file star set against the committed gold v1.1.0.

## What changed

- `src/metricmine/context/compile.py` (new): `build_compiled_context` — pure artifact builder harvesting the governing contracts, keyed by the emitters' own manifest_key literals so C3 passes by construction; `main()` mints `context/compiled/vNNNN.json` + meta sidecar via the profiles/ writer discipline, fail-closed. Deliberately NOT run here: the artifact mints at the v1.2.0 amendment PR.
- `src/metricmine/engine/reader.py`: `load_compiled_context` — newest committed vNNNN, fail-closed on absence and on source-version staleness.

author: taipanbox
body:
it-rat.com **has not published since 08:13 today**. Three pushes since then went green on the merge and red on the deploy. Four commits are live-in-name-only, including the scopyx diagram merged in #11 and the claim removal in it-rat/it-rat.github.io#34.

Two faults, both from the gate wave earlier today, both the same shape: a check wired into an environment it cannot run in.

**1. `deploy-target-current.sh` check 1 can only fail in CI.** It asks whether an `upstream` remote exists and points at the live repository. Actions checks out one repository with one remote called `origin`. The workflow carried a comment saying check 1 was "skipped here by construction". It was not skipped, it failed, on every run.

Now skipped when `GITHUB_ACTIONS` is set, and skipped **loudly**, for the same reason check 3 is. Checks 2 and 3, the two a workflow can answer, still run.

**2. The `gates-have-teeth.sh` step had no `GH_TOKEN`.** It runs the two network gates as its baseline before mutating anything, so `demo-bundle-current.sh` could not reach the API, came back red on a clean tree, and every case standing on it reported `UNJUDGEABLE`. The harness worked; it is the only reason the failure was readable.

## Reproduced before fixed

In a fresh shallow clone of the live repository with only `origin`, which is the shape CI makes:

```
GITHUB_ACTIONS=true ./scripts/deploy-target-current.sh
  FAIL no upstream remote in this clone
GH_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/empty GH_TOKEN= ./scripts/demo-bundle-current.sh
  FAIL: could not ask TAIPANBOX/genaryx for its current apps/web commit
```

Both green in that same clone with the fix and a token. `gates-have-teeth.sh` still 9 of 9 locally.

body:
Resolves neomjs/neo-agent-brain#48

Related: neomjs/neo#16830

Native Ollama embedding callers now settle independently from already-dispatched provider work: `TextEmbeddingService` refuses pre-aborted calls, stops forwarding a later caller signal into the provider request, returns the exact caller-owned reason promptly, and keeps the provider activity open until response or the existing provider timeout. Native readiness warms now dispatch without an abort signal, coalesce identical in-flight work, and return an explicit `pending` disposition when only the readiness wait expires. The intervention-shaped inference health probe and its obsolete classifier are retired; safe container detection and recovery remain in neomjs/neo#16830.

Evidence: L2 (150 focused unit controls, syntax/alignment gates, and zero surviving production canary references) → L4 required (AC4, AC5, and AC10 exact CPU-only natural/early-cancellation witness). Residual: AC4, AC5, AC10 [#16853].

## Deltas from ticket

- The direct `Ollama.embed({signal})` API remains unchanged for independent callers whose contract is transport cancellation. The repaired boundary is the production `TextEmbeddingService` composition, which no longer presents caller-local settlement as provider settlement.
- Readiness deadline expiry is not classified as provider failure. It returns `OLLAMA_WARM_PROVIDER_PENDING`, preserves a handled provider promise, and coalesces by exact host, role, model, context, and keep-alive shape.
- `/api/ps` remains residency/control-plane evidence only. The unsafe `/api/chat` inference canary is removed rather than renamed into a misleading serving check.
- The issue marks its external Ollama controls as L4-deferred; this PR does not claim that unit tests reproduce the four-core host outcome.

## Test Evidence

- Native embedding caller/provider composition: `npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/ai/services/memory-core/TextEmbeddingService.spec.mjs --workers=1` → 25 passed.
- Full touched-surface set: `npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/ai/services/memory-core/TextEmbeddingService.spec.mjs test/playwright/unit/ai/scripts/runners/runSandman.spec.mjs test/playwright/unit/ai/daemons/orchestrator/Orchestrator.invariants.spec.mjs test/playwright/unit/ai/services/graph/providerReadinessHelper.spec.mjs --workers=1` → 133 passed.

author: dhsorens
body:
Addresses #11575 (does not close it — see *What remains*).

## The issue's premise is stale: all 8 forks already exist

#11575 asks to fork `header_extract_number`'s pattern to its 8 mechanical siblings. **All 8 already carry a sorry-free whole-routine triple.** What was actually missing is *registration*.

Verified against `main` at `372162cc2`:

| | State on main |
|---|---|
| `header_extract_logs_bloom` | already a `.proven` row (`Routines.lean:227`) |
| `header_validate_extra_data_length` | already a `.proven` row (`Routines.lean:237`) |
| 6 forkable `chain_validate_*` | `*_spec_within` triple present in each `…LoopClose` module; **zero `sorry` across the whole `ChainValidate*` family**; no registry row, no correspondence row, no axiom witness |

That last line is the #11637 row-existence class — proven work counting toward nothing. `scripts/registry-coverage-allow.txt` already recorded all six, *and* graded them: 2 tier A ("registrable as .proven, not yet rowed"), 4 tier B ("needs `Fn.retSpecFlat` before a `.proven` row is honest").

`header_extract_number`'s own row note generalises: *a missing row was never evidence of a missing proof.*

## What this PR does

Registers the **2 tier-A** routines and drains their allowlist entries — required, not optional, since an entry goes STALE and fails the run once its symbol gains a row.

- **`chain_validate_consecutive_numbers`** — 93-instruction cross-header accessor; RLP field 8 (`number`) consecutive across adjacent headers (`num[i] = num[i-1] + 1` in `BitVec 64`). Three-way post, total over the header list: all-consecutive / first-violation / first-parse-failure, each header's number genuinely decoded via K34's `Result`.
- **`chain_validate_increasing_timestamps`** — same frame, hypothesis set and post shape over the timestamp field.

**Graded against the rubric, not assumed.** `.proven` and not `.conditional` because every hypothesis is resource/ABI: `hspC` (frame base), `hret` (ret alignment), `hnWord` (definitional), `hN : lengths.length < 2 ^ 64`, and six `hAll*` per-header alignment / length / slack / non-overflow / `isValidByteAccess` facts. `Routines.lean`'s own header: these "are the ABI, not a gap, and do **not** make a row `.conditional`". There is no input-domain gate.

Both witnesses report `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, read back from the build log.

One divergence is recorded in the row note rather than left to be discovered: `consecutive_numbers` proves the `+1` step in `BitVec 64`, which matches the execution spec on all reachable block numbers — the wraparound at `num[i-1] = 2^64-1` has no u64-decodable successor.

## Counts

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| routine registry rows | 33 | 35 |
| `.proven` routine rows | 24 | 26 |
| distinct symbols | 23 | 25 |
| axiom witnesses | 145 | 147 |
| registry-coverage uncovered / allowlisted | 95 / 95 | 93 / 93 |

## What remains — why I did *not* do the rest

**The 4 tier-B routines stay allowlisted** (`blob_gas_used_multiple`, `blob_gas_used_under_max`, `extra_data_length`, `gas_used_under_limit`). PLAN.md is explicit that grading a tier-B spec `.proven` to drain the allowlist "converts a visible backlog into a false census, which is the defect the gate exists to prevent." They need `Fn.retSpecFlat` first.

**No `Correspondence.lean` rows**, though the issue asks for them. A row there needs a `_of_decode` bridge tying the machine triple to `SpecRef` — compare `header_extra_data_length_of_decode`, whose row carries a full port-fidelity clause table. This family has no such bridge, so a row would be `.machineOnly` at best, and asserting a verdict I have not derived is exactly what that registry exists to prevent.

So #11575 should stay open, but its description is worth rewriting: the remaining work is `Fn.retSpecFlat` for four routines plus six correspondence bridges, not eight forks. Happy to retitle/re-scope it if you agree.

## Gates

`lake build` (4726 jobs, green) + check-progress, check-drift, **check-registry-coverage** (OK — 93/93), **check-registry-crosscheck** (OK, 25 witnessed symbols; `--self-test` fires), check-routine-liveness, check-forbidden-tactics, check-unimported, check-file-size, check-layering, check-heartbeats-approved, check-statement-tamper — **all pass**. PROGRESS.md and DRIFT.md regenerated.

`check-axioms.sh` **cannot run in this checkout** and I'm not claiming it: `scripts/lib/worktree-build-lock.sh` needs `flock` (absent on macOS) plus GNU `sha256sum`. CI is the authority; the two new axiom reports are quoted above from the build log.

No new proofs, no guest bytes; `.text` unchanged.

body:
Prevents workflow validation from failing with exit code 141 when a repository has more than five branches. The diagnostic branch listing now uses `sed`, which consumes the complete input stream and remains compatible with `set -o pipefail`.

Replaces `git branch -a | head -5` with `git branch -a | sed -n '1,5p'` in `.github/workflows/validate-workflows.yml`. Unlike `head`, `sed` reads the entire input stream, so the upstream `git branch` never receives SIGPIPE and genuine validation failures are still detected under `set -euo pipefail`.

author: ctol3r
body:
## What production actually did

#1306 deployed and the board filled — **188 opportunities, every single one from `onemedical`.** The other eleven employers were never fetched.

```
organizations:
  onemedical: 188
```

I predicted 454 across 12 employers. The gap was the bug.

## Cause

The fetch loop broke out as soon as the running total reached the limit:

```ts
for (const board of this.boards) {
  if (listings.length >= limit) { allBoardsSucceeded = false; break; }
  …
}
```

`onemedical` returns ~339 listings in a single response. It filled the 200-row budget on iteration one, so `twochairs`, `charliehealth` and the rest were **never requested at all**. Roster *order* silently decided which employers existed — and the roster read like twelve while behaving like one.

Second-order effect: because the run always ended with `complete: false`, **expiry never ran**, so stale rows would never close.

## Fix

Every board is read, then the limit is applied by taking from each in turn. Twelve explicit tokens is not an unbounded pull — the roster is what bounds this feed — so the ceiling should govern how many rows are *kept*, not which employers get *asked*.

Verified against the live API, same 200-row budget:

| before | after |
|---|---|
| 188 rows, **1 employer** | 200 rows, **8 employers** |

```
onemedical     72     firsthand       12
twochairs      71     parsleyhealth    4
charliehealth  32     valerahealth     4
                      galileo  3 · midihealth  2
```

`complete` is now true only when every board answered **and** nothing was dropped to fit the limit — so expiry can conclude when a run genuinely saw everything, and still cannot conclude after an outage.

## Verification

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| Ingestion suites | **65 passed** (was 60) |
| **Injection** — restore `break` once the budget is spent | **2 red**, restored green |
| `tsc --noEmit` | clean |
| Live API | 200 rows across 8 employers |

New cases pin the defect directly: one asserts every board is *requested* even when the first exceeds the limit (`fetch` called 3×), another asserts a small board still gets rows against a much larger one, and `roundRobin` has its own tests including termination on empty input.

## Note on how this was found

Not by a failing test — the wave was green and merged. It surfaced from checking what production actually contained after deploy, and noticing 188 ≠ the 454 I'd claimed. The number being *lower* than predicted is what made it visible; had `onemedical` been smaller, the same bug would have shipped looking correct.

author: waterwang
body:
## What

Wrap the `IAuthenticationManager.authenticate()` call in the NACOS/LDAP login branch with a try-catch that returns a unified `401 Unauthorized` response on any authentication failure.

## Why

The `/v1/auth/login` and `/v3/auth/user/login` endpoints leak whether a username exists by returning different HTTP status codes:

- **Non-existent user**: returns `HTTP 500` with body `caused: User xxx not found`
- **Existing user + wrong password**: returns `HTTP 403` with body `User not found! Please check user exist or password is right!`

This side-channel allows unauthenticated attackers to enumerate valid system accounts (username enumeration vulnerability).

## Fix

Catch `AccessException | RuntimeException` (which covers both `AccessException` from wrong-password and `UsernameNotFoundException` as a `RuntimeException` from non-existent users) and return a unified `HTTP 401` with the generic message `"Login failed"` for both cases.

Apply the same fix to both:
- `UserController.java` (v1 endpoint `/v1/auth/login`)
- `UserControllerV3.java` (v3 endpoint `/v3/auth/user/login`)

Fixes #15682

author: azarquiel
body:
Dos constantes del render de Gaia aplastaban información que el cálculo ya tenía bien. Las dos salieron observando, no leyendo el código.

## El fondo de cielo no distinguía un sqm 21 de un sqm 22

`SB_CIELO_NEGRO` valía 22,5, y el clamp de `nivelCielo()` pintaba del mismo negro cualquier fondo por debajo de esa cifra. En un 18" a 158x la pupila de salida (2,9 mm) y la transmisión restan 2,3 mag, así que sqm 21 llega al ojo a SBe 23,3 y sqm 22 a 24,3: los dos bajo el suelo, los dos idénticos en pantalla.

El observador los separa de sobra — con ese equipo distingue 21,2 / 21,4 / 21,6 / 21,8 — porque el ojo adaptado no tiene un suelo absoluto en 22,5. Ese número no era el umbral de nadie, era un redondeo.

Con **24,5** el rango se abre donde de verdad se observa, y sqm 22 queda en 6 niveles (0,03 % de luminancia: negro con cualquier luz ambiente), que casa con el otro extremo de lo reportado — 21,8 y 22 ya no se separan. La saturación hacia el negro no se modela: la aporta la gamma del monitor, que comprime los códigos bajos.

En el 18" a 158x:

| sqm | 22,0 | 21,8 | 21,6 | 21,4 | 21,2 | 21,0 | 20,0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| antes | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| ahora | 6 | 12 | 19 | 25 | 32 | 38 | 70 |

## El salto de brillo entre dos estrellas salía comprimido

`rangoBrillo` valía 12, y `flujoDeValor()` lee ese mismo intervalo 0-1 como `SB_NEGRO - SB_BLANCO` = 11,5 mag. La rampa metía 12 magnitudes donde la conversión de vuelta esperaba 11,5, así que cada magnitud real se pintaba como 0,958: mag 8 contra mag 10 daba **5,84x en vez de 6,31x**.

La aureola, que usa `10^(-0,4g)` directo sin rampa, sí daba 6,31x — disco y aureola de la *misma* estrella iban en escalas distintas.

Ahora `rangoBrillo` se **deriva** de `SB_NEGRO - SB_BLANCO`. Es la misma cantidad física (cuántas magnitudes caben en los 0-255 de la pantalla) escrita dos veces, así que si se tocan esas constantes acompaña sola.

Con eso el salto entre dos magnitudes es exacto y **no depende del equipo**: el `mlim` se cancela al restar dos estrellas.

| | mag 8 vs mag 10 |
|---|---|
| 18" f/4.5 a 158x | 6,3096x |
| 8" f/10 a 156x | 6,3096x |

## Tests

Bloque 17 nuevo en `test_difuso.js`: el 6,31x en ambos equipos, la ley de 2,512x por magnitud en 56 puntos de 4 equipos distintos, el residuo del `-1` acotado al 2 %, y — el que de verdad importa — que `rangoBrillo` **es** el rango de tono y no un número que se le parece.

`test_consulta_gaia.js` recibe el invariante que destapó todo esto: una estrella justo en `mlim` se pinta con el mismo alpha y el mismo tamaño en un 18" que en un 8", que es lo que hace que `mlim` signifique lo mismo en cualquier equipo.

Pasan los 38 scripts de `scripts/` salvo `test_salud_globo.js` y `test_segundo_auxiliar.js`, que **ya fallaban en `main`** antes de esta rama (verificado con stash) y van de otra cosa.

## Lo que hay que mirar en pantalla

`SB_CIELO_NEGRO` sube el suelo sobre el que se suma todo lo demás (`pintarFot`), así que el contraste percibido de lo difuso baja aunque el incremento físico no cambie. Es una perilla artística, no una calibración, y depende de la luz ambiente de quien mire. Merece un par de campos difusos conocidos antes de mezclar.

- [ ] ❓ Other (please specify)

## Related Issue

Fixes #3038

## Describe this PR

Wires Field-TM into the shared HOT login (Hanko SSO), the same way the other
HOT apps do it.

Until now the header had its own `<wa-button id="login-btn">` that redirected to
the login page by hand, and the `<hotosm-auth>` web component was hidden away in
a `display: none` div purely to validate the session after the redirect back.
This PR drops the custom button and puts `<hotosm-auth>` in the header slot
directly, so the shared component renders both states: the login button when
logged out, and the user profile dropdown with logout when logged in.

Two things run off the component's `hanko-login` event, both guarded so
navigation doesn't re-trigger them:

1. **User sync** — registers/syncs the authenticated user into the Field-TM
   database via `/api/v1/auth/profile/me`, once per browser session
   (`sessionStorage`). Same behaviour as before, just moved.
2. **Language adoption (#3038)** — reads the user's language from their HOT
   login profile and applies it via `?lang=`, which the existing locale
   middleware persists into the `ftm_locale` cookie. This is one-way
   (login → Field-TM) and only fires when the profile language *changes*: we
   remember the last value we saw in `localStorage`, so a profile change shows
   up on the next load, while a manual choice in the language switcher is
   respected as long as the profile language stays put.

On logout both flags are cleared, so a different user logging in on the same
browser gets a fresh sync and their own language.

Also included: a `deploy-testlogin.yml` workflow and `compose.testlogin.yaml`
that stand up the test environment described below, pointing at
`dev.login.hotosm.org`.

## AI Tool Usage

- [ ] No AI tools were used
- [x] AI tools were used (complete below)

**If AI-assisted:**

- Tool(s) used: Claude Code (Claude Opus 5)

## Screenshots

N/A — the header login button and profile dropdown are the shared component's
own UI, unchanged apart from the brand colour noted below.

## Alternative Approaches Considered

**Theming the login button.** The obvious way to colour it was
`--login-btn-bg-color: var(--ftm-brand)`, but `--ftm-brand` is itself
`var(--hot-color-primary-600)`, and that nested indirection resolves
inconsistently once inherited into the component's shadow DOM — it fell back to
gray-600. So the CSS sets the HOT red as a literal `#d73f3f`. Only the login
button is affected; the profile dropdown keeps the component's defaults.

**Syncing language both ways.** Deliberately not done. Pushing a Field-TM
switcher choice back up to the login profile would make the central profile
mutable from every app, and two apps disagreeing would fight over it. One-way
adoption with change-detection gives the useful behaviour (your profile language
follows you into Field-TM) without that.

## Review Guide

**A live test environment is deployed from this branch:**
👉 **https://fieldtm.testlogin.hotosm.org**

It runs against `dev.login.hotosm.org` for auth, so you can log in with a dev
Hanko account and exercise the whole flow without touching production. It
redeploys automatically on every push to this branch.

Worth checking there:

- Logged out → the header shows the red **Login** button; clicking it takes you
  to the central login page and returns you to where you were.
- Logged in → the button is replaced by the profile dropdown, and logout works
  from it.
- First login → the user appears in the Field-TM database (the profile sync).
- Set a language on your HOT login profile, then reload Field-TM → the UI
  switches to it.
- Then change the language with Field-TM's own switcher and navigate around →
  your manual choice sticks, it doesn't get overwritten on every page load.
- Log out and back in as a different user with a different profile language →
  you get theirs, not the previous user's.

author: draper1
body:
# Description

Adds SLA domain support for Azure Postgres flexible servers, in two commits:

1. **The object type.** `AZURE_POSTGRES_FLEXIBLE_SERVER_OBJECT_TYPE` added to the SLA `ObjectType` constants and to `AllObjectTypesAsStrings`. This is distinct from the existing `POSTGRES_DB_CLUSTER_OBJECT_TYPE`, which covers self-managed Postgres DB clusters rather than the Azure managed service.
2. **The object-specific configuration.** `AzurePostgresFlexibleServerConfig` with `BackupRetentionInDays`, wired into `ObjectSpecificConfigs` as `azurePostgresFlexibleServerConfigInput`.

`BackupRetentionInDays` is the point-in-time restore retention RSC enforces on the source server, 7 to 35 days. Zero leaves the server's existing Azure-side retention untouched, which is also the effect of omitting the configuration: the backend resolves an absent config and a zero retention to the same no-op.

**Review note:** gofmt realigned the `ObjectType` const block in the first commit and the `ObjectSpecificConfigs` struct in the second, because both new names are longer than any existing one. Use `git diff -w` to see the lines that actually changed.

## Related Issue

No existing issue. Second of three stacked SDK PRs; based on #406.

## Motivation and Context

The Terraform provider validates `polaris_sla_domain`'s `object_types` against `AllObjectTypesAsStrings()`, and reads object-specific configuration off `ObjectSpecificConfigs`, so both pieces are needed before an SLA domain can protect Postgres flexible servers.

The configuration was initially missed. It is required because RSC models the flexible server's PiTR retention as SLA state rather than as a property of the server, so an SLA without somewhere to put it cannot manage retention at all.

## How Has This Been Tested?

* `gofmt`, `go build ./...` and `go test ./pkg/polaris/graphql/sla/...` clean.
* Verified through the Terraform provider against a live RSC deployment: a `polaris_sla_domain` declaring this object type plans cleanly, which exercises the provider's validation against `AllObjectTypesAsStrings`.
* The field name and semantics were taken from the RSC schema and the backend's own retention resolution, cross-checked against the mutation the RSC UI issues when creating a Postgres SLA.

Not yet exercised: creating an SLA domain with the configuration populated against a live deployment. The provider-side block that would drive it is in a follow-up PR.

## Notes for the provider side

Two constraints come from the backend and the RSC UI rather than the schema, and the provider PR enforces them:

* A Postgres flexible server SLA **cannot be combined with other object types**. The RSC UI disallows it.
* A backup location is **mandatory**. The Postgres object adapter reports `SupportsMultipleBackupLocations` true and `SupportsMultipleArchival` false, so these SLAs use `backupLocationSpecs`, not the legacy `archivalSpecs`.

body:
Closes `BACKLOG.md` §1 NEW-5, NEW-8 and NEW-6. Independent of PR #2 — this branch is cut from `origin/feat/foundation` and touches no file that PR carries.

## Why these three

`ORDER.md` NOW is A7, whose **S gate is awaiting the founder's approval** on #2. Track B is the founder's legacy machine, Track L is the founder and their counsel, and NEW-7 needs a machine with Obsidian. These three were the whole of what an agent could finish alone.

Each is a place where two parts of the product disagreed with each other:

| | Defect | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| NEW-5 | `index-drift` wrote its line number into English and set `line: null`; every other class uses the field | the field carries it; the prose is gone; the field's contract now defines the frame for a generated artifact as well as a note |
| NEW-8 | `contentRoot` was wrapped in a code span, and escapes do not work inside one, so a backtick in the value closed it | plain escaped text, the way the tag cloud below it already does |
| NEW-6 | `duplicates` grouped titles on raw bytes while `catalog.md` renders the *screened* form, so two byte-identical rows were reported as no duplicate | the grouping key is screened first, then NFC-folded; spec §7 amended in place and registered in BACKLOG §8 |

- `npm run check` green at every commit — 821 passing, 1 skipped.
- Fresh-context review by an agent that did not write the code. Six findings, all addressed in `ebd5634`; the tree was verified untouched by the reviewer before and after.
- The most serious finding was documentation, not code: `docs/architecture/brain.md` still described two of these defects as open, in a file `ORDER.md` makes mandatory reading before touching Brain code.

- **One new backlog item, NEW-10**, found by the review: `note.ts` accepts a title made only of invisible characters, because `trim()` removes neither U+200B nor U+00AD. XS, recorded rather than fixed here — it is a validation gap, not a lint one.

author: mortonanalytics
body:
Autonomous scheduled `backlog-pipeline` run. Closes #40 (opened this same run by the scheduled `idea-scout inbound` pass, from cross-repo signal `morton-analytics-llc/eo#316`).

## Provenance

Weekly scheduled maintenance run (`idea-scout inbound` → `backlog-pipeline next`), no live human input this session. `eo#316` (a Codex review finding from eo's 2026-08 validation pass) named this as a "vendor change — dolphinRust upstream, pointer bump into eo," which `idea-scout` turned into dolphinRust#40 and labeled `backlog-ready` directly (Build-now: clear, well-scoped, no external blocker).

## The gap

`SpatialProducts::timeseries_residual_rad` (→ `timeseries_residual_rms.tif` / `DisplacementOutput::timeseries_residual_rms`) was populated from the L2 SBAS **network-inversion misclosure RMS** (residual of `A·φ = Δφ` — how well the interferogram network closed), not from the **temporal motion-model fit residual** the name implies (the per-pixel scatter of displacement around the fitted velocity model). `dolphin-timeseries` already computed the correct quantity internally (`VelocityOutput::residual_rms`, `estimate_velocity_with_model`'s `residual_rms`) — `fit_velocity` in `dolphin-workflows` just discarded it before it reached `SpatialProducts`.

Two concrete consequences on `main`:
1. On the default `TimeseriesMethod::L1` path, and plain L2 without `write_posterior_uncertainty`, the raster was **absent entirely**.
2. Where present (L2 + `write_posterior_uncertainty`), it answered "did the network close," not "does displacement fit the model" — the two can and do diverge.

## Fix

- `VelocityFit` gains `residual_rms: Option<Array2<f64>>`, populated on every velocity path that computes a model fit (weighted linear, seasonal, step). `None` only on the unweighted-linear fast path, matching `sigma`'s existing `None` rule there (that path computes no fit statistics at all).
- The weighted-linear-without-`write_velocity_uncertainty` branch now calls `estimate_velocity_with_uncertainty` instead of `estimate_velocity_with_precisions` — bit-identical velocity output, but the residual that fit already computes is no longer thrown away.
- `InversionProducts::residual_rms` → `network_misclosure_rms` (same value, honest name). `SpatialProducts`, `ScaledOutputs`, `QualityLayers`, and `DisplacementOutput` each gain a distinct `network_misclosure_rad`/`rms` field alongside the now-correct `timeseries_residual_rad`/`rms` field.
- `write_outputs` emits a new `network_misclosure_rms.tif` alongside the existing `timeseries_residual_rms.tif` name (which now carries the fixed meaning).
- `trim()`'s bounded-target re-fit path now also refreshes `timeseries_residual_rad` after re-referencing (re-referencing shifts the displacement series, which shifts the temporal-fit residual; the network misclosure is unaffected, computed upstream of re-referencing).

## Red → green

New analytic contract `network_misclosure_and_temporal_fit_residual_are_decoupled` (`dolphin-workflows/src/displacement.rs`): builds an over-determined (redundant) network whose interferograms are exactly consistent with a true phase history (misclosure ~0), where that same true history contains a late jump that a linear velocity model fits badly. Confirmed RED first — referencing `VelocityFit::residual_rms` / `InversionProducts::network_misclosure_rms` failed to compile before the fields existed — then GREEN after implementing: network misclosure `< 1e-9`, temporal-fit residual `> 0.5`, proving the two quantities move independently rather than sharing one number.

## Verification (real exit codes, no `tail` piping)

```
cargo check --workspace --no-default-features --features no-gpu         # exit 0
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --no-default-features \
  --features no-gpu -- -D warnings                                       # exit 0
cargo test --workspace --no-default-features --features no-gpu           # exit 0, 0 failed across every suite
cargo fmt --check                                                        # exit 0
```

`dolphin-workflows` lib tests: 42 passed (including the new contract). Full workspace `cargo test`: every `test result: ok` line, zero `FAILED`, zero `error` lines.

## Numeric risks / caveats

- **Breaking output-schema change.** A consumer reading `timeseries_residual_rms.tif` for the *old* (network-misclosure) meaning must switch to the new `network_misclosure_rms.tif`. Flagged in `CHANGELOG.md` under `### Fixed`. `eo#316` item 2 names `gp-dolphin::sample_output` as the direct consumer — that side needs its own coordinated pointer-bump pickup, out of scope here.
- The unweighted-linear fast path still reports `residual_rms: None` by design (documented in code and `docs/usage.md`) — computing a fit residual there would mean fitting a second model per pixel on the cheapest, highest-volume path just to report a number nothing currently asks for. Flagged as an open question in dolphinRust#40 itself if a future consumer needs it.
- `oracle/fixtures/*` is gitignored in this environment, so the existing fixture-gated end-to-end test (`l2_uncertainty_products_are_opt_in_and_unit_aligned`, extended here to also assert `network_misclosure_rms.tif` + both `DisplacementOutput` fields) skips locally; the analytic contract is the load-bearing proof for this PR.
- Documentation updated in lockstep: `docs/usage.md`'s output-schema tables, `README.md`'s quickstart raster list, and `VALIDATION.md` (a historical-note added, not rewritten, at the one section whose analysis specifically concerns the pre-rename raster name).

## Hard boundaries respected

No merge, no `../eo` submodule pin bump, no release tag — stopping at this open PR per the scheduled run's instructions.

author: davisdelivery
body:
**ONE DIVERSIFIED would not scan on Mandi's truck.** The gun read both barcodes — verified by scanning them into a notes app — and the app did nothing at all. No sound, no message, no count.

Having to leave the app and scan into something else to find out what the gun sent is a diagnosis nobody should run on a dock at 5am.

## Two blind spots

**1. The raw log was camera-only.** `rawLog` was fed from `startScanner`'s `onRaw`, and the "Scanner detail" panel rendered behind `{camOn ? …}`. In gun mode the app kept **no record of a single read** and displayed nothing — so a barcode it didn't recognise left no evidence anywhere on screen.

Every gun read is now logged and classified *before* anything can drop it, and the panel shows for the gun too.

**2. An unrecognised barcode was silent.** `classifyBarcode` wants exactly 7 digits for a PRO, or `OG` + 10 digits for a piece ID. Anything else — a check digit, a prefix, another symbology on the pallet — went into `pairFrame`'s `unknown` bucket and was discarded without a word, while the gun beeped happily on every read.

That combination reads as *"the app is ignoring me."* It now plays the orphan tone and **names the exact string** it couldn't use, alongside what the two shapes should be.

## Why naming the string matters

It is the one fact that separates:
- a **wrong label**, from
- a **gun adding characters** (prefix/suffix/check digit in the DataWedge profile), from
- a barcode that was **never freight**

The app was the only place that knew it, and the only place not saying it.

## Verification

```text
PASS  245 tests
PASS  build + smoke
PASS  "not a PRO or a piece ID" / "A PRO is 7 digits" / "Scanner detail" all present in the shipped bundle
```

author: snrraptopack
body:
## What changed

- extend opaque volatility analysis through local helper return values
- allow structural list views such as `resource.data?.map(...)` when rooted in opaque third-party values
- forward volatile owner pulls through loading and error conditional regions
- add end-to-end `$fetch` coverage for loading, success, errors, keyed lists, snapshot destructuring, cancellation, explicit argument replacement, cleanup, and remounts
- scope the data example runtime and actions to component ownership and clear them through the existing `cleanup` lifecycle
- correct the data documentation: current rendering uses the generic opaque pull fallback; a push protocol is optional, not required for third-party libraries

## Root cause

The documentation described a future mandatory integration even though memoized-dom already supports imported live objects through opaque frame polling. At the same time, the structural list validator did not consume the opaque analysis result, conditional regions were not replayed from volatile owners, and local helper wrappers could hide opaque factory results.

## Impact

`$fetch` and similarly shaped third-party query objects work without compiler name recognition or method allowlists. Direct getters update scalar and structural JSX through the existing fallback, component-owned work uses explicit cleanup, and libraries remain free to use their own API shapes.

## Validation

- `bun run test` (425 workspace, 33 data, 35 router, 4 Vite, and 9 language-service tests)
- `bun run example:build`

author: fusefib
body: For years, ScummVM skipped one of *Hopkins FBI*'s stranger detours. In the underwater base, the game suddenly turns into a real-time first-person maze: Hopkins walks corridors, opens doors, fights guards, and eventually emerges into one of six adventure rooms. ScummVM previously replaced this sequence with a static destination map, similar to some official game ports. This PR restores the missing Windows WBASE subsystem. WBASE is effectively a small engine inside Hopkins. It has its own map and object data, 35 doors, guard and combat logic, collision, weapons, sound effects, six entrances and exits, death handling, and a 320x200 indexed-color software raycaster. The restored implementation loads and validates the original WBASE resources, runs the recovered simulation at its original fixed cadence, renders walls, floor, ceiling, doors, guards, corpses and HUD elements, and hands completed rooms or death back to the ordinary Hopkins engine. The restoration was reconstructed primarily from the original game data and executable behavior, then progressively tested and corrected. The implementation is kept Hopkins-local. ScummVM supplies the surrounding infrastructure for surfaces, streams, events, audio, timing, keymaps and engine lifecycle, while the small integer algorithms that define WBASE remain close to the behavior of the original. Only on the last leg of the work - and too late - was the lineage of the 3D engine pinned down properly. The raycasting and rendering core is Hopkins' port and adaptation of [**ACK-3D**](https://github.com/gered/ack3d) or **Animation Construction Kit 3D**. Quite a lot of the underlying graphics machinery remains recognizably ACK(-3D), in places down to original tables and familiar algorithms. That makes ACK-3D useful for reading and understanding the graphics code, but far from a replacement specification. Hopkins changed important constants, door and collision details, object geometry, texture transfer and other rendering behavior. The distinction caught real bugs. One apparently reasonable renderer assumption caused huge black gaps between the walls and the floor. A development-only per-tick capture path recorded the actual CLUT8 frame alongside ray distances, wall coverage and the floor pixels that should have been written. The problem eventually came down to a Hopkins-specific projection value: the executable initializes its view height to 31 rather than the value assumed during reconstruction. Restoring that behavior reduced more than ten thousand missing floor pixels in the captured starting frame to none. Other graphics details needed the same treatment. Hopkins disables ACK-style distance shading, uses its own deterministic integer object calculations, and has a particular centered texture-column transfer which differs from the obvious generic implementation. The sound side is separate from the ACK-3D graphics inheritance. WBASE uses four original Hopkins sound resources and the recovered Hopkins three-voice routing rather than ACK's sound system or a new mixer model. Player fire, doors and guard effects can overlap according to those original channel rules, and the WBASE samples are scoped to the session so ordinary Hopkins audio can resume normally afterward. WBASE returns distinct outcomes to the surrounding engine, keeping normal room completion, death, static fallback, and host quit or Return to Launcher separate. Save/load obviously remains disabled while WBASE is active. The simulation has enough transient state that supporting saves properly means serializing guards, doors, animation, combat and the rest of the live WBASE state, rather than merely saving Hopkins' surrounding adventure state. Testing has covered all six WBASE starts, real-game entry through Hopkins, the complete active resource set, movement, doors, combat and exits, the WBASE death transition, and deterministic routing across every entrance and destination combination (entries 194-199 and exits 94-99). Automated runs were also used to reproduce navigation and rendering problems instead of relying entirely on manual play. But, um, I skipped the actual original game in favor of YouTube videos. ### Regression risk The static fallback has been tested with WBASE data deliberately unavailable, and (some) ordinary Hopkins gameplay has been rechecked after the shared engine changes. I'm a bit worried about the first commit, which affects the shared sound code. The reassuring part is that the most invasive change, the voice routing, appears to be more correct for Linux too. ### Imminent next PR I did a separate QoL stack on top of the restoration, exposed via game options: 1) a live navigation map derived from WBASE data, autoplay routing with locations as dialog choices, mouse/touch HUD controls for them; 2) forced autoplay mode (for platforms where control is hard). Those changes will remain separately reviewable from the restoration itself. ### Testing the new ScummVM FPS - Skip the intro sequences. - Use `Play Game` from the game's Main Menu to get in the first room (the debugger won't work well until then). - Type `CTRL+ALT+D` for the debugger. - Type and submit `teleport 194`.

body:
# Description

Adds an `AzurePostgresFlexibleServer` inventory object so a flexible server can be resolved from the inventory root by name, turning a server name into its RSC object ID for SLA domain assignment.

The type mirrors `AzureSQLManagedInstanceServer`: alongside the common object fields it exposes the parent subscription details, because the inventory query has no subscription filter and flexible server names are only unique within a subscription, so callers narrow by subscription client-side.

RSC spells this `HierarchyObjectTypeEnum` value in SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE, `AZURE_POSTGRES_FLEXIBLE_SERVER`, unlike the CamelCase `AzureSqlManagedInstanceServer` value. The test asserts the filter so that inconsistency does not get "corrected" later.

## Related Issue

No existing issue. Third of three stacked SDK PRs; based on `draper-azure-postgres-sla-object-type`.

## Motivation and Context

Needed by the `polaris_object` data source in the Terraform provider, so a Postgres flexible server can be fed into `polaris_sla_domain_assignment`.

## How Has This Been Tested?

This is the only change in the stack that touches `inventory_root.graphql`, the query shared by every inventory caller, so it was verified against live deployments rather than only the mock server:

* On a deployment holding one flexible server, the query returned it with its parent subscription details populated, and the type filter selected it correctly.
* The pre-existing SQL Managed Instance lookup continues to work through the same query.
* On a deployment with no flexible servers the query is accepted and returns an empty result, confirming the new inline fragment does not error for accounts without the feature.

Also:

* `go generate ./...` regenerated `queries.go`; `go vet` and `go test ./pkg/polaris/graphql/hierarchy/...` clean.
* `TestAzurePostgresFlexibleServer` covers the type filter and unmarshalling, including the nested subscription details.

If RSC ever does 500 on the new inline fragment for accounts without the feature, the fallback is the dedicated `azurePostgresFlexibleServers` query, the same escape hatch the GitHub organization lookup already uses.

author: mrostan
body:
## What's new?

### 1. The default node pool now tracks the cluster version

`default_node_pool` set no `orchestrator_version`, so the node pool kept whatever version it was created with while the control plane moved with `kubernetes_version`. Bumping the cluster version upgraded **only the control plane** and left kubelet on the older version.

There's no error and nothing in the plan to hint at it — the plan shows only `kubernetes_version` changing, and Kubernetes tolerates the skew — so a "completed" upgrade can quietly leave the nodes behind. We hit exactly that: control plane on 1.34.9, nodes still on 1.32.11.

The node pool now defaults to the cluster's `kubernetes_version`, so both upgrade in the same apply. `orchestrator_version` is exposed on the `default_node_pool` object for staging the node pool upgrade separately:

```hcl
cluster = {
  kubernetes_version = "1.36"
  default_node_pool = {
    vm_size              = "Standard_DS2_v2"
    node_count           = 1
    orchestrator_version = "1.35"   # optional; defaults to kubernetes_version
  }
}
```

**Behaviour change:** the next apply upgrades the node pool for any deployment whose nodes had fallen behind. That's the intended fix.

### 2. Fix `terraform validate` failure on `oauth_secret_name`

`make sanity-check` currently fails on `main`:

```
Error: Output refers to sensitive values
  on outputs.tf line 57:
  57: output "oauth_secret_name" {
```

`local.use_oauth` derives from `var.oauth_credentials`, which is marked `sensitive`, so the ternary condition taints the resulting name even though a secret's *name* isn't a secret.

Fixed with `nonsensitive()` rather than marking the output `sensitive` — the latter would force every consumer that re-exports the name to mark theirs sensitive too. Same defect and fix as terraform-aws-mcd-k8s-agent#13.

Unrelated to the node pool work, but it was blocking a green `validate`, so it's a separate commit and can be dropped or split.

## Verification

```
terraform init -backend=false
terraform fmt -recursive -check -diff
terraform validate
```

All pass. `validate` fails on `main` without the second commit.

Confirmed live: after pinning `orchestrator_version` in an equivalent standalone config and applying, the control plane and node pool both reported 1.34.9, and the next version bump planned them together.

The README also picks up a short note that AKS limits which versions are reachable in a single upgrade, and that `az aks get-upgrades` should be checked beforehand — we had an apply rejected for targeting a version two minors ahead. The rejection is clean and leaves the cluster untouched.

author: fmeum
body:
### Description

`RemoteRewoundActionSynchronizer` keeps a rewound action from preparing for its re-execution while other actions are still consuming its outputs. Both keys were derived from the generating action key of the artifact itself, which is wrong for actions generated by an `ActionTemplate`: their outputs are `TreeFileArtifact`s owned by the expansion, whereas consumers depend on the parent tree artifact, which is owned by the template. A rewound expansion action thus acquired a write lock that no consumer would ever lock.

Both sides now derive the key from the outermost tree artifact containing the artifact, so the outputs of an expansion are guarded by the key of the template, which is shared by all tree artifacts a template declares.

Since the actions of a single expansion may form a chain, an action can have an input that is guarded by the very key it holds the write lock of. The locks aren't reentrant, so a rewound action now skips the read lock of that key.

Also keys `outputUploadTasks` by `ActionLookupData` instead of by the `Action` instance, which isn't stable across rewinding for actions generated by an `ActionTemplate`.

### Motivation

Without this, an action that consumes a tree artifact populated by an `ActionTemplate` can read its files while the expansion action that generated them is being rewound.

### Build API Changes

No

- [ ] I have updated the documentation (if applicable).

RELNOTES: None

author: ooples
body:
## Summary

Completes the automated cloning/serialization work for #1993 and removes the remaining concrete model/layer lifecycle plumbing. The acceptance baseline is merged `master` commit `1f3bc962ca` (#2035); the current PR head is `de55b75e05`.

Concrete model and layer authors now declare configuration, parameters, buffers, fitted state, and scratch state. Construction replay, cloning, parameter discovery, and serialization are supplied by generators and shared base classes.

## Architecture

- Removed concrete `Clone`, `DeepCopy`, `CreateNewInstance`, `Serialize`, `Deserialize`, network-specific serializer, and extra-parameter ownership methods from governed model/layer types.
- Added `ADN0063`, promoted to an error in this repository, so concrete lifecycle overrides cannot grow back. Abstract/shared bases remain the implementation boundary; optimizers and distributions are outside this model/layer rule.
- Generated constructor replay excludes `[Scratch]` graphs and supports model-owned trainable `Vector<T>` state.
- Shared parameter discovery covers the tabular base families without per-model overrides.
- Shared sharded-model serialization now persists and validates constructor-derived topology.
- Content-classifier configuration/state now round-trips through the shared model-state contract.
- Bayesian posterior epsilon tensors are scratch state, so training cannot change the optimizer-visible parameter surface.
- DiffWave shape resolution and StandardVAE lazy graph reconstruction no longer depend on warm-up-only concrete state.

## Timeout and regression hardening

- Timeout failures are evaluated with the agreed sequence: parallel result first, exact isolated retry second, and fixture shrinking only when the isolated test still exceeds its cap.
- The INT8 timing canary and sparse variational GP test failed only under parallel load and passed unchanged in isolation; no timeout was inflated.
- `FluxInpaintingModel` and `SiDDiTModel` genuinely exceeded 120 seconds alone at paper scale. Their model-family tests now inject small real predictor/VAE graphs, retain production defaults, and run in the normal PR lane instead of hiding lifecycle checks behind `HeavyTimeout`.

## Automated CI proof

The workflow now exposes a dedicated **CI Regression Proof** job and uploads a compact `test-outcome-ledger-<sha>` artifact. It reports:

- total/passed/failed/incomplete shards;
- raw failing results and distinct failing tests;
- persistent, fixed, one-run, confirmed-new, touched-surface, and green-to-red failures;
- targeted retry outcomes for provisional new failures;
- strict and hybrid acceptance criteria against the exact master baseline SHA.

Current run: https://github.com/ooples/AiDotNet/actions/runs/32599415024 (queued for GitHub-hosted capacity). This PR is not declared merge-ready until that run publishes its final proof.

## Local verification at `de55b75e05`

- Strict `net10.0` test-project build: **0 errors**. `ADN0063` is active as an error.
- Preserved 84-test PR regression corpus: **82/84** in the parallel batch; the only two load-sensitive failures passed exact isolated retry, for **84/84 hybrid**.
- Generator/base/analyzer integration gate: **212 passed, 1 intentional census skip, 0 failed**.
- Bayesian trained-clone and parameter-surface stability: **10/10 assertions** across five fresh test processes.
- Promoted Flux inpainting + SiDDiT model-family contracts: **26 passed, 0 failed** in 25 seconds.
- VAE-backed clone regressions plus DiffWave: **8 passed, 0 failed**.
- CI regression-analysis script tests: **all assertions passed**.
- `git diff --check`: no whitespace errors.

No assertion was weakened, tolerance loosened, or timeout increased to obtain these results.

## Reviewer focus

- `src/AiDotNet.Generators/CloneAutomationAnalyzer.cs`
- `src/AiDotNet.Generators/ClonePlanGenerator.cs`
- `src/AiDotNet.Generators/ModelParameterGenerator.cs`
- `src/Models/Parameters/GeneratedParameterDiscovery.cs`
- shared model/layer base-state changes and lifecycle declaration removals
- `.github/scripts/test-regression-analysis.ps1`
- `.github/workflows/sonarcloud.yml`
