author: testtest126
body:
Closes #212.

## Honest result up front: this is NOT a demonstrated strength improvement

A properly-powered SPRT (800 games, full schedule, did not resolve either way) found **no measurable Elo effect**: -1 ± 16 Elo, essentially a coin flip. Unlike LMR (#218), which resolved cleanly positive, this one genuinely didn't move the needle. I'm opening the PR as requested (correct, tested implementation with real infra value), but **not recommending it merge as a strength win** — that call is the orchestrator's/owner's, with this data in front of them. Details and a plausible explanation below.

## What

Adds `Board.see(_:)` (`ChessKit/Sources/ChessKit/Board.swift`) — the standard "swap algorithm" Static Exchange Evaluation over the mailbox board: net material result of the full capture/recapture sequence on a square, least-valuable-attacker order each step. X-ray/battery attackers are picked up for free — `attackers(to:by:excluding:)` recomputes sliding attacks from scratch against the reduced occupancy at every step of the exchange, so a piece revealed behind a captured blocker is naturally found without separate bookkeeping.

Wires it into `Search.quiesce` (`ChessKit/Sources/ChessProtocol/NegamaxEngine.swift`, ~:493-530): out of check, a capture with `see(move) < 0` is skipped rather than searched. Promotions are exempt (SEE only prices the destination-square material exchange, not the new queen). Never applied while in check — the existing "search every evasion" branch is untouched.

Adds a `seePruning: Bool` toggle (default `true`) to `NegamaxEngine`/`PersistentNegamaxEngine`/`EngineConfig`, and `--baseline-see`/`--candidate-see`/`--candidate-evaluator default` flags to `EngineLab`'s `abtest` CLI, mirroring the `lateMoveReductions` seam from #218 — this is what let the heuristic be isolated and SPRT-measured against an otherwise-identical baseline.

Re-pins the `EngineLabTests` bench determinism signature.

## SEE correctness — `SEETests.swift`

Six hand-verified cases: a clean undefended win (+100), a losing queen-takes-pawn-defended-by-pawn (-800), an equal rook trade (0), en passant (whose victim isn't on `move.to` — a naive implementation would score it as a free capture), a no-recapture edge case, and a battery/x-ray position specifically constructed to discriminate a correct implementation from a naive one: two White rooks doubled on a file, only the front one initially able to reach the target square, with Black holding one defending rook. Correct answer (x-ray-aware): **+500**. A SEE that only looked at attackers *before* any capture (missing the rear rook, since it starts blocked) would return **0** instead — this is the actual bug the test catches, not just a smoke check. All 6 pass.

## SPRT result

`abtest`, `DefaultEvaluator` held fixed both sides (`--candidate-evaluator default`), 15,000-node budget both sides (equal-budget, not equal-depth — matches the LMR methodology), 400 openings sampled (seed 1) from [testtest126/books](https://github.com/testtest126/books)' `noob_3moves.epd`, `--elo0 0 --elo1 10`:

```
games: 800 (full schedule — SPRT never resolved)
candidate (SEE on) results: +179 =440 -181   score: 49.9%
Elo(candidate - baseline): -1 ± 16  (95%)
SPRT: llr -0.71 (bounds -2.94 .. 2.94) -> inconclusive — keep playing
```

## Node-count effect — real, but inconsistent (helps explain the neutral SPRT)

Measured via a local scratch probe against the built library (not committed), SEE-on vs SEE-off at equal depth:

| position | depth 3 | depth 4 | depth 5 | depth 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| startpos (quiet) | 1.00x | 1.02x | 1.01x | 1.05x |
| middlegame | 1.27x | 1.51x | 1.38x | **0.76x** (more nodes) |
| kiwipete (dense tactics) | 2.07x | 1.95x | 1.69x | 1.78x |
| tactical | 1.14x | 1.24x | 1.12x | 1.13x |

SEE pruning genuinely cuts nodes in capture-rich positions (kiwipete: consistently 1.7-2.1x fewer) and barely matters in quiet ones (startpos), as expected. But it's not monotonic — at middlegame/depth 6 it used *more* nodes than the unpruned search, from pruning interacting with move ordering and alpha-beta cutoffs elsewhere in the tree (a real, known effect, not a bug — confirmed by `SEEQuiescenceTests` passing, including a dedicated `testSEEPruningReducesNodes` on a different fixture where the reduction does hold).

**Plausible explanation for the neutral SPRT**: quiescence is a much smaller, shallower slice of total search cost than the whole main tree LMR (#218) prunes recursively at every ply — LMR's node savings compound across the tree, SEE's don't. The captures SEE prunes are also often ones MVV-LVA ordering already pushes late and alpha-beta already cuts off cheaply, so the *marginal* compute actually freed may be smaller than the raw "captures skipped" count suggests — leaving little left over to reinvest into useful extra depth at this node-budget regime.

## Verified locally at 863398f (this PR's exact head), in a detached scratch worktree

- `ChessKit`: `swift test` (release, and separately confirmed in debug for the bench signature + both new test files) — **EXIT:0**
- `chess-server`: `swift test` — **EXIT:0** (99 tests; unaffected by this change, verified for the record)
- `ios-chess-client`: `xcodebuild build` (iPhone 15 Simulator, iOS 17.5) — **EXIT:0**

## Baseline note

This was tested against current `main` (`f80248c`), which does **not** yet include #218 (LMR, still unmerged as of this writing). If/when both merge, the combined effect should be re-validated — LMR and SEE-pruned quiescence touch different parts of the same search and aren't guaranteed to be perfectly additive (LMR changes which nodes get reduced-depth looks in the main tree; SEE changes which captures quiescence bothers searching at all — plausible interactions either way).

## Scope / classification

- Not security-sensitive (pure engine search algorithm) — opening ready for review, not draft.
- Does not touch the app UI, `ChessOnline`, or `ChessKit/Sources/ChessOnline/Messages.swift`.
- Only touches what SEE needs: `Board.swift`, `NegamaxEngine.swift`, `PersistentNegamaxEngine.swift`, `EngineLab/CLI.swift`, `EngineLab/SelfPlay.swift`, `EngineLabTests/BenchTests.swift` (re-pin), and the two new test files. Does not touch PR #116 or the LMR branch (`feature/lmr-search`) — separate worktree, separate branch off `origin/main`.

Per repo convention, requesting the orchestrator review this — not merging it myself, and given the inconclusive result, it may be one for the owner to explicitly decide on rather than a routine merge.

author: yenchang265-afk
body:
## Problem

Every first invocation of an engineering verb in the OpenCode TUI vanished — no turn, no toast, no error, no log line — and the retry seconds later "worked". Five swallowed invocations are visible in one day's opencode log as a `command=agentic-workflow:engineering` line followed by nothing.

## Root cause

opencode's `Plugin.trigger` awaits `command.execute.before` hooks with **no try/catch**, and only reaches `Session.prompt` after the trigger resolves; the SDK's fetch back into the server sets `req.timeout = false`. So a hook that rejects — or never settles — kills the command before the model turn exists, silently. The plugin's hook had ~60 unguarded lines before its dispatch `try` (config re-read, kind check, slice), its error paths awaited `log(...)` over the same channel that had just failed, and the one-shot guards (`reportAgentModelsOnce`, `reconcileOnce`) set their flags before their unguarded awaits — so attempt 1 died inside them and attempt 2 skipped them. Second shipping of the class the `gateFirst` comment documents.

## Fix

A hook the host will not catch must be total:

- One `try` around everything after the prefix match; the catch writes `failurePrompt` (the only channel a dead command has) and never awaits a TUI call on the way out.
- `log` never rejects and is time-boxed — it is also `deps.log`, so the driver inherits the guarantee.
- The per-command config read is time-boxed; a timeout lands in the existing misconfig arm (last-good config, working command).
- `reconcileTimely` contains the startup sweep: time-boxed + caught, degrading to a toast instead of discarding a gate move that already landed. Background overlap is safe: `releaseOrphanedClaims` re-judges staleness atomically.
- Toasts fire-and-forget everywhere (`.catch()` guards a rejection, not a hang); `event` hook guarded; `warnIgnoredUserConfigOnce` flag-first.
- No timeout on `handleCommand` — interrupting a real gate move is worse than waiting.

Deferred deliberately: the `tidy()` fixpoint in `command-slice.ts` is roughly cubic (CPU stall, untouchable by try/catch or timeouts) — separate follow-up.

Design record: `docs/design/improvements/20-total-command-hooks.md` (+ zh-TW twin, README rows); AGENTS.md gains the rule (second occurrence of the class).

## Tests

- Hanging config read (mock timers) → command still handled, not swallowed.
- Rejecting logger → command still handled (drives the exact error-path pairing that killed first invocations).
- Malformed `event` payload → hook resolves.
- Full suite green: 230/230 in `plugins/opencode`, `test:all` clean.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck -w agentic-workflow`

author: happyseaurchin
body:
`pscale_stream_engage` — the V-L-S envelope over a spine-mirror-tree family, standing **beside** `pscale_pool_engage`, not inside it.

## The divergence

Named at `proposals:weft:2.5`: VLS is built on pools, coordination is built on spines, and nobody joined them. A located engage at a family address returns an empty buffer and an empty spool while the mirrors *at that very address* hold the substance. Commits go **into** the mirrors (the #248 face routing); reads never come back **out**.

Verified live before building: `pool:arrival` at `at=1` returns liquid 0 / contributions 0 while `arrival:weft` holds five dated entries there — and `function:audit`'s own POOL LAW says why ("where a stage is discussed, never where status is recorded").

## Why a fork and not a flag

A mount-gated hybrid on `pool_engage` was considered and rejected: it would make the pool a **contested component by construction** (`grips:7.1`) — one primitive behaving two ways, the confusion recurring in every session forever. It is also *less* reversible, not more: a hybrid entangles both behaviours in one code path; a fork deletes as one tool plus its blocks.

Bar for a new primitive (CLAUDE.md — *"the envelope is observably what's missing, and conventions have failed to carry it"*): the missing thing **is** an envelope shape, and `tree:8`/`tree:9.1` have been correct and undelivered for a fortnight. Same argument that earned `pool_engage` and `networking`.

## The design

**A stream stores nothing.** A pool owns two blocks; a stream owns none — it composes over `spine:<field>`, the `<field>:<handle>` mirrors and the bare `<field>` fold, so it cannot drift and needs no lock.

- **L** — every mirror's reading at the address, listed and attributed: the *snapshot*, useful with no LLM in the room. **No buffer** — a mirror is revisable by its holder forever, so **stage and commit collapse into one act** (`say`). That collapse is what made pools unexplainable to their own keeper.
- **S** — the fold, synthesised by the *calling* mind under the operator's law (read from `spine:<field>:9`, per `ways:deck:2`) delivered in the same envelope. The primitive never synthesises — no central resolver, as with pools.
- **The ladder** — every ancestor's voicing, coarsest to attended, so a located read arrives self-contextualised.
- **Named rungs** — `today`, `this week`, `season`, `year`, `now` computed from the clock. A human is never asked for a ten-digit address (`function:molequle:5`).
- **The fold is ephemeral by default** (`tree:3`). `keep='personal'` → `history:<handle>` (#247's salvage rider); `keep='collective'` → the bare name at the same address, endorsed by pointer, never a gate.

CADO gets one surface per grip: C says at their own mirror, A authors the spine, D the operator, O the view — and what O renders is **S, never L**.

## Blast radius

None. `pool.ts`, liquid buffers, windows, dice and every RPG path are untouched. The RPG keeps `pool_engage` as it is. If streams prove out, that molecule migrates afterwards and the pool becomes legacy — deliberately, not by drift.

## Verification

`npm run smoke:stream` — **23/23**: helpers offline, plus a **live read** and a **live `say`** against the `beach-venture` ladder. Typecheck clean.

```
# The ladder — this address in its own context, coarse to fine
  p8 [2000000000] the 2000s — the century this work is set in.
  p7 [2020000000] the internet reconstituted as beach …
  p6 [2026000000] millions of players on the Onen RPG through xstream …
  p5 [2026300000] Summer 2026, Jul–Sep …
  p4 [2026320000] August 2026 — access COMPLETE and user-friendly …
  p3 [2026322000] The week of 10–16 August 2026 …
  p2 [2026322300] 10 August 2026 — three strands …

# Readings at 2026322300 — 1 voice (the SNAPSHOT …)
- weft (you): DOING — the stream primitive built and standing BESIDE the pool …
  silent here: happyseaurchin — honest absence, not a gap to be filled (tree:5e)
```

author: atharv-tw
body:
Postgres, Redis, the API and the worker move off Render/Neon/Upstash into a single compose project; the web app stays on Vercel. Render's free tier spins down, so the OAuth callback and the Pub/Sub push endpoint both paid a cold start, and every request crossed three providers' networks to reach a database this app opens an RLS-bound session against per request.

One image serves the API and the worker - they share a codebase and must run the same environment. It installs editable and keeps the repo layout, because settings.py finds the root .env via parents[3] of its own path and a flattened install resolves that inside the interpreter.

Neither Postgres nor Redis publishes a port. Only the API does, on 127.0.0.1, because cloudflared runs as a host unit and cannot resolve service names - and loopback keeps it off the LAN. The dev compose file keeps its published ports; that one is for laptops.

The systemd unit stays in the tree. It is the rollback path, and its section in DEPLOYMENT.md is now marked as the older split topology rather than current.

APP_DB_PASSWORD and POSTGRES_PASSWORD are documented in .env.example for the first time. Migration 0002 reads the former when it creates outreach_app and otherwise falls back to a literal, guessable default.

author: dlduarte
body:
Duas dores relatadas, com a mesma raiz no watcher.

## O erro ao trocar de branch

`Not a directory: ...\.git\objects\d3` vinha de o watcher vigiar o `.git` recursivamente: o git cria e apaga diretórios em `objects/` mais rápido do que dá para listá-los, e o refresh pedia `list_dir` de uma pasta que já não existia.

Três camadas de correção:

- **Lista de pastas ignoradas** (`src-tauri/src/ignore.rs`), aplicada de uma vez à árvore, à varredura de markdown e ao watcher — para "ignorado" significar a mesma coisa em todo o app.
- A comparação é **relativa à raiz**, não absoluta: uma pasta que viva dentro de um diretório com ponto (`~/.config/docs`) teria tudo descartado. Tem teste para o caso.
- `refreshDir` passa a **falhar em silêncio** e só relê pastas já carregadas. Um refresh que chega depois de a pasta sumir é normal, não merece um toast vermelho.

A lista: nomes com ponto por regra (`.git`, `.venv`, `.next`, `.idea`, …), mais `node_modules`, `bower_components`, `vendor`, `pods`, `target`, `build`, `dist`, `out`, `bin`, `obj`, `coverage`, `__pycache__`, `venv`.

> Inclui `build`, `dist`, `out` e `bin`. Se a documentação de alguém morar numa pasta com um desses nomes, ela desaparece da árvore. Risco pequeno para o ganho, e é uma constante fácil de ajustar — pode virar configuração se incomodar.

## Não acompanhar mudanças externas

O watcher já existia, mas só atualizava a **árvore**; o conteúdo das abas nunca era relido — daí ter que fechar e reabrir o arquivo.

- Aba **sem edição pendente**: adota o disco em silêncio.
- Aba **com edição pendente**: nada é sobrescrito. O conteúdo do disco fica guardado e o `ConflictToast` oferece "Usar do disco" ou "Manter a minha".

O debounce virou **acumulação de caminhos**. O anterior descartava eventos dentro da janela de 200 ms, e como salvar num editor costuma virar "grava temporário + rename", o rename para o `.md` — o único que interessa — era justamente o que se perdia.

## Efeito colateral corrigido de passagem

O `single-instance` passa a valer só em **release**. O lock é por identificador, então com o app instalado aberto um `tauri dev` era capturado por ele e morria no arranque — impossível desenvolver com o app em uso.

## Verificação

| O quê | Resultado |
|---|---|
| Editar `.md` por fora, aba aberta | Conteúdo atualiza sozinho ✅ |
| `git checkout` de outra branch | Conteúdo atualiza ✅, sem toast de erro ✅ |
| Eventos com caminho `.git` | zero ✅ |
| Árvore de um repo com `node_modules`/`dist`/`.git` | só `docs` aparece ✅ |
| Testes do módulo `ignore` | 4 passando ✅ |

`npm run build`, `npm run lint`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings` e `cargo test` passam.

Verificado num repositório git de teste, com duas branches e conteúdo diferente em cada, dirigindo tudo por linha de comando.

body:
## 🐞 문제
분석이 **부분성공(`PARTIAL_SUCCESS`)** 으로 끝나면 결과가 멀쩡히 있는데도 화면엔 **30초 뒤 "분석이 지연되고 있습니다"** 오류가 떴습니다.

`AnalysisStatus` 타입에 `PARTIAL_SUCCESS`가 빠져 있어서, 폴링 종료 판정에서 `COMPLETED`도 `FAILED`도 아닌 값이 되어 **계속 폴링하다 20회를 채우고** 타임아웃으로 끝났습니다.

## 📋 작업 내용

### 1. `PARTIAL_SUCCESS` 상태 추가 (`api/analyses.ts`)
- `AnalysisStatus`에 추가
- `hasResult(status)` / `isTerminal(status)` 헬퍼 추가 — 종료 판정을 문자열 비교로 흩뿌리지 않도록
- 폴링 종료 조건을 `hasResult()`로 교체 → 부분성공도 완료와 같이 결과 렌더

### 2. 부분성공 안내 배너 (`HomePage`)
점수는 그대로 보여주되 **어떤 분석이 빠졌는지** 상단에 안내합니다.
> 일부 분석을 마치지 못했어요
> **문맥 분석 · 링크 보안 분석**을(를) 확인하지 못했습니다. 아래 결과는 남은 검사만으로 판단한 것이라, 실제 위험도가 더 높을 수 있어요. 링크·전화에 응답하기 전에 공식 번호로 한 번 더 확인하세요.

- `failedTracks` 값이 `TEXT:GEMINI`·`URL:VIRUSTOTAL` 같은 **영어 + 내부 엔진명**이라 그대로 노출하지 않고 3중 스코어 레이어(문맥/링크/글자 패턴)로 환원합니다
- 전용 필드가 비면 `ANALYSIS_TRACK_FAILURE` 지표에서 뽑는 **폴백**을 둡니다 — 서버가 지표 문자열을 파싱해 그 필드를 만들기 때문에 한쪽만 비는 경우가 있습니다

### 3. 실패 통지를 위험 근거 카드에서 분리
`ANALYSIS_TRACK_FAILURE`는 위험 신호가 아니라 '이 분석을 못 돌렸다'는 알림인데 근거 카드에 섞여 **영어 원문이 노출**됐습니다. 필터링하고 배너로만 안내합니다.

### 4. 누락된 지표 라벨 3종 추가
`FINANCIAL_ACTION`(금전 요구) · `SENSITIVE_INFORMATION`(개인정보 요구) · `URGENCY`(긴급성 압박)가 라벨에 없어 **영어 enum 이름이 그대로** 사용자에게 보였습니다.

## 🧪 테스트 결과
- `npm run build` — 통과
- `npm run lint` — 8 errors, **`develop`과 동일**(기존 `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`, 이 PR과 무관)
- 상태 문자열 직접 비교가 남아 있지 않은지 확인 완료

## 참고
Flutter 앱에서 같은 문제를 겪고 고쳤습니다(SafeFam_FE #98·#99). 백엔드 계약상 종료 상태는 `COMPLETED`·`PARTIAL_SUCCESS`·`FAILED` 셋이고, 점수를 신뢰할 수 있는 건 앞의 둘입니다.

## 🔗 관련 이슈
Closes #22

## ✅ 체크리스트
- [x] 백엔드 계약 대조(종료/결과보유 상태 구분)
- [x] 내부 엔진명(GEMINI·VIRUSTOTAL) 사용자 노출 없음

## Summary

Stage 6 now publishes Rule 144A and approved Regulation S as independent execution series. The immutable Rule 144A history remains the panel ancestry; the first dual-series child makes the guarded config transition, and later deltas continue even when no Regulation S mapping is available.

Missing or ambiguous Regulation S evidence omits only that Regulation S row. It never removes or degrades the Rule 144A row, and neither series falls back to the other.

## Safety

- All four panel surfaces carry explicit distribution rule, Rule 144A reference CUSIP, and mapping-decision identity.
- CUSIP and ISIN collisions fail closed for the affected Regulation S rows while preserving Rule 144A.
- Removed or unavailable Regulation S mappings close only the affected Reg S lane; they do not create false Rule 144A terminal exits.
- A 144A-only bootstrap is permitted only when zero Reg S mappings and exact typed omission coverage are proven for both windows.
- The pointer guard permits only the direct legacy-to-dual child and subsequent direct-parent dual deltas.
- The retired Regulation-S-only config cannot become or remain the serving root.

- Latest exact-scope suite: `164 passed, 4 skipped`; the skips require the optional `SEC_TEST_DATABASE_URL` integration database.

body:
## Summary
Adds a second document-generation tab to the application: a **Hotel Confirmation Voucher** generator alongside the existing Proposal Generator. The voucher form captures guest and hotel details, auto-calculates stay duration, performs optional address lookup via OpenStreetMap Nominatim, and generates a Word document from a new `voucher_template.docx`.

## Key Changes

- **Tab Navigation UI**
  - Added `.tabs` and `.tab-btn` styles with active/hover states and underline indicators
  - Implemented `switchTab()` function to toggle between proposal and voucher panels with proper ARIA attributes (`aria-selected`, `aria-controls`, `role="tab"`)
  - Both panels use `.tab-panel` with `.active` class for visibility toggling

- **Form Styling Enhancements**
  - Extended input selectors to include `textarea`, `input[type="date"]`, `input[type="time"]`, and `select`
  - Added `.voucher-grid` (2-column layout, responsive to 1-column on mobile) for grouped form fields
  - Added `.form-hint` styling for inline validation/helper text with error state support
  - Added `input[readonly]` styling (muted text, disabled cursor, no hover border change)
  - Updated `.main-wrapper` to use `flex-direction: column` and removed `justify-content: center`

- **Hotel Confirmation Voucher Form**
  - Hotel Details section: hotel search with auto-address capture via Nominatim API
  - Guest & Booking Details: guest name, confirmation number, arrival/departure dates
  - Stay Details: number of guests, room type, meal plan, check-in/check-out times, special requests textarea
  - Auto-calculates "Duration of Stay" (nights) from arrival/departure dates with singular/plural handling
  - Validates that departure is after arrival; shows inline error if invalid

- **Address Lookup (Nominatim)**
  - On blur of hotel search field, queries OpenStreetMap Nominatim API
  - Gracefully handles network failures and no-match results without blocking form submission

author: tamnd
body:
Second of the two crashes from the S3 exit runs, tracked in #62.

The 6h run on server2 died with `PANIC: invalid max offset number` inside the redo worker. The record at 69E9BC00 is a cross page heap update touching blocks 19 and 18 of rel 2619, and the batch being replayed was block 18's. The worker had no real copy of block 19, only what an earlier init record in block 18's chain had created, one tuple on an otherwise fresh page. On the primary that page kept growing through records that only touch block 19, which block 18's chain never carries, so when the update landed its new tuple offset was past the worker's maxoff and heap redo panicked.

The fix is a target set. The pool now declares the batch's target blocks up front with a new T frame, and inside the worker redo skips every buffer reference outside that set, returning BLK_NOTFOUND the same way stock recovery does for a missing page. Init references pass through because redo routines expect a valid buffer from an init, and a page built by one cannot be read again past the filter. The bystander's own batch replays the shared records against its full history, so nothing is lost, only replayed in the right context. A pool that declares no targets gets the old behavior, so an old pool against a new worker keeps working.

While in there the page service also grew a refusal for a genuinely bare chain: a main fork block with records but no base image anywhere, whose first record cannot build the page alone. Before this, redo would grow whatever it could out of zeros and hand back a partly fabricated page. Now it errors with the block and the first LSN.

The regression test is the exact production shape: fat rows kept plain so they do not compress, an index so updates are not HOT, and alternating updates from far apart source pages in a single session so the target block cache steers all the new versions into one shared destination page. Then every block of the table and the index is replayed alone against only its own record chain and compared to disk. Before the fix that test dies with the same panic and the same `failed to fill whole buffer` the server run produced.

Patch 0005 regenerated, all five patches apply cleanly on the pin. Full zou-pg suite and the workspace are green locally. Server2 verification with redoprobe and a full recovery of the crashed store comes before merge.

author: eremenko789
body: ## Проблема `asset pull` падал с `unexpected EOF` на файлах больше ~4 ГиБ. Причина: после рефакторинга скачивание шло через `DownloadToBuffer` → `io.ReadAll`, то есть весь файл буферизовался в RAM. Для multi-GB ассетов это приводит к OOM / обрыву соединения, который клиент видит как EOF. Дополнительно `http.Client.Timeout` (30 мин) был короче `downloadTimeout` (60 мин) и обрывал body mid-stream — тоже часто как EOF. ## Решение - `DownloadFileByUrl` снова стримит на диск через `io.Copy` (как раньше и как уже делает `ComputeHashFromDownloadURL`) - убран client-wide `Timeout`; для зависания на заголовках используется `ResponseHeaderTimeout`, для body — per-request context - `UploadFile` стримит с диска с явным `Content-Length` - `TransferFile` (sync) идёт через temp-файл, а не через RAM - тесты на streaming download / incomplete body / upload stream ## Тесты `go test ./...` — OK

author: ilpanich
body:
## What

**X1 — Reactors**, stages a and b. The SDK runtime fan-out and contract §16 follow in X1c.

A **Reactor** is an external process, in any SDK language, that subscribes to hook events on the AMQP bus and answers back (veto / mutate / observe) under a signed, timeout-bounded, field-allow-listed protocol.

Zitadel Actions embed user JavaScript in the IAM process; Keycloak SPIs load user JARs into the JVM. Both put third-party code **inside the security kernel** — a bug in an extension is a bug in the authorization server. This keeps the kernel closed: a reactor can only influence the server through a narrow reply schema, and every way it can fail is a case the server already has a policy for.

| Crate | What lands |
| --- | --- |
| `axiam-core` | Event registry, domain model, `ReactorGate` trait |
| `axiam-db` | Schema v29 + repository |
| `axiam-amqp` | Wire protocol (§8 HMAC both directions) + dispatch chain |
| `axiam-api-rest` | `/api/v1/reactors` CRUD + `/api/v1/reactors/events` |
| `axiam-server` | Repository wiring; `sdks/openapi.json` regenerated |

**The registry lives in `axiam-core`, not `axiam-amqp`** (a deliberate deviation from the plan's file layout). Three consumers need it and none should need the broker: REST validates a registration against it, the dispatcher validates a patch against it, and `axiam-auth`/`axiam-oauth2` call through `ReactorGate` without knowing AMQP exists. Putting it in the broker crate would moot the trait's whole reason for existing.

## The security decisions worth reviewing

**`token.pre_issue` may write only into the `ext.` namespace.** Prefix matching is exact — `ext.` (the bare namespace) and `extra` are both *outside* it — so a reactor cannot reach `sub`, `aud`, `exp` or a scope claim. A hook that can rewrite `sub` is a hook that can mint a token for anyone. Asserted twice: against the spec helper, and again through a fully valid **signed** reply.

**`authz.check` is not hookable, and a test asserts it is absent from the registry.** A reactor round-trip is milliseconds; the check path's budget is microseconds at 1k–12k req/s. Adding it should be a decision someone makes while looking at that assertion, not a line someone appends.

**An omitted `failure_policy` takes the strictest default among the subscribed events.** A reactor registered for both `token.pre_issue` (fail_open) and `login.post_auth` (fail_closed) can veto a login, so it inherits fail_closed. Taking the *first* event's default would let the order of a JSON array decide whether an unreachable fraud check passes.

**No partial patch application** — one forbidden key rejects the whole reply. Applying the acceptable half would leave the reactor author believing a field was set when it was dropped.

**Reply validation order is identity → freshness → signature → semantics.** Checking the allow-list first would spend that logic on unauthenticated bytes, and would leak which fields are accepted through differing rejections.

**An exhausted chain budget applies each *remaining* reactor's own policy** rather than skipping it, so an unreached fail_closed veto still denies. Otherwise the budget is a way to skip a security check by registering slow reactors ahead of it.

**`require_mfa` is sticky** across the chain, and is refused outright on any event but `login.post_auth` — elsewhere it sets a flag the path has no way to honour, and the operation would proceed as if it had.

**The in-flight limiter uses `try_acquire`, never `acquire`.** Queueing behind the cap would turn a concurrency bound into an unbounded latency bound, which is the failure the cap exists to prevent.

## REST (X1b)

**The registry is served, not documented.** `GET /api/v1/reactors/events` returns `EVENT_REGISTRY` verbatim, so an admin UI, an SDK generator and an operator all read the list the dispatcher enforces. A hand-maintained copy goes stale on the next hook added, and the copy nobody looks at is the one that drifts. A test asserts the served length equals the registry's, so a copy cannot be introduced silently.

Route order matters: `/reactors/events` is registered **before** `/reactors/{id}` because actix matches in registration order and the UUID parser would otherwise swallow it. There is a test whose failure message says so.

**Update validates the merged registration, not the request.** A PUT that only replaces `events` is valid in isolation; the violation lives in the *pair* — stored `mode: intercept` plus a listen-only event from the request. Validating the request alone would let exactly that through.

**Replacing `events` without naming a policy re-derives it.** A reactor that was enrichment-only and is now also registered for `login.post_auth` can veto a login, so the stored `fail_open` predates the capability and must not survive it. An explicit policy is still honoured even when it is the looser one — the re-derivation is a default, not an override.

## Schema v29

`mode` and `failure_policy` carry `ASSERT`s for the same reason v25's `effect` does: both decide behaviour on the security path, the read path defaults an unparseable value to the **safe** side rather than erroring (one bad row must not take token issuance down), so the write path is the only place the column can be kept honest. `events` is deliberately **not** asserted — the valid set lives in `EVENT_REGISTRY` and grows with the code; encoding it in DDL would mean a migration per hook and a mismatch resolved in favour of whichever was edited last.

An unrecognised stored `mode` is demoted to `listen` and an unrecognised `failure_policy` to `fail_closed`. Same reasoning as SEC-092, with a genuinely inert value available here that grants did not have.

## Verification

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Reactor tests | **71** — 15 core registry, 31 protocol + dispatcher, 3 row-mapping, 12 repository integration, 10 REST integration |
| `cargo test -p axiam-core --lib` | 92 passed |
| `cargo test -p axiam-db --lib` | 144 passed |
| `cargo test -p axiam-amqp --lib` | 72 passed |
| `clippy -D warnings`, `fmt --check` | clean, incl. `axiam-api-rest`/`axiam-server` under `--no-default-features` |
| `sdks/openapi.json` | regenerated from `--dump-openapi` so the drift gate passes |

**Mutation-checked three ways:**

| Mutation | Tests that fail |
| --- | --- |
| Patch allow-list accepts everything | 7, across two crates |
| `fail_closed` treated as `fail_open` | 4 |
| Exhausted budget silently skips remaining reactors | 1 (the one written for it) |

---

Implements §5 steps 1–2 of the approved P0 plan. Steps 3–6 remain planned, not started.

## Step 1 — registry + guard

`scripts/onboarding.py`. File-only per ruling 1; `data/onboarding/*` and `data/staging/*` added to `.gitignore`. Unknown domain names are a hard error.

The guard makes divergence fatal, which is what lets the 11 dbt tests stay untouched:

| declared | rows | action |
|---|---|---|
| yes | >0 | ok |
| **yes** | **0** | **ABORT** — a load failure, not an absence |
| no | 0 | ok |
| **no** | **>0** | **ABORT** — stale registry or an unintended path |

## Step 2 — fail-closed ingest

The sample-fallback branch is **deleted**. No registry → every contracted domain required, all missing reported at once. With a registry → declared domains must have a file; undeclared load nothing (typed zero-row table, rewritten every run).

## Required cross-domain dbt finding

**No false aborts** — `declared:[employees]` and `declared:[payroll]` both give 157/157 and 11/11, no nulls. Ruling 4 holds.

**But §0.3's rationale was wrong** and is corrected in place: the marts are not zero-row. Each emits one `COALESCE`d row, so tests pass on fabricated values. `mart_attendance_kpis` → `(0.0, 494.0)` — every employee absent every workday of a period never uploaded. Reclassified as **P0-3**.

## The guard caught a defect in its own cycle

The first implementation wrote empty tables before the 21 per-table ingest blocks, which re-ingested from sample and overwrote them. Arm 4 aborted the run with `populated but NOT declared: [...]`. Fixed via a named sentinel path so those blocks skip.

## Pre-merge items

- `UNDECLARED_SENTINEL_DIR` hoisted to a named constant with a docstring; two tests make it an invariant (directory absent; path appears once in source).
- Plan §0.3 corrected in place with a dated note, original text struck through.

(f) declared:[employees] -> employees 3 real rows; other five 0 rows
    before: (19, 446175.0, 50.0)   after: (3, 0.0, 100.0)
    NO FABRICATED ROWS PRESENT: True

author: jesyspa
body:
A failed proof is reported at warning level, so that turning the plugin on cannot
break an adopter's build. Anyone who wants the opposite — a failed proof breaking
the build — had only `-Xwarning-level=VIPER_VERIFICATION_ERROR:error`, which is not
part of the plugin's surface and is documented nowhere.

This adds the switch:

```kotlin
formver {
    verificationErrorSeverity("error")  // or "warning", the default
}
```

and the corresponding compiler-plugin option `verification_error_severity`.

## Design

The Kotlin diagnostic API fixes a severity per `KtDiagnosticFactory`, so a
configurable severity takes one set of factories per severity. `VerificationErrors`
keeps the warning-level factories and `StrictVerificationErrors` holds error-level
ones; both implement `VerificationDiagnostics`, which is what the reporting path
now takes. Because a factory's name is its property name, the two sets carry the
*same* diagnostic names — so which set is in use is invisible to anything that
refers to a diagnostic by name: a `@Suppress`, an `-Xwarning-level`, a test's
expected tags. The shared interface is also what keeps the two sets from drifting:
a diagnostic added to one must be added to the other.

The switch covers every failed-proof diagnostic, not only
`VIPER_VERIFICATION_ERROR` — a build that broke on an unproven postcondition but
not on a possible index-out-of-bounds would be incoherent.

## Tests

`testData/diagnostics/verification/error_severity/` holds the same failing proof
twice, differing only in the `FAIL_ON_VERIFICATION_ERROR` directive. The
`.viper.diag.txt` goldens record the severity, so the pair asserts `warning:`
against `error:`.

The harness collects diagnostics rather than compiling, so it cannot assert that a
build fails. That was checked by hand against a consumer project resolving the
plugin from mavenLocal: on the default the failed proof is `w:` and the build
succeeds; with `verificationErrorSeverity("error")` it is `e:` and `:compileKotlin`
fails.

`./agent-scripts/check-all.sh` passes.

author: itsjoshpark
body:
The bottom of the app was a single slot. `App.vue` rendered either the rename bar **or** the narrow footer holding `SizeSlider`, never both:

```vue
<RenameBar v-if="aperture.rename.active.value" />
<footer v-else …><SizeSlider /></footer>
```

So the moment you entered rename mode — dragging a tile, `Cmd`+arrow, or the toolbar button — the zoom control vanished for the whole session, exactly when you most want it: zooming out to see the folder and back in to check one photo is half of arranging it. Getting the slider back cost you the session.

## What changed

- **`src/App.vue`** — the `<footer>` renders unconditionally and `RenameBar` stacks above it as a sibling in the existing `flex h-dvh flex-col` shell. No positioning, no z-index, no padding compensation: the grid scroller is already `min-h-0 flex-1`, so it gives up the height and both bars stay fully visible.
- **`src/components/RenameBar.vue`** — root gains `shrink-0`, which the footer already had. With two bars competing for the leftover height, a flex column otherwise squashes the rename panel at the widths where its affix row wraps and the info line plus `Progress` stack.
- Comments in `useRenameSession.apply()`, `RenameBar.vue` and `AGENTS.md` that promised "the size slider comes back" now say only that the rename panel closes — plus a new entry under *Grid, input, dialogs* recording that the bottom is two panels rather than one slot, so nobody folds it back into a `v-if`/`v-else`.

Applying a rename still ends the session and hides the panel; that half needed no code, since `apply()` already finishes in `cancel()`.

## Tests

`e2e/gallery.spec.ts` — the rename test asserted `await expect(sizeSlider).toBeHidden()` mid-session, which is now the opposite of the intended behaviour. It asserts the slider is visible instead, and goes one step further: it presses `ArrowRight` on the slider with the rename panel open and expects `aria-valuenow` to change, so the control is proven usable and not merely rendered. The post-apply half now also asserts the rename button is gone while the slider stays.

Verified locally: `pnpm check`, `pnpm test run --project unit` (188 passed), and the Playwright suite (48 passed). One pre-existing failure — "re-reads the photos when a rename hands their names to other files" — reproduces identically on a clean `main` checkout in this sandbox, which only has a mismatched Chromium build; it is untouched by this diff.

author: aallan
body:
Part of the #1213 burndown (PR C1) — the module-routing cluster. Six commits plus the rebase resolution.

## What this fixes

**#1207 — one effect-op result table** (`3718b817`). Monomorphization discovery and the WASM rewrite previously derived an effect-op's result type independently and disagreed on a `get(())` array element driving a generic instantiation (`pick$Nat` vs `pick$Int` — a dangling call target, loud E602 drop). `vera.slots.effect_op_result_names` is now the single derivation; codegen's declared-effect-row registry, `_translate_handle_state`, and discovery's new scoped walk all read it. Scope is mirrored, not approximated: a `handle` installs its table over its body only (init and clause bodies stay in the enclosing context, per #1211's rule), and a declared-row op is never injected where a user function owns the name.

**#1223 — generic-under-generic helpers instantiate their own callees** (`58dc60e0`). The #1002 machinery instantiated the nested helper but never walked the helper's own callees, so a top-level generic called from inside the helper body went unregistered — E602 skip, E620 cascade, zero exports from check-clean verify-clean source. Hoisting and the top-level worklist are now a fixpoint over one shared leaf (`collect_generic_helper_instances`) that the verifier drives too; that same review surfaced and fixed the sibling case in the growing body set.

**#1241 + #1243 — clone bodies route through the declaring module, both halves atomically** (`32f02c12`). An imported generic's clone resolved its bare body calls through the IMPORTER's registries — running the importer's same-named private function (999 where the declaring module's returns 111), with type-discriminating shapes emitting invalid WASM from check-green source. The verifier's `_declaring_module_scope` now carries the module's function registry beside env/source/file, and codegen's clone-emission path threads `_module_intra_renames` the way Passes 2.5/2.6 already do. The pairing constraint is measured, not asserted: with the codegen half stashed, `vera verify` reports clean and the run raises the postcondition violation — so every test asserts the verify verdict AND the runtime value in one test against a standalone-module oracle, making it impossible for either half to pass alone. This closes the **private / non-generic** dimension only: the same routing question for an imported **public generic** whose name the importer also declares is a distinct hole in the *clone-name* space — both modules' `gen2` mangle to `gen2$Bool` and one overwrites the other — tracked as [#1274](https://github.com/aallan/vera/issues/1274), pre-existing and byte-identical at `ef7c04c0`.

**#1244 — every module's bodies check under its own import filter** (`03adbe6d`). Import visibility was entry-point-dependent (E200 warn when checked directly, silence when reached as an import). Measured blast radius before implementing: ZERO — 7 corpus programs import a non-stdlib module, none of whose modules carries a standalone diagnostic. One existing expectation moved, toward strictness: the module-builtin-effect redeclaration fixture now expects exactly its standalone verdict. The change also removed a duplicate error-surfacing path (codegen-only, errors-only) in favor of one collection with the memo threaded.

**#1253 — codegen's ADT membership is scoped** (`b711e2e9`). Membership now derives from the owning namespace plus the module's own imports, public and in-filter — closing both the issue's measurement (`['Array<?>', 'Array<Int>']` vs `['Array<Float>', 'Array<Int>']`) and the private-sibling visibility dimension appended from PR #1254's review.

## Rebase provenance

Rebased onto `ef7c04c0` (post-C5) with the resolution as the visible final commit. Content integrity: diff-of-diffs over `vera/ tests/ spec/` identical modulo hunk offsets across all 24 code files. The C5 interaction was probed with a purpose-built fixture (an imported `forall<T>` throwing a provably-negative payload, so #1268's new obligation lands inside a clone verified under this PR's pinned registries): identical verdicts on both trees, both variants. That probe surfaced a pre-existing C5 residual (the throw obligation does not survive monomorphization), recorded on #1268 — not this PR's.

## Adjacent defect, filed not fixed

#1271: discovery inside a still-generic scope binds a callee's type variable to the enclosing variable's name, emitting a spurious `pick$U` clone that is loudly E604-skipped on every generic-under-generic program — the reason #1223's shapes live in pytest rather than conformance. Suppressing it changes the shared discovery walk with its own blast radius; queued separately.

## Gates

pytest 9,917 passed / 132 skipped / 26 deselected (10,075 collected, oracle-matched); mypy clean; ruff + `--select S` clean; conformance 207/207; examples 42/42; corpus canonical 255/255; doc counts, site assets, diagnostic fields, limitations sync (45 rows), e602-clean, explicit encoding all green. Every commit passed the full 33-hook pre-commit gate; the rebased tree re-gated by hand end to end.

Closes #1207.
Closes #1223.
Closes #1241.
Closes #1243.
Closes #1244.
Closes #1253.

(Keywords take effect at the release PR.)

author: rodrigok
body: > **PoC — not for merge as-is.** Draft, stacked on #41657. > **Base is `feat/persistant-chat`**, so this diff shows only the native-provider work. Review #41657 first. ## Proposed changes Adds **LiveKit as a native video conference provider**, so a call can run inside Rocket.Chat instead of handing the user off to someone else's page. Every provider until now has been a URL. The workspace knows a call is open and nothing else: not who is in it, not what was said, and certainly not how to record it. Running the call in-process changes what the server is able to know, and most of this diff is the consequence of that rather than the SFU itself — conferences now carry the participants actually connected, so presence stops being inferred from who clicked join. On top of that: multi-party calls with a grid and spotlight, screen sharing, hand-raise and reactions, egress-based recording that lands as an ordinary upload posted in a thread under the call's message, and opt-in live captions from a worker that joins each room as a hidden participant — with note-taking on, the transcript is kept and summarised when the call ends. The provider is **enterprise and off unless configured**. A workspace with no LiveKit deployment behaves exactly as before. Deployment (CloudFormation + walkthrough): [`docs/features/native-video-conference/deploying-livekit.md`](docs/features/native-video-conference/deploying-livekit.md). ## Where this came from Ported from #40726 (`feat/vc-poc`), **minus that PR's persistent-chat work**, which this stack already carries from #41657. That PR's history splits cleanly: commits up to `7e617cc8a8c` are the LiveKit work, everything after is its own conference-window integration. Only the first range was taken, so none of `client/views/conference/`, `client/views/root/`, `appLayout`, `desktop-api` or `startup/routes.tsx` came across. Reconciling against a newer `develop` needed six things: - **`app/` was restructured** — the settings, notifications and file-upload imports across eight EE files point at their new homes (`server/settings`, `server/lib/notifications/core/lib/Notifications`, `server/lib/media/file-upload`, `server/meteor-methods/messages/sendFileMessage`). - `useGoToRoom` left `ui-contexts` for the app. - fuselage no longer accepts the `w` / `h` / `bg` shorthands. - `MediaCallRoomActivity` gained `MediaCallViewProvider` and container-height sizing on develop while the PR replaced that sizing with `useTileGridLayout`; the PR's layout wins, since it is what the rewritten section expects. - `IVideoConference` took **both** sides — this stack's membership predicates *and* the provider's participant / recording / transcript records. - `@livekit/agents` and `@livekit/rtc-node` were pinned at `latest`, which a committed lockfile cannot honour. Pinned to what resolved (`^1.6.2`, `^0.13.33`). ## Then it was wired to the conference window Testing against a live LiveKit found the seam between the two features, and it was worse than "not wired": with both enabled, the room's call button led to a preflight that never went anywhere. An embedded provider answers the join with an empty `url` — there is no page to send anyone to — and the conference page read a missing url as "not joined yet", so it re-rendered the preflight forever. - The page now waits on having **joined** rather than on having a url, and renders the call itself when there is no page to embed. - The connection is registered with the bridge **above** the route, which is the same slot the in-room path uses — a call cannot be claimed twice, and it survives the page re-rendering. - **One bottom bar.** The call brings mic, camera, screen, hand and hang-up; the window already had a bar carrying members and chat. The call's controls are handed to that bar and take its centre. They are *moved, not rebuilt* — the same nodes in the same component — so the two placements cannot drift. - The **floating mini-view is gone**. It followed the user out of the call's room, which a call that always has a window of its own never needs; in that window it drew a second copy of the call over the members panel. - Twelve strings in the call's bar were hardcoded English or asked for keys that were never added, so recording, notes, captions and the camera tooltip rendered as `Start_recording` and friends. The hang-up button read "End call with Call" on group calls. ## Steps to test or reproduce Requires a LiveKit deployment; see the deploy doc. Then, as admin: 1. **Admin → Video Conference** — enable LiveKit, set URL / API key / secret, make it the default provider. 2. Open a channel and press **Video call**. The preflight opens in a dedicated window; set mic/camera there. 3. Confirm — the call runs in that window with its chat and members panels beside it, and the controls in the single bottom bar. ## Verified Against a live LiveKit (`wss://livekit.dev.rocket.chat`): | | | |---|---| | `video-conference.capabilities` | reports the provider `embedded: true` | | `video-conference.start` | creates the conference, posts the call block | | `video-conference.join` | returns `url: ""`, records the participant | | `…livekit.transport.config` | mints a real room token | | The call | connects; live 1280×720 camera track; members panel populates | | Preflight honoured | started with mic **off** / camera **on** — the inverse of the provider defaults — and the call came up muted with video | | One bar | 1 footer; 8 call controls + 2 panel toggles in it | | Layout | call column `min-width: 0`, no horizontal overflow | `yarn typecheck` clean · jest 309 suites / 2214 passing · mocha 2258 · definition 152 · eslint clean over the ported tree. ## Not verified — please exercise before this goes anywhere near merge - **A second participant.** Grid and spotlight layout, per-tile speaking indicators, hand-raise queue positions and reactions have all only been seen with one person in the call. - **Recording.** The egress path, S3 upload, and the thread reply were never triggered. - **Captions / transcripts / AI summary.** The agent worker was never dispatched. - **The 1:1 VoIP path.** `MediaCallRoomSection` now renders `CallStage` for direct calls too, replacing develop's `MediaCallCardList`. That is the ported PR's design, but it changes existing VoIP call rendering and deserves a look on a running workspace. - Docker: `Dockerfile.alpine` gained a musl build of the LiveKit FFI binding; the image was never built here. ## Further comments `MEDIA-CALLS-FEATURE.md` and `deploy/livekit/deploy.md` moved under `docs/features/native-video-conference/`, where this repo keeps feature docs. The CloudFormation templates stay in `deploy/livekit/`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

body:
## Finding (383c3463 reassessment, prod log measurement 2026-08-10)

The card asked whether the 2026-06-02 'plugin submenu not found' incident was a #238 regression or a TUI render change. Measuring the CURRENT prod dashboard.log instead of chasing the two-month-old incident:

- **89** `channel-mcp-reconnect: completed` (stage-1 works)
- **79** `plugin submenu not found` + **68** `could not place cursor on target option` (it also fails a lot)
- **16** pane-busy defers
- The failures CLUSTER by dashboard generation: pid 34662 produced 28/28 submenu failures with zero successes, while other generations succeed — a per-generation persistent condition (CC version? pane state? menu render variant?), not random flake.
- An honest self-correction is part of the record: my first per-pid slice suggested 48/48 structural failure; the refuter grep on the success-path wording (`completed`) overturned it.

**The blocker for root-causing — in June and now — is that neither failure warn records what the TUI showed.**

## Change

`paneDiagSignature()`: a REDACTED signature attached to both failure warns — `inBlockingMenu` (was any menu open), `sawPluginRow` (was the plugin row rendered), `paneState` class, non-empty line count, capture flag. Booleans/counts only: the pane is the main session's screen and may carry conversation text, so raw pane content never reaches the log. A test pins the redaction contract (`JSON.stringify(sig)` must not contain pane text).

Next time the failure fires, the log discriminates the hypotheses directly: menu open without the plugin row (row-id/pagination issue) vs no menu at all (lost keystroke / wrong pane state) vs busy race.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` 0; full suite **3527/3527** (4 new tests).
- Mutation control: forcing `sawPluginRow: true` makes exactly the 2 discriminating tests fail; restored, all green.
- Diff is log-only (no behavior change on any path): the walk gains a `lastPane` holder, both warns gain fields.

Investigation continues on the card once live signatures accumulate; this PR is the instrument.

body:
## What this is

The **second ratified R2 (v2.1 addendum) increment**, composing directly with A9/A8 (#119). It implements **A10 — nearest-rupee rounding per tax component**.

## Changes

- **`packages/finance/src/inclusive-tax.ts`**:
  - `roundToNearestRupeeMinor(minor)` — rounds a paisa amount to the nearest whole rupee: **≥50 paisa rounds UP, <50 paisa rounds DOWN** (correct for negative amounts too). Rejects a non-whole paisa input.
  - `roundToNearestRupee(breakdown)` — applies it to the taxable value and **each tax component** of an extracted breakdown, and states the resulting **round-off explicitly** (P-08 — the invoice "Round Off" line, which may be ±). A rounding that moves money is never silent.
  - **The exact paisa breakdown (A9) is left untouched** and still reconciles to the MRP; this is purely the additional whole-rupee view an invoice prints beside a single round-off line.
- **`services/finance/src/tax.ts`** — `GET /v1/finance/tax/from-mrp` now returns the exact breakdown (A9/A8) **plus** a `nearestRupee` view (A10), so an invoice can print either without re-deriving the rounding. Same route, same `finance.period.read` gate — no new surface.
- **`tests/unit/finance-inclusive-tax.test.ts`** — the exact **≥50p-up / <50p-down boundary** (0/49/50/99/149/150/249/250) and the per-component rounding worked through end to end: ₹9.99 @ 18% intra → exact `847 / 76 / 76+1` → rounded `800 / 100 / 100`, round-off **+₹0.01**; and a zero round-off when every part is already whole. Plus the non-whole-paisa refusal.
- **`tests/integration/tax-from-mrp.test.ts`** — the route serves the `nearestRupee` view correctly while the exact view still reconciles.
- **`docs/traceability.md`** (A10 row) + **`docs/STATUS.md`**.

## Validation

`typecheck` + `lint` + `secret-scan` clean; full default suite **4,765 tests / 332 files green**. **No new dependency, no new permission, no new route.**

## Context

The CORE-04 pure-read seam is complete (five increments, #114–#118) and confirmed exhausted; work now advances the owner-ratified R2 scope (#106), holding the gated items (turnover-triggered e-invoicing, chart of accounts, payroll ownership, product-line decisions, the ten owner decisions) for pre-deployment.

## Next

Continue R2 with the next self-contained non-gated requirement — e.g. A11 (s.15(3) discount eligibility) or A6 (GST slabs with time-of-supply).

Tax amounts come out in paise, but a printed invoice usually shows whole rupees with a small "Round Off" line at the bottom. author: aryeh-stark
body:
## The incident

`--commit-all` runs `git add -A`, which stages **untracked** files as well as modified ones. On 2026-08-10 that swept a repo's `.envrc` into a PR and pushed it.

**The existing secret scan did not catch it and could not.** It is **content**-based, and the file held only paths and email subjects — every entropy and token rule passed it cleanly. The hazard was the file's **identity**, not any string inside it.

## Why it was exposed at all

Worth stating, because the file wasn't unprotected by accident:

1. `.envrc` **was** covered by the operator's **global** gitignore.
2. The repo's own `.gitignore` carried `!/*.*` to re-include root files with extensions.
3. **A repo-level negation overrides the global ignore** — punching a hole straight through the cover.

Nothing looked wrong at any single layer.

## The fix

Adds the **path**-based half, complementing the content scan rather than duplicating it. Before `git add -A` runs, list what it would newly stage (`git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`) and refuse on anything shaped like local config or credential material:

`.envrc` · `.env*` · `*.pem` · `*.key` · `id_rsa` · `client_secret*.json` · `service-account*.json` · `credentials.json` · `*.tfstate` · `.direnv/` · `.claude/` · `.netrc` · `.DS_Store`

Three properties it holds:

| Property | Why |
|---|---|
| Refusal runs **before** `git add` | The index is never touched — nothing to unstage, no half-staged tree to explain |
| Published examples never flagged | `.env.example`, `.envrc.sample`, `*.pub`, `*pubkeys/*.pem`. Friction that stops ordinary work gets disabled, and then it protects nothing |
| Correct `.gitignore` ⇒ **no** behaviour change | `--exclude-standard` means the guard never sees the file |

## Override

`--allow-untracked-config`, deliberately **separate** from `--allow-secret-commit`: that one asserts the content is fine, this one asserts you meant to publish a config file — and the `.envrc` case passed the content scan.

The refusal names each file, its reason, and both remedies, pointing at `git check-ignore -q` and warning that a matching `.gitignore` line is not proof.

## Verification

- **375/375** tests pass (7 new).
- Guard verified **live** against a scratch repo reproducing the original negation bug: fires on `.envrc`, silent on ordinary new source files.

body:
💡 **What:** Optimized horizontal and vertical border scanning loops in `backend/segmentation/segmenter.py` to use `zip()` instead of array length index iteration (`range(len(y_coords))`). Fixed linter check issues by explicitly adding `strict=False` in `zip` configurations for ruff standard checks (B905).

🎯 **Why:** Array length iterations and multiple subsequent access lookup operations using identical indices across different arrays (such as `x_coords[i]`, `left_ids[i]`) are slower and recognized as an anti-pattern compared to Python's built-in array unpacking using `zip()`.

📊 **Measured Improvement:** A local benchmark using a dense 2000x2000 matrix with heavy regional segmentation (each 2x2 grid representing a distinct region to maximize touch point borders) demonstrated the bottleneck function `shared_border_segmentation` executing in ~173 seconds versus the original implementation at ~190 seconds (a roughly ~8.98% runtime improvement purely due to loop unpacking mechanics).

author: hamidshirzad
body:
Follow-up to #13. The last Codex review ran against `8af741f` — the commit that merged — so its three findings were never addressed and are now on `master`. All three are in files I wrote in that PR. Each was verified against the merged code before I changed anything.

## 1. The README invited putting secrets into a tracked file (P1)

"Multiple environments" still offered supplying per-tenant values *"by editing the mappings"* — meaning SMTP passwords and provider client secrets written into `auth0/config.json`, which is tracked. That is permanent once committed; deleting the file later does not remove it from history.

It also contradicted two other parts of the same document: the instruction to keep mappings in the environment secret, and the file table's promise that `config.json` holds no credentials. Leftover wording from an earlier revision I failed to reconcile.

The file-based option is gone. A second tenant now means a second GitHub environment with its own `AUTH0_KEYWORD_REPLACE_MAPPINGS` secret and its own credentials, and the section now also flags that markers must be quoted.

## 2. Pre-flight ignored the config file's delete switch (P1)

`preflight.mjs` read only `process.env`, so `"AUTH0_ALLOW_DELETE": true` in `auth0/config.json` passed silently — not even the deletion warning — and the `a0deploy import` that `npm run auth0:import` runs seconds later *does* read that file and performs a destructive sync.

The guard exists to make deletion an explicit opt-in, and it was blind to the one place the setting is version-controlled.

It now checks both sources and names which one enabled it:

```
AUTH0_ALLOW_DELETE=true (from auth0/config.json) — deletion is ENABLED for this import.
```

A real boolean `false` in the config file is the intended default and passes untouched — only *strings* are dangerous, since those are what the raw truthy checks in `handlers/default.js` and friends misread.

## 3. Unquoted YAML markers were invisible (P2)

Scanning walked *parsed* values, but:

```yaml
client_secret: ##SMTP_PASS##      # → parses to null; ## starts a YAML comment
client_secret: "##SMTP_PASS##"    # → parses to "##SMTP_PASS##"
```

So an unquoted marker was invisible to pre-flight, and the import would write `null` over the credential rather than preserving or substituting it. A CLI-written export is safe — `js-yaml` quotes strings beginning with `#` — but hand-editing is exactly what the multi-environment section asks for, so this is reachable by following the documentation.

Markers found in raw text but absent from every parsed value are now reported as unquoted, naming the file.

## Testing

Seven cases, starting with the **round-5 regression** since that is the one most at risk:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Bootstrap: quoted standalone markers, no mappings | pass (no regression) |
| `config.json` `AUTH0_ALLOW_DELETE: true` | warns, names source, passes |
| `config.json` `AUTH0_ALLOW_DELETE: "false"` | refuses |
| env `AUTH0_ALLOW_DELETE=false` | refuses |
| Unquoted marker | refuses, names file |
| Quoted marker | passes |
| `node --check`, workflow YAML parses, `workflow_dispatch` still the only trigger | pass |

`cd backend && npm test` → **41/41** (up from 40 now that #11 is merged).

## Still unverified

No `a0deploy` command has ever run against `dev-sfv34zclvdf4noih`. This makes the guards more correct on paper; it does not demonstrate the tooling works. That needs the M2M application, and one real export would validate more than further static iteration — six review rounds on #13 turned up a genuine defect every time, several of them in guards added the round before.

author: rutgerfick
body:
First of the staged port that makes the **replay-pack pipeline public**: this lands the *produce* and *compress* halves so the public package can run a walk once and compress it into the replay IR — the same production code that already generates the substrate-commons packs (planes/cylinders/spheres). Behavior-preserving; nothing new physics-wise, just relocating the proven producer/compression layer into the public package.

## What this adds
- **Producer** — `core.simulate_trajectories(..., save_relaxation_data=)`: walk once, emit the trajectory + compartment/boundary channels.
- **Compression** — `compression.py`: `encode_{temporal_dct,lowrank,gaussian,marginal}`, boundary-local-time / bound-fraction (MT) / compartment channel codecs, `auto_select_modes`, `default_envelope`, `acquisition_battery`, `measure_fidelity`. Default codec `temporal_dct` (robust to the aarch64 OpenBLAS SVD issue).
- **Replay operators on a master walk** — `trajectories.py`: `replay`, `replay_jax`, `replay_bloch`, `replay_bloch_jax`, plus `mt_walk.simulate_mt_trajectories`.

This is the generator *behind* the `.rpk` pack. The pack decoder (`replay.py`, #15) is already public; this opens the produce+compress side so a public user can make packs, not only consume them.

## Namespace reconciliation with #15
The landed `replay.py` (#15) owns `dmipy_sim.replay` as the `.rpk` pack-forward **module**. Python's submodule import binds that name on the package, so the trajectory-replay **function** can't also be a bare top-level `replay`. It's now reached via `dmipy_sim.trajectories.replay` (internal call sites already imported it directly from `.trajectories`, so the producer path is unchanged). `replay_jax`/`replay_bloch`/`replay_bloch_jax` don't collide and stay top-level. Full unification of the two `ReplayPack`/replay surfaces is deferred to PR-B (the `build_replay_pack` port).

## Verification
- Fast tier (CI-equivalent, `-m "not slow and not gpu"`): **209 passed, 5 skipped** — merge with `main` (#11 Bloch permeability + #15 replay) broke nothing.
- Produce→compress→replay parity on GPU (`test_replay_parity`, `test_replay_fields_mt`, `test_engine_dispatch`): **62 passed, 5 skipped** — the compressed-master replay reproduces the `simulate` forward across free / box1d / sphere / cylinder / mesh, for pure-gradient, scalar-T2, per-compartment-T2, and surface-relaxivity; vector-Bloch + susceptibility + MT replay match `simulate_bloch` / the analytic oracle.

## Next in the series (not this PR)
- **PR-B** — `build_replay_pack` + `build_to_floor` + `ReplayPack` unification (the certified-pack assembler).
- **PR-C** — bank federation (`publish`/`pull`/`stage_pack`/card/croissant) behind a `[bank]` extra.
- **PR-D** — public shard contribution (HF dataset PRs against the public bank).

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #7, addressing a review finding: the 9119 dashboard route refresh ran as a second box `command()` inside `ensureBoxAwake`'s health-probe retry loop, which is bounded by a 180 s deadline and sits on the hot path of every turn (chat, iMessage, email). Each `command()` can run up to 180 s right after resume, so doubling the per-iteration work could exhaust the wake window and turn a recoverable resume into `hermes … not healthy after resume`.

`refreshHostedRoutes` is split:

```
refreshApiServerRoute()   – 8642 only, stays inside the retry loop, still fatal on failure
refreshDashboardRoute()   – 9119, fire-and-forget (`void …`) AFTER the health check passes;
                            never throws, never blocks or fails a turn
```

The dashboard token still gets refreshed on every resume that actually rotated it (the background call fires only when the loop performed a refresh), it just no longer consumes any of the wake deadline. Nothing on the request path reads `UserBox.dashboard` today, so eventual consistency is fine.

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/9a1bd6b57cc34a3dbe49207c5f33711b

author: jansen-w
body:
## Summary

Runtime filesystem capacity errors can be temporary, but disk-buffer writes previously treated them as fatal I/O failures. This change makes `disk_v2` writers:

- recognize `StorageFull`, `ENOSPC`, and `EDQUOT` errors;
- retain partially written bytes and resume from the committed offset without duplication;
- apply backpressure within the owning write or flush future while waiting for reader progress or exponential retry;
- preserve logical `when_full` behavior while physical capacity exhaustion consistently backpressures every policy;
- emit one structured capacity-exhausted event and one recovery event per episode, with buffer path, operation, retry count, delay, and duration;
- preserve structured fatal synchronization errors and keep startup/non-capacity failures fatal.

Production writes remain session-owned synchronous syscalls. A kernel write cannot be portably cancelled and can delay cancellation until it returns; keeping it session-owned prevents writes from outliving the buffer lock or racing a reopened buffer.

## Vector configuration

No new configuration is required. The behavior applies to existing `disk_v2` buffers.

## How did you test this PR?

- `cargo test -p vector-buffers` (132 passed, 2 pre-existing ignored)
- `cargo clippy -p vector-buffers --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo vdev check events`
- `cargo vdev check changelog-fragments`
- Deterministic regressions for partial writes, cancelled flush/write resume, small and large writes after cancellation, timer/reader wakeups, retry ownership and telemetry, atomic/fallback file opens, rotation synchronization, startup failures, and non-capacity errors

Real exhausted-filesystem and Windows-specific behavior remain covered through deterministic fault injection rather than platform integration tests.

## Is this a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Does this PR include user facing changes?

- [x] Yes. A changelog fragment is included.
- [ ] No. A maintainer will apply the `no-changelog` label to this PR.

## References

None.

body:
Part of #81230

## What?

Moves `ValidatedSelectControl` out of the `@wordpress/components` private APIs and into `@wordpress/dataviews` as internal code.

## Why?

See #81230

DataForm is the only consumer of `ValidatedSelectControl` as per https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/81306#issuecomment-5215240967

## How?

- Move the component to DataViews, as well as the supporting ones (`ControlWithError` + `ValidityIndicator` foundation). The CSS namespace renamed from `components-validated-control` to `dataviews-validated-control`.
- Remove usage of private API in favor of the internal component.

One intentional typing change: the old wrapper's props omitted `multiple`/`value`/`onChange` and re-typed them as single-select only, while DataForm passes `multiple` for `array`-type fields (which previously typechecked only because `unlock()` returns `any`). The internal wrapper now passes through `SelectControl`'s own discriminated union, so both single and multiple selection are typed correctly.

## Testing Instructions

1. `npm run test:unit packages/dataviews/src/components/validated-form-controls packages/dataviews/src/dataform packages/components/src/validated-form-controls`
2. `npm run build:package-types`

    2. Submit the form with the invalid select: focus should move to it and the error should be announced (the message is wired via `aria-describedby`, merged with the `help` text).
4. Confirm the `ValidatedSelectControl` story is gone from **Components → Selection & Input → Validated Form Controls**, while the other validated control stories still work.

author: fontanierh
body:
## Description

`/pod-state/databases` is workload-writable by design, and litestream replicates whatever SQLite file lands there. `dsbx db reconcile` chmods the databases it creates to `0660` precisely so litestream (user `dust-state`, group `agent`) can write them — but a function that opens a database directly, without going through reconcile, bypasses that.

Those files land at the process umask. In production today:

```
-rw-r-----  1 1003 1002   4096  arena.db        # agent-proxied:agent, 0640
-rw-r-----  1 1003 1002  32768  arena.db-shm
-rw-r-----  1 1003 1002 288432  arena.db-wal
```

`dust-state` is in group `agent`, so it could read the file but never write it. Litestream needs to write the source database (it creates a `_litestream_seq` table), so every sync failed:

```
sync failed: sync database: db sync: create _litestream_seq table:
attempt to write a readonly database (8)
```

That database therefore never replicated at all, and the sandbox failed its pre-sleep flush on every reaper sweep — it never slept for three days, and once a kill was requested for the image rollout it could not be destroyed either, blocking the rollout.

The image already sets the directory up to make this work: `install -d -o dust-state -g agent -m 2770` plus `setfacl -R -d -m g::rwx`. The setgid bit gives new files group `agent`, but a default ACL only *masks* the mode the process requests — it cannot add back bits the umask stripped. So the `g::rwx` intent silently never took effect for function-created files.

This sets `process.umask(0o007)` in the functions runner, the single entry point for `dsbx function run/serve` and every `dsbx db` subcommand, and the process the untrusted function bundle is imported into. Everything a function creates is then group-writable, matching what reconcile already does by hand.

`007` rather than `002`: `other` stays empty. Group `agent` (`agent`, `agent-proxied`, `dust-state`) is the sandbox's existing trust boundary — and since the directory is `2770` and group-writable, the `agent` user could already unlink and replace any file in it, so this widens no boundary that was actually closed.

Bumps dsbx to 0.1.45 and dust-base to 0.8.70 so the change ships in the image.

Companion PR: #30269 stops an unflushable sandbox from blocking a rollout forever.

## Tests

- New `runner.test.ts` case runs a fixture function that creates a file with no explicit mode and asserts it comes out `0660` — it fails on `main` (`0644`).
- `bun test functions-runner/` — 109 passed.
- `npm test lib/api/sandbox/image/registry.test.ts` — 20 passed (version-bump assertions).
- Verified against the live sandbox: root `chmod 660` on the three `arena.db*` files made litestream log `sync recovered` and upload its first LTX file, and the next reaper sweep destroyed the sandbox cleanly.

## Risk

Low, and the blast radius is limited to files created inside a sandbox.

- The umask only widens the group bit, and only for the runner process. It does not touch existing files, does not run as root, and cannot make anything world-readable.
- Group `agent` already had directory-level write on both shared directories (`2770`), so a group-writable file grants the workload nothing it could not already do by unlinking and replacing the file.
- Files the runner writes outside `/pod-state/databases` (e.g. under `/files`) also become group-writable. Same trust group, same setgid + `g::rwx` ACL intent, so this is the designed behaviour rather than a new exposure.
- The riskiest part is not the one-line umask but the version bump: shipping 0.8.70 kill-requests every sandbox on 0.8.69 and recycles the fleet. That path runs on every image release and ran today.
- Rollback is a revert plus a version bump back; no data migration, no persisted state depends on the mode.

Not fixed by this PR: databases already created at `0640` inside a live sandbox stay unwritable until that sandbox is recycled. Fleet-wide there are currently none — a 30-day sweep of litestream errors found four sandboxes, all the same `arena.db` in workspace `0ec9852c2f`, three already destroyed and the fourth repaired by hand today.

## Deploy Plan

1. Merge, then run the **Release dsbx CLI** workflow to publish the `dsbx-v0.1.45` release artifacts. The image build pulls the binary from that release tag, so it must exist before the image is built.
2. Build and publish the `dust-base` 0.8.70 image.
3. Deploy `front`. The kill-requester marks every sandbox whose version differs from 0.8.70, and the reaper recycles them over subsequent sweeps — the same rollout path as any image bump.
4. Watch `@source:litestream @status:error` and the pod-state health metric during the rollout. A recurrence of `readonly database (8)` on a sandbox already running 0.8.70 would mean the umask did not take effect and should be investigated before the rollout completes.

Ordering matters between steps 1 and 2 only; step 3 is safe at any point after, since older sandboxes keep running their existing image until recycled.

author: phsb5321
body:
## The close-and-relaunch oracle — done with a REAL window close

The actor closes the window through the X server (`xdotool windowclose` =
the **WM_DELETE_WINDOW** client message a window manager sends on the close
button) — **not** a process kill, which would prove nothing about
`CloseRequested` and would pass a broken fix. The close is a detached spawn
issued immediately after the actor's last action — as fast as a physical
user could manage. `xdotool` added to the flake devShell (the ONE toolchain
source).

Four phases, one hermetic profile, fresh app process per phase.

## DL-2 (reading position lost on close): CONFIRMED RED

```
==> PHASE dl2-create  (resume page 2 → Next → page 3 → genuine close, inside the 500 ms debounce)  1 passing
==> observer: library row after dl2-create
E2E Resume Fixture A|2            ← the write never flushed
==> PHASE dl2-verify  (relaunch → resume → expected page 3)  1 FAILING
DIAG dl2-verify: {"landedPage":"2"}
```

`useAutoSave`'s 500 ms debounce never fires before the teardown kills the JS
context, and `checkUnsavedProgress` (the beforeunload localStorage fallback)
has **zero callers** — nothing recovers the position. The 112 fix must flush
the pending page write on `CloseRequested` (or wire the dead fallback).

## DL-1 (highlight lost after the app said it saved): REFUTED for genuine closes

```
==> PHASE dl1-create  (resume → drag-select → Yellow → toast captured → genuine close)  1 passing
DIAG dl1-create: {"toastText":"Highlight created"}
==> observer: v_highlight_citations after dl1-create
1                                         ← the row LANDED
==> PHASE dl1-verify  (relaunch → resume → highlight must still be there)  1 passing
DIAG dl1-verify: {"highlightSurvived":true}
```

Even with the fastest achievable close (~150 ms after the create, well
inside the 500 ms debounce window), the highlight **survives** — the app's
graceful close teardown outlives the debounce, so the flush completes. The
success toast is **truthful** in this scenario. DL-1 only reproduces under a
SIGKILL — which proves nothing about `CloseRequested`. The audit's
code-reading predicted loss; the packaged lane shows the teardown latency
prevents it. Result stable across two full runs.

## The lane

`e2e/close-journey.e2e.mjs` (4 phases) + `e2e/run-close-journey.sh`
(observer DB checks after each create phase). Inherits only the shared entry
points. The lane is the oracle for 112: after the fix, `dl2-verify` must go
green; `dl1` stays green.

## Gates

- `pnpm test:run` — 92 files / 1043 tests · lint 0 errors · typecheck +
  type-coverage ≥99.9 clean · alignment gate PASS (2 files, 0 errors)
- Lane output pasted above (all four phases + observer rows)

Not self-mergeable as-is (dl2-verify is red for a product reason — the 112
fix flips it green). `Analyze` red on every branch incl. main — known,
Pedro-gated.
