Pascal a commencé à dérouler le TP de 5e pour en prendre les captures. Il
n'est pas allé loin : dès le deuxième palier, « après avoir cliqué sur
Esquisse, quel plan je choisis ? ». Le TP répondait « le plan Top ». Ses
captures montrent que l'interface française d'Onshape affiche, dans la liste
de gauche : Origine, Haut, Avant, Exact. Un élève qui cherche « Top » ne le
trouve pas.

Trois écarts, tous du même genre, corrigés dans les trois scénarios d'un
coup puisque les mêmes termes s'y étaient propagés :

  Top / Front / Right      →  Haut / Avant / Exact
  Part Studio              →  Partie Studio
  un onglet au démarrage   →  DEUX : Partie Studio 1 et Assemblée 1

« Exact » est la traduction — mauvaise — que fait Onshape de Right. La règle
n°73 impose de citer le bouton tel qu'il est écrit, même quand c'est écrit
mal : le TP dit donc Exact.

Et un piège qu'aucune traduction ne résout : les étiquettes dessinées DANS LA
ZONE 3D sont restées en anglais alors que la liste de gauche est en français.
Le même plan porte deux noms sur le même écran. Le TP le dit maintenant
explicitement, avec le cube d'orientation qui affiche « Dessus ». Les
raccourcis g et r du menu rectangle sont notés au passage.

CE QUE ÇA CONFIRME. La règle n°70 disait qu'une capture doit parler la langue
du poste. Il faut l'étendre au TEXTE : un TP rédigé d'après une documentation
anglophone décrit un logiciel que l'élève n'a pas sous les yeux, et aucune

author: dbczumar
body:
## Related issue

Closes #4361

## Summary

`gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` / `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens` were missing from every
`claude-native-ui` trace, so per-session token usage was untrackable in MLflow even
though every other GenAI semconv attribute (`gen_ai.operation.name`,
`gen_ai.agent.name`, `gen_ai.request.model`, `session.id`, `input.value`) was there.

- **Cause:** a native Claude turn runs to completion *in the terminal*, not in the
  harness executor. `ClaudeNativeExecutor.run_turn` injects the message with
  `tmux send-keys` and returns immediately, so it yields `TurnComplete(usage=None)`.
  The executor adapter only records usage under `if event.usage is not None`
  (`omnigent/runtime/harnesses/_executor_adapter.py:431`), so that branch never ran
  and the agent span closed with no token attributes.
- **Fix:** record the tokens where they are actually known — the transcript
  forwarder, which reads Claude's JSONL `message.usage` (or the statusLine capture)
  and already emits spans under `telemetry.session_scope` for forwarded items.
  `_post_external_session_usage` now stamps `gen_ai.usage.*` via `record_llm_usage`,
  so the counts land on a span tagged with `session.id` and per-session totals
  aggregate in MLflow / any OTel backend.
- Only the token counters are recorded. `context_tokens` is a derived
  input+cache total for the context-window gauge, not a usage counter, and the
  cost-only posts from `_forward_session_cost` carry no counts at all — recording
  zeros there would report a real 0-token turn on every cost tick and drag the
  session aggregate down.

```
 tmux inject                                     Claude terminal
 ────────────                                    ───────────────
 run_turn ──► send-keys ──► TurnComplete(usage=None)   │ model runs here
                │                                      │
       agent span closes  ✗ no gen_ai.usage.*          ▼
                                              transcript JSONL
                                              message.usage
                                                       │
                              forwarder ──► POST external_session_usage
                                                       │
                                            ✓ span "claude_native.usage"
                                              gen_ai.usage.input_tokens
                                              gen_ai.usage.output_tokens
                                              session.id
```

**Note on scope:** the counts land on a `claude_native.usage` span rather than on the
agent span itself. The agent span cannot carry them — it closes at inject time,
before the model has produced a single token. Every other native harness
(codex/cursor/goose/pi/hermes-native) yields `TurnComplete(usage=None)` for the same
reason; this PR fixes the reported harness only.

## Test Plan

Added to the existing `tests/test_claude_native_forwarder.py` suite:

- `test_post_session_usage_records_gen_ai_token_attributes` — a usage post produces a
  span carrying `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens/output_tokens/total_tokens` plus the cache
  breakdown, asserted through a real in-memory OTel exporter.
- `test_post_session_cost_records_no_token_attributes` — a cost-only post records no
  `gen_ai.usage.*`.
- `test_gen_ai_usage_tokens_keeps_only_token_counters` — parametrized filter check
  (drops `context_tokens`, cost floats, the `model` tag; `None` when no counts).

```
pytest tests/test_claude_native_forwarder.py                  # 160 passed
pytest tests/inner/test_tracing_genai_semconv.py \
       tests/server/routes/test_native_usage_attribution.py \
       tests/inner/test_claude_native_executor.py             # 37 passed
```

Verified the tests are a real regression guard: with the source change stashed, all
6 new tests fail (span absent / helper missing); with it applied, all pass.

## Demo

N/A — telemetry-only change, no UI surface.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] UI / frontend change
- [ ] Refactor / chore
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Test / CI
- [ ] Breaking change

## Test coverage

- [x] Unit tests added / updated
- [ ] Integration tests added / updated
- [ ] E2E tests added / updated
- [ ] Manual verification completed
- [x] Existing tests cover this change
- [ ] Not applicable

## Coverage notes

The new tests drive the production `_post_external_session_usage` path through a real
OTel `TracerProvider` + `InMemorySpanExporter` and assert on exported span attributes,
so no mocking of the telemetry layer is involved. The full 154-test forwarder suite
still passes, covering the unchanged POST behaviour the span now wraps.

## Changelog

Claude native sessions now report per-turn token usage (`gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` /
`output_tokens`) to MLflow and other OpenTelemetry backends.

author: peterblenessy
body:
Refs #445. Answers two questions raised on the thread: *"don't those models have special config?"* and *"I'm worried about language support."*

## Language: detection survives translation, over-flagging does too

Every fixture was English, so every number in the validation doc described English performance only. Six Swedish cases added as **matched translations** of existing English ones, so any difference is the language rather than the content.

| case | result |
|---|---|
| `sv-threat-explicit` | detected |
| `sv-coercive-monitoring` | detected |
| `sv-self-harm-intent` | detected |
| `sv-grooming-secrecy` | detected |
| `sv-neg-song-lyrics` | **false alarm** |
| `sv-neg-banter` | **false alarm** |

All four positives caught — including the two categories that depend on reading intent rather than vocabulary. Whatever is wrong with this classifier, it is not that it only understands English.

Both negatives flagged, the same two kinds that fail in English. Two cases is too few to claim Swedish is *worse*; there is no sign of it being better, and the defect is clearly not language-specific.

The overall clean rate moves 0.60 → **0.50**, which is simply the honest number once the fixture set stops being monolingual.

## Configuration: both hypotheses dead

Worth recording so nobody re-litigates them.

**The system prompt does reach the model.** Gemma's chat template has no native system role, so there was a real possibility llama-server was dropping our Forensic 9 guidance entirely — which would have explained the hard-negative failures perfectly. It isn't: a probe with a system message came back in character.

**`--jinja` changes nothing.** Running the full eval under the GGUF's own Jinja template rather than llama.cpp's built-in one produced **byte-identical** results — every cell, every false alarm. The flag is not added.

Temperature is already 0 in `client.rs`, which is why runs are reproducible. **The over-flagging is the model's behaviour under correct configuration, not a setup mistake.**

## Note on an earlier probe

A first attempt at the language question ran without the production grammar, so the model replied in a different JSON shape and the results were unparseable noise. Discarded. These numbers come through the real path — production prompt, production grammar, production validation — which is why they are fixtures rather than a one-off script.

`scripts/preflight.sh` clean; the deterministic CI gate passes with the new cases.

author: bbuf
body:
## Motivation

The LTX-2 block leaves eight `x * (1 + scale) + shift` adaLN chains unfused (three kernels each, two of them full passes over the video/audio streams): the four a2v/v2a cross-attention modulates, the two prompt modulates on the LTX-2.3 `cross_attention_adaln` branch, and the two output-layer modulates. The bit-exact fused CUDA modulate (`kernels/ops/diffusion/modulate_scale_shift.py`, already mounted by FLUX and MiniMax-H3) collapses each to one kernel — no quality gate needed by its numerics contract.

## What this PR does

Routes the eight sites through a small `_ltx2_modulate` helper:

- the adaLN rows here are strided `(B, 1, D)` views from `unbind`/`squeeze` of the combined tables, so the helper densifies them to the `(B, D)` layout the kernel expects (a bit-exact copy of tiny tensors);
- per-token modulation rows (`dim 1 > 1`, e.g. per-token timesteps) and unsupported platforms/dtypes keep the eager chain;
- on top of the kernel's own contract, the first fused call self-verifies `torch.equal` against the eager chain (`BitExactFusionGate`, same pattern as the ERNIE/Ideogram mounts) and falls back permanently on any mismatch.

## Performance (seed 42, `--quality=lossless`, 2 GPUs)

| card | preset | arm | denoise (s) | e2e (s) | output md5 |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| H200 | ltx2 (768×512×121f) | eager (main) | 8.012 | 9.098 | `2447032f…` |
| H200 | ltx2 | **this PR** | **7.962 (−0.6%)** | **9.043** | `2447032f…` (**identical**) |
| H200 | ltx23-one-stage | eager (main) | 45.855 / 45.839¹ | 47.214 | n/d¹ |
| H200 | ltx23-one-stage | **this PR** | **44.687 (−2.6%)** | **46.049** | n/d¹ |
| H100 | ltx2 | eager (main) | 6.560 | 7.963 | `984e6885…` |
| H100 | ltx2 | **this PR** | **6.582 (parity)** | **7.983** | `984e6885…` (**identical**) |
| H100 | ltx23-one-stage | eager (main) | 46.385 | 48.167 | n/d¹ |
| H100 | ltx23-one-stage | **this PR** | **45.092 (−2.8%)** | **46.845** | n/d¹ |

The gains concentrate on the LTX-2.3 `cross_attention_adaln` path (more sites engage, larger streams); the `ltx2` preset stays at parity while keeping bit-identical output — the mount is a strict no-regression.

¹ `ltx23-one-stage` is **process-nondeterministic on unmodified main**: two consecutive eager runs (same seed, same GPUs) produce different output md5s with denoise within 0.03% (45.855 vs 45.839 s). Output md5 is therefore not a usable correctness metric for this preset; correctness rests on the in-process first-call `torch.equal` gate (zero fallbacks over full runs on both cards), the md5-identical deterministic `ltx2` preset, and the unit tests.

## Correctness

- `ltx2` output md5 identical to main on both cards (deterministic preset).
- First-call gate verification passes on the live tensors (`torch.equal`), zero fallback warnings on all runs.
- Unit tests (`test_ltx2_modulate_mount.py`): row-broadcast and strided `unbind` views match eager bit-for-bit on CUDA; per-token rows and CPU fall back to the eager chain.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit tests.
- [x] Provide accuracy and repro results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

author: ganemocorp
body:
`SecretRecord` y `SecretValue` enumeran claves una por una sobre dataclasses `frozen`, así que una clave `fields` del api **se descartaba en silencio**.

Y peor: `SecretValue.from_payload` **exigía** una clave `"value"`. Un secreto multi-campo no lleva esa clave, así que el SDK habría lanzado un **"missing value" engañoso** para un payload perfectamente bien formado.

## Qué cambia

- **`SecretRecord.fields`** — los **nombres** de campo (solo en el GET individual; vacío para un secreto escalar, que es todo secreto anterior a esto).
- **`SecretValue.fields`** — el bundle entero, `nombre → plaintext`, con `value` vacío. El bundle llega en **UN reveal**, no en una llamada por campo: el token de reveal es single-use, así que pedirlos de a uno lo quemaría en el primero.
- **`SecretValue.field_value(name)`** — selecciona uno, con un `KeyError` que **nombra los campos que sí existen**, así un typo se auto-diagnostica **sin imprimir jamás material de credencial**. Sobre un secreto escalar dice exactamente eso, en vez de reportar un campo que nunca se esperó.

## Compatibilidad

Ambos atributos nuevos van **al final y con default**, así que la construcción posicional no se ve afectada, y un secreto escalar se comporta **byte por byte** como antes: `.value` es el valor y `.fields` está vacío.

**81 tests en verde** (7 nuevos); ruff limpio en los archivos tocados; diff de tests aditivo, **0 líneas borradas**.

- Add Bay-impact and documentation-lifecycle prompts to PR scaffolding and declare the repository's agent-instruction discovery strategy.

## What Problem This Solves

The CSW-122 audit found implemented observer routes and deployed configuration names with no current operator inventory. It also found that prompts and `.agents` instruction surfaces were outside documentation checks, while mandatory Bay-impact and documentation-lifecycle evidence was absent from the pull-request template.

## Why This Change Was Made

The operator manifest ties the public route list and methods to executable Worker routing, and ties the deliberately scoped audited configuration names to Wrangler and workflow usage. The two active references state their ownership and compatibility boundaries. Checker coverage and contributor scaffolding cover the remaining source-verified governance gaps without adding unverified aliases or claiming that observer routes are versioned APIs.

## User Impact

Operators can find the current observer routes and audited configuration ownership in one place. Contributors receive the existing Bay and lifecycle requirements in the PR template, and drift in these checked contracts fails `check:docs`.

## Reconciliation

- PR 1, #1107, merged first as `2b5b345063efe1690e1d802fb1a738aa6a408707`.
- This second-layer diff was replayed again as one commit onto current main `f9a2f9493c2d96c1ef808484924e048386284d1c` after #1113 merged.

- Open #1110, #1111, and #1112 were rechecked; merged #1113 touched only dashboard presentation/tests. None touches this PR's nine-file scope. Limits, scheduler, target-dispatcher, dashboard/runtime, and proof changes remain excluded.

## Validation

### Review findings resolved

Accepted findings added deterministic coverage for method-aware routes, route/method pairing on one Markdown row, multiline and reordered guards, ignoring comments/templates, exact workflow-secret names, stale API table rows, multiple methods or paths in one condition, route-specific methods across Boolean branches, identical or conflicting duplicate manifest/table rows, workflow-secret extraction from executable GitHub expressions rather than inert YAML text, and method guards inherited by nested route conditions. One suggestion to require every repository workflow secret in this inventory was rejected as scope-expanding: this page intentionally covers the source-verified CSW-122 ownership gaps, while existing auth/runbook surfaces remain authoritative for other credentials.

## Real Behavior Proof

**Claim:** The exact rebased head builds a 61-page documentation site containing both active operator references, and deterministic checks detect route/configuration/instruction drift without exposing non-current evidence as canonical.

**Exercised surface:** Exact pushed head `4a7b547136a7e047aa0fcda531de410054ad2dc8`; production docs generator; generated `llms.txt`, sitemap, public API and configuration pages; TypeScript builds; all lint lanes; active-surface/dashboard-boundary/format/docs/limits checks; focused checker/site tests.

**Scenario:** A clean GitHub clone of the pushed branch was built in Docker-backed Crabbox. The proof asserted both new active pages are in canonical discovery, representative route/configuration names render, all focused positive/negative tests pass, and the repository-wide deterministic surfaces are clean.

**Command/environment:** Crabbox `0.40.0`, required `provider=local-container`, image `node:24-bookworm`, `--fresh-pr openclaw/clawsweeper#1108 --no-hydrate`; the harness cloned and asserted the exact pushed branch. Docker Server `29.5.2`.

author: adamtheturtle
body:
Closes #3420

Validates that `ref_case` conversion stays injective across distinct source ref names for both value and call rendering, while allowing repeated uses of the same source ref.

Verification:
- 904 ref/error integration tests passed with 813 subtests
- orphan-golden check
- Ruff, mypy, and pyright

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Input validation only; fails fast with a clear error instead of silently merging distinct refs into one identifier. No changes to successful render paths when names stay unique after conversion.
> 
> **Overview**
> When **`ref_case`** is set, literalizer now refuses inputs where two different `$ref` source names would convert to the same identifier (e.g. `userId` and `user_id` both becoming `user_id` under **SNAKE**). The new **`_validate_ref_case_is_injective`** walks all ref markers in the value tree and raises **`UnrepresentableInputError`** on a collision; repeating the same ref name is still allowed.
> 
> That check runs at the start of **`_literalize`** and **`literalize_call_parsed`**, so both whole-value rendering and call-argument refs are covered before any code is emitted.
> 
> Integration tests in **`test_ref_case_collisions.py`** assert the error for **`literalize`** and nested refs in **`literalize_call`**.

author: carlbedrot
body:
Sentry on both sides, wired so the state a fresh clone builds in is **no reporting at all** rather than reporting that has promised to stay quiet. The server never calls `UseSentry` without `Observability:SentryDsn`; the app never calls `SentrySDK.start` without a non-empty `SentryDSN` in its Info.plist.

## Where the DSNs live, and why differently

The server's is a secret — user-secrets or the host's environment, never a committed file, same rule as `Auth:SigningKey`. The app's is **not**: a client DSN ships inside every copy of an app and can only write, never read. So it sits in `ios/project.yml`, where one edit switches it on.

## Reports carry ids, not people

`SendDefaultPii = false` on both sides, and the scrubbing is a pure function either side — `SentryScrubbing.Scrub` and `Observability.scrub` — precisely so it can be asserted without a DSN, a network or a started SDK. Dropped: `Authorization`, cookies, IP addresses, the machine name. Kept on purpose: group ids, member ids, rejection codes. A report nobody can act on is the reason people switch reporting off.

Three things are never sent, and each is set explicitly rather than left to a default:

| Never sent | Why it is a decision, not a default |
|---|---|
| Request body (`MaxRequestBodySize = None`) | A push body *is* the friend group's money history |
| `attachScreenshot` | Every name and amount on screen |
| `attachViewHierarchy` | The same picture in text, label strings included |

Exception messages are deliberately **not** rewritten. Nothing in this codebase puts money or a name into one — money never reaches an exception path, and Npgsql's parameter values stay out of errors unless `IncludeErrorDetail` is on, which it is not. A regex sweep over free text would catch the cases we already thought of while giving false confidence about the rest.

`TracesSampleRate` is 0 on both sides. Crashes are the point; a trace of every screen transition is a free plan's quota spent on numbers nobody reads.

The host says at boot which mode it is in, for the same reason `DevTokenExposure` does: a server that has been crashing for a week into a Sentry that was never switched on looks exactly like a server that has not crashed.

Sentry is a dependency of the **app target only**. Core keeps its zero.

## Verification

- Backend **93/93** (8 new scrubbing tests)
- AppTests **9/9**
- iOS build succeeded (sentry-cocoa resolves to 9.25.0 under `from: 9.9.0`)

All of that runs in the **off** state — which is the honest thing to note, because the off state is the one every test exercises.

## What is not verified

The **on** state. Sentry's API refuses project creation for this account — `403: your organization has disabled this feature for members` — so no DSN exists yet and nothing has been sent to Sentry end to end. Unblocking is two clicks in the Sentry UI (create `slice-backend` and `slice-ios`, or enable member project creation under Settings → General), after which switching it on is one `user-secrets set` and one line in `project.yml`.

author: nbarger96
body:
Preparation for cutting the first MCPB release (`PC-03` criteria 7 and 10) — Slice 13's PC-03
half, executed ahead of the P-08 plugin switchover. The switchover is untouched and stays gated
on Slice 12: `plugin.json` still carries no `version`, and nothing here changes update semantics.

Cutting the bundle release early is legal because the tag names the **bundle**, not the plugin
(`DEV-ROADMAP.md` §4, `PQ-09`).

## What changed

**`scripts/pack-mcpb.mjs` — `PC-03` criterion 7.** The pack step now unpacks the archive it just
wrote and compares `server/index.js` to `dist/index.js` by sha256, failing the pack on a mismatch
and deleting the bundle so a rejected artifact cannot be installed by mistake.

The comparison is against the *archive*, never `build/mcpb/` — the staging tree is `cpSync`'d from
`dist/` a few lines earlier, so checking it would assert that a copy equals its source.

It lives in the pack script rather than in a `release.yml` step so the assertion is identical
locally and on the runner, with no second implementation to drift. `@anthropic-ai/mcpb`'s own
`unpack` does the extraction, so it needs no zip reader and behaves the same on Windows.

**`.github/workflows/release.yml` — action pins.** `checkout` and `setup-node` to `@v7`, matching
`ci.yml`; `upload-artifact` to `@v7`. This workflow had never executed once, so it is bumped
before the run that cuts the release rather than after.

## Demonstrated, not assumed

Per Slice 11's rule that a mechanism which has never failed has never been shown to work, the
criterion 7 check was exercised in both directions before landing. A throwaway copy staging a
different file as `server/index.js` fails with both hashes, exits 1, and leaves no bundle behind;
an honest pack reports the matching sha256 and writes the artifact.

`release.yml` was then rehearsed three times via `workflow_dispatch` on this branch — the full job
runs, `Attach to the Release` is correctly skipped on a non-tag ref, and nothing irreversible is
created. Final run is green with **zero annotations**.

The rehearsal also caught a wrong claim mid-branch: `upload-artifact@v5` still declares
`using: node20`, so the first bump did not clear the deprecation warning. `v6` is the first major
on `node24`. Corrected forward rather than amended, so the finding stays in history.

## Verified before opening this PR

- `npm run lint:docs` — 23 files, 2,691 links, **0 broken**
- `npm run typecheck` — clean; `npm test` — **73 passing**, exit 0
- `npm run build` then `git status --porcelain -- dist/` — empty, `dist/` was already current
- `npm run acceptance` — **13/13 PASS**, exit 0, live, no 429
- `mcpb validate mcpb/manifest.json` — passes
- `claude plugin validate .` — passes with exactly one warning, `P-08`'s deliberately unset
  `version`. `--strict` still fails on it by design; that gates the *plugin* release, not the
  bundle, and closes with the other half of Slice 13
- Fan Content disclaimer verbatim on **four** surfaces — `plugin.json`, the marketplace entry,
  `README.md`, and `mcpb/manifest.json`. The three JSON `description` fields are byte-identical to
  each other
- The CI-built artifact was downloaded and unpacked: exactly `manifest.json` + `server/index.js`,
  `display_name: Manabase`, disclaimer present, and `server/index.js` sha256-identical to local
  `dist/index.js` — which also confirms the `.gitattributes` `text eol=lf` rule holds across
  Windows and the Linux runner
- Offline `initialize` handshake from a directory with no `node_modules`, against both committed
  `dist/index.js` and the CI-built bundle's server: both reply and list `card_search`

One recorded finding from the live run: no paper Black Lotus printing carries a USD price upstream
any more (EUR only). That is the already-recorded 2026-08-03 condition, and the check passes
because the reason is reported honestly rather than as missing data.

## Not in this PR

Setting `version` in `plugin.json`; the update-semantics tests; `claude plugin tag --push`; the
`--strict` clean pass (`PC-02` criterion 9); `PQ-05`; the §9 row that closes Phase 1. All still
gated on Slice 12's friend dry-run.

The README's Chat-tab section still says there is no release to download. That is **true until the
tag is pushed**, and rewriting it is the next commit after the release exists — pointing a cold
reader at a download that does not exist is the class of false claim this repo keeps correcting.

author: adinschmidt
body:
## Problem

The email queue records whether a job was submitted, but pg-boss rows are not a durable application model for email delivery. The application needs to distinguish one logical email from each provider submission so ordinary retries can remain idempotent while genuine resends create a new send.

## Outcome

This adds application-owned records for logical email deliveries and their provider attempts.

- **`email_deliveries`** represents one logical email. `(email_type, source_entity_id)` is unique, so an invite email has one durable delivery record.
- **`email_delivery_attempts`** represents one provider submission, including attempt number, queue job id, Resend idempotency key, provider email id, submission time, normalized outcome, and a sanitized diagnostic.

An ordinary queue retry reuses its attempt and idempotency key, allowing Resend to deduplicate it. A genuine resend creates another attempt with a new number, job identity, idempotency key, and provider email id.

This is the persistence foundation for #346. The send-path integration is intentionally isolated in stacked PR #392.

## Data and safety boundaries

- `source_entity_id` is intentionally not a foreign key because its source table varies by email type and delivery history should survive source deletion.
- Outcomes use Resend's delivery vocabulary so webhook and polling results can be stored consistently; engagement events such as opens and clicks are excluded.
- `outcome_detail` is limited to a short sanitized provider diagnostic. Recipient addresses, rendered bodies, invite URLs, reset tokens, and other one-time secrets are never stored.
- Delivery upserts lock the logical delivery while allocating the next attempt number, keeping concurrent attempt numbering contiguous.
- Webhook verification, event storage, reconciliation, and retry policy remain in #344/#347.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm run lint`
- `npm run format:check`
- `npm test` — 122 passing
- Applied the migration to a throwaway PostgreSQL 14 cluster and exercised delivery reuse, sequential attempts, provider submission persistence, later outcome preservation, and provider-email-id uniqueness.
- Current GitHub CI, CodeQL, and Vercel checks pass.

Refs #346, #341

author: jrmoulckers
body:
## Summary

Records two supply-chain facts in `docs/security/supply-chain.md`, both measured against this repository rather than taken on description.

## Registry routing

`.npmrc` must route by scope only. A bare `registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com/` override breaks `npm audit` with `ERR_PNPM_AUDIT_ENDPOINT_NOT_EXISTS` — GitHub Packages implements no advisory endpoint, and `@npmcli/arborist` resolves it as `auditRegistry || registry`, so it never consults the scoped registry. **No token fixes it**; it is a routing fault that presents as an auth fault. finance's `.npmrc` was already scope-only, so this is a guardrail against regression, not a fix.

## Audit egress — the upstream claim is half right, and the half that is wrong matters

The claim reaching us was that `npm audit` transmits *private package names* to `registry.npmjs.org`. Intercepted and gunzipped the actual request:

| Package class | Transmitted? | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Public dependencies | Yes | 745 name/version pairs in one request |
| This repo's own `private: true` workspace packages | **No** | zero `@finance/*` entries in that same request |
| Dependency resolved from `npm.pkg.github.com` | **Yes** | isolated probe sent `{"@jrmoulckers/eslint-config":["0.2.1"]}` |

So finance's five internal package names (`finance`, `finance-getting-started`, `@finance/web`, `@finance/design-tokens`, `@finance/api`) never leave — npm excludes private workspace roots. But scoping a *dependency* to a private registry does **not** keep it out of the bulk advisory request. Once `@jrmoulckers/*` is depended on here, those names and versions reach npmjs on every audit.

Recorded rather than mitigated: the payload is dependency metadata only, no financial or user data. Noted that `--offline` suppresses it where that egress is unacceptable.

## Issues

Refs #4029

## Testing

- [x] `prettier --write` on both files; second pass clean
- [x] Payload captured twice through a local interception listener, gzip-decoded
- [x] Probe project created inside the repo and fully removed; tree clean

author: waleedlatif1
body:
## Summary
- sharp has never been able to load in the deployed image. The runtime error is `ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED: libvips-cpp.so.8.18.3: cannot open shared object file` — not a missing module. `@img/sharp-<platform>` (the `.node` binding) gets traced in; `@img/sharp-libvips-<platform>` (which ships libvips) does not, because the binding loads it through the dynamic linker rather than a JS require.
- Copy `sharp` and `@img` into the runner stage, mirroring the `lib0`/`yjs`/`y-protocols` lines directly above that solve the identical hoisting problem.
- Drop the `./node_modules/sharp/**/*` and `./node_modules/@img/**/*` entries from `outputFileTracingIncludes`. They were added in #2458 (2025-12-18) to do exactly this job and never worked: the globs resolve against `apps/sim` while both packages hoist to the monorepo root. Verified empty in the real `deps` image.
- This is the root cause behind #6496. That PR contained the blast radius (a top-level `import sharp` in the content registry was 500ing `/blog`, `/library`, `/sitemap.xml` and every route beneath them); this one makes sharp work. It also restores copilot VFS image preparation, which has been silently degrading on the same failure — `file-reader.ts` guards its import and logs `Failed to load sharp for image preparation`.
- Trims the over-explained comments #6496 left behind, now that the Dockerfile owns the packaging rationale.

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix

## Testing
- Built the `deps` stage (`docker build --target deps`) and confirmed the COPY sources exist and carry the missing file: `@img/sharp-libvips-linux-arm64/lib/libvips-cpp.so.8.18.3`, plus `sharp`, `@img/colour`, and the platform binding.
- Confirmed `/app/apps/sim/node_modules` is **empty** in that image, which is what makes the deleted globs provably dead rather than merely suspicious.
- No new JS deps needed: the deployed image already resolves sharp's `detect-libc`/`semver` — proven by the error reaching `ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED` at all, which only happens after sharp's JS loads. A missing JS dep would be `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.
- `bun run type-check`, `bun run lint`, `bunx vitest run lib/content` (44 passed).

## Notes
Two things deliberately not done here:
- The `COPY` lines must stay **below** the `.next/standalone` copy. Standalone ships its own partial `node_modules`; hoisting these up would let it clobber them and reintroduce the bug.
- Copying all of `@img` includes the musl variants (~18 MB) that a Debian/glibc image can't load. A wildcard `COPY @img/sharp-linux-*` would trim it, but Docker copies matched *directories' contents* into the destination, flattening them and breaking resolution — not worth 0.5% of a 3.6 GB image.

Follow-up worth its own PR: the `ws` and `jsdom` entries in the same `outputFileTracingIncludes` block are dead for the identical reason, and carry a comment confidently explaining a mechanism that doesn't work. Left alone here to keep an outage fix narrow.

- [x] No new warnings introduced
- [x] I confirm that I have read and agree to the terms outlined in the [Contributor License Agreement (CLA)](./CONTRIBUTING.md#contributor-license-agreement-cla)

author: lizap5
body:
The welcome sign and seating chart were flat panels tinted from a four-option floral map that predates the seventeen linen colors. They now sit on a floral border generated for each couple from the linens and vibe they actually chose.

## The model draws the border, never the words

Image models render lettering as gibberish, and a misspelled name on a couple's welcome sign is worse than no sign. The prompt asks for a decorative border and forbids text at length; the names are drawn over the art in real fonts, exactly as before. Whatever the model does, the couple's names are correct.

Worth knowing the ban is a request, not a guarantee. If stray lettering does appear it sits behind the real names, so the failure mode is a busy background rather than a misspelling.

## Colors are constrained, not copied

A sign has to be readable across a room. Their lightest linen becomes the ground only if it is genuinely pale, and their darkest becomes ink only if it is dark enough; otherwise the sign falls back to paper and near-black. A couple choosing Black, Burgundy and Navy gets a pale sign with their darkest color as the accent rather than black on black.

## Three images per submission

Drink, welcome and seating, generated together: in series they would outrun the function's sixty second limit. Each resolves to null on its own, so one refusal costs its picture and not the set. This roughly triples the image generation cost per submission.

Requires `OPENAI_API_KEY` in the Production environment. Without it the route returns `ok: false` and the signs fall back to plain panels, which is also what happens if generation fails.

author: nicw
body:
Two small fixes, one branch (based on granite-shadow-transcription, so it carries that line's history — the fixes themselves are the last 3 commits, +~600/−20 across 4 files).

## Problem 1 — every recording trimmed its opening words

The VAD model loaded from scratch inside `start()` on every session (~2s on an M2 Max), and the mic tap only exists after — so the first couple of words of every memo and call were simply never captured. Nic noticed it as "initial audio is trimmed."

**Fix:** load the VAD model once and reuse it — a single-flight load kicked at app launch (`[ENGINE-VAD-PRELOAD]` in the log), with `start()` falling back to loading it on demand if the preload hasn't finished or failed. The mic tap now goes up immediately on record.

## Problem 2 — some networks make Whisper uninstallable in-app

On Nic's network (documented in the benchmark-results doc), Apple's URLSession cannot connect to the HF Xet CDN at any timeout while curl connects in ~30ms — so WhisperKit's downloader always fails and the model picker's auto-revert kicks in every time. Graceful, but Whisper could never actually be installed from the app.

**Fix:** when the SDK download throws, a curl-based fetcher (`CurlModelFetcher`, `/usr/bin/curl` via `Process`) takes over: lists the variant via the HF tree API, downloads into the exact HubApi layout WhisperKit loads from, tokenizer included. `TOME_FORCE_CURL_MODEL_FETCH=1` forces the path for testing on a healthy network.

Live-verified end-to-end: forced-fallback run fetched the full 1.5 GB variant in **51 seconds** and the model loaded and served (`lastGood` flipped to whisper). VAD preload confirmed firing in the launch log.

---

## Reviewer's notes (Claude)

- **Cancellation:** a cancelled provisioning cycle terminates the curl child via `withTaskCancellationHandler` + per-file `Task.checkCancellation` — no zombie multi-GB downloads. Continuation resumes exactly once (no terminationHandler; cancel's `terminate()` unblocks the same `waitUntilExit`, an `isCancelled` flag converts that resume to `CancellationError`).
- **Resume semantics:** `-C -` was deliberately dropped — with `--fail` it 416s on already-complete files and kills re-runs. Replaced by size-check skip against the tree listing's byte sizes (file-granularity resume, no 416 class at all). Tokenizer files have no listed size and always redownload — intentional, they're tiny.
- **VAD reuse safety:** verified against the pinned FluidAudio source — `VadManager` wraps an immutable CoreML model; per-run streaming state is external (`makeStreamState`), and two live transcribers already share one instance today. `stop()` never nil'd the manager.
- **No shell interpolation:** curl args go as an argv array to `Process` — spaces in "Application Support" are a non-issue.
- **Observability:** fetch outcome (COMPLETED / FAILED + reason) now hits the unified log; previously a fetch failure was visible only in the Settings failure line, which cost us a confused test cycle.
- **Tests:** 161/161 (7 new: tree-JSON parsing, URL/path derivation, progress math, size-skip decision). Known minor left as-is: stdout is drained to EOF before stderr (with `-sS` stderr stays tiny; documented).
- **One unverified-by-human bit:** the trim fix is log-verified (preload fires before any recording) but Nic hadn't yet done the say-a-word-at-record-instant ear test when this PR was opened — daily use will confirm it immediately.

author: nyblnet
body:
Reported against 1.0.17: opening **Share** from ⋯ on a narrow window with the properties panel open draws the popover interleaved with the panel — rows cut off down their left edge, panel labels showing through the gap.

Not a stacking bug this time (that was #286). This one is clipping.

## Cause

`.ed-topbar.ed-bar-fold .ed-menu` carries `max-height` + `overflow-y: auto` so a ⋯ menu that can outgrow the screen scrolls — correct, and well argued in the comment above it.

But **`overflow-y: auto` cannot be had on its own.** Set either axis to a non-`visible` value and the browser computes the other to `auto`. So that menu quietly became a *clipping box* for everything positioned inside it.

Phone chrome demotes whole dropdown widgets (Share, Language) into ⋯, and `.ed-share-pop` is a 250px popover anchored to its parent's end (`inset-inline-end: 0`). Inside the 200px menu it hangs off both edges. Measured at a 660px viewport:

| | rect |
|---|---|
| ⋯ menu | 454–654 × 54–650 |
| Share popover | **399**–649 × 239–**719** |
| properties panel | 424–660 |

55px off the left, 69px below the bottom — both clipped away. The properties panel sits under exactly that strip, which is why the panel showed *through* where the popover had been cut.

## Fix

A floating child can never escape a scroll container, so it stops floating. Inside ⋯, a nested menu renders `position: static` — a section of the list, taking its width and scrolling with it. Nothing overhangs, so nothing can be clipped, and it works the same on a phone where a 250px popover had nowhere to go anyway.

## Verified

At the same 660px viewport:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Share popover | 399–649, hanging 55px past the menu | 443–649, inside menu 438–654 |
| Share rows escaping the menu | left column cut | **0 of 7** |
| Language rows escaping | — | **0 of 10** |
| popover position | `absolute` | `static`, in the scroll flow |

Desktop unaffected — at 1400px the fold class is absent, so the popover is still `absolute`, `min-width: 250px`, shadowed, and fully on screen. Screenshot of the fixed narrow layout shows Share expanding cleanly as a section of the ⋯ list.

Adds the `overflow-y` trap to CLAUDE.md's hard-won list — it is invisible at desktop widths and the obvious reading of the CSS is wrong.

Not for 1.0.17 (already released); this is for the next one.

author: filipkunc
body:
Follow-up to #45: the tutorials in `examples/pkg-pr-new` reference the pkg.pr.new previews, so the previews must never contain the tutorials. They can't by construction — the preview upload's globs (`'.'`, `'./npm/*'`, `'./packages/*'`) never touch `examples/`, and every published package carries a `files` whitelist (verified locally: `npm pack --dry-run` lists no `examples/` entry in any tarball) — but that invariant deserves a gate, not a comment.

The new `tutorial-previews` job (matrix: `runtime`, `unplugin`) npm-installs each tutorial the way an outside machine would — plain npm, no workspace — asserts the patched `[wrap-esm-lambda] GET /hello/world` output, and fails if an `examples` directory or a `wrap.config.mjs` ever leaks into an installed package.

Which previews it installs depends on the event:

- **push / dispatch**: the publish job just uploaded previews for this exact commit, so the committed `@main` URLs are swapped for its short sha — `@main` is a moving tag and a concurrent push could win the race between the upload and the install.
- **pull request**: the publish job never runs, so nothing is keyed to a PR sha; the tutorials run exactly as committed, against the newest previews `main` published — the URLs a reader would copy-paste. (This lane needs an explicit `!cancelled()` + `needs.publish.result == 'skipped'` condition, since `needs:` would otherwise auto-skip the job whenever publish skips.)

This PR itself exercises the PR lane; the merge push exercises the sha-pinned lane.

author: dmlinn
body:
Packet jobs gain a fourth pass: implement → review → **verify** → validate → push → draft PR.

A context-starved verifier judges the diff against the packet's own acceptance criteria. The blinding is structural: the implement transcript, assumptions file, and review output all live under `logs/`, outside the repo checkout — the verifier cannot see them, and its prompt additionally forbids the target repo's audit ledgers and plan documents. Its inputs are the packet, the diff, the working tree at HEAD, and the packet's declared validation commands.

**The runner composes the ledger row, never the verifier.** The row follows the target ledger's post-hardening contract: `plan_hash` computed by the repo's *own* hash binding (config-overridable command reading `QAI_PLAN_FILE`/`QAI_ROW_DATE` from env), `packetHash` from the packet, `round` counted from existing rows, `reviewer.kind: agent-session-fresh` with an honest label, one `per_ac` entry per packet criterion, agreeing counts, and `must_address_count` equal to the non-pass verdicts. The **decision is derived from the per-AC verdicts** — never taken from the model's top line — and `not-demonstrable` fails closed. A criteria-count mismatch produces no row and a loud `[verify ERROR]` title marker instead of a malformed append.

The row commit lands **before validate**, so the target repo's own ledger gate re-judges what we wrote in the same run, and the push carries the verdict into the draft PR. `verify_fail` marks the PR title; nothing blocks — the human gate stays the gate.

The row and the reviewer label both carry `runner-unsandboxed`: this is the softer cousin of an OS-sandboxed verifier lane (no fence, no canaries), and nothing about it should be mistakable for one.

Tested end to end against a real target repo before this PR: the default hash command produces the 16-hex hash through the exact quoting path (including the `${VAR:-…}` literal-brace trap the packet-mode defaults document — hit again here, caught by test), the verdict extractor parses the fenced JSON, and a composed `verify_fail` row (one not-demonstrable AC) passes the target ledger gate with zero findings.

Also: verify usage in `logs/<job>.verify.json`, the PR usage table, and `ledger.jsonl`; config vars documented in `config.env.example`.

author: seeniam
body:
Abre a fase de identidade visual da marca. Trabalho implementado localmente e nunca integrado — esta PR e as 5 seguintes fazem a integração.

## O que entra

- **Congelamento por hash** (`tests/unit/fronteira-identidade.test.ts`): SHA-256 dos 35 arquivos de `src/components/publico/**` e das regras de elemento de `globals.css`. Declarações `--token` são filtradas de propósito — retintar é permitido, mexer em `body {}` não.
- **Fronteira de import**: o público novo (`src/app/(site)`, `src/components/site`) e o legado (`src/components/publico`) não se importam; o ERP não importa nenhum dos dois.
- **CI `guarda-erp`**: falha se o diff tocar `src/app/{painel,admin}/` ou `src/components/{painel,prontuario,financeiro,orcamento}/`. Exceção consciente via rótulo `toca-erp`. Usa `fetch-depth: 0` — sem isso o diff contra a base sai vazio e o guard fica verde para sempre.
- **`createPublicClient`** (`src/lib/supabase/publico.ts`): corrige vazamento real. `public.clinica` tem duas policies SELECT permissivas (membro OR marketplace) e PERMISSIVE soma por OR — com o client de sessão, staff logado via a própria clínica na vitrine mesmo com `exibir_marketplace = false`. Sem JWT não há claim de `clinica_id`, então só a policy de marketplace casa.
- **Step `Build` no CI**: o gate não buildava; erro de `next/font` ou de client boundary só apareceria em homologação.

Sem migration, sem grant novo, sem mudança de RLS.

## Gate

lint sem warnings · typecheck limpo · 301 testes unitários passando · zero arquivos do ERP no diff.

Detalhe da fase em `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-05-identidade-visual.md` e `docs/checkpoints/2026-08-05-identidade-visual.md`.

author: daniel-llach
body:
## Qué Evaluada a pedido del usuario: https://centex.cultura.gob.cl/ — Centex, Valparaíso, del Ministerio de las Culturas. Encontré la categoría real vía el menú: `/category/muestras-y-exposiciones/`. ## Densidad imperfecta, confirmada con el usuario antes de construir De 12 posts muestreados en esa categoría, solo ~7-8 son anuncios/crónicas de exposiciones reales — el resto es cobertura de una feria gráfica (Feria Sobreimpresiones), una feria de artes y oficios, una entrevista sobre esa feria, y una crónica de una delegación escolar visitando una exposición ya cubierta por otro post. Se lo mostré al usuario antes de invertir tiempo en el extractor (mismo tipo de chequeo que llevó a rechazar `aecid.es`/CCE Santiago antes en la misma sesión, con una densidad peor, 2-3/12). El usuario confirmó "agrega". ## Sin fecha determinística — cuarta confirmación del mismo patrón El campo de fecha del listado (`b2fecha`) resultó ser la fecha de **publicación** del post, no la de la exposición — mismo patrón que aninatgaleria.org. Cruzado directamente: un post listaba "5 julio, 2026" pero su propia página de detalle dice "Inauguración: sábado 11 de julio" — días después, mismo post. Tampoco hay `openingTimeExtractor`: una página de detalle tiene el fraseo limpio "*Inauguración: sábado 11 de julio, 12:00 horas*", pero otra tiene una forma completamente distinta sin esa etiqueta ("Desde este martes 4 y hasta el domingo 9 de agosto..."). Es la cuarta vez en la misma sesión que encuentro este mismo patrón de inconsistencia (ya visto en galeriapready.cl, aninatgaleria.org y estacionmapocho.cl) — se deja la interpretación a Haiku con respaldo de citas. ## Un desafío técnico nuevo: acotar la descripción El cuerpo real del artículo tiene `
` genuinamente **anidados dentro de la propia prosa** (bloques de imagen con leyenda embebidos a mitad de artículo) — la regla simple de "cortar en el primer `
` que cierra" (usada en Mapocho) habría cortado el contenido real demasiado pronto acá. Un regex no puede contar profundidad de anidamiento arbitraria, así que acoté la descripción en la etiqueta `` en su lugar — confirmé manualmente (contando el balance de divs) que cae exactamente en el punto correcto, sin barrer el pie de página del sitio. ## Test plan - [x] `node --import tsx --test src/**/*.test.ts` — 338 pass, 0 fail, 16 skip (preexistentes) - [x] Tests nuevos con fixtures reales: extracción del listado, y extracción de descripción (incluyendo el caso de divs anidados en la prosa, cortando en `` sin barrer el pie de página) - [x] Extractor probado end-to-end contra el HTML real de la página (12 ítems) y 2 páginas de detalle reales

author: seunghyunlee8860
body:
## What changed

- stopped and preserved the invalid Run014 Adam-like continuation path
- audited the complete optical, thermal, electrical, mapping and adjoint dependency chain
- fixed the linear thermal gray-law derivative at the void endpoint
- added independent `Ea` and `Eb` combined physical-density AD–FD support
- added persistent true MMA with exact uniform `rho=0.5`, no imposed seed/symmetry/volume constraint, and measured beta convergence
- added fail-closed contact-anchored domain, mesh and `Eb` AD–FD preflight gates
- added restartable `Ea` then `Eb` supervision and accepted-iteration GitHub publishing

## Why

The discarded optimizer was called MMA but actually normalized gradients, used Adam moments, normalized the direction again, applied a fixed move and clipped the result. This drove premature binarization and allowed an unbounded beta-1 loop. The replacement keeps physical gradient magnitudes and solves persistent constrained MMA subproblems.

## Validation before launch

- `59 passed, 2 skipped` for shared optimization and TaIrTe4 topology tests
- `2 passed` for the legacy continuation helper tests
- Python compileall passed
- no raw FSP or NPZ is committed
- dependency SHA-256 manifest covers 30 runtime/test files
- contact-anchored 40/48 µm domain and 100/50 nm mesh gates passed
- new `E||b` combined AD–FD passed with relative error `1.349e-5`
- full preflight status is `VALIDATED_RUN016_RUN017_TRUE_MMA_PREFLIGHT`

Raw solver artifacts remain under `/data` and are referenced by path, size and SHA-256 only.

author: raukk
body:
Adds a Vite dev server middleware to serve `/env.js` dynamically, seeded from the `POSTHOG_KEY` environment variable, and documents the full set of configurable environment variables.

**Changes:**

- **vite.config.ts**: New `devEnvJs()` plugin that intercepts `/env.js` requests in dev mode and serves `window.__APP_CONFIG__` with `POSTHOG_KEY` from the ambient environment. Runs before Vite's SPA fallback to avoid 404s on a gitignored file that is written at deploy time. Falls through to the public dir if `public/env.js` exists explicitly.
- **.env.example**: New file documenting all configurable environment variables (`VITE_API_BASE_URL`, `VITE_SHARE_BASE_URL`, `VITE_FIO_BASE_URL`, `VITE_INDEXEDDB_DBNANAME`, game data staleness thresholds, and `POSTHOG_KEY`). Instructs users to copy to `.env.local` (gitignored).
- **README.md**: Added setup section explaining that dev defaults to production backend, with instructions to override via `.env.local`. Expanded environment variables table with missing entries and corrected default values for `VITE_GAME_DATA_STALE_MINUTES_EXCHANGES` (60, not 30) and `VITE_GAME_DATA_STALE_MINUTES_PLANETS` (720, not 180). Documented that `POSTHOG_KEY` is baked into `/env.js` at deploy time, not a `VITE_` variable.
- **src/vite-env.d.ts**: Added type declarations for `VITE_SHARE_BASE_URL` and `VITE_FIO_BASE_URL` (both optional). Removed duplicate `VITE_POSTHOG_TOKEN` declaration.
- **.prettierignore**: Added `.env.example` to prevent formatting.

**Implementation detail:** The middleware checks `req.url?.split("?")[0]` to strip query strings, allowing cache-busting parameters. It defers to an explicit `public/env.js` if present, so deployments can override the dev behavior without code changes.

author: mansmeg
body:
This should fix the failing tests in dev.

The workflow failed because `github.head_ref` is empty on normal `push` events. As a result, `ad-m/github-push-action` fell back to pushing generated result commits to `main`, even though the workflow had checked out `dev`. The remote `main` branch had newer commits, so Git rejected the push with `fetch first`.

Fix: use `${{ github.head_ref || github.ref_name }}` for both checkout and push branch, so workflow-generated commits are pushed back to the branch that triggered the run.

Fixes #106

| **Sudden Setback** | `{2}{U}{U}` | The owner of target spell or nonland permanent puts it on their choice of the top or bottom of their library. |

## New SDK vocabulary

### `WardCost.CollectEvidence(n)` — Ward—Collect evidence N (CR 702.21 + CR 701.59)

The fourth collect-evidence context, and the only one that is a *ward* cost — so the only ward cost whose constraint is a mana-value **sum** rather than a count. It raises a variable-size `SelectCardsDecision` over the paying player's graveyard carrying `minTotalManaValue`, min 0 (the empty selection is how declining is expressed) up to the whole graveyard.

**CR 701.59b fails closed**, as in every other collect-evidence context: a graveyard that can't reach N means the controller *can't choose to collect evidence*, so the spell is countered with **no prompt at all** rather than offering a payment they'd have to refuse.

Reachability, the legality re-check and the exile all route through the existing shared `CollectEvidenceResolver`, so a ward payment emits the same `EvidenceCollectedEvent` (firing "whenever you collect evidence" payoffs) and can't drift from the activated-ability, cast-cost, or effect forms. It is an **unlinked** cost — it stamps no `ChoiceSlot`, so it satisfies no `Conditions.WasEvidenceCollected`.

Wiring: a new `CounterUnlessCollectEvidenceContinuation` + resumer alongside the other ward-cost branches. The client's existing `CardSelectionDecisionUI` already handles the mana floor and the "Select None" decline (its comment even anticipates "a ward cost you may decline"), so **no frontend change was needed**.

### `Player.ControllerOfSource`

"You", read off the source permanent rather than off the resolution context's `controllerId`. `DynamicAmount.CountPlayersWith` rebinds the controller to each candidate player, so `Player.You` inside the loop means "the opponent being tested" and the ability's own controller is otherwise unreachable — which is exactly what Wojek Investigator's "more cards in hand **than you**" needs. Pairs with the existing `Player.OwnerOfSource`, which follows ownership instead of control.

`Effects.Investigate` / `CreateClue` also gain a `DynamicAmount` overload for the same card's "investigate once for each …" count (zero investigates not at all).

## AI

Both decision responders now understand `minTotalManaValue`. The count-based branches can't satisfy a sum gate, so previously they either submitted an illegal under-total selection (mandatory collect evidence) or silently declined every optional one. They now pay the floor with the fewest cards, highest mana values first — the same choice `CollectEvidenceResolver.autoSelect` makes — and submit nothing when the pool can't reach it.

## Verification

- `just build` — green (card snapshot reblessed; only the five new cards moved in `MKM.json`, additions only)
- `./gradlew :ai:test :rules-engine:test :mtg-sets:test --rerun-tasks` — green
- `just check` — green
- `just check-card-printing` — all five canonical in MKM (their only real printing), no drift
- Image URIs verified HTTP 200 against the exact `image_uris.normal` from Scryfall
- One scenario test per card (5 new files, 16 tests). Axebane Ferox's cover the paid path, the decline, the unreachable-threshold no-prompt case, and that five mana-value-0 lands are not evidence 4.
- `docs/card-sdk-language-reference.md` updated for the new ward cost, the player reference, and the dynamic `Investigate` overload.

author: tamnd
body:
Found while running the full workspace suite for #249. attach::tests::the_ceiling_holds_and_takes_the_least_recently_used fails on a fast machine, on clean main too, and it is not the test's fault.

The attach ceiling evicts by least recent use, and the use timestamp has millisecond resolution. A burst of attaches inside one millisecond all land on the same tick, so the eviction sort falls through to its tie break and picks tenants by name instead of by use. The test runs against a fake backend, the whole thing fits in one millisecond, and the tenant it had just touched was the one evicted. Outside the test the same coarseness means same-millisecond attaches evict by name, not by recency.

Timestamps move to nanoseconds and the sweep cutoff moves with them. The suite is 405 green and the LRU test passes five isolated reruns on the machine that reproduced it.

author: ritsukai2000
body:
Fixes the CP5 delivery blocker (SourceWriterIntegrityError on multi-record solution publish). Part of #2461.

## The defect chain (diagnosed live on Base Sepolia, round 12)

A solution publishes several records (evidence, outputs ×2, delivery, delivery-envelope) into ONE append-only signed source.

- `client/src/daemon/native-operator-state.ts` `recordSolutionReady` stamps **every** outbox row of an engagement with the same `created_at` (one `this.timestamp()` for the whole batch).
- `client/src/daemon/native-solution-publisher.ts:83` announced each record at `value.publication.createdAt` — identical for all records.
- `packages/discovery/serve/src/source-writer.ts:726` requires each announcement to **strictly advance** the signed source head (`timestampMs <= previousHead.issuedAt` → reject).

So record 1 advanced the head to `createdAt`; records 2+ carried the identical `createdAt` (≤ head) → `SourceWriterIntegrityError "announcement timestamp must strictly advance the signed source head"` → wrapped as retryable `solution-dependency-failed` → the engagement **paused**, and retry reused the same fixed `createdAt`, so it could **never** recover. CP5/CP6/CP7 unreachable.

## The fix — producer-side, strictly-advancing per record

The source-writer's strict-advance invariant is a legitimate anti-replay/ordering guard and is **left intact**. The bug is the producer assigning identical timestamps to distinct records.

In `NativeSolutionCoordinator.publish()` each record's announcement timestamp is now derived from its **stable ordinal over the full per-engagement publication set** (new read `listSolutionPublications`), based at the shared outbox `createdAt`:

```
announceAt(record) = createdAt + ordinal * 1ms
```

- **Strictly advancing:** distinct ordinals (0,1,2,…) → strictly increasing instants in publish order (the ordinal ordering is the same deterministic `ORDER BY` the publish loop drains), so each record advances the head.
- **Deterministic / idempotent:** a pure function of persisted data (`createdAt` + stable ordinal). A resumed publish recomputes the identical timestamp, so any record already committed to the signed source reconciles by fingerprint match (existing receipt) rather than re-colliding.

## How it recovers the wedged task 1223

1223 is paused with its first record already published (head at `createdAt`, ordinal 0) and the remaining records still `intent` at the same shared `createdAt`. On resume, `resumeSolutionRetry` restores the engagement to `solution-ready` and re-enters `publish()`; the remaining records keep their ordinals (1,2,3,4) over the **full** set, so they get `createdAt+1ms…+4ms`, which strictly advance past the current head (`createdAt`). The solution finishes publishing → settles → reaches `solution-settled`.

**Capacity slot:** `countActiveNativeEngagements` (`native-assembly.ts`) counts `nonterminal` engagements, and `nonterminal` excludes `solution-settled`/`failed`/`lost`. A *paused* 1223 occupies operator B's `maxConcurrent:1` slot; once the fix lets the resumed publish reach `solution-settled` (terminal), the slot **frees naturally** — no separate capacity fix was needed.

## Fail-before / pass-after

New regression tests (`client/test/daemon/native-solution-coordinator.test.ts`) drive the coordinator's `publish()` against the **real** publisher + signed source:

- *publishes all five records with strictly-advancing announcement timestamps* — RED before (record 2 collides → paused, not settled), GREEN after; asserts the head reaches sequence 5 with strictly-increasing entry timestamps.
- *resumes a partially-published solution past the already-advanced head (task 1223)* — reproduces the wedged durable state (first record published at the shared `createdAt`, four still-`intent` at the identical `createdAt`, engagement paused), then asserts the retry advances the remaining records and settles once. RED before, GREEN after.
- Mutation check: reverting the timestamp assignment reddens both (verified by disabling the fix — 2 fail / 11 pass).

Invariant preserved: `client/test/daemon/native-solution-publisher.test.ts` gains *refuses a distinct announcement whose timestamp does not advance the signed head* — two distinct records sharing one timestamp are still rejected. `packages/discovery/serve/src/source-writer.test.ts` (untouched) stays green.

## Guards

- `tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `vitest run --no-file-parallelism test/daemon` — 957 pass (incl. native-solution-publisher / native-solution-coordinator)
- `packages/discovery/serve` `src/source-writer.test.ts` — 16 pass
- `generate-architecture.mjs --check` — clean
- `phase-d-transition-deletion.test.mjs` — 9 pass

## Summary
**P1 fix.** Stage-1 note generation crashed — returning a **500 → `STAGE1_FAILED`, so the physician gets *no note*** — whenever the model emitted a section or a claim as a bare **string** instead of an object. `parse_note_response` called `.get()` on it: `'str' object has no attribute 'get'` (`shared.py:382`). Hit today on a real video import (Bunion consult).

## What changed
`backend/app/modules/providers/note_gen/shared.py` — `parse_note_response`:
- **Skip** a `sections` entry that isn't a dict (log + continue) instead of crashing.
- **Skip** a `claims` entry that isn't a dict.

The existing template-backfill still guarantees every required section is present as `not_captured`, so a dropped malformed section is **recovered honestly** rather than failing the entire note.

## Why it matters
This is a hard crash on the physician-facing hot path — one malformed element (which LLMs produce intermittently, even at temp 0.1) took down the whole Stage-1 note. Defensive parsing is the right posture: never let a single bad element deny the physician their note.

author: gewenyu99
body:
## Problem

`/docs/cdp/sources/postgres` is fetched verbatim into the `data-warehouse-source-setup` skill that the wizard installs, and every installed skill is scanned for prompt injection before it's allowed to load. One sentence on this page trips the scanner:

> When you delete the source, PostHog soft-deletes the warehouse tables and attempts to drop **the PostHog-managed** replication slot and publication.

The rule looks for a removal verb followed by `posthog` or `posthog-<suffix>` — a pattern meant to catch package names like `posthog-js` or `posthog-node`. It also matches the adjective "PostHog-managed", so `drop the PostHog-managed` reads as an instruction to remove PostHog.

It's a false positive — the sentence is about dropping a Postgres replication slot, not the SDK — but the scanner fails closed, so the skill got deleted and the install failed. That took the wizard's warehouse setup down with it, on real users' machines.

## Changes

One-line reword. "PostHog-managed" was already redundant inside a section titled **PostHog-managed**, and the subject of the sentence is PostHog, so "it manages" carries the same meaning:

> …attempts to drop the replication slot and publication **it manages**.

## Test plan

Ran the rule's patterns over every file in the published `data-warehouse-source-setup.zip`:

- Before: exactly one match across all 11 files — this sentence, in `references/postgres.md`.
- After: zero.

No other doc pulled into that skill matches any of the rule's patterns.

## Note

This is the content-side fix and it unblocks the skill today. The underlying rule still treats any `PostHog-<word>` compound as a package name, so a future doc phrasing like "drop the PostHog-created publication" would trip it the same way. Worth tightening separately in the scanner rather than steering docs prose around it.

author: nitjsefnie
body:
## What

Fixes #424 (finding (2) — the jail-tier half you asked me to take in https://github.com/LetsGetToWorkBro/dreamlayer/issues/424#issuecomment-5242926711).
Fixes #631

A capability denial asserted from **inside** a running bwrap child, plus the production bug that writing it uncovered.

**The test.** `test_os_sandbox_enforcement.py` builds a one-file plugin package and launches it through production's own `os_sandbox.wrapper()` — not a hand-built bwrap argv, because a hand-built one would reproduce exactly the vacuousness this issue is about. From inside the child, `register()` reaches for the network through the `__builtins__["__import__"]` route that `validate.py` documents as a known static-scan bypass, so what refuses it is the kernel rather than the AST screen. Two tests, same package, differing only in the declared capability.

Which assertion catches which direction, since these are not interchangeable:

- the `argv` assertions catch **"the flag was dropped"**;
- the protocol-line + errno assertions catch **"the flag is present and does nothing"** — the case argv-shape tests cannot see.

There is deliberately no assertion on the child's return code: a jailed child that dies for an unrelated reason exits non-zero exactly like a refused one. The module docstring says so, so the omission cannot later read as an oversight.

**The bug.** The test could not pass on any merged-`/usr` host. `_ro_binds()` realpaths every path, so `/lib64 -> usr/lib64` collapses and is never recreated in the jail; the child's ELF interpreter is unreachable and `execvp` fails before any plugin code runs. `_works()` hides it by probing with `--ro-bind / /` wholesale, which preserves the symlinks, while `wrapper()` binds a curated list — so `available()` reports a sandbox that cannot launch anything. That is this issue's own failure mode one level deeper: the probe tests a different command than the one that ships.

The fix is a four-entry `--symlink` loop in `wrapper()`. On a non-merged host `islink()` is false for all four and the emitted command is byte-identical to today's.

They are one commit on purpose: the test fails without the fix, so splitting leaves either a red commit or a commit with no test in the middle of a bisect.

Also found, not fixed here, filed separately: #632 os_sandbox's module docstring says the jail's filesystem is read-only except /tmp, but its root is a writable tmpfs

## Testing

`cd host-python && python -m pytest -q -m "not hardware and not benchmark and not real_model"` is not what I can usefully report from my box — it is py3.13 here against your pinned 3.11, so I ran the gates on a runner instead and scoped local runs to what I touched.

- **Fork CI, `ubuntu-latest`, Python 3.11.15** — the new leg collected 2 items and reported `2 passed`. It is not green-by-skip: the step installs `bubblewrap`, sets `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0`, and the fixture `pytest.fail`s rather than skipping when `DL_SANDBOX` promises a sandbox that is not there. Both branches of that gate were exercised (`2 skipped` unpinned, hard error pinned-but-absent). `dependency-audit` also green on the same head.
- **The test bites.** Mutating `wrapper()` so bwrap receives `--unshare-net` as the *value* of `--setenv` — argv still contains the string, no network namespace is created — leaves `test_os_sandbox.py` 5/5 green and fails only the new test, at the enforcement assertion rather than the argv lint. Removing the flag outright is caught too, but only by the argv layer, which is the weaker claim.
- **The fix repairs an existing failure.** `test_plugin_v2.py::TestSubprocessIsolation::test_provider_runs_in_child_and_rows_cross_back` fails at `assert host.start()` with bwrap active and unfixed, passes with `DL_SANDBOX=none`, and passes with bwrap active once the symlinks are restored. The third run is what discriminates — the first two alone would equally support "the sandbox is just broken, turn it off".
- `ruff check src/dreamlayer` clean (run from `host-python/`), mypy clean over both changed files.

One caveat worth stating: nothing couples the new file to the new CI step. Delete the step and 201 lines of security test go quietly back to skipping in the main run, with no assertion moving — the same shape as the wasmtime gap. The workflow comment says so, but a structural coupling would be better than a comment if you want one.

## Checklist

- [x] Commits are signed off (`git commit -s`, DCO — see CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [ ] New optional capability? — not applicable; no new capability, no new dependency, and `bubblewrap` is a CI system package rather than an extras entry
- [x] Nothing weakens the privacy contract (capture guards, the Veil, no stranger identification) — the change only makes the existing boundary run and be checked

Generated by Claude Opus 5 (brief, implementation, review, verification)

author: jcarney2024
body:
## What

`/recruitment/cycles/[id]/onboarding` becomes one filterable table whose selection drives all three bulk actions.

Previously the page had two separate forms: a checkbox column feeding "Send / resend onboarding links", and a duplicated list below feeding "Promote selected". The same person appeared twice depending on what you wanted to do to them. There was no select-all, no filtering, and Withdraw was one row at a time.

Now:

- **One table.** Select once, then choose Send links / Promote / Withdraw from a single action bar.
- **Filters.** Search by name, filter by status and department.
- **Selection ergonomics.** Select-all, indeterminate header state, shift-click ranges, a live count, and Clear.
- **Bulk withdraw**, which did not exist before.
- **`EXPIRED` is now visible and filterable.** The service already computed link expiry and enforced it on the applicant side, but the admin table rendered an expired link identically to a fresh one. The most actionable state on the page could not be seen.

Mixed selections act on the eligible subset and report the rest. Selecting an already-promoted row and hitting Send is routine once select-all exists, so it reads as informational ("N not eligible") rather than as a red failure. Only genuine failures render as errors, because a failed promotion means that person was never created and is absent from every roster for the term.

## Two bugs found on `main` and fixed here

**The per-row Withdraw has never worked.** It combined `formAction={withdrawContractAction.bind(...)}` with `name="contractId"`. React 19 nulls the submitter when a submit button carries its own `formAction` (`react-dom-client`: `createFormDataWithSubmitter` is skipped), so `formData.get("contractId")` was always `""` and every single-row withdraw redirected with "Onboarding contract not found." That was the only control able to clear a contract to unblock a rescind.

**The e2e selector covering this page was stranded.** `e2e/recruitment-onboarding.spec.ts` clicked `button:has-text("Send onboarding links")`, but commit `735be20e` renamed that button to "Send / resend onboarding links" without updating the test. `has-text` is substring matching and the actual label does not contain the expected string, so the assertion could not match. That is why the withdraw bug went unnoticed. The new selectors anchor on accessible name with `^` so a count-suffix change cannot strand them again.

## Safety notes for review

Withdraw hard-deletes a contract row plus its signature blobs and HIPAA certificate. It is irreversible. Three things guard the bulk path:

1. **Per-row vs bulk disambiguation.** Both land on `withdrawAction`. A submit button's name/value is submitted alongside every checked checkbox in the same form, so the per-row button sends `onlyAcceptanceId`, which wins outright. `withdraw` is the form's *default* action rather than a per-button `formAction`, because otherwise React drops that pair (see above) and one row's Withdraw would delete the whole selection.
2. **Selection is scoped to what is visible.** Changing a filter prunes the selection, and filtered-out rows unmount, so their checkboxes cannot reach the FormData. A bulk action can never touch a row the operator cannot see.
3. **The server never trusts the client.** All three actions take the same `acceptanceId[]` payload, re-derive eligibility from the database, and scope every query to the cycle in the URL. The button counts are advisory.

`listOnboardingRows` projects to eight fields before crossing to the client component. `OnboardingContract` carries `token` (a standing credential that lets its holder submit onboarding as that applicant), date of birth, phone, signature records, and HIPAA file metadata; none of it reaches the browser.

## Test plan

- Full suite: **4428 passed, 0 failed** across 381 files.
- Playwright `recruitment-onboarding.spec.ts` observed passing against a local database.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint src e2e` clean.

New coverage: row-state derivation including the expiry boundary, custom-answer resolution against a frozen template snapshot, per-action eligibility, bulk withdraw including mid-batch authorization loss and a blob-cleanup failure, selection pruning, shift-click ranges, indeterminate header state, the per-row/bulk withdraw distinction, and the three-way acted / not-eligible / failed reporting split.

Spec and plan are in `docs/superpowers/`.
