author: gkissel
body:
Closes #145

## Approach

The seared tank block entity already synced its contents to the client (`getUpdateTag` returns `saveWithoutMetadata`, and bucket interaction worked), but nothing painted the fluid, so a filled tank rendered as an empty frame -- the block's derived textures already carry the alpha-cutout window (`seared_tank_side.png`, `seared_gauge_side.png`, `seared_window_side.png` all have real alpha holes, confirmed by pixel inspection), the client was just never drawing anything behind it.

Adds `SearedTankBlockEntityRenderer` (`BlockEntityRenderer<SearedTankBlockEntity>`), registered client-only via a new `ForgeweaveBlockEntityRenderers` (`EntityRenderersEvent.RegisterRenderers`, same `@EventBusSubscriber(..., Dist.CLIENT)` idiom as `ForgeweaveFluidClientExtensions`/`ForgeweaveItemColors`). One block entity type backs the tank, gauge and window (`SearedTankBlockEntity`'s own javadoc), so one registration covers all three.

Per-frame, it draws an inset quad column (4 side faces always, top face only when not full -- skipped bottom, matching the task's face list) sized to `amount/capacity`, textured with the fluid's registered still sprite (`IClientFluidTypeExtensions#getStillTexture`) and tinted (`#getTintColor`), on `RenderType.translucent()` so it composites against the block's own cutout window faces. Ported from upstream 1.12's `TankRenderer`/`RenderUtil#renderFluidCuboid` (NOTICE.md row added) -- technique only (quad-per-face inset column), not code: modern NeoForge uses `VertexConsumer`/`PoseStack` instead of immediate-mode `Tessellator`/`GlStateManager`, and unlike upstream every face uses the still texture (no separate flowing texture for sides) with UV mapped to the whole sprite per quad rather than a tiled slice, since a tank is always exactly one block wide with no multi-block seam to align.

Kept deliberately simple/allocation-light: no persistent buffers, no per-tick allocation beyond the handful of local floats/quads every render already needs; block light emission from a lit fluid (upstream's `getLightValue`/`getBrightness`) is out of scope for this issue (rendering the fluid, not lighting it) and not implemented.

## Verification

- `./gradlew build` -- green.
- `./gradlew runGameTestServer` -- green, all 117 required tests pass. Per SCOPE, in-world rendering itself is GameTest-exempt (no automated pixel assertion exists for it); this only confirms nothing else regressed and the mod still boots.
- **Visual verification: not completed in this sandbox.** `DISPLAY`/`WAYLAND_DISPLAY` are set and `glxinfo` is present, so I attempted a real client run (a throwaway one-shot harness that placed a lava-filled `seared_window` and screenshotted it, mirroring the existing `ScreenshotHarness` pattern -- removed before this PR, not part of the diff). The client process logs `Backend library: LWJGL...`, runs mod/common setup, then calls `Minecraft.close()` within about a second, before ever reaching the title screen -- it cannot sustain a render loop in this environment. I did not get a screenshot and am not claiming visual confirmation. **The orchestrator should verify on a real display**: place a seared tank/gauge/window, fill with a lava bucket, and confirm the fluid is visible and rises with fill level.

## Reviewer concerns

- I have not visually confirmed correct UV orientation/winding per face -- the vertex order and per-face UV assignment were derived carefully from upstream's known-correct winding, but since I couldn't render it, a mirrored or rotated texture on one face (most likely NORTH/SOUTH or WEST/EAST) is the most probable defect, not backface culling or an invisible fluid.
- `INSET = 0.01f` is a guessed epsilon to avoid z-fighting with the block's own faces; if it's visibly too tight/loose against the cutout window edges, it's a one-constant tweak.
- Fluid-driven block light (upstream's tank glows when holding lava) is intentionally not part of this change.

author: smaniches
body:
## Summary

Hardens the release pipeline along three axes:

- **Python 3.12 release anchor with an exact uv toolchain.** New `requirements/release-tools.{in,txt}`: an exact hash-locked closure for the release/build/SBOM tools (`build==1.5.0`, `hatchling==1.31.0`, `cyclonedx-bom==7.3.1`; 39 packages, 324 artifact hashes), resolved with uv 0.12.3 explicitly against Python 3.12 on linux-x86_64, wheel-only (`--no-build`) from clean state (`--no-cache`). Two clean-state regenerations produce byte-for-byte identical output. The lock carries no `python_full_version` markers, so any 3.12.x patch the runner supplies satisfies it. `scripts/install_release_tooling.sh` refuses non-3.12 interpreters and installs with `pip --require-hashes --only-binary=:all:`, so consumption can neither accept an unhashed artifact nor fall back to building an sdist, then verifies installed tool versions against the pins. The AF-03 paths (release.yml build/sbom, ci.yml release-path-proof) pin `setup-uv` to exactly `0.12.3`; a contract test forbids `latest` there. Validated locally on CPython 3.12.11 and 3.12.3.
- **Deterministic build/SBOM path.** The release build job builds with isolation disabled from the locked toolchain and asserts exactly one wheel + one sdist (`scripts/build_release_dist.sh`); the sbom job generates CycloneDX from the exact wheel installed into a dedicated 3.12 environment, binds SHA-256(wheel) into the SBOM root component (`scripts/bind_sbom_wheel.py`) append-or-confirm, never repair — a conflicting pre-existing digest, or multiple SHA-256 entries, fails closed leaving the SBOM byte-for-byte unchanged, while unrelated non-SHA-256 hashes are preserved — then independently verifies root name/version/digest against the wheel METADATA (`scripts/verify_sbom_binding.py`) and runs negative substitution tests that must fail closed (`scripts/verify_sbom_negative.sh`). Provenance-subject hashes are computed before base64 encoding under `pipefail`.
- **Canonical dry_run + unprivileged pre-merge proof.** `resolve_release` computes one canonical `dry_run` output via `scripts/resolve_dry_run.sh` from `github.event_name` and the new `workflow_dispatch` boolean input; tag pushes (absent `inputs` context) deterministically resolve `false`, so ordinary releases always publish. All four externally mutating jobs (`provenance`, `publish-pypi`, `publish-github`, `publish-mcp-registry`) are gated with the fail-closed `dry_run == 'false'` form; the non-mutating resolve/build/sbom chain stays executable in dry-run mode. The unprivileged CI job `release-path-proof` (`permissions: contents: read` only, required by `all-checks`) executes the complete deterministic chain on GitHub-hosted runners before merge, via the same scripts the release workflow runs.

66 release-contract tests cover the dry_run truth table (including tag-push-with-absent-inputs), workflow gate/permission/partition contracts, the exact uv pin, lock discipline and wheel-only install, and hermetic SBOM binding positive/negative cases. Full suite: 886 passed with the 100% line+branch coverage gate intact. No runtime application behavior changes.

## Type of change

- [x] `fix` / `feat` / `perf` — changes runtime behaviour
- [ ] `docs` / `refactor` / `test` / `chore` / `ci` — no behaviour change

## Checklist

- [x] Branch is up to date with `main`.
- [x] Commits are signed off (`git commit -s`; DCO, requested — see `CONTRIBUTING.md`).
- [x] PR title follows Conventional Commits (the changelog is generated, not hand-edited).
- [x] `ruff format --check`, `ruff check src/`, and the full pytest suite (886 passed) with the 100% line+branch coverage gate pass locally.
- [x] New code has tests at the right layer; the 100% line+branch coverage gate still holds (no `src/` changes; scripts are exercised by the new subprocess-level tests).
- [x] Public APIs have docstrings; new tools have MCP annotations. (N/A — no MCP tool surface changes.)
- [x] No new tracked secrets and no new outbound endpoints without an allowlist entry.
- [x] If the change touches security or the audit trail, the relevant docs are updated. (Workflow-level comments document the dry_run gating and the deterministic build/SBOM contract in place.)
- [ ] If the change touches biosecurity or dual-use risk (a roadmap area), a bioethics-aware reviewer is requested. (N/A)

author: luckypipewrench
body:
Unblocks #157 and removes this repository's dependency on Pipelock's release cadence. No workaround to revert later.

## The problem

The scan step installs the latest published Pipelock release. That means this repository is gated by the last release rather than by the current scanner, so it inherits every bug that shipped until the next release goes out.

That is live now. Whole-file-deletion hunk parsing was fixed in pipelock#1145, which is on Pipelock's default branch and absent from v3.3.0. The released binary therefore rejects any pull request that deletes a file with `unverifiable input: content outside unified diff hunks`, and the action surfaces that as `Secrets detected in PR diff` when no secret exists. #157 is failing on exactly this and contains no secret.

## What changed

The action still runs the whole-tree audit and still resolves the shared config; only its built-in diff scan is turned off. Both diff scans now use a scanner built from Pipelock's default branch, placed first on `PATH` so the scan commands themselves are unchanged.

The `workflow_dispatch` path keeps its existing behavior and gains the same current scanner. The `pull_request` path gets an equivalent explicit scan rather than the action's internal one. Exclusions and config handling are identical on both paths.

Both diffs are now generated with `--text`, so a path marked binary by an in-repo `.gitattributes` cannot reduce its content to a `Binary files differ` marker and pass unread. That hardening was identified while reviewing the equivalent change in the Pipelock repository.

## Why this rather than the alternatives

Waiting for a Pipelock release fixes it once and leaves the same lag in place for the next scanner bug. Filtering deleted files out of the diff is sound in isolation, since a deletion removes lines and cannot introduce a secret, but it is a divergence that has to be remembered and reverted later.

Building from source removes the class. When Pipelock fixes a scanner bug, this repository has it on the next run, and nothing here needs to change.

## Verified

Simulated against #157 locally: merge base resolved, a 347399 byte diff generated exactly as the workflow does, scanned with a binary built from Pipelock's default branch, result `No secrets found in diff` and exit 0.

`make preflight` passes, including the workflow-shape tests that pin the dispatch trigger and the dispatched scan step.

## Note for #157

Because a `pull_request` run uses the workflow from the pull request's own head, #157 needs to merge `main` after this lands before it picks up the new scan path.

author: mjodheim
body:
Opens the first endogenous result to address generality gate **G2**, recorded as fully open
before this work. No model call, no network, no external task, no third-party attestation.

## Result

One persistent deterministic agent consumes a UTF-8 instruction, an ordered structured mapping
and a raw 1728-byte RGB888 raster, and emits both symbolic `set_dial` calls and embodied effector
moves scored from terminal grid state only.

| Arm | `pixel_target` | `structured_dial` | `language_route` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| full | **12/12** | **12/12** | **12/12** |
| pixel_ablated | **0/12** | 12/12 | 12/12 |
| structure_ablated | 12/12 | **0/12** | 12/12 |
| language_ablated | 12/12 | 12/12 | **0/12** |
| blind_guess (measured floor) | 0/12 | 1/12 | 2/12 |

Each matched ablation zeroes its own dependent family and leaves both non-dependent families at
**exactly** the full-arm score. That exact-equality half is the preregistered claim: an arm that
degraded everything would show only that inputs matter. Ablations preserve byte length, key order
and token count, so no arm can detect its own ablation.

## Ordering

1. `cd55035` froze the protocol before the harness existed; the salt was drawn first.
2. `4a56de6` added the harness and recorded amendment A1.
3. `5fdf7b4` bound the 36-episode suite before any arm ran.
4. `5733361` preserved the first result, attempt 1, no retry.

Suite commitment `20ff63f3…a4f7e`; result `aa312e95…a52639`.

## Recorded defect

Amendment A1 is in the protocol permanently. The first freeze paired a chance-distribution floor
with a bound of one success across 36 episodes, which no faithful guessing policy can satisfy. The
bound was corrected before materialization with its arithmetic recorded. Implementing the floor as
fail-closed instead would have been a fourth ablation arm dressed as a floor, making every
zero-scoring ablation self-confirming.

## Local qualification

- Full suite: **1405 passed, 2 skipped** (40m11s); repository integrity clean.
- M076 regressions: 26 passed. `scripts/check_m076_result.py` reports `failures: []`.

## Claim boundary

G2 moves from open to **partial mechanism evidence** and is **not closed**. The rasters are
project-authored 24x24 synthetic panels in one domain; the agent is deterministic and does not
learn, so persistence is identity and audit, not adaptation. No natural-image perception, no
cross-domain transfer, no continual learning, no Genesis Gate 2/3 evidence, no AGI evidence.
Independent reproduction is still required.

Does not touch or weaken the M075 pre-private readiness boundary, which remains fail-closed.

author: krish-verma
body:
## What was wrong

The responsive width sweep (`e2e/specs/layout-widths.spec.ts`, 1280/1024/768/640/390/375/320) and the 200%-zoom project both iterate `e2e/surfaces.ts`. **Not one of those surfaces can render a run card** — every one is a read of committed state, and a run only exists after `POST /api/experiments/{id}/runs`. `rg -l 'run-card|data-run-id|Add Run' apps/web/e2e/` names exactly one file, `e2e/mutation/runs.spec.ts`.

So the Run vertical slice shipped a new multi-control card that no width measurement in this repository had ever seen, and the outstanding human narrow-viewport / 200%-zoom gate had nothing mechanical behind it for this surface.

## The defect that was found (measured, not inferred)

At **320px**, the longest inherited path the app renders — `sample.composition.CuO2_mass_fraction` — was painted **245px wide inside a 184px content box**, overflowed `article.run-card`, and because that card is `overflow-x: hidden` **the text was lost rather than scrollable**. Card `scrollWidth 294` vs `clientWidth 240`.

Cause: `.run-inherited-path` carries `flex: none` (= `flex: 0 0 auto`) in the base rule. The narrow-width media block already dropped its fixed `190px` to `width: auto`, which makes the used width **max-content** — and an item with `flex-shrink: 0` can never be shrunk below that, so `overflow-wrap: anywhere` never got the chance to break the string. Restoring shrinkability and clearing the automatic minimum size is the entire fix (3 declarations).

## Why the spec is in the mutation suite

`playwright.mutation.config.ts`'s header says "ONE viewport project, not five … layout and accessibility at five widths are the other suite's job". That was true of every spec in the directory when it was written; a run card is the case it did not anticipate. The alternative — making the read-only suite create a run — would put a mutation inside the single worked-example session that five viewport projects read in parallel, which is the collision the two suites exist to avoid. The reasoning is stated in the new file rather than left as a contradiction.

## What is asserted

Scoped to `section.runs-section`, with **two runs open** (the pressure case), at **1440 / 1280 / 1024 / 768 / 390 / 320** and at **640x400 @ DPR2** (the `zoom-200` emulation, parameters proved in the live page):

- no nested overflow · no lost text · no obscured control (probed at both scroll extremes, as `findObscuredControls`' own docstring asks)
- `Add Run` visible and enabled
- the accordion still collapses and re-expands through its header button
- a **perceptible** focus indicator on the header, via `helpers/focus.ts` (focused-vs-resting paint diff, not "a rule matched")

Plus two cases the sweep structurally cannot see:

The 320px test **failed on the unfixed CSS** with exactly the output quoted above, and passes after. The guard has teeth on the defect it was written for.

The first focus check called `locator.focus()` and reported "no visible focus indicator" on a header whose ring is fine (`{outlineWidth: 3, outlineStyle: "none", boxShadow: "none"}`). `e2e/helpers/focus.ts` already says why: only real keyboard focus engages `:focus-visible`. author: johnn05
body:
Closes release-gate item 7 from the project review.

## What it does
`backend/scripts/preflight.py` runs the same set of self-contained checks a deployment healthcheck would run:

| Check | Catches |
|---|---|
| `ffmpeg`, `latex`, `dvisvgm` on PATH (with `-version`) | Missing binary; present-but-broken |
| Manim imports cleanly | Broken install (cairo/pango linkage) |
| Manim renders a Text-only scene end-to-end | Manim + ffmpeg + Pango wired correctly (no LaTeX) |
| Bedrock config schema | Empty model id / region; `boto3` unimportable |
| Writable storage | Artifact / meta db parent dirs |
| Feature flags | Prints resolved values so the deploy log names the live feature set |

Each check prints `OK  <name> <detail>` or `FAIL <name>: <detail>`, one line. Exits nonzero on any required failure. `--skip NAME` for deploys that intentionally omit a dep.

## Not covered (out of scope)
- Live Bedrock reachability — needs credentials. The `NoCredentialsError` handler in `app.main` catches the runtime case with a 503.
- MathTex render — pytest already exercises the LaTeX chain and it takes long enough to defeat "fast preflight."

## CI integration
Wired into `.github/workflows/backend-tests.yml` between the dep-install and pytest steps. If a system-dep drifts out (e.g. LaTeX cache restored without `dpkg --configure`), the preflight fails with a targeted diagnostic instead of pytest emitting a mysterious per-test error.

## Test plan
- [x] `python -m scripts.preflight` locally — 8/8 OK
- [ ] CI: `Backend tests` workflow green on this PR
- [ ] CI: preflight step appears in the log with per-check output

author: propertytitan
body:
⚠️ **Ez egy megismételt hiba javítása.** Tegnap reggel „lezártuk" ezt a rést, és őrt is írtunk hozzá. Zöld lett. A független mérés mégis megtalálta — mert a **tünetet** javítottuk, nem az **osztályt**.

## Mi maradt nyitva

A `beforeSend` **kizárólag hiba-eseményen fut**:

```js
if (isErrorEvent(processedEvent) && beforeSend) { ... }   // @sentry/core client.js
```

A teljesítmény-események (`tracesSampleRate: 0.1`) **másik borítékban** mennek — a `beforeSendSpan` / `beforeSendTransaction` hookokon, amiket **sehol nem állítottunk be**. A kimenő fetch spanjének attribútumai közt pedig ott van `url.full` (teljes URL query-vel) és `url.query` (nyers search string). Vagyis pontosan ugyanaz, amit tegnap a breadcrumbból kivettünk:

- az **élő SeeMe API-kulcs**, a **6 jegyű átvételi kód**, a telefonszámok
- a begépelt cím (Nominatim), az adószám (VIES)
- böngészőben a **jelszó-reset és e-mail-verify élő tokenje** az oldal-URL-ből

## A tanulság

**Rossz kérdést tettem fel.** Nem az volt a kérdés, hogy „milyen *mezőket* ír az SDK a breadcrumbba", hanem hogy „**hányféle borítékban hagyhatja el ugyanaz az adat a rendszert**". A tegnapi őr pontosan olyan mély volt, mint a gondolkodásom — egy szinttel a probléma alatt.

## A javítás

1. **Mind a három hook** beállítva, **mind a három** init-fájlban.
2. Új `scrubSentrySpan` + `scrubSentryTransaction` — span-attribútumok, a span leírása, a beágyazott spanek és a tranzakció **neve** is.
3. ⚠️ **A felismerés tartalom-alapú lett, nem kulcsnév-alapú.** Ezt **maga az új őr mérte ki**: a kulcsnév-minta az `url.full`-t nem fogta — pedig épp az hordozza a teljes URL-t. A felsorolás mindig azt hagyja ki, amire nem gondoltunk.
4. **Új osztály-őr** (`tests/sentry-boritekok.test.js`): kiolvassa az SDK forrásából, **hány** `beforeSend*` hookot ismer, és megköveteli, hogy mindegyikre legyen szűrő mindhárom init-fájlban. Egy jövőbeli SDK-verzió új borítéka pirosra váltja a buildet. **Igazoltan fog** — a hookok kivételekor megnevezi, melyik hiányzik és melyik fájlból.

## ⚠️ Teendő neked

Ha a Sentry valaha elkapott SeeMe-hibát vagy sampled tranzakciót a gateway-hívással, a **`SEEME_API_KEY`-t rotálni kell**. Ellenőrzés: Sentry → Performance → `HTTP GET seeme.hu`. Kódból ez nem állapítható meg.

## Ellenőrzés

+9 teszt. Backend **690/690**, web **87/87**.

author: toddhebebrand
body:
## Problem

A `configuration_policies` row is either **org-owned** (`org_id` set) or **partner-owned / "partner-wide"** (`org_id NULL`, `partner_id` set). Four agent-facing resolvers only ever matched the first kind, so a partner-authored policy was fully authorable in the UI and **silently never reached a single agent**.

I verified all four against `origin/main` before touching anything — the state was not what the issue described:

| Resolver | App-layer predicate | DB context | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `event_log` | org-only ❌ | org-scoped ❌ | broken, fixed here |
| `monitoring` | org-only ❌ | org-scoped ❌ | broken, fixed here |
| `pam` | org-only ❌ | org-scoped ❌ | broken, fixed here |
| `patch_source` | **already dual-axis** ✅ | org-scoped ❌ | **half-fixed** — still RLS-blind, fixed here |
| `helper` | fixed in #2911 ✅ | system ✅ | already correct |
| `onedrive_helper` | org-only | system ✅ | **correct as-is — see below** |

`patch_source` is the interesting one: its predicate was corrected along with the rest of `featureConfigResolver.ts`, but it still ran inside the org transaction, so it resolved nothing anyway. That is the whole reason this bug class needs both halves fixed.

## The two failure layers

1. **App layer** — `eq(configurationPolicies.orgId, device.orgId)` can never match an `org_id NULL` row.
2. **RLS** — partner-owned rows are gated by `breeze_has_partner_access`, and every agent-facing context carries `accessiblePartnerIds: []`. Under those the read returns **zero rows rather than raising**, so a corrected predicate still resolves nothing.

## Changes

- **New `apps/api/src/services/configPolicyOwnership.ts`** holds the two primitives that were being re-derived inline in four places: `policyOwnershipCondition()` (dual-axis join predicate) and `withPartnerWideVisibility()` (system-context escape). `featureConfigResolver.ts` imports both instead of keeping private copies; `routes/agents/helpers.ts` now uses them too.
- `event_log` / `monitoring` / `pam` switched to the dual-axis predicate; the already-fixed `helper` resolver drops its inline copy of the same SQL.
- `resolvePatchConfigDetailsForDevice` gains the visibility escape it was missing.
- **Monitoring's escape covers the watches read too.** `config_policy_monitoring_watches` RLS walks `settings_id → feature link → configuration_policies`, so splitting the two reads across contexts would find the policy and then resolve **zero watches** — and the resolver returns `null` on empty watches. Easy half-fix to ship by accident.
- **`heartbeat.ts` hoists all four builders out of the org transaction** into one shared system context, matching the existing `policyProbeConfig` / `onedriveSettings` / `helperSettings` treatment (#1105).

### Two design calls worth reviewing

**One shared system context, not four.** The four already shared the org transaction, so per-resolver isolation was never real; four extra connection acquisitions per heartbeat is not affordable against the 25-connection production ceiling. Per-resolver `try/catch` is preserved inside it, so each feature keeps its documented fallback.

**An outer catch around that context.** The inner catches cannot see a transaction setup or COMMIT failure, and a locally-caught SQL error still leaves the shared transaction aborted — so the commit throws. By that point the org transaction has committed and the commands in the response are already marked delivered, so letting it escape would 500 the heartbeat and **lose the claimed commands**. It now degrades to "no config update this cycle"; everything here is re-resolved on the next heartbeat.

### Deliberately NOT changed

`onedrive_helper` stays org-only. It is the sole member of `ORG_SCOPED_ONLY_FEATURE_TYPES` — its settings carry per-tenant M365 library mappings that a partner-wide policy has no owning org to anchor to, and `featureLinks.ts` rejects the link with a 400 at write time. I initially "fixed" it as a sibling of the other four and backed that out. There is now a regression test asserting it does **not** use the dual-axis predicate, plus a comment at the call site, so the next audit sweep for this bug class doesn't make the same mistake.

## Verification

- **New integration suite** `agentPolicyResolversPartnerWide.integration.test.ts` (real Postgres, `breeze_app` role, RLS forced) drives all four resolvers **inside an org-scoped `withDbAccessContext`** — the realistic agent path — and covers fan-out across sibling orgs, org-beats-partner precedence, and cross-partner isolation. Redis cache keys are purged per test so a cache hit can't mask a resolution failure.
- **Non-vacuity checked:** with the production files reverted to `main`, 5 of its 8 cases fail. The 3 that pass (precedence, foreign-partner isolation) held before too, as they should.
- Unit coverage for the emitted SQL (compiled through the real `PgDialect`, so a dropped partner branch changes the text and params) and for the escape's escalate/no-op branches.
- `apps/api` unit suites: 47 files / 784 tests green (agents + featureConfigResolver + new module). The full API unit suite was swept green after the shared module's named `db` imports required completing one `vi.mock` factory (`helpers.pam.test.ts`).
- Integration: 3 files / 25 tests green (new suite + both existing partner config-policy suites).
- `tsc --noEmit` clean.

## Reviewer notes

- **Integration suites should be dispatched for this branch** (`gh workflow run CI --ref fix/2930-partner-owned-config-resolvers`) — the RLS-context behaviour here is exactly the class that only fails under **Integration Tests**, not the unit job.
- The other two callers of these resolvers (`routes/agents/eventlogs.ts`, `routes/devices/software.ts`) run inside a request-long org transaction, so `withPartnerWideVisibility` briefly double-holds a connection there. That is the same shape already shipped for `resolveBackupConfigForDevice`, and those paths are orders of magnitude lower-volume than the heartbeat — but it is a deliberate trade, not an oversight.
- No schema or migration changes.

Closes #2930

author: peterblenessy
body:
Resolves #618

## Summary

iOS folder view rows now support the standard iOS swipe-to-reveal list idiom. Swiping a file row left reveals a Share action, wired to the existing `ios_share_file` command. No new backend/write surface is introduced.

## Red tests added

Since the issue body didn't include an explicit `Red tests` list, the following were derived from its acceptance criteria + assumptions and written first (confirmed failing before implementation):

- `src/components/mobile/__tests__/SwipeRevealRow.test.tsx::hides the action until the row is swiped` — no action visible before any gesture
- `SwipeRevealRow.test.tsx::reveals the action after a leftward swipe past the reveal threshold`
- `SwipeRevealRow.test.tsx::snaps back closed when the swipe distance stays under the reveal threshold`
- `SwipeRevealRow.test.tsx::invokes the action's onSelect when tapped after reveal`
- `SwipeRevealRow.test.tsx::supports a second action without any change to the gesture handling (extensibility for #619)`
- `SwipeRevealRow.test.tsx::a plain tap with no drag still fires the row's own click handler`
- `SwipeRevealRow.test.tsx::tapping an already-revealed row closes it and suppresses the row's click instead of activating`
- `mobile-app.test.tsx::folder view row swipe actions (issue #618) > hides the Share action on a file row until it is swiped`
- `mobile-app.test.tsx::… > reveals a Share action when a file row is swiped left`
- `mobile-app.test.tsx::… > invokes ios_share_file with the row's relPath when the revealed Share action is tapped`
- `mobile-app.test.tsx::… > a plain tap (no swipe) on a file row still opens the document — functional parity`
- `mobile-app.test.tsx::… > does not reveal a Share action when a directory row is swiped`

## Green implementation

- `src/components/mobile/SwipeRevealRow.tsx` (new) — reusable swipe-to-reveal wrapper. Pointer-event drag gesture (fixed 72px-per-action width so the reveal threshold is deterministic both in jsdom tests and on device), snaps open/closed on release past a half-width threshold, and closes-without-activating when the row is tapped while already revealed (suppressing the trailing click the same way `LibraryBrowser`'s existing long-press ancestor menu already does). Takes a plain `actions: SwipeRevealAction[]` array.
- `src/components/mobile/FileRow.tsx` — wraps the existing tappable row in `SwipeRevealRow` with a single Share action for file rows (directories excluded — `ios_share_file` copies a single file to a temp location for the share sheet, same as its only other consumer, the Reader).

## Refactor

Skipped — implementation is already minimal (one new component, one call site).

## Decisions made

- **Directories get no Share action.** `ios_share_file` presents the native share sheet over a temp copy of a *file*; it has no directory-sharing behavior and its only existing consumer (Reader) always shares a single open document. Extending it to folders was out of scope and unverified, so directory rows render zero actions (swiping a directory row is a no-op).
- **Reveal-row extensibility (assumption from the issue body).** `SwipeRevealRow` takes `actions: SwipeRevealAction[]` rather than a single hardcoded prop, so #619 (Delete) is an additional array entry — verified directly by a dedicated test that renders two actions and confirms both reveal together with no gesture-code changes.
- **Fixed action width vs. measured width.** Used a fixed 72px-per-action constant instead of `getBoundingClientRect()` measurement. jsdom always reports 0-sized layout boxes, so a measured width would make the reveal/snap threshold impossible to exercise deterministically in tests; a fixed width also keeps the same gesture math on device.
- **Gesture implemented with Pointer Events**, matching the existing `onPointerDown`/`onPointerUp` idiom already used elsewhere in the mobile chrome (`Chrome.tsx`'s `liquidPressHandlers`, the resize-handle drag pattern) rather than introducing raw Touch Events.

## Verification

- [x] Red tests were red before implementation (`SwipeRevealRow.test.tsx` failed to resolve the not-yet-created import; 2 of the 5 new `mobile-app.test.tsx` cases failed — the other 3 covered pre-existing/unchanged behavior and were expected green, per the TDD skill's additive-change exception)
- [x] All red tests now green (52/52 in the two touched test files)
- [x] `pnpm test` passes (full suite: 417 files, 6691 passed, 6 skipped, 0 failed)
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` clean
- [x] No unrelated files modified (`git diff --stat` touches only `FileRow.tsx`, the new `SwipeRevealRow.tsx`, and their tests)

## Notes for reviewer

- This is a frontend-only, web-implemented gesture (per the issue's own assumption — folder-view rows are DOM elements in the webview, not native UIKit). It has not been hand-verified on a physical device/simulator in this environment (no macOS/Xcode available here); the automated tests exercise the same pointer-event code path a real touch triggers and assert the exact user-observable outcomes (reveal, tap-to-share, tap-elsewhere-still-opens, directories excluded). Recommend an on-device pass per `docs/features/mobile.md`'s embedded-simulator harness before merge, matching the project's own guidance that CSP/gesture-adjacent behavior should be device-verified.
- Lint script does not exist in this repo (`package.json` has no `lint` script) — that hard gate was a no-op, not skipped for cause.

author: joshnroy
body:
## TL;DR

`Pick`'s hypothesis did **not** hold — success is not a smooth function of either parameter alone; a real, diagonal failure valley cuts through `(distance, rotation)` space (119/156 = 76.3% of cells are a clean `12/12`, but 9/156 are a clean `0/12`, and the valley between them explains the oracle-vs-pooled-EES "sign asymmetry" as a marginalisation artifact rather than a genuine rotation effect — the oracle's own point sits in a `12/12` cell, whose two nearest distance-neighbours at the same rotation are also `12/12`). `MoveToThrowPose`'s hypothesis **mostly held**: a single reliable plateau exists (`[1.150, 1.325]`, `12/12` at every one of 9 consecutive standoffs), but it is narrower than the classifier's own accepted band (`[1.150, 1.375]`) — the upper 0.05 m is a labelling overreach (`8/12`, then `2/12`), not a hard noise floor. Both skills are (a)-dominant: a genuinely reliable region exists and is large, so the residual EES-plateau failures are a sampling/labelling problem a better sampler or a tighter classifier could fix, not an execution-noise floor with no safe region to find.

## Question / goal

Does either of Tossing3D's two parameterized skills (`Pick`, `MoveToThrowPose`) have a genuinely reliable region of its sampling parameter space, and how large is that region relative to the bounds the sampler actually draws from? Every number on this domain before this experiment was a coarse bin, a handful of spot-checks, or pooled EES-practice data (which mixes parameters non-uniformly, since it is whatever the sampler happened to draw rather than a controlled grid). This runs the real thing: a dense, controlled grid over each skill's *entire* sampling parameter space, many real KINDER episodes per grid point, labelled by the same classifiers EES trains against.

## Background

Two prior findings on this domain motivated running the full grid rather than another spot-check:

- **`Pick`'s own non-stationarity.** A fixed `rotation=0.65` measured 5/30 success across 30 different scene seeds — even `rotation=0.0`, the tested-safest point, got 29/30, not 30/30. Pooled EES-practice data showed success correlating with `|rotation|` (roughly 99% near 0, dropping to roughly 75% at the ±π/4 extremes), but with an unresolved sign asymmetry against `SkillOraclePolicy`'s own fixed point (`ORACLE_PICK_DISTANCE=0.5682351863248143`, `ORACLE_PICK_ROTATION=-0.7008563047585579`), which is reported at 100/100 in the committed `skill-oracle` arm despite sitting in a rotation region the pooled data put at roughly 81%. A separate, narrower investigation is checking that specific discrepancy directly; this experiment does not attempt to resolve it, only to characterise the full parameter space it lives in.
- **`MoveToThrowPose`'s residual informed-mode failures** cluster at the edges of `RobotAtSuccessfulThrowPoseClassifier`'s accepted standoff band, tightened to `[1.150, 1.375]` in a companion PR (`#193`) from the wider geometric prediction `[1.125, 1.425]`. Separately, low standoffs in the *sampler's* range (`THROW_STANDOFF_BOUNDS`, currently `(0.45, 1.75)` in `skills.py`) were suspected of driving the base into scene geometry, since upstream's base motion planner has collision checking hardcoded off — a correctness fix to `(1.10, 1.75)` is separately in flight and not yet merged as of this experiment.

Both classifiers are the real ones EES trains its per-skill success predictors against (`HoldingClassifier` for `Pick`, `RobotAtSuccessfulThrowPoseClassifier` for `MoveToThrowPose` — both in `src/hitl_pmp/environments/tossing3d/predicates.py`), not a hand-rolled check, so this experiment's labels are directly comparable to what a learner actually sees.

## Hypothesis

Success is a smooth, unimodal function of each parameter, with a single reliable region per skill — rather than a fragmented, discontinuous, or uniformly noisy one.

**Did not hold for `Pick`, held (with a caveat) for `MoveToThrowPose`.** See Results.

## Guidance given

- Grid `Pick` over its full 2D sampling bounds (`PICK_DISTANCE_BOUNDS=(0.5, 0.6)` × `PICK_ROTATION_BOUNDS=(-π/4, π/4)`), ~10-15 steps per axis, ~10-15 scene seeds per cell, labelled by `HoldingClassifier`.
- Grid `MoveToThrowPose` over a *wider* range than any `THROW_STANDOFF_BOUNDS` this domain has used, at fine resolution, with `Pick`'s own params held fixed at the oracle's point (a deliberate methodological choice: `MoveToThrowPose` needs a post-`Pick` state to run from, and letting `Pick`'s own variance leak into this sweep would confound "does this standoff work" with "did the grasp even land this attempt"), labelled by `RobotAtSuccessfulThrowPoseClassifier`.
- Use the real classifiers, not a hand-rolled check.
- Run under the real KINDER simulator, as a memory-capped `systemd-run --user --unit=` service, and report progress rather than going dark for hours.
- Commit a regenerable analysis module, a figure per skill, and a dated experiment log; open a draft PR with the figures embedded.

## Methods

**Grid.** `Pick`: 12 distances × 13 rotations (odd, so rotation=0.0 lands exactly on the grid) over the full sampling bounds, 12 scene seeds/cell = 1,872 episodes. `MoveToThrowPose`: 61 standoffs from 0.35 m to 1.85 m at 0.025 m resolution — wider than both the old `(0.45, 1.75)` and the in-flight proposed `(1.10, 1.75)` sampler bounds on both ends — 12 scene seeds/cell = 732 episodes, `Pick` fixed at the oracle's point (`ORACLE_PICK_DISTANCE`/`ORACLE_PICK_ROTATION`) throughout.

**Seeds are paired, not independent.** The same 12 scene seeds (`0`-`11`) are reused at every grid cell in a sweep, rather than drawing fresh seeds per cell — this isolates the parameter's effect from scene-to-scene variance, matching the methodology of the companion throw-band sweep. The cost is that a single pathological seed would shift every cell by the same `1/12`; the per-seed breakdown in the committed log's own report output is what makes that checkable rather than assumed away.

**Every cell also records physical diagnostics beyond the classifier label**, because `RobotAtSuccessfulThrowPoseClassifier` reads only the base's final pose after `move_to_target` terminates (plus a lateral conjunct) — it does not look at what the base hit on the way, so a step-function success curve alone cannot reveal a collision. Each `MoveToThrowPose` cell records the bin's and the barrier's own position before and after the skill sequence; a genuine collision shows up as a nonzero position delta, independent of what the classifier says.

**Driven by** a new script, `scripts/tossing3d_skill_parameter_sweep.py`, run under the KINDER venv with this worktree's `src` on `PYTHONPATH`. Unlike every other simulator-driving script in this repo, it imports `hitl_pmp` directly (the module's own docstring explains why: the whole point of this experiment is to check outcomes against the *real* classifiers, not a re-derived equivalent) — made possible because `KinderBackend` is the only module in `hitl_pmp` that imports KINDER, and only lazily, so importing the rest of the package costs nothing beyond `pydantic`/`numpy`/`gymnasium`, which the KINDER venv already carries. Ran as `t3d-skill-param-sweep.service` (`systemd-run --user --unit=`, `MemoryMax=8G`, `MemorySwapMax=0`, `OOMPolicy=continue`). RSS was measured flat across two pilots (~1.1 GB across 108 episodes, no leak) before the full run was launched.

## Results

The sweep ran 1h 23min 58s wall-clock, 959.4 MB peak memory. 2,604 episodes total: 1,872 for `Pick`, 732 for `MoveToThrowPose`.

### `Pick`: 1,643/1,872 overall (87.8%) — but the aggregate hides a real 2D structure

greps `inventory_app/` for `product_generic_standins`. Other tests drop 100 MB

author: veldkornet
body:
## Why

A follow-up code review of #461 caught two regressions in the fix that PR introduced:

1. The shared `condition:` detects an except handler's `as` clause with an unanchored `r"\bas\b"` regex over the captured exception expression's text. This false-matches on the literal word "as" appearing anywhere in that text — e.g. inside a string literal passed to an exception constructor (`except (CustomError("used as fallback"), TypeError):`) — silently suppressing the rule for a genuine PEP 758 violation.
2. The factory-call test added in #461 (`except* factory(...)`) doesn't actually exercise the Tuple-vs-Call condition it claims to: without an explicit outer paren, the exception expression never reaches the pattern's `${exceptions}` capture at all, so the test was passing for the wrong reason (pattern-stage mismatch, not condition-stage exclusion).

## What changed

- Anchored the `as`-clause regex to a trailing `as <name>` (`r"\bas\s+\w+\s*$"`) so it only matches a real as-clause, not the word "as" occurring earlier in the text.
- Fixed both rules' factory-call test to wrap the call in an explicit outer paren (`except (factory(...)):`) so it actually reaches and is excluded by the `node_type == "Tuple"` condition.
- Added coverage for a single-element trailing-comma tuple (`except (ValueError,):`), which is structurally a `Tuple` and should be flagged — distinct from the untested no-comma case (`except (ValueError):`, a bare `Name`).

## Testing

- Verified the YAML parses and anchors resolve correctly.
- Verified the anchored regex's behavior against several plausible capture-text hypotheses with Python's `re` module — matches genuine trailing `as <name>` clauses, does not match "as" embedded in a string literal regardless of position.
- **Caveat**: I don't have a local Sourcery engine to validate against the real `${exceptions}` capture semantics — the new regression tests (and Sourcery's own CI check on this PR) are the actual validation, same mechanism that caught the original config error in #461.

Same fix applied to [ha-hyxi-cloud](https://github.com/Veldkornet/ha-hyxi-cloud) to keep the two `.sourcery.yaml` files in sync.

## Summary by Sourcery

Tighten PEP 758 exception grouping rules in the Sourcery config to correctly detect `as` clauses and ensure tuple vs factory-call cases are exercised by tests.

Bug Fixes:
- Anchor the `as`-clause detection regex so it only matches genuine trailing `as <name>` clauses and no longer misfires on the word `as` inside exception expression contents.

Tests:
- Expand regression tests for both standard and `except*` PEP 758 rules to cover factory calls wrapped in parentheses and single-element trailing-comma tuples.

author: rjrodger
body:
jsonic side of tabnas/parser#74. Adds the cross-port fixture rows for base-prefixed integers beyond int64.

The fixture carries **both** `0x8000000000000000` and `0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF` deliberately: the first agrees even under the clamped (wrong) implementation, by coincidence — `float64(MaxInt64)` and `float64(2^63)` round to the same double — so a fixture with only that row would pass an implementation off by 2× on the second. Signed forms, a 2^76 literal, and the in-range/decimal siblings are the controls.

Mutation-checked both ways: fails against the clamped implementation and against the unfixed one.

Go green, TS 403/403.

author: ko-tarou
body:
## PREP

**結論**: chat-service の残る Cloudflare Queues 依存（`EVT_NOTIFICATION` の chat.* fan-out + `AUDIT_QUEUE`）を無料の `@dub/freeq` D1 outbox に置き換えた。RTハブの ChatRoom Durable Object は無料枠で動くため温存し、Queue依存部分だけ freeq 化。event-service(#128)/auth/mail-gateway と同一パターン。

**理由**: Cloudflare Queues は有料機能で無料プラン deploy にバインドできない。producer INSERT を耐久性保証にし、Cron drain が実consumerへ転送する outbox パターンで「取りこぼしゼロ」を保つ。

### 撤去した Queue と freeq 使用箇所
| 項目 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| 撤去 producer | `EVT_NOTIFICATION`（chat.* → notification）／ `AUDIT_QUEUE`（audit.record） |
| consumer | chat-service は producer 専用（Queue consumer は元々なし） |
| freeq 使用 | `src/outbox.ts` = `outboxQueue()` shim ＋ `buildPublisherEnv()`（binding有無フォールバック）。`index.ts` の `buildPublisher`/`buildAudit` が binding 不在時に outbox へフォールバック |
| consumer route (drain先) | `src/drain.ts`: `audit.record` → audit-log `POST /internal/audit-async`（`x-dub-internal` ガード・envelope verbatim・非2xxでpending保持）／ `evt.*` は defer（durable/pending・循環再導入なし） |
| Cron | `scheduled()` が 5分毎 drain（best-effort・失敗はlogのみ）。FREE 5-cron上限に配慮した単一schedule |
| DO温存 | ChatRoom DO（WS fanout/presence/ws-ticket）は無改変。`wrangler.free.toml` に DO binding ＋ `new_sqlite_classes` を維持 |

### 無料構成
- `wrangler.free.toml` 追加: **Queue無し**・共有 `dub-core` D1（`d663f9c6-…`）・`DUB_DEFAULT_ORG_ID=org_devhub`・`workers_dev=false`・5分 cron・DO binding/migration 保持・SVC_AUDIT等の service binding（dub- 名）。
- `db/0001_freeq_outbox.sql` 追加（`@dub/freeq` OUTBOX_DDL と lockstep）。
- **有料 `wrangler.toml` は不変**（queue-wiring conformance 維持）。

### テスト実測
| 検証 | 結果 |
|---|---|
| `pnpm --filter @dub/chat-service test` | 79 pass（従来70＋新規9）|
| 新規: `test/outbox.test.ts` (5) / `test/drain.test.ts` (4) | green（node:sqlite で freeq_outbox 実SQL）|
| `typecheck` | green |
| queue-wiring conformance | 5 pass |
| e2e-smoke conformance | chat-service 16/16 routes・drift 0 |

### 本番反映準備
**保留（直列）**。deploy は行っていない（PRまで）。本番反映は高岡さんの合図で直列に。手順は `wrangler.free.toml` 冒頭コメント（outbox テーブル作成 → `WS_TICKET_SECRET` 設定 → `wrangler deploy --config wrangler.free.toml`）。

author: calixtothebughunter
body:
Closes #23

The first three stages of the pipeline, each job named so its `name:` **is** the required status check context.

## SPEC

[**Engineering Standards § CI pipeline order**](https://github.com/CalixtoTheBugHunter/talos/wiki/Engineering-Standards#ci-pipeline-order) — binding lines, verbatim:

> ```
> lint (SwiftLint + SwiftFormat --lint)
>   → build
>   → test (Swift Testing)
>   → spec-guard (see below)
>   → perf-budget
>   → a11y (XCUITest)
> ```

> Every stage is a required status check on `main`.

[**§ Toolchain**](https://github.com/CalixtoTheBugHunter/talos/wiki/Engineering-Standards#toolchain) — verbatim:

> | Unit + integration tests | **Swift Testing** | CI, required check |
> | Linting | **SwiftLint** | CI, warnings-as-errors |
> | Formatting | **SwiftFormat** | CI runs `--lint`; developers autofix locally |

[**§ The suite installs nothing**](https://github.com/CalixtoTheBugHunter/talos/wiki/Engineering-Standards#the-suite-installs-nothing) — why the report never fakes a pass:

> a skipped test is indistinguishable from a passing one on a green run

[**Technology & Distribution § Decisions**](https://github.com/CalixtoTheBugHunter/talos/wiki/Technology-and-Distribution#decisions):

> | Architecture | Apple Silicon only (arm64) |

## DoD criterion

**Advances none directly**, which is the justification the board item's `DoD` field carries rather than a blank:

> Advances none directly — CI configuration is backlog work per [Decision 16](https://github.com/CalixtoTheBugHunter/talos/wiki/Decision-Log#process-decisions). lint/build/test are the prerequisite stages for spec-guard (#11), perf-budget (#9), and a11y (#10), which the sibling items advance.

## SPEC changed in this PR (step 4)

**None.** No page contradicts this change. [Decision 54](https://github.com/CalixtoTheBugHunter/talos/wiki/Decision-Log#engineering-decisions) left an obligation for whoever authored this pipeline — "when that pipeline is authored, the `build` stage carries these overrides" — and the `build` job discharges it, so the SPEC was already correct.

## Acceptance criteria

| # | Criterion | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Runs on PRs and pushes to `main` | `on: pull_request` + `push: branches: [main]` |
| 2 | macOS runner able to build macOS 26 arm64 | `runs-on: macos-26` — the arm64 image (`macos-26-intel` is x64) |
| 3 | SwiftLint warnings-as-errors; SwiftFormat `--lint` | `swiftlint lint` with `strict: true` from `.swiftlint.yml`, no `--strict` flag; `swiftformat --lint .` |
| 4 | Release configuration | `swift build -c release` **and** `xcodebuild -configuration Release` |
| 5 | Swift Testing results reported in the PR | `--xunit-output`, parsed with `xmllint` into a step-summary table, XML uploaded as an artifact |
| 6 | Xcode and toolchain pinned explicitly | `DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode_26.6.app/...`; SwiftLint `0.65.0` and SwiftFormat `0.62.1` pinned by version **and sha256** |
| 7 | Dependency caching | `actions/cache` on `.build` keyed by `Package.swift`/`Package.resolved`, and on the linters keyed by version+checksum |
| 8 | Read-only permissions by default | top-level `permissions: contents: read`, no `secrets.*` reference, every action pinned by commit SHA |
| 9 | A failure at any stage fails the check with actionable output | every stage `exit 1` with a `::error::` annotation carrying the fix command and the wiki link |

## Verification

Every step body was extracted from the YAML and **executed**, rather than read:

```
install, clean run          → exit 0; swiftlint 0.65.0, swiftformat 0.62.1
install, tampered checksum  → exit 1, ::error::checksum mismatch, nothing installed
swiftlint    clean / dirty  → exit 0 / exit 1 with annotation
swiftformat  clean / dirty  → exit 0 / exit 1 with annotation
swift test + report         → exit 0; summary table 1 / 0 / 0 / 0
report, failing fixture     → 4 / 2 / 1 / 1, all 3 failed cases named, skip warning
report, missing XML         → exit 0, warning, "no result is claimed here"
lipo assert, real / missing → exit 0 printing arm64 / exit 1
xcodebuild Release + ARCHS  → BUILD SUCCEEDED, 23 s, app + TalosCore.o both arm64
YAML parse, bash -n × 12    → all OK
```

Signing needs no secret: the project resolves `CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY = -` with `_DEVELOPMENT_TEAM_IS_EMPTY = YES`, so the runner ad-hoc signs and the release build succeeds unmodified.

## What this does not cover

Stated because a green run is otherwise read as a claim it never made:

- **Three of six required contexts.** `spec-guard` (#24), `perf-budget` (#108, #26), and `a11y` (#26) are produced by no workflow, so this PR cannot satisfy the ruleset on `main` and needs a knowing owner bypass — the ruleset being overridden, not a routine merge.
- **The no-values rule.** [Foundations: Accessibility § How the gate is checked](https://github.com/CalixtoTheBugHunter/talos/wiki/Foundations-Accessibility#how-the-gate-is-checked) assigns "rejects fixed point sizes" and "rejects hex literals and bundled color assets" to `lint`, and neither tool does that out of the box. The workflow header says so explicitly; #136 decides who owns it. A green `lint` here is **not** a claim about either row.

## Two additions that trace to no acceptance criterion

Named rather than buried, both approved before they were written:

- `concurrency:` — cancels superseded runs on branches, never on `main`. Saves runner minutes; serves no AC.
- `.gitignore` — `.ci-tools/`, the directory the lint stage installs into, so a 36 MB binary cannot be committed by anyone reproducing the stage locally.

No test file is added. The SPEC's test rule is about product behavior, and there is no Swift-testable behavior in a YAML file; the workflow is asserted by running its steps, above.

body:
## Was / Now
Currency picker was a centered 8-button Alert.alert with no indicator of the current selection; AddCategoryModal was a raw Modal with a hand-rolled overlay and a monthly budget field; category delete was an Alert.alert.
Now: all three are the house bottom Sheet (ui/Sheet), currency selection is indicated by shape + label, AddCategoryModal is on redesign tokens with the budget field removed (D10), and category delete reuses a new shared ConfirmSheet (same pattern as app/habit/[id].tsx's stop-breaking confirm).

## Why (origin)
Unit U3 of the approved design-cohesion batch: every user-facing selection/confirmation surface on the happy path should use the house bottom Sheet.

## Improvement
- CurrencySheet: left-aligned rows (name + code, matching the Profile row's own vocabulary), sage check + accessibilityState.selected on the current currency (status reads by shape and label, not color alone), Cancel is the only centered, tertiary text.
- AddCategoryModal: converted off a raw Modal onto ui/Sheet; styles migrated off theme.surface/text/textSecondary/border/raw fontWeight onto theme.fonts.*, ink/slate/mist/cloud/snow, typeScale, and the radii token set. Monthly budget field deleted entirely (input, state, handlers, strings) per D10; app/category/[id].tsx's static budget display line and its now-orphaned string are gone too. types/category.ts keeps `monthlyBudget` on the Category type since stored data may still carry it.
- Extracted components/ui/ConfirmSheet.tsx (title/body/confirm/cancel, coral destructiveFill + secondary) from the inline pattern already in app/habit/[id].tsx, so the category delete confirm doesn't duplicate it.
- Retired the now-orphaned alert-only strings (currencyAlertTitle/Message, currencyOption, categoryDetail.budget, addCategoryModal.monthlyBudget/budgetPlaceholder) and brought a few Title Case sheet strings into sentence case while touching them.

## How we measure success
`npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Full jest suite: 49 suites / 609 tests passing, including 3 new test files covering the sheets that replaced alerts (currencySheet.test.tsx, addCategoryModal.test.tsx, categoriesDeleteConfirm.test.tsx).

## Lane (ADR 0012)
needs-user-test: three user-visible surfaces (currency picker, add/edit category, category delete).

## Capture / screenshots
Not captured in this pass (no simulator build run). What to test on device:
- [ ] Currency sheet: opens from Profile > Currency, current currency shows a sage check and is the only row with `accessibilityState.selected` (VoiceOver: "selected"), rows are left-aligned with name + code (e.g. "US Dollar (USD)"), Cancel is centered/tertiary and the only centered text, selecting a currency updates the Profile row and closes the sheet.
- [ ] Add/edit category sheet: bottom sheet with grab handle and radius-20 top (not a full-screen modal), no budget field anywhere, name/icon/color pickers behave as before, Save disabled until a name is entered, keyboard behaves normally with the amount... er, name field.
- [ ] Category delete: tapping delete on a custom category opens a bottom sheet (not a native alert) naming the category, "Keep category" cancels, "Delete category" removes it and its expenses keep their history.

matches design/PATTERN_VOCABULARY.md: yes, no named deviations. Sage check icon on the currency selection state is used analogously to the vocabulary's existing "active tab tint" allowance for sage (a selected-state indicator, never touching a spend figure).

Do not merge.

body:
## What changed

- add an audited Attend Master action to open one active cinema location in support mode
- issue a location-scoped access token that expires after 15 minutes and has no usable refresh path
- mark support access explicitly in the signed token
- reject every non-read HTTP request from support sessions in the central API authentication guard
- restore a support session from a URL fragment, then immediately remove the fragment from the address bar
- show a persistent Attend Support / Read only banner and disable cinema-admin form controls
- add real-Postgres coverage proving read access works and mutation attempts return 403

## Why

Attend operators need to troubleshoot what a cinema client sees without requesting the client's credentials. This creates a deliberate support boundary instead of silent impersonation: one location, short expiry, visible UI, server-enforced read-only access, and an audit event when the session is created.

## Security properties

- only platform owners/operators with write permission can create a session
- suspended organizations and inactive locations cannot be opened
- the token is carried in the URL fragment, not query strings or server logs
- all POST, PATCH, PUT, and DELETE requests fail before reaching controllers
- the session cannot change a password, log out another account, or refresh itself

## Validation

- API, Attend Admin, and Attend Master TypeScript typechecks
- focused ESLint
- API unit suite: 31 passing
- authentication package suite: 12 passing
- Attend Admin production build
- Attend Master production build

author: wesley-perkins-software
body:
## Summary

This PR adds comprehensive documentation of a canonical naming and terminology audit for the site's public-facing vocabulary, URL structure, and navigation conventions. The audit was conducted as research ahead of homepage redesign work to validate existing terminology choices against the frozen architectural standards.

## Key Findings

The audit confirms that the site's naming system is already well-chosen and requires no changes:

- **No URL changes recommended** — `/skills`, `/{grade}`, and all current route structures are appropriate and should not be migrated
- **No terminology changes recommended** — existing labels (Skills, Core Spelling, High-Frequency Words, Themed Spelling Practice) are correct and coherent
- **Terminology already correctly implemented** — the Skills Hub already uses "Spelling Practice by Skill" as the full H1/title while keeping "Skills" as the short navigation label, which is the correct layered-terminology pattern
- **Two clarifications already required by frozen standards** — "Core Spelling" and "Themed Spelling Practice" benefit from one-sentence explanatory framing on first exposure (already mandated by the Grade Hub and Gateway standards)

## Documentation Scope

The audit:
- Validates all public-facing naming against the Constitution, Content Model, Skills Architecture, and five canonical page-family standards
- Evaluates specific terminology candidates (Skills vs. Spelling Skills vs. Spelling Patterns, grade-naming conventions, etc.) against evidence from production code, frozen standards, and qualitative search/literacy research
- Confirms that legacy terminology (sight words, Heart Words, common words) has been fully purged from production
- Identifies the current homepage as pre-Constitution and appropriately stale, not as a terminology baseline
- Flags one already-documented architectural discrepancy (grade-label reconciliation across strands) as relevant context for future work, not as a new finding

## Implementation Implications

No code changes, migrations, or renaming work is required. The audit output is primarily for homepage research: treat the frozen inner-page standards as the terminology baseline, preserve the nav/H1/body-copy/URL layering pattern already in place, and carry forward existing clarifying-sentence requirements into homepage copy.

author: copilot
body:
Bring `@types/node` up to date and add consistent spacing rules for standalone SQL comments, which previously had no dedicated formatting treatment.

## Package updates
- Bumped `@types/node` devDependency from `26.1.1` → `26.2.0`
- Confirmed `typescript` and `@types/vscode`/`engines.vscode` are already at their latest published versions — no change needed there

## Comment formatting rules
Added a shared `emitCommentRun` helper for standalone comments (comments on their own line, not trailing code) with the following spacing rules:
- Blank line above the first comment in a run
- Blank line before **and** after block comments (`/* ... */`), even mid-run
- Consecutive single-line (`--`) comments are packed with no blank lines between them

```sql
SELECT a FROM T;
-- first
-- second
/* block */
SELECT b FROM T2;
```
formats to:

```sql
SELECT
    a
FROM T;

-- first
-- second

/* block */

SELECT
    b
FROM T2;
```

Applied at the three call sites that already treat comments as standalone: `formatStatementList`, `formatOptionalClauses`, `writeSubquery`. Inline/trailing comments (e.g. `WHERE x = 1 -- note`) are left untouched, since tokens carry no source-line info and can't reliably be distinguished from standalone comments in those contexts.

## Internal fixes enabling correct spacing
- Added a `currentLineTouched` flag so `finishLine()` is a true no-op when nothing was written since the last reset, preventing spurious blank lines from defensive `newLine()`/`blankLines()` calls after a comment run
- Reworked `blankLines(count)` to top up to `count` blank lines rather than always appending `count` more, avoiding duplicate blank lines when callers already inserted one

author: edurcampos86-jpg
body:
🟢 **FAIXA VERDE** — só documentação. Um arquivo markdown novo, zero código, zero escrita, zero migration.

Cria `docs/onix-co-estado.md`, para uma sessão nova (ou o Eduardo) saber o estado real do projeto Onix Co sem auditar o repositório do zero.

Confirmado que o arquivo **não existia** antes de criar.

---

## Procedência marcada em cada afirmação

O arquivo separa três tipos de afirmação, porque elas não valem o mesmo:

| marca | significa |
|---|---|
| 🔎 **verificado** | conferido no repositório, com `arquivo:linha` ou commit |
| 📋 **declarado** | número de produção informado pelo Eduardo. **Uma sessão não alcança produção** (o gateway responde `CONNECT tunnel failed, 403`), então isso é registro, não prova |
| ⚠️ **em conflito** | duas fontes do próprio repositório discordam |

Isso não é enfeite: foi exatamente por não separar as duas primeiras que o "lote verde de 12+ PRs acumuladas" sobreviveu sem nunca ter existido — ver o achado 3.

## Seções

**Modelos existentes** — `Empresa` (#288 · `2d460fe`), `PessoaGrupo` (#292), `ClienteBackoffice.pessoaGrupoId`, `EmpresaBootstrapLog`, `PessoaEmpresa`. Todos conferidos em `prisma/schema.prisma`, incluindo `incluiDescendentes @default(true)` e o fato de a régua de profundidade viver em código (`hierarquia.ts`), não no schema.

Com um aviso explícito: **`PessoaEmpresa` (autorização) e `PessoaGrupo` (identidade) não têm relação nenhuma** apesar do nome parecido — uma fala de pessoa do time ↔ empresa, a outra de cliente ↔ documento. O nome é armadilha real.

**Árvore em produção** — raiz + 5, com o porquê documentado de os slugs antigos terem sido mantidos: `Implementacao.empresaId` tem linhas em produção, `PessoaEmpresa.empresaId` tem FK, e `NOS_ECOSSISTEMA`/`EMPRESAS` casam por valor. Renomear é PR própria com UPDATE em massa, nunca aos pedaços.

**Identidade** — régua de união travada, números do backfill B2 (#299), e as filas de conferência humana pendentes (~331 pares CPF↔CNPJ, 117 documentos multi-conta).

**RBAC** — estado do eixo CGE, os 7 clientes sem CGE invisíveis sob escopo restrito (`rbac.ts:131`, correção é dado e não código), e a composição por AND que falta.

**Política de alçadas** — verde/amarela/vermelha, com a regra de que PR vermelha só mergeia na sessão que a especificou. E o domínio correto (`www.ecossistemaonix.com.br`; o apex não resolve).

**Pendências** e o roteiro de manutenção do próprio arquivo.

---

## Três achados durante a redação

### 1. ⚠️ Conflito aberto — a PR #301 propõe 3 níveis

**#301 está aberta (draft, tier vermelho) e contradiz a árvore de 6 nós ponto a ponto:**

- hierarquia de **3 níveis**, 20 nós, `tipo` como enum `TipoNo` e `transversal` como flag
- **Agro e Corporate deixam de ser empresa** → departamento
- **Educação e Contábil passam a existir como empresa** — o oposto do que está travado hoje
- `"Onix Imobiliária"` volta a `"Onix Imob"`
- o eixo `cadastrada` do catálogo desaparece

**O que trava:** a migration da #301 adiciona `tipo NOT NULL` **sem DEFAULT**, deliberadamente, como guarda — ela **falha com `23502` se `Empresa` tiver qualquer linha**. A própria PR declara que não conseguiu confirmar se `Empresa` está vazia em produção.

Se a árvore de 6 existe mesmo em produção, **a #301 não aplica como está**. Registrei como conflito aberto, **sem escolher lado** — é decisão de produto, não de documentação. A conferência é um comando: `SELECT count(*) FROM "Empresa";`

### 2. ✅ Pergunta fechada — `isAdmin(ctx)` **não** é `Papel.adminGlobal`

Estava listada como "aberto, verificar antes de usar como gate". **São desconectados:**

| | onde | resolve |
|---|---|---|
| `isAdmin(ctx)` | `rbac-papeis.ts:28-30` | `ctx.role === "admin" \|\| ctx.pessoa?.teamRole === "admin"` |
| `Papel.adminGlobal` | só em `rbac.ts:57` | escopo de CGE |

`adminGlobal` **não participa** de `isAdmin()`. Gatear por ele deixaria a rota inacessível na prática: `Pessoa.papelId` é nullable e as Pessoas existentes seguem sem papel pela Fase 1 do RBAC. Usar `isAdmin` no eixo empresa é coerente com todas as rotas admin atuais.

### 3. ⚠️ Correção de registro — o "lote verde de 12+ PRs" não existe

Há **8 PRs abertas**, e **nenhuma** corresponde aos temas listados (`acoesDisponiveis`, probe no smoke, `divergencias` no GET, ensaio no CI, campo `operacao`, `Implementacao` órfã, …):

| # | título | criada |
|---|---|---|
| 301 | hierarquia de 3 níveis (draft, 🔴) | 2026-08-10 |
| 180 | backfill de conversas DataCrazy | 2026-06-16 |
| 166 | tipa `no-explicit-any` de `datacrazy.ts` | 2026-06-13 |
| 161 | import server-side do Saldo em CC | 2026-06-12 |
| 154 | carrossel (draft) | 2026-06-09 |
| 113 | busca inteligente de clientes | 2026-05-30 |
| 27 | remove credenciais em claro | 2026-05-18 |
| 2 | rename Cockpit → Ecossistema Onix | 2026-05-05 |

Esses itens foram **sugeridos em conversa e nunca viraram PR**. Ficam no arquivo como backlog declarado, com o estado real das 8 abertas ao lado — não como trabalho pendente de revisão.

**Também registrado:** `RBAC_ENFORCEMENT` é flag de Config DB com `default OFF` no código (`rbac.ts:26`, lida via `getConfig` em `:33`). O valor de produção **não está no repositório** e não se deduz lendo o código — só se confere em `/api/configuracoes/flags`.

---

## Gates

Nenhum — é só markdown. Não toca código, teste, build ou schema.

```
 docs/onix-co-estado.md | 1 arquivo novo
```

## Para o auditor

Faixa verde: sem migration, sem escrita, sem RBAC, sem segredo. Pronta para aprovação e merge por sessão separada.

Dois pontos que valem revisão de conteúdo, não de forma:

1. o **conflito com a #301** está descrito sem tomar partido — confirmar se é assim que deve ficar registrado;
2. os números de produção estão marcados 📋 porque **não pude conferi-los daqui**. Se algum estiver errado, o arquivo propaga o erro para todas as sessões seguintes.

---

author: romazes
body:
#### Description
`FixOrderProperties` now owns `LocateBroker` — the broker the shares are borrowed from for a short sale. Brokerages send it only on short sell orders; the FIX tag carrying it is brokerage specific (e.g. 5700).

- `TerminalLinkOrderProperties` and `WolverineOrderProperties` now extend `FixOrderProperties` and inherit `LocateBroker`; their own copies are removed.
- `TerminalLinkOrderProperties.Notes` is removed too — the base class already has the same property.
- `BloombergFixOrderProperties` inherits the property with no changes of its own.

Existing usage of the property in the plugins, both only on short sells:
- TerminalLink: [emits `EMSX_LOCATE_BROKER` only when the side is SHRT](https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean.Brokerages.TerminalLink/blob/44547bee75fc6c7eeb531affc11ee839b3f99e42/QuantConnect.TerminalLink/TerminalLinkBrokerage.cs#L403-L409)
- Wolverine: [sends the locate broker on the FIX order message](https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean.Brokerages.Wolverine/blob/44bbc15cb365af98eeb843851e550b6d17463b13/QuantConnect.Wolverine/WolverineOrderRoutingSessionHandler.cs#L166)

**Locate clean-up before submit.** A locate belongs only on a short sell — one broker complained we sent tag 5700 on buys and long sales. New helper `BrokerageExtensions.TryRemoveLocateFromNonShortOrder` (returns true when it removed something) drops the locate (the `LocateBroker` property plus tags `5700` and `114` in `AdditionalProperties`) from any order that does not open a short position. A `PositionSide` set in the TerminalLink/Wolverine order properties overrides the holdings-based mapping. Called from `QCAlgorithm.PreOrderChecksImpl`, which runs for every algorithm order.

`TerminalLinkBrokerageModel.CanSubmitOrder` also calls the helper, because TerminalLink adds two things of its own: holdings decide a short only when `AutomaticPositionSides` is on ([the plugin maps the SHRT side from holdings only then](https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean.Brokerages.TerminalLink/blob/44547bee75fc6c7eeb531affc11ee839b3f99e42/QuantConnect.TerminalLink/TerminalLinkBrokerage.cs#L560-L581)), and `LocateId` is cleared together with the locate broker.

To keep the cleanup from touching the algorithm's own object, `CreateSubmitOrderRequest` now clones the order properties into every request — callers often reuse one properties instance across orders (liquidate then short, combo legs), and before this the cleanup on a close leg would silently strip the locate a later short still needed.

#### Related PR(s)
QuantConnect/Lean.Brokerages.Fix.Bloomberg#15 — the Bloomberg FIX plugin will consume these properties to send the short locate tags (114=N + 5700).

#### Related Issue
N/A

#### Motivation and Context
The Bloomberg FIX integration needs a locate broker on short sells (broker requirement). Two brokerages (TerminalLink, Wolverine) already had their own `LocateBroker` property — instead of adding a third copy, the property moves to the shared FIX base class.

#### Requires Documentation Change
No

#### How Has This Been Tested?
- `AlgorithmTradingTests.MarketOrderKeepsLocateOnlyOnShortSells` — 8 cases placing a `MarketOrder` with locate order properties: one per position (BuyToOpen/BuyToClose/SellToOpen/SellToClose), locate as property vs tags 114/5700, and the `PositionSide` override in both directions. Each case also asserts the caller's properties object is never mutated. All pass.
- `AlgorithmTradingTests.MarketOrderLocateCleanupDoesNotMutateReusedProperties` — reuses one properties object for a close leg and then a short leg: the close goes out without the locate, the short with it, and the caller's object keeps it.
- `TerminalLinkBrokerageModelTests.CanSubmitOrder_KeepsLocateOnlyOnShortSells` — 6 cases: `AutomaticPositionSides` on/off, cross-zero short, and the `PositionSide` override in both directions; asserts `LocateBroker` and `LocateId` are kept or cleared together.
- `TerminalLinkOrderPropertiesTests` (3 tests, including the Python locate-fields test) and new `WolverineOrderPropertiesTests.InheritsLocateBrokerFromFixOrderProperties` — all pass.

#### Types of changes
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] Refactor (non-breaking change which improves implementation)
- [ ] Performance (non-breaking change which improves performance)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] Non-functional change (xml comments/documentation/etc)

#### Checklist:
- [x] My code follows the code style of this project.
- [x] I have read the **CONTRIBUTING** document.
- [x] I have added tests to cover my changes.
- [x] All new and existing tests passed.
- [x] My branch follows the naming convention `bug-<issue#>-<description>` or `feature-<issue#>-<description>`

author: neo-opus-vega
body:
Resolves #16611

The last three parity rows now carry a **decision** instead of a deferral. Two of the three changed under measurement, and one of my own acceptance criteria was falsified by the gate itself.

Evidence: L1 (static contract audit + the gate run, with a positive control proving the surviving baseline row is load-bearing) → L1 required (no runtime-verify AC). No residuals.

## Deltas

**`ai/scripts/lint/lint-openapi-service-parity.mjs`** — one row removed and re-added corrected, one row's reason replaced. No other file.

### `get_context_frontier.depth` — my AC was measured on the wrong method

The row read `TRANSITIONAL`, and this ticket's AC said: *"`depth` is **removed** from `getContextFrontier`'s signature. Measured dead (0 occurrences in the method body)."*

**There are two `getContextFrontier`s.** The one bound to this operation is `MemoryService.getContextFrontier()` — it declares no parameters and calls `GraphService.getContextFrontier()` forwarding nothing. The live `depth` read belongs to **`GraphService`**'s same-named method, whose sole caller is `GoldenPathSynthesizer` passing a literal `{depth: 1}`.

So the parameter is **neither dead nor reachable through MCP**. Deleting it breaks an internal traversal knob in use; declaring it advertises a knob the bound method cannot forward. `PERMANENT` is the only truthful disposition.

I found this by deleting the row and running the gate, which immediately red with `get_context_frontier reads depth → ai/services/memory-core/GraphService.mjs`. The AC's premise did not survive its own execution — I had checked `MemoryService`, noted in passing that two same-named methods existed, and still measured the wrong one. The comment above the row keeps that history, because the next author will hit the same name collision.

### `get_session_memories.memorySharing` — the decision, and why the default doesn't make it

The row stated a reason and then deferred (*"disposition under #16611"*). The AC required the decision made, including whether the two declaring siblings are precedent or over-exposed.

`policy === 'team'` sets `tenantScope = null`, dropping the `userId` predicate so the query returns **every maintainer's records for the session** (`MemoryService.mjs:1174-1184`). The shipped default *is* `team` (`configBase.mjs:920`), so on a default plane a declared parameter grants nothing — it can only narrow to `private`.

**That is precisely why the default does not decide it.** A deployment configuring per-org isolation sets `defaultPolicy = 'private'` (recorded at `MemoryService.mjs:2304`), and there a declared parameter lets a caller re-select `team` and read past the isolation the operator asked for. The risk concentrates on the one deployment shape that opted in, so `PERMANENT` / never declared.

**Verdict on the siblings, which the AC demanded:** `query_raw_memories` and `query_summaries` declare it, so they are **not precedent — they are over-exposed on a private-default plane.** Repairing that is a breaking contract change plus a security disposition, and a lint row is the wrong instrument. Recorded, not silently widened, and not silently narrowed either.

I nearly filed this as a security finding on the inverse premise. Reading `tenantScope = null` first, I had "agent-settable read-scope escalation" — then checked the default and found `team`, which flips it. Both facts are needed; either alone gives the wrong answer.

### Rows already satisfied, verified rather than assumed

`viaMcp`, `staleStrategy`, `includeMetadata`, `who_is_online.now` all already carry `PERMANENT` dispositions with their rationale intact, including the "do not helpfully widen this" warnings.

## Test Evidence

```
npm run ai:lint-openapi-service-parity
→ OK — 40 wrapped service(s), 121 operation-bound + 142 object-dispatch handler(s),
  0 consumed-but-undeclared, 0 declared-but-unused (advisory), 17 positional handler(s)
```

**Positive control — the surviving `depth` row is load-bearing, not a no-op beside an already-green state.** Mangling only its key (`...depth` → `...depthX`) reds the gate; restoring it returns to OK. Without this, "the lint is clean" would be indistinguishable from "the lint no longer looks at this."

**Falsification receipt** — deleting the row outright:
```
FAILED — 1 consumed-but-undeclared parameter(s):
- get_context_frontier reads `depth` — not declared in .../memory-core/openapi.yaml
    ai/services/memory-core/GraphService.mjs → getContextFrontier()
```
That output is what corrected the AC.

```
UNIT_TEST_MODE=true npx playwright test --config=.../playwright.config.unit.mjs --workers=1 \
  test/playwright/unit/ai/mcp/validation/
→ 88 passed
```

Pre-commit chain green, including the parity gate itself as a staged-file hook.

## Post-Merge Validation

None deferred. Every acceptance criterion is static and discharged above; the gate is the verifier and it runs in CI.

## Review

Cross-family seat needed (author is opus). The `memorySharing` disposition is the one worth a second reader: I claim the *private-default* deployment is the case that decides it, and that the two declaring siblings are consequently over-exposed rather than precedent. If you think the sibling declarations are deliberate and correct, that is a real disagreement and it changes this row.

Authored by @neo-opus-vega 🌿

author: batonogov
body:
## Summary

- treat project-window close as non-destructive for terminals and agents, so it no longer presents the misleading active-process warning
- preserve the existing unsaved editor Save, Discard, Cancel, and failed-save safeguards
- keep terminal-tab, pane, Quick Terminal, and aggregate application-quit authorization unchanged
- verify the exact ProjectManager, TerminalTab, process identity, and agent session survive background and reopen

Closes #1406

## Independent review gate

Three fresh-context read-only reviewers covered:

- correctness and architecture: window/background/reopen boundary, same-manager identity, tab/pane and quit safeguards
- concurrency, security, and lifecycle: MainActor delegate re-entry, cancellation, dirty authorization TOCTOU, retained PTY/task ownership, macOS 26/27 APIs
- tests, UX, and compatibility: no-alert fidelity, process termination detection, Save/Discard/Cancel/error coverage, active-agent XCUITest, shard balance

Findings fixed before push:

- P2: foreground overrides survived TerminalTab.stop(), so tests could false-pass; added explicit nontermination assertions before close, after windowWillClose, and after reopen
- P2: successful dirty-file Save with an active agent was not covered; added isolated EditorSettings, disk persistence, background/reopen, and identity assertions
- P3: lifecycle comments still described window-close terminal revalidation; corrected the documented consumers and invariants

Final verdict from all three reviewers: CLEAN, no unresolved P0-P3 findings.

## Verification

- full app/test compilation through xcodebuild: pass
- targeted unit suites: 68/68 pass
- active-agent close/background/reopen/Open Folder XCUITest: 1/1 pass
- strict SwiftLint on all changed Swift files: pass
- UI shard validator: 226 tests, delta 3
- git diff --check: pass
- post-#1410 merge tree identity verified; the reviewed candidate and published head are byte-identical

Local environment: macOS 27.0 (26A5388g), Xcode 27.0 beta (27A5194q), SDK 27.0 (26A5353p), deployment target macOS 26.0. macOS 26 runtime is the required CI compatibility gate.

Ready to merge when every required CI check is green.
