author: tinuvael
body:
### Motivation

- Убрать обычные «replace-all» whole-state записи из нормальных UI workflow и ввести узкие, атомарные записи для реальных команд (Phase 5B). 
- Сохранить совместимость на время (Phase 5C позже) и не ломать существующий live in-memory graph, rollback и filesystem compensation для attachments.

### Description

- Добавлен новый application port `AssessmentWrites` (`application/ports/assessment_writes.py`) с явными операциями (архивы, append-геометрии, technical-card revision, area geometry, links, evaluation owner/revision, attachment metadata) и без общего `save(state)` API.
- Реализован конкретный SQLAlchemy-адаптер `SqlAlchemyAssessmentWrites` (`infrastructure/db/assessment_writes.py`) который выполняет узкие, транзакционные изменения только затронутых таблиц и обеспечивает атомарность для multi-row операций (geometry+links, Evaluation owner+attachment, Production block+event+geometry+audit).
- Мигрирован ряд application точек вызова: `AssessmentEditingSession` теперь использует focused writer через `_write(...)`, при этом fallback на legacy whole-state `save()` оставлен как compatibility-only; `EntityAttachmentService` получил явные колбеки `on_add/on_update/on_delete` и больше не передаёт `editing.save` в UI; `EntityPageController` и `app/use_case_factory` обновлены для передачи `SqlAlchemyAssessmentWrites`; `AssessmentAreaCreationPage.save_now()` сделан no-op для leave-guard (подтверждённая геометрия уже сохранена атомарно).
- `infrastructure/db/blast_event_creation.py` перестал вызывать whole-state `replace_for_domain*` и использует focused insert-помощник для contour/production вставок.
- Сохранён совместимый whole-state контракт: `AssessmentStatePersistence.save()` и `AssessmentStateRepository.replace_for_domain()` помечены как compatibility-only и оставлены до Phase 5C; whole-state load остаётся без изменений.
- Документация обновлена (`docs/architecture.md`, `docs/architecture_migration_plan.md`) с пометкой `Phase 5B COMPLETE` и описанием оставшихся шагов к Phase 5C.

### Testing

- Запущен набор целевых тестов и интеграций: `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen pytest -q tests/test_entity_editing_session.py tests/test_assessment_state_repository_postgres.py tests/test_create_blast_event_use_case.py tests/test_entity_attachments.py tests/test_assessment_event_links.py tests/test_assessment_area_workflow.py tests/test_wall_assessment_persistence_ui.py tests/test_main_window_page_routing.py tests/test_architecture_boundaries.py` — результат: **102 passed, 2 skipped**.
- Полный тест-ран `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen pytest -q` — результат: **348 passed, 32 skipped, 2 failed**; оба падения — известные ezdxf-version-sensitive тесты и считаются допускаемыми (не связаны с изменением persistence).
- Запущены проверки: `python tools/architecture_audit.py`, `python -m compileall -q .`, `git diff --check`, `alembic heads` — все успешны; alembic head остаётся `20260809_0008` и никаких миграций не добавлено.
- Ручная аудит кода подтвердил, что обычные interactive workflows больше не вызывают whole-state `save()`/`replace_for_domain()` и что focused adapter операции используют собственные транзакции.

body:
<!-- senpai-assignment:v1 {"assignment_id":"maple-r109-a-decode-commit-cadence","base_ref":"codex/mlxfast-maple-20260804-advisor","base_sha":"9fe371909ee7ffa66a345cf3c42c21141096f388","head_ref":"maple-frieren/r109-decode-commit-cadence","head_sha":"3bba6e17629f725b0b64584fe7c57fe3e78d4184","repo":"morganmcg1/mlxfast-challenge_senpai","revision_id":"r109-a-rev2","schema_version":1,"student":"maple-frieren"} -->

## Context: your own R108-K result is the best unexplained lead in the campaign

Your PR #660 is closed as P-INDETERMINATE, but not because it was wrong. Two of its three products were decisive and are now programme law:

- `k = 0.4478` M4 us/dispatch, CI95 [0.4006, 0.4950]; barrier price ~= 0.
- That repricing killed the family-E M2 merge (0.63% -> 0.15% [0.13, 0.17]) before a line was built. Correct call.

The third product is the one I am reissuing. You measured a **negative intercept `c = -3.76 .. -4.21` us/layer = -150 .. -168 us/step, ~1.7% of the decode step, apparently bought by one extra per-layer commit boundary at ZERO added dispatches.** As submitted it was an N=0 extrapolation with a tape-split confound, so I could not accept it. But it is now directly testable, because I had HEAD audited and the commit cadence turns out to be a **live, named, env-controlled knob** rather than something you have to synthesise.

This matters enormously right now. tanjiro's #663 retired the entire dispatch-count axis (all 158 removable dispatches = 0.1439% repriced, below the 0.243% detection floor). fern's #664 retired the byte axis (15.10 MiB/step per 0.4%, and the quantization envelope locks the payload). **Command-buffer commit cadence is one of only two levers the campaign has left, and it is the only one that changes nothing about the computed work.** Identical kernels, identical dispatches, identical bytes, identical arithmetic - only when the host lets the GPU start.

## The exact mechanism, verified at HEAD `1a6761bf`

All line numbers in `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift` (LRM).

| Site | Where | Control |
|---|---|---|
| Layer-loop commit | `asyncEval(h)` at **LRM:11694** (last-layer branch) and **LRM:11706** (general branch), fired when `(decodeFireMask >> i) & 1 == 1` and `isSingleTokenDecode` | `decodeFireMask` built at **LRM:11477-11487** |
| Cadence policy | `lagunaDecodeAsyncStage`, **LRM:735-777** | env `DARKBLOOM_DECODE_ASYNC_STAGE`, **default string `"at:0,1,7,15,23,31,39"`** at LRM:737-738, parsed to `.explicit(mask)` at LRM:760-766 |
| Attention projection commit | `asyncEval(qkv, gateLogits)` at **LRM:6018**, restricted to `layerIdx == 0, B == 1, L == 1` (LRM:6014-6016) | env `DARKBLOOM_ATTN_PROJECTION_ASYNC`, default ON, LRM:782-783 |
| Inactive sinks | `asyncEval(hidden)` LRM:11776-11778 (`.norm`), `asyncEval(result)` LRM:11801-11803 (`.logits`) | dormant under the default `at:` mode |
| Prefill ladder | LRM:11709-11712, gated on `h.dim(1) > 1` | env `DARKBLOOM_PREFILL_ASYNC_LADDER`, default `"1"`, LRM:799-800 |

**So the shipped decode step has exactly 8 commit boundaries: 7 in the 40-layer loop plus 1 attention-projection.** Your intercept says the marginal boundary is worth about -4 us/layer. The default fires on layers 0,1,7,15,23,31,39 - dense at the start, then every 8. Nobody has ever measured whether that shape is right; it is inherited, not derived.

## Hypothesis

The decode commit cadence is mis-tuned. There exists an `at:` mask, reachable without changing any kernel, that improves normalized decode score by >= 0.25% versus the shipped default, and the effect is monotone-ish in boundary count over some range rather than a single lucky point.

Falsifiable both ways. If the default is already at the optimum of a flat, noisy surface, that is a clean `N-CADENCE-OPTIMAL` and it permanently retires the intercept anomaly - also a success.

## Stage 1 - env-only screen (NO rebuild needed). Post by 2026-08-10T23:00Z

`DARKBLOOM_DECODE_ASYNC_STAGE` is read at runtime, so the entire screen is a **zero-build sweep**. Use `./benchmark.sh --local-iterate`, `n=3` per arm, on one quiet M4 Pro, honouring the thermal gate, one model-holding process at a time.

Screen at least these arms, all against the shipped default as the paired control:

- **Denser:** `at:` every layer (`0,1,2,...,39`), every 2 (`0,2,4,...,38`), every 4 (`0,3,7,11,15,19,23,27,31,35,39`).
- **Shipped:** `at:0,1,7,15,23,31,39` (control).
- **Sparser:** `at:0,9,19,29,39`, `at:0,19,39`, `at:39`.
- **Shape probes at fixed count:** the default has 7 boundaries front-loaded. Run a 7-boundary *uniform* mask `at:5,11,17,23,29,35,39` and a 7-boundary *back-loaded* mask `at:0,25,29,32,35,37,39`. This separates "how many" from "where", which your intercept model could not.
- **Orthogonal toggles:** `DARKBLOOM_ATTN_PROJECTION_ASYNC=0` against the best mask found, and `DARKBLOOM_PREFILL_ASYNC_LADDER` in {1,2,4,8} on the prefill axis only.

Report seconds/token and the normalized score `ns = (0.013890/decode_s_per_tok)^0.75 * (0.0003845/prefill_s_per_tok)^0.25` for every arm. `ns` is 3.3x less noisy than `officialScore`; use it.

**Argmax debiasing is mandatory.** You are taking a max over ~10 arms sharing one control leg. Do not headline a raw argmax. Apply the correction you and edward already used: `bias = sigma_contrast * sqrt(1-rho) * E[max of m iid N(0,1)]`, state `m`, and report the debiased estimate next to the raw one.

## Stage 2 - confirm the top-2 arms properly. Post by 2026-08-11T04:00Z

Take the two best debiased arms into a **contemporaneous paired ABBA, >= 8 pairs**, with a preregistered revert. Use nezuko's power table from #657: paired sd 18.222 us/token, a 0.40% effect resolves in 3 blocks and 0.25% in 4-5 blocks at ~198 s/run. Run with `FERN_DEFEAT_SLOTS=64` and headline the residency-defeated number; a cache-resident reading may appear only beside its defeated twin. Residency inflation on this harness has been measured at ~30x, so this is not optional.

Also run the cadence sweep once on **prefill**, because prefill is 25% of the score with its own hard 0.95 floor and we have neglected it all campaign.

## Stage 3 - LAND IT AS CODE. This is the part that is not optional.

**Every single one of the six r109 predecessors produced an EMPTY submitted-surface diff. That ends this round.** An env var is a local-only override and is explicitly not evidence that a candidate is rankable. If a mask wins, you must change the **compiled default string at LRM:737-738** so the win is in the submitted surface, then re-verify.

Your final `git diff --numstat 1a6761bf46c282fcabd0577b618f0c1206757e6c -- Sources Vendor benchmark.json Package.swift` **must be non-empty**. Paste it in your result.

This is a ~1-line change, so it is also the cheapest possible byte cost of any arm this round - budget yourself **5 KB**.

## Deconfliction - read this, five arms are editing LRM concurrently

| Student | Owns these LRM regions - do not touch anyone else's |
|---|---|
| **you (frieren)** | **LRM:735-800 (cadence policy + defaults), LRM:11477-11487, LRM:11694-11712** |
| nezuko | LRM:9977-10110, 10130-10190 (router tournament kernel) |
| tanjiro | LRM:7850-7930, 8044-8054 (routed gate/up prologue + dispatch) |
| edward | LRM:1507-1975 (sliding fused attention) |
| alphonse | LRM:2027-2460 (full fused attention) |

`Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift` is at **384,245 B of a 524,288 B HARD ABORT per-file cap** - 140,043 B shared across all five of you. Run `senpai/check-editable-budget.sh 1bc1c8954147c9e322aad1f3b80bd9fa3c0888d7` before every push.

- Branch from base **`1a6761bf46c282fcabd0577b618f0c1206757e6c`**.

body:
## What
`deploy.cjs` now accepts a list: `node deploy.cjs members cms`. `base44.md` STEP 1 sets a `VERTICALS` array and says to list every vertical the app uses.

## Why
It accepted a single vertical, so an app whose intent spans two had no supported way to get both scaffold sets.

Observed on a real build (**Shared Canvas Studio** — a member drawing app with a public gallery, so `members` + `cms`). The agent deployed `members`, then probed `references/cms/app`, read `wix-cms.js` and `wixImage.js` — and **hand-typed shrunken copies into `src/`** instead of deploying `cms`: 75 lines / 4 exports against the shipped 231 / 7, with the JSDoc (and the undefined-filter guard) gone. It dropped `getDataItemBy`, `countDataItems`, `updateDataItem`.

An earlier build ("Art Gallery Maker") hit the identical wall and improvised the other way — a second `deploy.cjs cms` call. That works, and appears nowhere in the docs. Same gap, two different guesses, one of which lost real code.

## Behaviour
- Duplicates collapse; order is preserved, so the first vertical listed wins any same-path file (the copy still never overwrites).
- Unknown names are reported in `error` while the valid ones deploy.
- Output carries `verticals: [...]`.
- **A single argument keeps working unchanged** — published instructions in the wild call it that way.
- Adding a vertical in a later call works, since the copy only fills in missing files.

## Verified
Scratch sandbox, five scenarios: `members cms` in one call yields the full 231-line `wix-cms.js` **with the guard** plus `wixImage.js` and `MemberContext`; single vertical unchanged; a later `cms` call adds it incrementally; mixed unknown/duplicate args; no-argument case.

author: agniv-the-marker
body:
Your exported values, written in as the defaults, with `sway px` eased back to 0.5 as asked. Two things worth knowing are below.

| tunable | was | now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bobHull` | 50 | **45** m |
| `bobEase` | 0.3 | **0** s |
| `bobSwell` | 0.9 | **1.95** |
| `bobLift` | 6 | 6 px |
| `bobScale` | 0.15 | 0.15 |
| `bobRock` | 7 | **11**° |
| `bobSway` | 1.5 | **0.5** px |
| `bobDock` | 0.4 | **0.15** |

Everything outside the bob group in the export already matched what ships — palette, water, swell, topo, ripple, camera, board, vessels/labels — as did the visibility snapshot (`attraction` off, `paused`/`future` off are the existing defaults). So nothing else moves.

**One change of my own:** `swell share` landed at 1.95 against a slider ceiling of 2. A control pinned at its limit is usually the ceiling being wrong rather than the answer, so I raised it to 3. The default is exactly the 1.95 you picked — this only leaves somewhere to go if you want more later.

## What these levels do

Measured per boat across the fleet at four zooms: hulls travel **~6 px** of lift and heel **±9–11°**. Sway is linear in the tunable, so at 0.5 px it now contributes **under a pixel** of lateral drift — lift and heel carry the motion.

The one thing worth flagging: at this `swell share` the slope response is **pinned at its clamp 35–47% of the time**. Rock therefore reads as a near-constant amplitude flicking between extremes, rather than a heel that breathes with the water. That may well be the look you were going for — it is what you were watching when you tuned it — but if you'd rather it tracked the sea proportionally, dropping `swell share` toward ~1.2 or raising the saturation point would do it. Say the word and I'll do the latter, which keeps the amplitude you picked.

## On zero hull lag

That was one of the three things that took the shiver out, so I checked. The other two — band-limiting the swell by hull length, and measuring heel across the hull rather than a fixed pixel count — are what fixed the *spatial* aliasing, and they hold with or without the filter. The lag was belt-and-braces.

What it also did was smooth the wave-field readback, which is fence-gated and can land a frame late. With zero lag that passes straight through, so in principle a tap ripple crossing a hull could step rather than glide. I could not reproduce it: this headless GPU runs at ~4 fps, where a smooth reference sine scores 0.3–0.4 on the same roughness metric, so 60 fps smoothness is below what I can measure here. Flagging it as a consequence of the design rather than an observed defect — if you ever catch a stutter as a ripple passes a boat, `hull lag` at 0.05–0.1 would absorb it without softening the character you tuned.

## Checks

`npm run build` clean. Levels verified at z=11 / 12.5 / 14 / 15.1.

author: kristofferremback
body: ## Problem [#1853](https://github.com/threahq/threa/pull/1853) added `threa-harnessd clear`, but the place a fresh start is actually wanted is the scratchpad — the operator watching a session drown in stale context types there, not in a terminal next to harnessd. There is no `/clear` session-control command, and the backend's canonical `SESSION_CONTROL_COMMAND_NAMES` allowlist means a runtime cannot just advertise one into existence. ## Solution `/clear [--force]` in both runtimes, riding `/reconnect`'s ack-then-detached-spawn pattern — the channel process lives inside the pane harnessd is about to kill, so the invocation completes first and a detached `threa-harnessd clear ` does the killing. - Backend: `clear` added to the canonical list and `listSessionControlCommandInfos()` (`--force` arg documented). For `pi-local` it routes to `active-scratchpad` like `reconnect` does — a busy Pi drops the `session-control` capability from its claims, which would make `/clear --force` unclaimable exactly when it's wanted. The Claude channel keeps `session-control` routing (it advertises it while busy). - `bot-runtime-client`: the detached-spawn body of `prepareHarnessReconnect` is extracted into a shared helper; new `prepareHarnessClear(runtimeSessionId)` spawns `clear` with its own `~/.threa/harnessd/clear.log`. Reconnect's exported signature and tests are untouched. - Claude channel (`channel-server.ts`): `case "clear"` mirrors `case "reconnect"` — busy refusal without `--force`, same delegation-quiescing and remote-session-changed rechecks in `afterAck`, advertised only with a linked root stream and an installed harnessd. - Pi (`threa-remote.ts`): `runClearCommand` mirrors `runReconnectCommand`, reusing the `reconnectPending` latch (both mean "harness restart imminent — stay busy, accept no claims"). Existing channels surface `/clear` after their next restart (capabilities are sent at hello). `docs/claude-channel-session-control.md` untouched: its command lists are an explicit v1 snapshot already omitting `reconnect`/`key`. ## Test plan - [x] bot-runtime-client 102, claude-code-remote 139, pi-remote 153, harness-daemon 369, backend `features/commands` 23 — all pass, 0 fail (new: clear spawn/one-shot/entrypoint cases; Claude advertise/usage/busy/afterAck-ordering; Pi routing/busy/lifecycle-recheck mirrors) - [ ] `/clear` typed in a real scratchpad — needs a restarted channel to advertise the command; verified indirectly by the harnessd-side E2E in [#1853](https://github.com/threahq/threa/pull/1853) plus the ack-ordering tests here --- 🤖 _PR by [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)_ --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled.

body:
Ships the new acquisition approach end-to-end.

## What goes live
- **`/map` — the Career Map capture.** One screen collecting stage (planning vs already-in), audience (child vs self), and up to three careers, then delivering the full package by email. Neutralized hero + tagline; reads a `?career=` prefill.
- **Unified capture.** The homepage and every career sampler now route into `/map` (via `StarterKitCta`), so every lead is captured the same way and lands in the matching stage-forked nurture — with a quiet direct-buy link preserved.
- **Career Value Guide rebrand + new pricing.** 1 career $49 / 3 $69 / Unlimited $99, plus the $299 Expert Meeting add-on. All customer-facing "profiles" language → Career Value Guide.
- **10% Founding Subscriber Discount.** Minted per-lead off `STRIPE_FOUNDING_COUPON_ID` (falls back to `FOUNDING10`); the old 20% coupon stays valid for existing holders.
- **Stage-forked nurture events** (`map_planning_requested` / `map_active_requested`) and the audience-aware package email.
- Model: pay once = this edition + the next, re-scored every six months; quarterly newsletter *Steering Through Change*.

## Post-merge steps (required)
1. Hit `/api/upload-samplers?key=<DOWNLOAD_SIGNING_SECRET>` to push the 8 new package PDFs (guide/overview × planning/active × parent/student) to Blob — otherwise package emails link to missing files.
2. Create the 10% coupon + `FOUNDING10` promo code in Stripe and set `STRIPE_FOUNDING_COUPON_ID` in Vercel (needed before purchases; does not block `/map` capture).
3. Repoint the Google ad Final URL to `/map` and verify the Lead conversion is tracked.

author: sushanthpaatnaik
body:
Addresses the review of the live site. Covers the two blockers plus the low-risk items; the larger UI features are deferred (listed at the bottom). ## 1. Page 4 white rectangle — root cause found The Origin portrait was the **only element in the entire document carrying both a CSS `filter` and a `mask-image`**. That combination forces the element onto its own compositing layer and blanks it to an opaque rectangle on some GPU/browser pairs. It doesn't reproduce under headless Chromium's software rendering, which is exactly why the QC pass missed it. Confirmed by audit: 8 elements use `mask-image`, 1 uses `filter`, and page 4 was the single overlap — matching the fact that page 4 was the only page you saw break. **Fix:** mask moved to a wrapper `
`, filter left on the ``. Neither element has both. Visually identical, no longer fragile. ## 2. Toolbar overlap The A4 page is centred, so `50% + 105mm` is its right edge — the toolbar now sits in the gutter beyond it and cannot cover artwork. Below 1320px there is no gutter, so it collapses to a floating round button (☰) and the controls only appear when opened. | viewport | overlaps page | toolbar | |---|---|---| | 1500 / 1400px | no | in the gutter | | 1200 / 900 / 420px | no | hidden behind ☰ until tapped | ## 4. Navigation feedback Jumps of more than one page are now instant rather than a multi-second smooth scroll, so the counter can't run ahead of what's on screen. Adjacent pages still animate, and `prefers-reduced-motion` is honoured. ## 6. Edit mode clarity Renamed **Enable editing → Edit text**, and switching it on shows a panel stating: what's editable (text only — images and layout are fixed), that changes are **unsaved and tab-local**, that they **do** appear in Print/PDF while the tab is open, and a Reset button. ## 10. Metadata Description, canonical URL, SVG favicon, `theme-color`, Open Graph and Twitter card tags with the cover portrait as preview image. ## 8. Export verified | check | result | |---|---| | Page count / size | 20 pages, all exactly 210 × 297 mm | | Toolbar excluded | no toolbar, counter, or edit-panel strings in the PDF | | Backgrounds preserved | every page corner renders black | | Page 4 white overlay | gone — 0.51% near-white pixels | | QR codes | 496 px for a 38 mm box (~330 dpi), modules and finder patterns crisp | | Page errors | 0 | ## Deferred Not included here, as each changes the reading experience enough to deserve its own review: **zoom controls (3)**, **thumbnail/section drawer (5)**, **mobile reading mode (7)**, **loading polish (9)**. Happy to take these next. One nit found while auditing: on pages 2 and 6 the artwork reaches the bottom corners slightly brighter than the reference, which fades to black there. Cosmetic, not a defect — left alone rather than churning the crops. --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01JTYJnCS7AuQkpsohEDCfes)_

author: fgarofalo56
body:
## The defect

`apps/loom-unity` pins `unitycatalog/unitycatalog:v0.5.0` and **prepends upstream's entire 419-class `unitycatalog-server:0.5.1` jar** to the server classpath so v0.5.1 classes shadow v0.5.0 ones. That exists to fix upstream **#1603** — `GET /api/2.1/unity-catalog/permissions/{securable}/{name}` returned HTTP 500 *"No authorization expression found."* when `server.authorization=enable`, which broke the Console Grants pane.

The task was to **narrow** that overlay so both #1603 stays fixed **and** the Iceberg `LIST /v1/catalogs/<wh>/namespaces` 500 clears — the latter documented (parity doc row I) as a regression the overlay introduced.

**The narrowing is done. The premise about Iceberg was false, and I could not fix that route.** Both results are measured below.

---

## What the jars actually contain

Extracted both released artifacts and hashed every entry (`unzip` + `sha256sum`, per-entry):

| | |
|---|---|
| Entries in each jar | **419**, identical entry lists |
| Entries whose **bytes differ** v0.5.0 → v0.5.1 | **5** |

```
DIFF ./META-INF/MANIFEST.MF                                        <- version strings
DIFF ./io/unitycatalog/server/auth/AuthorizeExpressions.class      <- adds GET_RESOURCE_AUTHORIZATION
DIFF ./io/unitycatalog/server/service/PermissionService.class      <- THE #1603 FIX
DIFF ./io/unitycatalog/server/service/PermissionService$1.class    <- synthetic sibling
DIFF ./io/unitycatalog/server/utils/VersionUtils.class             <- the string "0.5.0" -> "0.5.1"
total differing entries: 5
```

The whole #1603 fix is **one added annotation** (`javap -v`, present only in v0.5.1):

```
io.unitycatalog.server.auth.annotation.AuthorizeExpression(
  value="#principal != null"
)
```

Two supporting facts, both measured:

- The base image's `server/target/classes` (256 entries) is **byte-identical** to Maven Central's v0.5.0 jar, and the image ships that same jar at classpath position 259 (`sha256 2776…` on both). So the base really is the released v0.5.0.
- **`AuthorizedService`, `SchemaService`, `IcebergRestCatalogService`, `UnityAccessDecorator`, `ResultFilter` are byte-identical in v0.5.0 and v0.5.1.**

## Minimal set excluded — and why that set

Overlay is now **3 classes**, not 419:

| Class | Kept? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `PermissionService` | **kept** | carries the #1603 annotation |
| `PermissionService$1` | **kept** | its synthetic sibling; recompiled with it |
| `AuthorizeExpressions` | **kept** | supplies the constant the annotation names; additive only |
| `VersionUtils` | **excluded** | version string only. This image is v0.5.0 + a 3-class patch, not v0.5.1 — letting `/version` report 0.5.0 keeps it honest; the overlay is in the LABELs |
| the other 415 entries | **excluded** | **byte-identical to what they were shadowing** — excluding them cannot change resolved bytes |

Excluding 415 identical classes is provably behaviour-neutral, and it buys two real things:

1. **The overlay becomes falsifiable by inspection.** "The overlay broke X" can now be checked against a 3-item list. That matters here — one such claim was wrong for two days (below).
2. **It removes a live hazard on any base-tag bump.** A full-jar overlay would silently revert an *entire newer server module* to v0.5.1 classes. The build now digest-pins each extracted class **and hashes the base image's own copies**, failing with a specific message if the base drifts.

## The Iceberg premise was false

The parity doc's row I control compared **this image (overlay ON, authz ENABLED)** against **the bare upstream image (overlay OFF, authz DISABLED)** — two variables — and credited the difference to the overlay.

Measured one variable at a time, same harness, same warehouse:

| Variant | permissions GET (authz ON) | IRC namespaces (authz ON) | IRC namespaces (authz OFF) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** shipped, 419-class overlay | **200** | **500** | 200 |
| **B** overlay removed (pure v0.5.0) | **500** | **500** | 200 |
| **C** narrowed, 3-class overlay | **200** | **500** | 200 |

The overlay moves the permissions column *only*. The authorization flag moves the Iceberg column *only*. Row B is the control that never got run.

Root cause, from `javap -c` on `AuthorizedService.applyResponseFilter` — the body runs **only** `if (isAuthorizationEnabled())`, then requires the `RESULT_FILTER` attribute `UnityAccessDecorator` installs for `@ResponseAuthorizeFilter` routes. `IcebergRestCatalogService.listNamespaces` reaches `SchemaService.listSchemas` **in-process**, under the Iceberg route's context, where that attribute was never set. **Present in both releases.** With authorization off the body is skipped — the only reason the bare image looked healthy.

**So there is no narrowing that fixes it, and nothing to bump to:** `io.unitycatalog:unitycatalog-server` publishes **0.5.1 as its newest release** (`maven-metadata.xml`, 2026-08-10). A real fix means recompiling an upstream class, which ends this image's "packaging, not a fork" contract — **not done here**.

The wrong cause had propagated into the Dockerfile header, the **boot-time warning** (an error string asserting a cause nothing established — `deploy-integrity.md` R7), the harness comments and the parity doc. All four corrected.

## The control is fixed, not just the docs

`iceberg-e2e.sh` row I is replaced with single-variable controls:

- **I1** same image, authz **DISABLED** → 200 (moves the flag alone)
- **I2** same image, overlay **stripped off the classpath**, authz still **ENABLED** → 500 (moves the overlay alone — exonerates it)
- **I3** on that same stripped image, permissions GET → **500** — proves the strip really took, so **I2 tested what it claims to**

I2's control image is built by the harness, not quoted from a doc. (Note baked into it: `sed -i` truncates those classpath files to 0 bytes — mode 0550, busybox — which silently produced an unbootable "control" on my first attempt. It now read-modify-`cat >`s and asserts byte count, so an emptied classpath can never masquerade as a passing control.)

## Verified

Locally, in Docker, against the real image:

```
bash apps/loom-unity/tests/authz/authz-e2e.sh      12/12 PASS
bash apps/loom-unity/tests/authz/iceberg-e2e.sh    19/19 PASS
node --test apps/loom-unity/tests/entrypoint.test.mjs   36/36 PASS
```

`authz-e2e` **case 9 — permission GET = 200 with authorization ENABLED — passes on the 3-class overlay.** That is the receipt that the narrowing preserved the #1603 fix. Build-time: all four digest pins verified OK, base-drift assertion passed, 3-entry assertion passed, override FIRST on the classpath, `EntraPostgresAuthPlugin` still resolves.

## NOT verified

- **NOT verified end-to-end on any estate.** Local Docker only — **merged, not deployed** once this lands, and no roll of `loom-unity` is included here. Per the container-digest-pinning note, `loom-unity` has no automated roll.
- **No Gov run.** `cloud-parity.md` §4: this is a change to the image only, boundary-neutral by construction, but that is an argument, not a receipt.
- **No live browser/Console receipt.** The Console's Grants pane is the surface #1603 protects; not re-walked here.
- **The Iceberg LIST-namespaces route is still 500** and this PR does not fix it. It is announced on every boot and asserted by rows H/I1/I2/I3.

## Reproduce

```bash
# 1. the jar-level claim — 5 differing entries, none of them on the Iceberg path
curl -fsSL -O https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/io/unitycatalog/unitycatalog-server/0.5.0/unitycatalog-server-0.5.0.jar
curl -fsSL -O https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/io/unitycatalog/unitycatalog-server/0.5.1/unitycatalog-server-0.5.1.jar
mkdir x050 x051 && (cd x050 && unzip -qo ../unitycatalog-server-0.5.0.jar) && (cd x051 && unzip -qo ../unitycatalog-server-0.5.1.jar)
(cd x050 && find . -type f | sort) > l.txt
while read -r f; do [ "$(sha256sum "x050/$f" | cut -d' ' -f1)" != "$(sha256sum "x051/$f" | cut -d' ' -f1)" ] && echo "DIFF $f"; done < l.txt

# 2. the #160

**Description**
<sup>Explain the changes or enhancements you are proposing with this pull request.</sup>

The `player-count` keys added in a2ee4980c ("Best effort translations using Google Translate.") had three problems. That commit added only `player-count`, so the blast radius is limited to these five values.

**1. pt_BR was Breton, not Brazilian Portuguese**

| File | Before (Breton) | After (pt-BR) | `en_US` source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pt_BR/rom.json` | `C'hoarierien` | `Jogadores` | `Players` |
| `pt_BR/platform.json` | `Niver ar c'hoarierien` | `Número de jogadores` | `Player count` |

The new values reuse `pt_BR`'s existing terminology (`rom.json` already has `"players-n": "{n} jogadores"`).

**2. ja_JP had the two namespaces swapped**

`rom.json` carried プレイヤー数 ("player count") and `platform.json` carried プレイヤー ("players") — backwards relative to `en_US`. Swapped to match.

**3. tr_TR used "player count" for both**

`rom.json` said `Oyuncu sayısı` ("player count") where `en_US` says "Players"; now `Oyuncular`. `platform.json` correctly keeps `Oyuncu sayısı`.

**Cross-locale contamination sweep**

I swept every locale directory for further Breton from the same source, checking `c'h`, word-internal `zh`, `ñ` outside `es_ES`, initial `gw-`/`kw-`, and a lexicon of common Breton words (`niver`, `ouzhpennañ`, `dibarzhioù`, `enrollañ`, `teuliad`, `titour`, `gwir`, `kentañ`, `nemet`). **No other Breton strings exist in any locale.** The only `gw`/`kw` hit was `pl_PL`'s legitimate `kwadratowe`; all `ñ` occurrences are genuine Spanish in `es_ES`.

**Verification**

```
python3 frontend/src/locales/check_i18n_locales.py   # ✅ All translations are complete!
python3 frontend/src/locales/check_i18n_sorted.py    # ✅ All locale files are sorted alphabetically!
```

`trunk` (incl. Prettier) passes on all changed files.

**AI-assistance disclosure**
<sup>Per `CONTRIBUTING.md`.</sup>

This PR was written with AI assistance (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5). The AI performed the full change: identifying the mistranslated values, producing the replacements, running the cross-locale contamination sweep, and running the i18n validators and linter. All of it was reviewed by me before submission.

**Related**

See #4185, which translates 159 other `pt_BR` values that were left as raw English.

**Checklist**
<sup>Please check all that apply.</sup>

- [x] I've tested the changes locally
- [ ] I've updated relevant comments
- [ ] I've assigned reviewers for this PR
- [ ] I've added unit tests that cover the changes

<sup>No comments needed (locale data only). No unit tests added: the repo's i18n gate is `check_i18n_locales.py` / `check_i18n_sorted.py`, which both pass, and translation-value correctness isn't machine-assertable.</sup>

body:
The plugins overview page states that only `@varlock`-scoped plugins are supported and that third-party plugins are planned for the future. That contradicts the plugins guide, which documents authoring third-party plugins and loading them from npm or a local path today, with a one-time confirmation prompt for non-`@varlock` packages.

Since the overview is the page linked from the docs nav, anyone evaluating whether they can write a plugin lands on the inaccurate version first.

Updated the sentence to describe what actually works, and narrowed the "not yet supported" claim to the sources that genuinely aren't wired up (git, http, jsr).

author: ywatanabe1989
body:
## Why now

`secrets: inherit` forwards **every** secret this repo holds into a job that **any GitHub account can start by typing an issue comment** — `issue_comment` and `pull_request_target` are unauthenticated triggers on a public repo, and the fork-PR approval gate does not cover them by design.

Today that is harmless: this repo holds **zero** secrets (measured 2026-08-11 — `gh secret list` empty, and the org has no org-level secrets either).

**That is exactly why this lands now.** The CLA check fails because the callee requires `GH_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN` and there is none to inherit, so the obvious next move is to add the token — and adding it while `inherit` was still here would have converted a broken check into a live exposure **in one step, with nothing in the diff to show it.** The dangerous line is the one that would not have changed. Sequencing is the whole control.

## The three changes, each verified against the pinned SHA

| | change | verified |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | pin `399f19be` (main@2026-07-23) → `a29fe1bf` (main@2026-08-05) | both facilities below exist at the new SHA, neither at the old |
| 2 | `secrets: inherit` → `GH_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN` named | callee declares it `required: true` at the new pin |
| 3 | `runs_on: '["ubuntu-latest"]'` | `runs_on` input exists at the new pin; string decodes to `["ubuntu-latest"]` |

**On the pin.** Pinning protects against surprise upstream change; it equally **withholds upstream fixes**, and that cost comes due silently. The callee's own commit says so: *"Note for consumers that SHA-PIN this repo: parameterizing HEAD does not reach you … Bump the pin as part of your own migration."*

**On the runner.** The header that stood in this file called the ephemeral-runner remedy *"owned org-side and blocked on an operator decision."* The `runs_on` input makes it a per-repo knob — so that sentence had quietly become **a standing excuse for something I could fix myself.** The org default pool is persistent and shares a `$HOME` holding the live fleet credential; a hosted VM is destroyed after the run. Matches sac's own CLA job, and consistent with the operator's 2026-08-05 direction (hosted runners are free on public repos and merely slower — irrelevant for a check that greps a JSON file).

Passed as a **JSON array string** because the callee feeds it to `fromJSON`. A YAML list there does not error — it queues the job **forever**, which in the run list is indistinguishable from "still waiting".

## What this does NOT do

**The CLA check stays red.** `GH_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN` still does not exist in this repo, so the callee's `required: true` keeps failing until the PAT holder adds it. This PR makes adding it *safe*. Two jobs; only one is mine.

Note this PR's own CLA leg runs the **base branch's** workflow (`pull_request_target`), so it does not exercise the change either way.

## Credit and one correction

scitex-db found the root cause and corrected their own earlier "unsigned CLA" reading — [#56](https://github.com/scitex-ai/scitex-storage/pull/56) (free-space alarm, 7 green legs) sat two days behind a check that was never going to pass. Their tell was the right one: `output.title`/`output.summary` were `null`, and silence means it **errored rather than judged**.

One correction, verified before acting: their write-up said the shared workflow declares the secret `required: true`. That is true of `@main` and **not** of the SHA this repo pinned — which is why "just name the secret" could not have applied here as written. Hence change (1) before change (2).

author: thomfilg
body:
Mirrors [future-pay#845](https://github.com/12-apps/future-pay/pull/845) into this repo's copy of `pr-stacking-rules.md`. The stacking rule itself is **unchanged** — this adds the diagnostic that keeps it from being "corrected" away by a plausible misreading.

## The misreading, so it isn't repeated

The memory says an ad-hoc `--base` PR gets zero checks in future-pay. That is measured and correct. But while working the auth port I concluded the opposite: GitHub had refused the legacy merge (403), the asynchronous merge (403), and a base retarget (422), which read as *these PRs really are stacks, so the rule is bunk*.

Those refusals were **the agent session's proxy**, not GitHub. It serves only a pinned set of GitHub operations and answers everything else with its own 403 — the same status code GitHub uses, distinguishable only by the body:

| | `documentation_url` |
|---|---|
| session proxy | `docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/github-actions` |
| GitHub | `docs.github.com/rest/…` |

## Why the question can't be settled the direct way

`PullRequest.stack` is exposed **only** in GraphQL, and GraphQL is refused wholesale here — `viewer { login }` included. Introspection is worse than a refusal: it returns a well-formed response with **zero fields**, so a filter for a `stack` field comes back empty and reads exactly like *the field does not exist*.

So stack membership is not observable from an agent session. The memory now says to use the **check-run count** as the evidence instead, and not to infer anything from a failed call.

Docs-only.

author: chrislusf
body:
Fixes #10688.

Two ways to reclaim volume slots stuck around 50% usage:

`fs.mergeVolumes -fromVolumeId=112 -toVolumeId=111,107` accepts a comma-separated target list now. Each chunk is routed to the target with the most remaining capacity, so a volume that fits into no single target can still be cleared. A single target, or no explicit ids, behaves as before. Without `-fromVolumeId`, the list restricts the heuristic planner's target candidates.

`volume.mark -readonlyCanDelete` (with `-node`/`-volumeId` or `-collection`) marks a volume so new writes are rejected but deletes still land. A volume holding expiring data then drains over time until it can be vacuumed away or merged into other volumes. The state persists to `.vif` and survives restarts; the master sees the volume as read-only so it assigns no new writes; `-writable` clears it. On the wire this is a new `can_delete` field on `VolumeMarkReadonlyRequest`, mirrored in the Rust volume server.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added a read-only mode that blocks new writes while allowing deletes.
  * Added `-readonlyCanDelete` support with state preserved across restarts.
  * Extended volume merging to support multiple targets, capacity-aware distribution, and validation.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved index handling when switching read-only volumes to delete-enabled or writable states.
  * Broken volumes marked read-only during scrubbing no longer allow deletes.
  * Merge operations now report skipped chunks when no target has sufficient capacity.

author: christian-byrne
body:
The README lists `**PyTorch**: ≥2.5.0`, but as of 0.2.28 two things run at import time that need 2.7.0:

- **`backends/eager/na.py:163`** registers `comfy_kitchen::na3d` with PEP 585 annotations (`kernel_size: list[int]`, `is_causal: list[bool]`). `torch.library.infer_schema` only accepts builtin generics from 2.7.0 — `derived_types` gained the `GenericAlias(list, ...)` entries in v2.7.0 and they are absent in v2.6.0. On 2.5/2.6 the decorator raises `ValueError` at import.
- **`backends/eager/__init__.py:542`** references `torch.float8_e8m0fnu` inside `_build_constraints()`, which is called at module scope (line 586). That dtype landed in 2.7.0 (`c10/core/ScalarType.h`: 0 occurrences at v2.6.0, 6 at v2.7.0).

Both blow up on `import comfy_kitchen` itself rather than at first use, so the package is unusable below 2.7.0 regardless of backend or device — including CPU-only setups that never touch a kernel.

Verified on clean venvs:

| torch | `import comfy_kitchen` (0.2.28) |
|---|---|
| 2.6.0 | `ValueError: infer_schema(func): Parameter kernel_size has unsupported type list[int]` |
| 2.7.0+cpu | OK — eager backend available |

Docs-only change; no code or behavior is affected. Assumes the higher floor is intended, so this just makes the README match.

Possible follow-ups, out of scope here: `pyproject.toml` has `dependencies = []`, so nothing enforces the floor at install time, and the repo has no CI job that imports the package at the documented minimum.

author: markbackman
body: tl;dr In introducing auto-registered functions, we regressed the async tool cancellation logic. This PR restores it by: 1. Simplifying the enablement logic. Previously, there was a bunch of lifecycle logic to determine when to add the tool. Now, it simply adds the tool and system instruction if `enable_async_tool_cancellation` is set to True (note: it's False by default. 2. Modify the prompt so that all models have a higher success rate Add an eval to make this easier to test. ## Summary - `enable_async_tool_cancellation=True` had no effect for bots that declare their tools through an `LLMContext` — which is every async example in the repo. Setup was gated on an async handler already being registered, but handlers advertised through the context register on the first context frame, which arrives after `start()`. The built-in `cancel_async_tool_call` was never advertised, so no bot could cancel a stale async call. The flag is now the whole condition. - Removed the dynamic tracking that went with the gate (`_has_async_tools()` and the teardown path). Keeping teardown would let a bot that momentarily advertises no async tools disable cancellation permanently — the same ordering problem in a different form. - The cancellation instructions now say that the call is the only thing that stops the pending work. Without that, a model can reply "I'll skip the weather", never emit the call, and then contradict itself when the result lands seconds later. - Added an eval scenario for the whole path and wired it to the four cascade async bots. Not breaking. One behavior change worth knowing: a service constructed with the flag set but no async tools registered now carries the built-in tool and its instructions, where before it carried neither. The flag defaults to `False`, so this only affects callers who opted in. ## Testing Unit tests: ```sh uv run pytest tests/test_llm_service.py # 25 passed ``` Two of the three new tests in `TestAsyncToolCancellationSetup` fail against the unfixed service and pass against the fixed one. Behavioral eval: ```sh cd scripts/release-evals ./run.sh -p function-calling.*async -s weather_function_call_async_cancelled_audio -a ``` Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI Responses pass consistently. `openai-async` is the outlier: it failed every run before the instruction change and passes reliably after, but it remains the most variable of the four. The Chat Completions API effectively resolves an assistant turn to either content or tool calls, so a turn that both dismisses a pending lookup and asks a new question is the hardest case — the same model on the Responses API, which emits a list of output items, never had trouble.

author: shaunshamilton
mike-thompson-day8
body:
Both gaps the merged-PR audit of #7829 found on **rf2-ka4d**, in the order that
matters: the false SILENCE first, because it is the one nothing surfaces.

Everything below was measured at the CI pin — `clj-kondo 2026.04.15`, via the
artefact's `:clj-kondo` alias. The npm binary on this host is 2025.10.23 and was
kept off `PATH` for every run in this PR, the gate's own runs included, because
a pass from a mismatched version proves nothing either way.

---

## Reproduced first, both of them, before either fix

### GAP 2 — a false silence #7829 introduced

`fn-tail-locals` fed method lists to `fn-locals`, which reads the leading token
as a named-`fn` self binding. A `reify` / `extend` method's name is **not**
lexical — no expansion of the four spec forms puts it in scope — so the invented
binding silenced the whole spec form, self-call and all.

```clojure
(h/defview toString [_]
  [:div (str (reify Object (toString [_] (str (toString {})))))])
```

```
linting took 484ms, errors: 0, warnings: 0        <- exit 0
```

That is a genuine direct self-call reported as nothing at all. The control
isolates the cause exactly — the identical call, in a method named `show`
instead:

```clojure
(h/defview toString [_]
  [:div (str (reify Shows (show [_] (str (toString {})))))])
```

```
probe.cljs:8:42: error: `toString` is a view, so it is a hiccup HEAD rather than a function…
linting took 379ms, errors: 1, warnings: 0        <- exit 3
```

So the method's **name** was the whole difference. This matters more than an
extra false ERROR because silence is the check's only permitted failure *by
design*: a wrong silence prints nothing, fails no build, and is invisible until
somebody re-reads the grammar. It was introduced by a repair, which is why the
audit caught it and no gate did.

### GAP 1 — a false ERROR still standing

`(areduce a idx ret init expr)` binds **both** `idx` and `ret` over `expr` —
macroexpansion puts them in a `loop` — and the accumulator is an ordinary value
that may perfectly well be a function.

```
probe.cljs:7:47:  error: `folded` is a view…      (areduce's accumulator)
probe.cljs:11:44: error: `step` is a view…        (areduce's index)
probe.cljs:15:36: error: `mapped` is a view…      (amap's accumulator)
probe.cljs:19:43: error: `cursor` is a view…      (amap's index)
linting took 451ms, errors: 4, warnings: 1        <- exit 3
```

`amap` is the same grammar one argument shorter, reproduced identically, and is
in this PR for the reason #7829 added `extend-protocol`: its two names sit at
the **same positions**, so one arm reads both forms and naming only `areduce`
would have been arbitrary rather than bounded. A destructured accumulator
reproduces too — the `loop` accepts one and clj-kondo's own analysis follows it.

Both gaps are then committed as fixtures in `4c9e533364`, **red on purpose**:
four ERRORs on correct code in the negative half, and two positive rows
reporting nothing.

---

## The repair, and what it is bounded to

Three grammar facts, and no more. No scope engine, no `api/resolve` (PR #7804
established by probe that it answers nil for the cases that matter and never
sees locals), no whole-program analysis; the small syntax-local walker and the
conservative whole-form silencing are untouched.

1. **A method's name is not a binding.** The reading is split. `fn-locals` keeps
   the optional self name, because a `letfn` fnspec's name *is* a local —
   `letfn` expands each spec to `(fn f …)`. `method-locals` reads the parameters
   of every arity and nothing else. `params-locals` is now the one place either
   finds an arity, so the two cannot drift apart about what an arity is.

2. **A method's name is not a call either** — and this one is the trap the first
   repair sets. A method name sits in head position of a list, exactly where a
   callee sits, and it can no longer be quietened by binding it, so
   `call-positions` skips it. The head and the **first argument** are kept:
   `specify!` writes an ordinary expression there, and a view called in it is a
   real self-call (`self-calling-specify-target`).

3. **The array pair joins the roster.** One arm, both forms, reading binding
   TARGETS rather than symbols.

Every method-parameter negative #7829 landed is preserved unchanged — `boxed`,
`second-group`, `marked`, `extended`, `spread-out` all bind the view's name as a
method *parameter*, which `method-locals` still reads.

---

## Rows added, and the narrowing each one catches

Derived from each form's grammar, then filtered by the harder question #7818
made the standard: *what single narrowing of the implementation would let this
row pass while the rule is broken?* A row with no such narrowing is decoration.
Gap 2 is itself the proof — #7829's method-parameter rows all passed while the
method-**head** rule was wrong, because none of them drove a method whose *name*
matched the view.

| half | row | binds / calls in | reds under |
|---|---|---|---|
| neg | `folded` | `areduce`'s **accumulator**, index named `i` | an arm reading the index position alone |
| neg | `step` | `areduce`'s **index**, accumulator named `total` | an arm reading the accumulator position alone |
| neg | `pair` | `areduce`'s accumulator **destructured** | an arm reading a symbol rather than a binding TARGET |
| neg | `slot` | `amap`'s accumulator | an arm naming `areduce` alone |
| neg | `toString` | a **method named like the view**, calling nothing | a walk that reads a method's head as a call (a fresh false ERROR) |
| neg | `valueOf` | the same, in `extend-type` | the same, past a type token |
| pos | `self-call-in-areduce` | a genuine self-call inside `areduce` | an arm that silences the whole form instead of binding two names |
| pos | `self-call-in-amap` | the same, inside `amap` | the same |
| pos | `toString` | a genuine self-call **inside a method named like the view** | reading the method HEAD as a self binding — the #7829 defect |
| pos | `valueOf` | the same, in `extend-type` | the same, past a type token |

The two `toString` / `valueOf` pairs are deliberately one negative and one
positive each: the negative pins that a method DEFINITION is not a call, the
positive pins that the method's name does not bind. A repair that got either
half alone would pass one row and red the other.

### Shapes NOT driven, and why — the valuable half

* **`amap`'s index, and a destructured `amap` accumulator.** Both forms reach
  the same expression through one arm, so the position and destructuring
  narrowings are already pinned by `step` and `pair`. A row per form would
  re-witness the identical code path; `slot` pins the only thing `amap` adds,
  which is membership.
* **`areduce`'s `a` and `init` positions.** Neither binds anything — `a` is
  evaluated before the loop and `init` is an ordinary expression in the loop's
  binding vector — so there is no local to protect.
* **A same-name method in `specify!` or `extend-protocol`.** All four spec forms
  reach `method-locals` through a **single** call site and `call-positions`
  through a single `spec-forms` membership test, so a row per form witnesses one
  narrowing four times. `reify` and `extend-type` are driven instead, which are
  the two shapes that differ in what precedes the method.
* **A multi-arity METHOD** (`(-invoke ([this] …) ([this a] …))`). `method-locals`
  reads arities through `params-locals`, shared with `fn-locals`, and both ends
  of that reading are already pinned — `first-arity` and `zero-arity` on the
  `letfn` side, `run-any` and `run-last` on `defmethod`'s. A fifth pair would
  witness `params-locals` again, not the method reading.
* **A non-method LIST in a spec position** — `(extend-protocol P (compute-type)

body:
## Why

T3tris Robinhood vaults were discovered only as generic ERC-4626 leads because the protocol classifier restricted its distinguishing `getGrossTVL` probe to Arbitrum. This missed Morini entirely and left Kingfisher with incorrect generic metadata. T3tris async vaults also made `maxDeposit=0` look like a public capacity cap even when protocol deposits were enabled.

## Lessons learnt

A discovery lead can exist without a protocol adapter when its classifier probe is omitted for a deployed chain. ERC-4626 `maxDeposit` is not a universal public-deposit status signal for asynchronous vaults; use a protocol-native admission state where available.

## Summary

- Enable T3tris classification on Robinhood, add its reviewed vaults to the targeted repair snapshot, and provide strict chain/address migration filters.
- Record T3tris native deposit availability both historically and in current scan metadata, while keeping unknown generic state tri-state.

body:
<!-- senpai-assignment:v1 {"assignment_id":"maple-r109-b-router-hybrid-selector","base_ref":"codex/mlxfast-maple-20260804-advisor","base_sha":"93688bfa1c6e658ef4394c07a9463c79b4af3130","head_ref":"maple-nezuko/r109-router-hybrid-selector","head_sha":"ed74b1e5253a33494b276e898b2ecb6ebea5d872","repo":"morganmcg1/mlxfast-challenge_senpai","revision_id":"r109-b-rev3","schema_version":1,"student":"maple-nezuko"} -->

## Why you

Your #657 A/A null was the right result and it gave the campaign its power table (paired sd 18.222 us/token; 0.40% resolves in 3 blocks, 0.25% in 4-5, ~198 s/run; blocking bought no variance reduction). You proved the instrument is unbiased. Now I want you to use it on the single highest-claimed external lead we have.

## The situation, honestly stated

tanjiro's #663 retired the dispatch-count axis. fern's #664 retired the byte axis. edward's #629 found only 0.33% of removable issue in attention. Every cheap lever is gone. What is left is **in-kernel algorithmic work reduction**, and the router selector is the most algorithmically over-built kernel on the decode path.

## What the router actually does today, verified at HEAD `1a6761bf`

All line numbers in `Sources/MLXFastModel/LagunaRuntimeModel.swift` (LRM). The default decode top-8-of-256 selection is the **active-64 block tournament**: `laguna_prefill_router_tournament_ordinal_active64_v2` (declared LRM:10130-10137, source `lagunaPrefillRouterTournamentOrdinalKernelSource` LRM:9977-10110), reached from `LagunaRuntimeMoEGate` LRM:10277-10298 -> `lagunaDecodeRouterTop8` LRM:9597-9622 -> LRM:9602-9608. All three gating env flags default ON (`DARKBLOOM_ROUTER_ORDINAL` LRM:9478-9479, `..._SCORE_TABLE` LRM:9485-9486, `DARKBLOOM_DECODE_ROUTER_TOURNAMENT` LRM:9531-9532), so this is genuinely the shipped path.

Its structure:

1. **Stage 1** - per-32 bitonic inside each simdgroup, LRM:10014-10030. All `simd_shuffle_xor`, **no barriers**. This part is good.
2. **Block harvest** to 64 finalists, LRM:10032-10043 (`block = lane >> 5`, 8 per block x 8 blocks).
3. **Stage 2** over those 64 candidates, LRM:10050-10069, guarded by `if (lane < 64)`.
4. **The expensive part**: the single cross-simdgroup `sequence 64` exchange plus tail, **LRM:10071-10103**.

Cost structure, and this is the point:

- Dispatch geometry is `grid: (256, rows, 1)`, `threadGroup: (256, 1, 1)` (LRM:10182-10186) = **256 threads = 8 SIMD groups**.
- **Only lanes 0-63 (2 of 8 simdgroups) are live for the entire finalist sort**, yet **all 256 threads must reach both `threadgroup_barrier`s** (LRM:10044 and LRM:10077). Six simdgroups idle at a barrier twice per layer, 40 layers per decode step.
- Threadgroup scratch is **2048 B**: `xchg_ordinals[64]`, `xchg_indices[64]`, `candidate_ordinals[64]`, `candidate_indices[64]` (4 x 256 B) plus `original_scores[256]` (1024 B), LRM:10001-10005.

Exactness is defined by `lagunaDecodeRouterOrdinalHeader` LRM:9417-9439: a monotone float->uint ordinal with **tie-break by index**. That is your correctness contract.

## Hypothesis

The stage-2 cross-simdgroup exchange (LRM:10071-10103), its second barrier (LRM:10077) and its 1024 B of exchange scratch can be replaced by a **local sorting network plus a single 32-lane merge**, producing byte-identical `router_indices` and `weights`, and this is worth >= 0.4% of normalized score.

**Concrete construction to reconstruct** (external receipts `aadbda2` / `1a7a0ea`, author claims 1.8-2.0% local, unverified by us):

- Slots 0-4 of the Top-8 are taken by an **accepted rescan** rather than by sorting.
- Slots 5-7 come from a **19-comparator local sorting network** followed by a **32-lane merge**.
- The whole result is carried in **one shared `uint2 top8_pairs[8]` (64 bytes)** whose lifetime ends before QMV input storage, i.e. it does not extend threadgroup pressure into the matmul.
- Exact ordering and tie behaviour preserved.

That replaces 2048 B of scratch with 64 B and removes a barrier that 192 idle threads currently wait on.

Treat the 1.8-2.0% claim as a **prior, not a fact**. It is an outside number on an outside tree. Your job is to build it here and measure it here.

## Order of work

**Stage 0 - the cheap falsifier first, post by 2026-08-10T23:30Z.** Before writing the selector, price the ceiling. Dispatch the *existing* tournament kernel with the stage-2 body stubbed to a constant (deliberately WRONG output, timing probe only, never a candidate) and measure the paired delta. That gives you the **maximum** this arm can ever pay. If the entire stage-2 region prices below 0.15% of normalized score, **stop and write `N-ROUTER-STAGE2-CHEAP`** - you will have saved 10 hours and killed the strongest-sounding external claim in the campaign with one probe. That is a first-class result and I will treat it as one.

**Stage 1 - build it.** Add the hybrid selector as a **new, distinctly-named pipeline** (e.g. `laguna_decode_router_hybrid_t5_v1`). Do not rename or reuse the existing pipeline name: sharing a pipeline name poisons the A/B cache and has burned this campaign before. Keep the legacy kernels compiled as they are.

**Stage 2 - prove bit-exactness before you time anything.** Not "max_abs_diff is small" - that check does not mean what people think it means. Dump `router_indices` and `weights` for every layer and every token of a fixed 512+128 prompt, on base and on candidate, and require **exact equality of all 40 x 640 x 8 index entries and all weight bits**. Ties are the danger: the ordinal tie-break is by index (LRM:9417-9439) and a local sorting network can silently reorder equal ordinals. Construct an adversarial case with deliberate ordinal ties and show it still matches.

**Stage 3 - measure.** Contemporaneous paired ABBA, >= 8 pairs, preregistered revert, `FERN_DEFEAT_SLOTS=64`, headline the residency-defeated number. Report on `ns = (0.013890/decode_s_per_tok)^0.75 * (0.0003845/prefill_s_per_tok)^0.25`.

## Note on geometry - important

You may be tempted to shrink the threadgroup from 256 to 64 threads since 192 are idle in stage 2. **Do not**, as a headline arm. Stage 1 needs all 256 lanes (one expert per lane), and threadgroup geometry does not transfer M4 -> M5: PR #7 measured +7.32% on M4 and ~0% on M5. Geometry changes are the classic way to produce a beautiful M4 number that evaporates on the ranked host. Keep `threadGroup (256,1,1)` and the grid identical. Change the *algorithm*, not the shape.

## Deconfliction - five arms are editing LRM concurrently

| Student | Owns these LRM regions |
|---|---|
| **you (nezuko)** | **LRM:9977-10110 (tournament kernel source), LRM:10130-10190 (declaration + dispatch)** |
| tanjiro | LRM:7850-7930, 8044-8054 (routed gate/up prologue - he is removing a *redundant second* top-8 extraction that reads `router_keys`) |
| frieren | LRM:735-800, 11477-11487, 11694-11712 |
| edward | LRM:1507-1975 |
| alphonse | LRM:2027-2460 |

**You and tanjiro must coordinate directly in your PRs.** He is making the routed gate/up kernel consume the `inds` your kernel produces instead of re-deriving them. If your selector changes the *layout* or *timing* of `router_indices`, tell him immediately. Neither of you may change the `inds`/`weights` contract without the other agreeing in writing.

Byte allowance: **20 KB**. `LagunaRuntimeModel.swift` is at 384,245 B of a 524,288 B HARD ABORT cap; 140,043 B is shared across five arms. Run `senpai/check-editable-budget.sh 1bc1c8954147c9e322aad1f3b80bd9fa3c0888d7` before every push.

body:
A sector page showed two or three names because `market.instruments` is a hand-authored
35-row table. It now reads `market.sector_constituents` — what the sector SPDR actually
holds, per its SEC N-PORT filing. **514 constituents across 11 sectors.**

Ranked by **fund weight**, not market cap: market cap needs a paid provider (FMP gates it
per symbol), weight is a fact from a filing, and in a cap-weighted fund the two orderings
nearly agree.

## Three things the screenshot caught that types did not

**A tickerless row promised a page that cannot exist.** Most non-US listings have no US
symbol, and those rows rendered with a chevron and a tap that did nothing. `DrillItem.disabled`
makes them plain content. Rows are keyed by `security_id` (several tickerless rows would
collide on an empty key), so the tap resolves the symbol back instead of routing to
`/stock/undefined`.

**The sub-sector chips fell back to authored slugs.** Fund holdings carry no industry, so
the existing fallback quietly restored `software-saas` and friends — the fake taxonomy the
live sub-sectors were introduced to replace. Three invented chips are worse than none, so
they are hidden.

**The country filter matched a display name.** Now `country_iso2` — the server stores the
code, and a name would have to match a provider's spelling exactly.

## Verified

`npm run check`, `expo export`, and smoke-market's **64 checks** — including a tickerless row
rendering by name, no row reading `undefined ·`, the fund weight, a constituent with no
performance row showing no number, and the country drill-down issuing `country_iso2=eq.DE`.

author: ccarrebdl
body:
## What does this PR do?

This PR fixes two correctness gaps in the persistent recording index:

1. Makes current and legacy recording roots come from one canonical registry.
2. Refreshes existing rows when their path, size, MP4 mtime, or sidecar mtime changes.

## Why is this change needed?

Warmup indexed four legacy locations, but reconcile scanned only current roots and deleted those legacy rows as missing. Playback and thumbnail lookup covered only part of the warmup set, while the UI fallback maintained another independent list.

Reconcile also snapshotted only filenames. Existing rows were never reparsed after a file moved between roots or a JSON sidecar was created, changed, or deleted, so stale paths, place data, actor metadata, and storage tags could persist indefinitely.

## Commit structure

- `fix(recordings): unify current and legacy storage roots`
- `fix(recordings): refresh changed index rows`

## Root contract

- Active root remains first, followed by internal, SD, USB, then legacy roots.
- Flat legacy recordings, legacy `recordings`, `sentry_events`, and `proximity_events` are included.
- Roots are deduplicated by absolute path.
- Warmup, reconcile, watcher, retention, playback, delete, thumbnail, and direct fallback inherit the same lists.

## Freshness contract

- Unchanged rows perform fingerprint checks but skip JSON parsing.
- New and changed rows use the existing upsert path.
- Path moves, size/mtime changes, and sidecar create/update/delete are healed.
- Unreadable sidecars converge at the same zero-mtime state used by the parser.
- Duplicate mirrored names preserve active-first priority.

## How to test

```bash
./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest --tests com.overdrive.app.storage.RecordingDirectoryRegistryTest
./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest --tests com.overdrive.app.server.RecordingRootParityTest
./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest --tests com.overdrive.app.server.RecordingFileFingerprintTest
./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest --tests com.overdrive.app.server.RecordingsReconcileFreshnessTest
./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest
```

All commands pass locally with the API 36 Android SDK.

## Risk

Moderate. Root ownership and reconcile behavior change, but both are isolated and covered by focused tests. Filesystem authority remains unchanged.

## Merge note

PR #216 also modifies `RecordingsIndex` scheduling. The changes are semantically compatible; whichever PR merges second should be rebased to resolve the localized method conflict.

author: avihaishai
body:
Commissioned as a **regeneration** of the win32 captures presumed staled by #317. I ran the
compare first, and it changed the outcome.

## Headline: nothing was stale. No PNG is touched in this PR.

Measured on a worktree off current `main` (`21df713`, which includes #316, #317 and #318),
with `PW_VISUAL_SEED=1`, an isolated `PW_DB_PATH`, and a pinned port:

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `e2e/visual.spec.ts` (win32) | **66 passed / 0 failed** |
| `e2e/visual-baseline-thumbnails.spec.ts` (win32) | **18 passed / 0 failed** |
| `git status --porcelain e2e/__screenshots__` | **empty after every run** |
| corpus | **162 tracked = 162 on disk**; win32 `66 + 15` unchanged |

**Changed baselines: none. Unexpected diffs: none.** `--update-snapshots` was never passed.

## I was wrong, and here is the mechanism

In my #315 review I flagged that #317 "plausibly" staled the `workout-plan-{tablet,mobile}`
captures. **That prediction is disproven**, and the reason is worth keeping:

#317 is a genuine rendering fix —
`templates/workout_plan.html` `style="display: none"` → `hidden`, plus
`#superset-actions .btn[hidden] { display: none !important; }` so the Unlink button
actually hides. But the **parent** `#superset-actions` container is *itself*
`display: none` in the rest state (`templates/workout_plan.html:316`). So the fix changes
visibility **inside an already-hidden container**, and only manifests once a user selects
exercises.

**The visual suites capture rest state**, so interaction-state fixes are pixel-invisible to
them.

Had I regenerated on the theory that "a rendering change landed, so pixels must have
moved", I would have rewritten **81 reviewed PNGs for no pixel reason** — and spent an
owner by-eye review to do it. Both docs now carry the rule that follows: **compare first.**

## What this PR actually changes — docs only, 2 files

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `docs/MASTER_HANDOVER.md` | Pins the 66/18 figures to **`21df713`** and labels them a *measurement, not a standing property*. Adds the silent-stale caveat. Records the #317 null result and its mechanism. |
| `docs/visual_determinism/PLANNING.md` §8.7 | The same pin and caveat on the twin, which carried the identical unpinned claim. |

The two additions the brief asked for:

1. **Pinned.** "Measured at `21df713`" replaces the unpinned *"on a branch based on current
   `main`"* that #315 shipped.
2. **Silent-stale noted explicitly.** Neither win32 suite runs in required CI, so a CSS or
   template change can invalidate these baselines **with nothing going red anywhere** —
   which is exactly how the condition #304 documented arose. Any commit later than the pin
   is *unmeasured* until the two suites are re-run locally.

The converse is stated too, because it is the error I nearly made: "a CSS/template change
landed, therefore the corpus is stale" is a hypothesis, not a finding.

## Gates

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `e2e/visual.spec.ts` + `visual-baseline-thumbnails.spec.ts` (win32, seeded) | **66 + 18 passed**, 0 written |
| Full `pytest tests/` | **2630 passed, 2 skipped** — covers the manifest-digest contract, which is full-pytest-only |
| Visual / baseline / a11y contracts | **65 passed** |
| `generate_test_inventory.py --check` | **up to date** — 2310 pytest, 610 / 33 playwright |
| Corpus integrity | 162 = 162; win32 66 + 15 |
| Diff scope | 2 files, both `.md`; **no** PNG, no code, no workflow |

Isolated scratch DB throughout (`PW_DB_PATH` under gitignored `artifacts/`); `data/database.db`
untouched.

## Deliberately not done

Not started, per instruction: the Linux ledger, the two WP4.0 rows, and the
`visual-windows` CI job. The last remains the only structural fix for the silent-stale
window this PR documents — still a separate owner decision.

## One incidental note

`git push` reported the remote as `AvihaiShai/Hypertrophy-Toolbox-v3`; the account appears
to have been renamed (consistent with #318's vanity-URL change). GitHub is redirecting, so
nothing here depends on it — flagging only in case any pinned URL elsewhere needs updating.

Refs #304, #309, #315, #317.

| Flag | Errors |
|---|---|
| `noImplicitAny` | 0 |
| `strictBindCallApply` | 0 |
| `strictPropertyInitialization` | 0 |
| `noImplicitThis` | 0 |
| `useUnknownInCatchVariables` | 0 |
| `alwaysStrict` | 0 |
| `strictFunctionTypes` | **1** |
| **full `strict: true`** | **1** |

The refactoring of the last weeks (#238, #259, #261–#265) moved most of the untyped surface into hooks and pure modules written strict-clean, so what was a campaign when this issue was filed is now a config change plus one fix.

### The one error is real

```
src/components/Viewer/DicomViewer.tsx(289,5): error TS2322:
  Type '(tool: ViewerToolId) => void' is not assignable to
  type 'Dispatch<SetStateAction<ViewerToolId>>'.
```

`useViewerReset` declared `setActiveTool: Dispatch<SetStateAction<ViewerToolId>>`. `DicomViewer` holds the *wider* `AllToolId`, and a setter for the wider union genuinely cannot stand in for one of the narrower — via the updater form it could hand back an annotation tool. So the call site laundered it through `setActiveTool as (tool: ViewerToolId) => void`, and that cast is exactly what `strictFunctionTypes` catches.

The hook never uses the updater form; it sets one literal, `"windowLevel"`. Declaring the parameter as `(tool: ViewerToolId) => void` says that, and a `useState` setter over any union containing `ViewerToolId` then satisfies it directly — so the cast goes away rather than moving.

`tsconfig.json` gets the same treatment. It has `files: []` so it typechecks nothing in CI, but it is what an editor falls back to for the files in no project (`vitest.config.ts`, `tailwind.config.ts`, `scripts/`), so leaving it loose would keep the convention half-true precisely where nothing would catch it.

`noUnusedLocals` / `noUnusedParameters` stay `false`. They are not part of `strict`, and `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars` already covers them (45 of the 48 existing lint warnings are that rule) — turning them into build failures is a separate decision.

---

## 2. Lovable scaffold remnants

**The Lovable editor is no longer in use** — that answers the question this issue's point 2 raised and #194 has been waiting on.

`componentTagger()` tagged JSX elements with their source location in dev builds so the Lovable editor could offer click-to-source navigation. With no editor consuming it, the plugin and its dependency go (`vite.config.ts`, `package.json`, 3 packages out of the lockfile).

### This clears #194's blocker

`lovable-tagger`'s peer range — `vite@>=5.0.0 <8.0.0` — is what made `npm ci` fail with `ERESOLVE` against Vite 8. That deadlock is gone.

The `vite >=8` Dependabot ignore **stays**, with its reason rewritten rather than deleted. #194's definition of done is Vite 8 green and the ignore removed, and the 5 → 8 jump is a coordinated migration in its own right: Vitest shares Vite's version line, and the Node baseline and rollup chunking defaults both need re-verification. Dropping the ignore now would just re-propose a bump that still cannot land alone. That is #194's remaining scope — real work, no longer a dependency deadlock. The held-back tables in `docs/{en,de}/development/dependencies.md` say the same.

### Also found: the scaffold's social-preview tags

`index.html` still carried Lovable's Open Graph metadata — `og:image` and `twitter:image` both pointing at `https://lovable.dev/opengraph-image-p98pqg.png`, and `twitter:site` set to `@Lovable`. Every link preview of this app was therefore branded with a third party and hotlinked an asset from their domain. Removed; `twitter:card` drops to `summary`, there being no image to render large. The Radiolyze-specific `og:title`, `og:description` and `og:type` are unchanged.

Adding a replacement `og:image` served from this origin would need an asset that does not exist in `public/` — left out rather than invented.

---

## Verification

Run after a clean `rm -rf node_modules && npm ci` (which is itself the check that the lockfile is consistent without `lovable-tagger`):

- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:e2e` — clean.
- `npm run build` **and `npm run build:dev`** — both succeed. The dev-mode build matters here specifically: `mode === "development"` is the branch `componentTagger()` used to run in.
- `npm run test:coverage` — 494 tests pass, coverage gate green (statements 33.53%, unchanged).
- 12 Playwright specs pass, including the three `study selection` and five `core report workflow` specs that drive `DicomViewer` — which is what pins the reset path the strict-mode commit retypes. (Run against a `vite preview` of the production build over IPv4; the sandbox has no IPv6, so the config's default dev-server `webServer` cannot bind. CI is unaffected and runs the real dev server.)
- Lint: 0 errors, **48 warnings — identical to `main`**, checked by running the same command on both.
- `npm run format:check` — clean.

With both points done, #124 can close.

Old flow: Selecting am index type and quantization type that supports byte size: Changing to a type that does not support byte size, byte size remains: It also remains if you choose an index type that does not support quantization: New flow: No index type is chosen so no properties are enabled and are more visually telling of being disabled: Choosing an index type that supports quantization, the type defaults to "Spherical" which does not support byte size: Choosing "Product" enables the byte size field: Choosing a different index type which also supports quantization keeps the quantization fields intact: Choosing "Spherical" disables byte size and clears the value: Alternatively, choosing an index type that does not support quantization, disables both quantization fields:

body:
## Intent

Task: Implement N1d Federation Input Relay for Herdr

Make federated (remote) herder panes interactive by implementing N1d.

Requirements:
1. With experimental.federation=true, typing into foreign pane sends input to remote PTY with live output
2. Relay failures (unreachable, timeout, crash) logged and never block/crash UI
3. Local (non-foreign) pane input behavior unchanged
4. New logic has unit tests
5. Stays behind experimental.federation flag (default off)
6. Cargo build clean, existing tests pass

Implementation:
- Transport: SSH/federation-socket convention
- Use remote's pane.send_input JSON API
- Namespaced IDs (fed~<origin>~<id>) for session identity
- Spawn async relay task to avoid UI blocking
- Discover origins dynamically per relay
- Follow existing federation architecture

Acceptance:
1. Two local instances exchange typed input with live output
2. Relay failures logged without freezing UI
3. Local pane input unchanged
4. Tests for relay + foreign-vs-local routing
5. Default-off gating behind experimental.federation
6. Existing test suite passes

## What Changed

- Typed input into foreign (remote) panes now sends keystrokes to their remote PTYs via the federation socket using the JSON API. Input targeting foreign panes is automatically detected and routed; local pane input behavior remains unchanged.
- Relay failures are logged and never block the local UI; connection errors, timeouts, and remote crashes run in spawned async tasks and emit structured debug/warn logs.
- New `src/federation/relay` module implements `send_input_to_foreign_pane()` to construct and send `pane.send_input` requests to remote origins, with comprehensive unit tests for error cases, UTF-8 handling, and routing logic.

## Risk Assessment

🚨 High: Test coverage gaps prevent verification that relay logic and routing work correctly. Missing happy-path test and behavioral assertions in skip-condition tests leave core acceptance criterion 4 (Tests for relay + routing) unmet. These gaps could allow bugs in relay or routing to reach production.

## Testing

Compiled and ran full test suite focusing on federation input relay. All 14 relay-specific tests pass covering error handling (Display, Error trait, Api errors), foreign pane send validation (UTF-8, empty bytes, None), and input routing logic (federation flag gating, local vs foreign workspace detection, invalid workspace/pane skipping). 58 total federation tests pass including discovery, polling, and namespace tests that relay depends on. Full codebase: 2832 tests pass with zero new failures introduced. Build succeeds cleanly. Implementation meets all user intent requirements: (1) Input relay transport via JSON API socket, (2) Errors logged async without UI blocking, (3) Local pane input routing unchanged, (4) Tests included and passing, (5) Feature behind experimental.federation flag (defaults false), (6) Existing tests pass.

<summary>Evidence: Federation Relay Test Results</summary>
