author: cto-new[bot]
body:
## Summary
Makes Standard's "Up to 50 overdue invoices tracked" an **enforced** limit in the backend, not marketing copy.

- **Watcher gate** (`app/src/pipeline/watcher.ts`): for active-Standard merchants, when pre-existing overdue count >= 50 and the incoming invoice has no existing task, skip task creation but still upsert the invoice (stays visible in the dashboard). Logs `[watcher] Merchant <id> at Standard 50-invoice limit — invoice <id> not tracked. Upgrade to Pro for unlimited.` and returns a normal HTTP-200 ack (Stripe never retries).
- **Semantics**: the 50th invoice is still tracked; the 51st is blocked. Paid/voided invoices free capacity; previously-blocked invoices are auto-picked-up on their next event once under the limit (gate skips only when no task exists). Pro and free merchants are never capped.
- **DB helpers** (`app/src/db.ts`): `countOverdueInvoices`, `getTaskForInvoice`, `invoiceLimitFor`, `isActiveStandard`.
- **Dashboard** (`app/src/ui/dashboard.html`): `GET /stats` now returns `invoiceLimit` / `overdueInvoices` / `overInvoiceLimit`; a notice banner ("You've reached your 50-invoice limit on Standard… Upgrade to Pro for unlimited tracking." with an Upgrade-to-Pro button) shows when over the limit; the Invoices stat card also surfaces the overdue count.
- **Downgrade (Pro → Standard, over limit) is non-destructive**: existing invoices, tasks, and in-flight sequences are untouched — the account simply sits over-limit (banner shows, new tracking blocked) until paid/voided invoices bring the count below 50.

## Tested (live, against :3002, fixture rows + crafted webhook events)
55 assertions, all passing — incl. Standard@50→51st blocked (invoice visible, no task, HTTP 200), Standard@49→50th tracked, Pro@51+ tracked, free tracked, full downgrade scenario (60 tracked → Standard → untouched, overInvoiceLimit=true, new event blocked → pay to 49 → tracked again, previously-blocked invoice picked up), and /stats shapes. `bunx tsc --noEmit` passes.

author: groxaxo
body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds bounded, named inbound WhatsApp consumers and a native reaction endpoint while keeping one Baileys socket authoritative.

Configured owner-DM command prefixes are routed exclusively to their named queue, so the default Hermes poller and local integrations do not race to drain the same message. Reactions preserve the complete inbound Baileys message key and use the existing serialized send queue.

The bridge reuse handshake now fingerprints the runtime helper modules and route configuration, preventing gateway restarts from silently reusing stale routing or reaction behavior.

## Related Issue

No linked issue.

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- Add configured, bounded consumer queues selected by an owner-DM chat ID and exact command prefix.
- Reject unconfigured consumer polling and keep group messages on the default Hermes queue.
- Add loopback-only `POST /react` using the full inbound message key and serialized Baileys send path.
- Restart stale bridges when runtime helpers, read-receipt behavior, or consumer routes change.
- Add focused JavaScript and Python regression coverage.
- Document the supported `gateway.platforms.whatsapp.extra.consumer_routes` configuration and
  loopback consumer/reaction contract in the WhatsApp guide.

## How to Test

1. Run `for test_file in scripts/whatsapp-bridge/*.test.mjs; do node "$test_file" || exit 1; done`.
2. Run `uv run python -m pytest -q tests/gateway/test_whatsapp*.py`.
3. Run `cd website && npm run build:fast`.
4. Configure two named owner-DM prefixes, start the gateway, and confirm `/health` reports separate bounded queues and a runtime hash.
5. Poll each consumer independently and send a reaction using the event's `readReceiptKey`.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Ubuntu Linux

The full repository gate was attempted after installing its declared dev, messaging, and ACP extras. It showed failures and temporary-directory logging errors outside the WhatsApp slice before being stopped at 6%. The complete WhatsApp gateway slice passed: 118 passed, 2 skipped. All eight WhatsApp bridge JavaScript test files passed.

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — or N/A

author: elliottkember
body:
## The change in Reanimated 4

`mutableGuestDecorator` in `react-native-reanimated@4.5.3/lib/module/mutables.js:141` defines `.value` on the JS runtime like this:

```js
set(newValue) {
  if (globalThis.__RUNTIME_KIND === 1) {
    checkInvalidWriteDuringRender();
    scheduleOnUI(() => { mutable.value = newValue; });   // async
  } else { mutable.setAsync(newValue); }
}
```

The getter returns a cached `latest` and only refreshes it when the UI runtime flags the value dirty. So **reading a SharedValue back after writing it on the JS thread returns the previous value.** Reanimated 3.16 assigned `mutable._value` synchronously (`valueSetter.js:64`), which is why this only appeared with the RN 0.86 upgrade.

Two places in this component relied on the old synchronous behaviour.

## The crash

`_resolveAndHandleTap` assigned `doubleTapFirstTap.value` and read it straight back:

```js
doubleTapFirstTap.value = { id: now.toString(), x: ..., y: ... };
_addTouch(doubleTapFirstTap.value);   // returns the PREVIOUS value
```

After any of the five reset sites the previous value is `undefined`, so `_addTouch(undefined)` put an `undefined` into `stateTouches` and the render crashed reading `touch.x`. It's a race, which is why it took several taps. Fixed by binding the tap to a local and passing that. `doubleTapFirstTap` stays a SharedValue — it's written from worklets at 1374, 1404, 1465 and 1619.

## The hang (likely)

`_addTouch` had the same shape one line apart — stale read, async write, then a second read the write hadn't reached:

```js
touches.value = [...touches.value, touch];
setStateTouches([...touches.value]);
```

No worklet ever read that SharedValue, so it's gone. Both callbacks now use functional updaters, where React guarantees `prev` is current:

```js
setStateTouches((prev) => [...prev, touch]);
setStateTouches((prev) => prev.filter((t) => t !== touch));
```

A stale read let `_removeTouch` write back an array still holding removed touches, which the next `_addTouch` would resurrect — remounting feedback views that animate, report done, and remove again. That's my best explanation for the release-build hang, but I haven't confirmed it on a device, so treat it as a candidate. The change also drops a cross-runtime serialization per tap.

## Also fixed

`_removeTouch` moving from `splice(indexOf(touch), 1)` to `filter` means an identity miss is a no-op instead of degrading to `splice(-1, 1)` and dropping an unrelated touch.

## Not the cause: the dev-only freeze

Worth recording, since it's where this investigation started. Reanimated freezes objects handed to worklets in `freezeObjectInDev` (`react-native-worklets/lib/module/memory/serializable.native.js:479`), guarded by `if (!__DEV__ || globalThis.__RUNTIME_KIND !== RuntimeKind.ReactNative) return`. Every index becomes a non-configurable accessor with a no-op setter, then `preventExtensions`; `length` stays writable.

Running the Hermes VM from RN 0.79.7's `sdks/hermesc/osx-bin/hermes` against a faithful copy of that freeze: `push` throws `cannot add a new property` — exactly #183 — but `splice` neither throws nor leaves a hole. It silently removes the wrong element (`splice(0,1)` on `[a,b]` yields `[a]`). So there was no path from the frozen array to an `undefined`, and being `__DEV__`-only it couldn't explain a release hang either. The stale read is the actual source of both.

## Verification

`eslint` and `tsc --noEmit` pass (husky pre-commit ran both). Not yet exercised on a device — the dev crash and the release hang both need a real build to confirm.

## SPECS.md

No change needed. The only touch-feedback entry is line 82, and this makes the code match what it already promises.

body:
## Scope

PR 4 from the V4 audit plan, targeting `delta`.

### Baseline validation
- Audited baseline: `d4bd8a883e9e68eb4021559c659b443a3fa1caf4`.
- `delta` HEAD at implementation validation: `e1393da31b840e15e660e8c563eda9c8de5d4d37` (three commits beyond the audited baseline).
- The intervening commits were reviewed and did not supersede the assigned firewall findings.
- Existing Cloudflare CIDR last-known-good caching and its 7-day fail-closed expiry are preserved.

## Changes

### UFW exactness and SSH preservation
- Reconcile Cloudflare web rules as exact TCP 80/443 ingress and require the final incoming default to remain `deny` or `reject`.
- Parse real UFW status direction semantics: ordinary inbound rows may omit literal `IN`; explicit `IN` is accepted; `OUT` cannot satisfy ingress readiness; routed/`FWD` allows remain fail-closed/ambiguous.
- Strip comments before direction/ambiguity classification so comments cannot spoof direction/source or hide broad/profile/range exposure.
- Preserve an existing explicit single-port inbound SSH `ALLOW` / `LIMIT`, including source-restricted rules. Add the broad default only if no suitable SSH rule exists.
- Fail before mutation if SSH is detected on port 80 or 443.
- Publish the initial Cloudflare CIDR cache atomically and propagate publication failure.

### Docker packet-path enforcement
- Enforce public Caddy admission in `DOCKER-USER`; UFW remains defense-in-depth rather than the proof point for Docker-published ports.
- Manage one project chain, `VW-CF-INGRESS`, scoped to Caddy's pinned `172.22.0.0/28` bridge destination.
- The state exception is **reply-direction only**: `ESTABLISHED,RELATED --ctdir REPLY -> RETURN`. Replies to Caddy-initiated outbound flows pass; ORIGINAL-direction packets from a direct connection that existed before reconciliation do not get the state bypass.
- Cloudflare IPv4 source + original destination 80/443 rules use `RETURN`, followed by project-scoped 80/443 `DROP` sentinels. No project forwarding `ACCEPT` shortcut or project MASQUERADE is added.
- First-install/orphan-chain reconciliation is fail-closed: install DROP sentinels, purge stale/orphaned project rules, install the REPLY-only established return, attach the clean chain to `DOCKER-USER`, then add Cloudflare returns.
- Exact-state verification requires the REPLY-only state rule, exact count/presence, one first-rule parent jump, and RETURN-before-DROP ordering. A legacy directionless established rule is drift and is reconciled.
- Remove only the exact OCI `FORWARD REJECT` and known legacy VaultWarden source-only ACCEPT/MASQUERADE exceptions when present.
- Require a successful `iptables-save` snapshot before mutation and restore on mutation failure/interruption.
- Inspect running `dockerd` argv/effective config, including `--config-file`, `--firewall-backend`, and `--iptables`, and reject unsupported backend/chain contracts.

### Transactional periodic updates
- Before any network refresh, validate the running Docker backend and determine whether the existing Docker gate is exact against a valid cached Cloudflare IPv4 generation.
- A proven-safe cached generation may remain serving if an ordinary refresh fails; an unproven/missing/expired/non-exact prior generation fails closed by stopping Caddy on backend/fetch/parse/UFW/snapshot/reconcile failure.
- Install a pre-transaction signal handler before backend/network validation: INT/TERM/HUP also stop Caddy when the prior gate is unproven. Once rollback snapshots exist, the transactional rollback signal handler takes over.
- Snapshot full iptables state before the first UFW mutation and snapshot managed UFW rule files before changing them.
- On later failure, restore UFW files/reload first, then apply the full `iptables-restore` snapshot as the final netfilter write.
- If rollback itself fails, attempt to stop Caddy; reconcile/verify both firewall layers before atomically publishing the new CIDR cache.

### Caddy and Docker lifecycle
- Publish Caddy web ports explicitly on IPv4 and use `restart: on-failure`, allowing independent crash recovery without auto-starting ahead of firewall reconciliation on dockerd restart.
- Normalize stale Caddy runtime bindings/restart policy on upgrade.
- Install and validate `docker.service.d/20-vaultwarden-runtime.conf` so Docker start/restart pulls in the existing firewall and startup owners.
- Keep `vaultwarden-iptables.service` runtime-only: no package installation or persistent netfilter-state ownership. Startup requires successful iptables reconciliation.

### Fail-closed setup and uninstall ownership
- Required UFW and Docker/OCI reconciliation failures are authoritative setup failures; firewall failure/interruption attempts to stop Caddy.
- Uninstall removes the exact managed Docker lifecycle drop-in, exact `DOCKER-USER -> VW-CF-INGRESS` jump(s), and uniquely named project chain while preserving foreign/unrecognized drop-ins and unrelated raw iptables state.
- Uninstall verification reports positively owned residual artifacts.

## Files changed
1. `docker-compose.yml.example`
2. `docs/COMMAND-REFERENCE.md`
3. `lib/firewall.sh`
4. `setup.sh`
5. `systemd/vaultwarden-firewall-update.service`
6. `systemd/vaultwarden-iptables.service`
7. `systemd/vaultwarden-startup.service`
8. `tests/suites/foundation/case-systemd.bash`
9. `tests/suites/operations/case-firewall-update.bash`
10. `tests/suites/operations/case-operations.bash`
11. `tests/suites/operations/case-uninstall.bash`
12. `utilities/maintenance-update-firewall.sh`
13. `utilities/setup-firewall.sh`
14. `utilities/setup-systemd.sh`
15. `utilities/uninstall-vaultwarden.sh`

Temporary PR-only self-modifying CI/patch helpers are removed from the final diff. UFW helper deduplication is intentionally deferred to a follow-up rather than mixed into this security-sensitive PR.

## Validation status
- Current helper-free head: `e9d235c64c5fa50f6448bf2bf361ebea36151f81`.
- Current PR metadata: 15 permanent files, 263 commits, +3,292/-642.
- The latest updater prior-generation/early-failure/signal changes passed changed-file Bash syntax, warning-level ShellCheck, the focused firewall regression, literal `./tests/run-tests.sh all` on Ubuntu 24.04, and `git diff --check` before temporary validation helpers were removed.
- Canonical PR CI run `31466610381` passed on this exact helper-free head: PR diff check, Bash syntax, strict repository-wide ShellCheck, Docker Compose validation, doc drift/generated command reference, systemd hardening, and the foundation, security, operations, and data-protection functional suites are all green.
- Two additional post-change inspection passes were completed on this exact helper-free head and both were clean (2/2). Pass 1 rechecked the REPLY-only Docker gate, updater safe-old-vs-unproven failure semantics, pre-transaction/transaction signal handoff, rollback ordering, lifecycle ownership, branch hygiene, and exact-head CI. Pass 2 independently challenged negative guarantees: pre-existing direct ORIGINAL traffic reaches DROP rather than the state exception, Caddy-originated reply traffic keeps its REPLY path, safe cached generations survive ordinary refresh failure, unproven generations fail closed, Docker retains isolation/NAT ownership, and uninstall removes the project gate only after project containers are gone.

## Remaining Noble / OCI integration
A disposable Ubuntu 24.04 Noble OCI host is still required before final merge approval. Hosted CI does not claim these packet-path/reboot results.

author: ljcl
body:
## Summary

Found from a real disconnect. The log opened with:

```
{"event":"oauth.refresh_replayed","clientId":"…/mcp-oauth-client-metadata","generation":1,"seen":15}
{"event":"security.rejected","hasAuthorization":true,"reason":"expired","status":401}
```

`generation: 1` is only ever minted by the **authorization code** grant, and it
was minted as a literal — `issue(…, 1)` — while the per-client counter stayed
where rotation had pushed it. So re-authorizing a connector that had already
refreshed handed back a token *below* the high-water mark. It authenticated
fine for one access-token lifetime (an hour), then died on its first refresh as
`oauth.refresh_replayed`: this server refusing, as stolen, the credential it had
itself issued. Re-consenting produced generation 1 again, so the loop was stable
and read as a client bug. Only a restart, which empties the map, appeared to fix
it — which is also why it survived: every deploy hid it.

`claimGeneration` is now the one place a generation is minted and both grants go
through it, so the counter is monotonic per client. The refresh path is
unchanged in behaviour (`max(seen, presented) + 1` reduces to the previous
`generation + 1` once the replay check has passed). The consequence worth
stating is that a second authorization for the same `client_id` supersedes the
first — reconnecting invalidates the session it replaced, which is what
reconnecting should mean.

**Second change, from the same log.** Two consent flows completed and then
nothing followed:

```
{"event":"oauth.authorize_prompt", …}
{"event":"oauth.authorized", …}
{"event":"security.rejected","hasAuthorization":false,"reason":"missing","status":401}
```

Only success was logged at `/oauth/token`, so every RFC 6749 refusal returned
silently. `oauth.authorized` followed by nothing therefore could not distinguish
"the code was presented and refused" from "the client never came back for the
token" — this server versus not this server, on the one question the log was
needed for. `oauthError` now writes `oauth.token_denied` with the grant, the
client, and the same description the caller is already given, so nothing is
logged that was not already sent. `oauth.refresh_replayed` stays beside it
rather than folding into it: the `generation`/`seen` pair is what makes a replay
attributable, and the gap between those two numbers is what exposed the bug
above.

`TokenDeps.generations` becomes required. Optional, it read as a knob and
behaved as a defect — a caller that omitted it got a throwaway map per request,
which is replay detection that detects nothing. The sole caller,
`createOAuthRouter`, has always passed one.

Two regression tests, both verified to fail against the previous
implementation: a re-authorized connector surviving its first refresh (400 → 200),
and a refused exchange appearing in the log.

Not fixed here, filed as #163: replay detection keys on the caller-supplied
`client_id` form field rather than anything in the verified token, so a thief
holding a stolen refresh token can bypass detection entirely by sending a
different string. It needs a new claim on the refresh token, which is a token
format change and does not belong in this diff.

## Verification

- [x] `bun run check` (or `bun run check:affected` on a branch) passes
- [ ] `bun run test:stories` passes for UI changes, if applicable — no UI change
- [ ] Storybook sweep for UI changes (desktop + `claudeIosCard` viewport), if applicable — no UI change

`bun run test:coverage` raised the branch threshold 95.5 → 95.6 (dead `??`
branches removed with the optional `generations`); the ratcheted value is
committed.

author: ryanklee
body:
Extracted from #4545 so it is small enough to actually be reviewed. #4545 is 279,503 diff
characters against the reviewer's 80,000-char cap — reviewers saw 29% of it, truncated by
position, so late files were invisible. This is 23,359.

## The defect

The coordinator made **2,590 dispatch attempts in 24 hours and was refused 2,590 times**, every
one of them `codex.headless.full -> epsilon`. Over 7 days: **7,238 ticks at `dispatched=0`
against 6 at `dispatched=1`.** 117 tasks sit in refusal cooldown at any moment. This is why
every lane has been launched by hand.

It is an ordering defect, not a bad guard:

| line | what happens |
|---|---|
| `:2345` | `_availability_recomposition_candidate_requests` builds candidates with the lane FIXED and no lane-compatibility filter |
| `:2353` | `adapter.admit` selects the best-scoring route from that unfiltered set |
| `:2418` | `platform_lane_compatibility_reason` refuses the selection |

The predicate is correct and runs downstream of the choice it should have constrained. Its own
"Next action" text names the remedy — *"rerun route selection for a route compatible with the
requested lane"* — which never happens.

`epsilon` is a Claude lane (tmux `hapax-claude-epsilon`; the coordinator's fallback roster gives
all eight greek roles `platform=claude`), so no Codex route was ever executable there.

## The fix

Filter candidates through the **same** predicate that refuses them later — deliberately not a
second notion of compatibility, which would drift from the one that gates dispatch and stay
invisible until it refused again.

It narrows the candidate set and never widens it. The real consequence, stated plainly:
admission may now select a **lower-scoring** route. A runnable worse route beats an unrunnable
better one, and where nothing is runnable the set is empty and the existing fail-closed path
refuses rather than downgrading past a quality floor.

## Why the registry commit rides along

`d988b2153` (cross-model downgrade disarm) is included because the dispatch tests reference
`platform_capability_registry` and it gained a load-time validator. Verified: the two
cherry-pick clean onto `main` and the suite passes standalone.

## Tests

New pins in `tests/scripts/test_dispatch_lane_compatible_recomposition.py` were written FIRST
and verified red before the fix.

One existing test is re-pointed and it deserves scrutiny rather than a footnote.
`test_claude_lane_recomposed_to_codex_fails_before_mq_consumption` pinned the **symptom** — that
an impossible selection is refused before MQ is consumed. Its load-bearing invariant is the MQ
state, and that is unchanged and separately verified: `state=offered`, `reason=None`, launcher
never invoked, `launched=False`. Only the stderr string and recorded platform moved, because the
refusal is now `no_eligible_dimensional_candidates` — earlier and more honest. Renamed to say
what it now protects, and it asserts the inverse so a regression fails rather than goes quiet.

`test_cx_lane_recomposed_to_codex_remains_launch_admissible` passes **unmodified** — that is the
evidence legitimate cross-platform recomposition still works.

## Draft because

One test (`test_launch_recomposes_from_subscription_receipt_without_account_live`) needs its
assertion restored to main's form. On #4545 it passes for a reason I misattributed: I claimed the
lane filter removed a codex reason code, but standalone testing shows the primary route here IS
codex, so it is still scored and still contributes that reason. The absence on #4545 came from
separate codex-quota work, not from this filter. Correcting that before marking ready.

author: mauricio-gg
body:
## Why

Part of #206's cleanup. The `Takion receive queue overflow (256 slots). Dropped 1 packet(s)` log misled three hardware investigations: it names a **control-channel** reorder queue that video/audio packets bypass entirely; the count was pinned at 1 because `takion_log_drop_summary` was invoked and reset on every single drop (`TAKION_RECV_OVERFLOW_LOG_INTERVAL_MS` existed but was never applied to it); "overflow" printed for any drop cause; and duplicate / late / true-overflow / gap-skip / teardown-flush drops were indistinguishable. The 611 identical lines in log `18107437792` turned out to be benign control-message retransmit noise — while everyone (docs included) read them as video-path saturation.

## What

- **`ChiakiReorderQueueDropReason`** (DUPLICATE / LATE / OVERFLOW / GAP_SKIP / FLUSH) threaded through the drop callback; all six invocation sites in `reorderqueue.c` pass accurate reasons; the sole implementor (`takion_data_drop`) tallies per-reason counters.
- **Truthful, rate-limited summary**: `Takion control-channel reorder queue dropped N packet(s) over last Xms (dup= late= overflow= gap_skip= flush=, last seq ...)` — emitted at most once per interval, real accumulated counts, first-emission window seeded truthfully, no contradictory "no drops in last 0ms" teardown line, and the load-bearing `error_reoder_queue:`→`beach:` fall-through documented.
- **Removed the `null entry` LOGE storm** — NULL is a documented, expected input from gap-skips of never-received slots (up to 8 unthrottled LOGE lines per push under queue pressure previously).
- **Docs corrected** (`MOTION_MACROBLOCKING_INVESTIGATION.md`, `FPS_HEALTH_INVESTIGATION.md`, `REMOTE_PLAY_SMOOTHNESS_PLAN.md`): the "PS5 ignores congestion control feedback" claims are replaced with the evidence-backed model — a downward-only bitrate ratchet driven by even 0.8–5% reported loss (logs `11782861312`, `18107437792`; fixed client-side in PR #213). The "RTP packet reorder queue" mislabel is corrected to the control-channel message queue.

## Review & validation

code-guardian reviewed; four required fixes applied (LOGE removal, header/impl comment agreement, truthful first window, teardown line suppression). Builds green: test suite + testing VPK v0.1.852. CI checks on this PR.

author: netadvanced
body:
Draft — opening now to track the work; further testing and a documentation review pass are planned before this is marked ready.

## The bug

`getSessionStorage()` in `tasks/index.ts` and `templates.ts`, and `downloadAttachment()` in `tasks/attachments.ts`, called `authManager.getSession()` directly on the closure-captured manager from tool registration instead of resolving through the ALS-bound per-identity one. In `oidc-http` mode the closure manager is never authenticated (no static `VIKUNJA_API_TOKEN` — every credential lives in the vault), so this threw `AUTH_REQUIRED` for a fully provisioned identity: `vikunja_tasks list`, every `vikunja_templates` subcommand, and `download-attachment` were all broken for real multi-user traffic — even though the wire-level credential (`resolveEffectiveAuthManager` in `vikunja-rest.ts`, landed 2026-07-21) was already correct.

## The fix

Threads the same ALS-first resolution already used at the wire layer into these three call sites: `hasRequestContext() ? await getAuthManagerFromContext() : authManager`, falling back to the closure manager only in `stdio` mode where no request context is ever bound.

## Validation (three layers, not just unit tests)

1. **TDD**: `tests/oidc/isolation.test.ts` gained a "Session-storage reads that bypass ALS resolution" class — 4 tests, verified failing with the exact `AUTH_REQUIRED` error before the fix, passing after. Full suite: 159/159 test suites, 3461/3461 tests, lint/typecheck/coverage-gate all clean.
2. **Automated live e2e**: `scripts/oidc-e2e.ts` extended with steps (d2)-(d4) — live `tasks list`/`templates list` against a real local Vikunja stack (previously broken, now pass), plus a second identity provisioned and calling tools concurrently with the first. All 8 steps pass.
3. **Real multi-user demo**: stood up a full lab (Context Forge + Keycloak + a dedicated Vikunja instance) with 3 real fake users, ran the full provision → concurrent isolated list/create → deprovision walkthrough through actual Keycloak-issued JWTs and a real gateway, and watched a task land live in a real user's real Vikunja project. Perfect isolation by name across concurrent identities; deprovisioning one user re-locked them immediately without affecting the other.

`docs/CONTEXT-FORGE.md`'s stale "known gap" paragraph (predated the 2026-07-21 wire fix, described neither bug accurately) is replaced with the current, accurate state.

## Deliberately deferred

`vikunja_auth refresh` gives a stdio-flavored "use vikunja_auth.connect first" error when called unprovisioned in `oidc-http` mode, instead of an oidc-appropriate message. Cosmetic only — `refresh` is a no-op informational subcommand either way, no functional impact.

## Notes for review

- Base is `feat/oidc-mode`, not `main` — that branch is itself unmerged and ~80 commits behind `main`; this fix belongs with the epic and gets rebased together with everything else when a merge-back happens, out of scope here.
- A setup runbook for the live-demo lab (Context Forge + Keycloak gotchas, troubleshooting) was written during testing and is currently parked outside the repo pending a decision on whether it's worth keeping as project documentation.
